author: br3nda
body:
## What

A third GitHub Actions workflow, `deploy-staging-branch.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` with a required `branch` input, deploys that branch/tag/ref to staging. For previewing an unmerged branch on staging before it's reviewed/merged to `main` - same thing `STAGING_BRANCH=that-branch make staging-deploy` already does locally (see AGENTS.md's `update-*`/deploy gotchas).

Otherwise a straight copy of `deploy-production.yml`'s own branch-input pattern (checkout the given ref, same AWS OIDC + SSM plumbing), retargeted at the `staging` Capistrano stage/environment/deploy key instead of production's.

Shares `deploy-staging.yml`'s `deploy-staging` concurrency group, so the automatic on-merge-to-main deploy and a manual branch preview can never run at the same time and stomp on each other's release.

## Stacked on #935

Depends on the same SSM/OIDC plumbing that PR sets up (`AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`, the SSM ProxyCommand steps) - based on `feature/staging-auto-deploy`, not `main`. Needs the same prerequisites #935 itself needs (openaustralia/infrastructure#710, #714) before it'll actually work.

## Note on the staging environment's branch policy

The `staging` GitHub Environment's deployment branch policy (set up for #935) restricts it to `main` - which would block this workflow's whole point. That policy likely needs relaxing (or this workflow needs its own, wider-scoped environment) before this is actually usable; flagged in a comment in the workflow file itself. Left as a decision for whoever configures the Environment, rather than guessing at the right policy here.

author: lynnswap
body:
## Purpose

[CI #628](https://github.com/lynnswap/CodexReviewKit/actions/runs/33283791373) exposed timing-dependent authentication failures. A native callback could publish a valid account before the operation recorded terminal success, so cancellation, runtime teardown, or a duplicate completion notification could still invalidate an otherwise successful login.

This change makes one authentication operation own request admission, notification replay, terminal outcome arbitration, and the final account-state commit across transport buffering and MainActor reentrancy.

## Changes

- model the primary login request from admission through challenge, definitive rejection, early completion, cancellation, and terminal commit instead of beginning ownership only after a challenge exists
- arbitrate callback success, notification success, and failure through one monotonic phase transition; the winning success is committed and published in one MainActor turn before rate-limit enrichment begins
- stage `account/login/completed` and `account/updated` notifications that arrive before the challenge response, then reconcile them by exact login ID and receipt order; staged failure is claimed exactly once by its processing owner
- prevent losing notification, callback, account-refresh, cancellation, and teardown work from overwriting the winner or taking its cleanup scope after suspension
- keep authentication metadata separate from cached quota state: metadata-only snapshots preserve existing limits and fetch diagnostics, while rate-enriched snapshots update them explicitly
- invalidate and roll back the primary runtime when a dispatched login has an unknown or unreadable outcome, while isolated login failures close only their isolated runtime
- distinguish active-operation rollback from retired-completion rollback: the former restores the account captured at admission, while the latter preserves any newer authorized account
- keep all new authentication regressions offline with fake transports, web sessions, and URL openers; test URLs use the reserved `.invalid` domain

## Review focus

- the single terminal phase transition shared by callback, notification, cancellation, and failure paths
- exact-ID replay of early completion/account-update notifications
- the synchronous account commit boundary before asynchronous rate-limit enrichment
- the ownership boundary between authentication metadata and cached rate-limit state
- primary-runtime invalidation versus isolated-runtime cleanup semantics

## Testing

- `swift test --build-system swiftbuild --no-parallel` (1,146 tests passed)
- targeted offline regressions for metadata-only refresh, persisted cache reload, transient rate-limit failure, and callback/notification arbitration
- `xcodebuild build-for-testing -project Tools/ReviewMonitor/CodexReviewMonitor.xcodeproj -scheme CodexReviewMonitor -destination 'platform=macOS,arch=arm64' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO`

author: eldad8802-prog
body:
**W7 run 4 delivered the first real runtime evidence — and it caught a regression I introduced in the native foundation (#276).**

```
ANR in co.il.promaxgroup.dubiz (co.il.promaxgroup.dubiz/.MainActivity)
Reason: Input dispatching timed out (Application does not have a focused window)
```

The artifact screenshots show the app **still sitting on the splash**; logcat shows `Waiting because no window has focus but ActivityRecord{...MainActivity} may eventually add a window when it finishes starting up. Will wait for 5000ms` → ANR 5s later.

## Cause
`launchAutoHide: false` — the splash lived until the **web** shell called `SplashScreen.hide()`. Safe for a bundled app; wrong for a **remote**-WebView app. On a cold emulator the remote page hadn't painted in time, so nothing hid the splash and the launch window never gained focus.

## Fix
- `launchAutoHide: true` + `launchShowDuration: 2000` — the system always retires the splash; a remote page can no longer hold the launch window open.
- `native-shell.ts` still calls `hide()` when the shell is interactive — now an optimization for the fast path, not the only exit.
- `android.backgroundColor: "#FEF8F2"` — the splash→content hand-off (and any remote-load gap) is DS cream instead of a white flash. That white-flash worry is what motivated the original `false`; this addresses it properly.

## W7 status: still **OPEN**
9/10 automated checks already pass on a Pixel-6/API-36 emulator (install, cold launch, activity alive, portrait, landscape, window/inset capture, edge-to-edge, in-app back). The logcat check must go green on a re-run **and** the screenshots must be reviewed by eye before anything is called closed.

author: dkaps6
body:
## Purpose
M77 is the first predictive test authorized by M76's qualified exact-personnel information layer. It is deliberately one frozen experiment, not another model zoo.

## Frozen foundation
- canonical-v3 football-only CSV committed on `main`
- SHA256 `c4a481a760657bb7516d52b9aa9ba84af096063a4e78660b12a541f59fd7b742`
- 884 stable-primary QB games: 444 in 2024 / 440 in 2025
- zero sportsbook/game-market features or cohort filters

## New information tested
Pregame personnel discontinuity only:
- offensive OL continuity/turnover and replacement prior role
- WR/TE/RB continuity/turnover and replacement prior role
- opponent DB continuity/turnover and replacement prior role
- opponent expected pass-rush continuity plus strictly-prior individual pressure/sack quality
- pre-registered OL×rush and skill×secondary interactions

Target-game snap counts/PFR outcomes are prohibited. The broken post-2024 nflverse injury feed is not used.

## Model boundary
One model family only: `StandardScaler + Ridge(alpha=10, fit_intercept=False)`.
Two corrections are fit separately:
1. attempt residual = actual attempts - canonical predicted attempts
2. YPA residual = actual YPA - canonical implied YPA

`fit_intercept=False` prevents M77 from winning via a generic baseline bias correction unrelated to personnel.

## Validation boundary
- early 2024 -> late 2024 development check
- full eligible 2024 -> untouched 2025 final evaluation
- uncovered games receive zero correction, so overall 2025 metrics remain honest

## Pre-registered promotion gate
M77 promotes only if **all** pass:
- 2025 personnel-feature coverage >= 0.85
- late-2024 development pass-MAE gain > 0
- 2025 pass-MAE gain >= 1.50 yards
- paired-bootstrap 2025 pass-MAE gain 95% CI lower bound > 0
- 2025 passing correlation gain >= 0.02
- 100+ yard misses do not increase
- at least one of attempt/YPA component MAE gains has paired-bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0

If M77 fails, the same personnel feature universe is rejected for retuning/model substitution. No Ridge/HGB/XGB remix migration is allowed.

## Decision
- PASS -> `M78_integrate_frozen_personnel_correction_into_2026_pregame_pipeline`
- FAIL -> seek genuinely new pregame information; do not retune M77

author: mishleyotis
body:
"Sixty-four agents" is a count, not a coverage statement. `scripts/audit_coverage.py` walks four chains — workbook tabs, report sections, deliverables, derived fields — and reports an owner or a **HOLE** for every link. It found four. One of them made the reports unproducible.

## The holes, and what closed them

### 1 · ERS was dead code (AUD-0152)

A contract column, a full calculator in `scripts/calculate_ers.py`, and **nothing joining them**: `append_evidence` took `ers` as an optional caller argument defaulting to `None`, no caller ever passed one, and the calculator ran over a JSON projection no stage feeds it. Measured on Golden 1: twenty evidence rows, twenty empty cells.

`engine/ers.py` computes it at the write. Two things are deliberate:

- **Corroboration counts source IDENTITIES, not rows** — three pages of one annual report cannot corroborate themselves, matching `single_source_fact`.
- **Specificity reads the RRF consensus and BM25 fit** from `02_search` where they exist, and **says so** when it falls back to the excerpt heuristic rather than scoring as if it had the signal.

Retroactively on Golden 1: mean 3.33, undated Tyfone podcast rows lowest at 2.75, dated corroborated press releases highest at 3.95.

### 2 · All sixteen report sections had no owner (AUD-0153)

The renderer read `Report_Narrative` and refused a missing section; nothing wrote one. Every run reaching the report stage would have failed there, and Golden 1 stopped before it — so "the pipeline works" and "the pipeline cannot produce a report" were true at once.

Filling the hole with "an agent that types it" would reproduce the defect, because the review's real questions were *how an argument is weighed, how an absence is confirmed against proxies, how assumptions and bias are named, how inference is tagged and confirmed, how accuracy is measured*. Prose cannot answer those. A section is now a **record**:

| field | refused when |
|---|---|
| `Weighing` | it names nothing on the other side — a weighing with one side is a summary |
| `Absence_Basis` | the body asserts an absence and no proxy ladder backs it |
| `Assumptions` / `Bias_Notes` | unnamed — an unnamed assumption reads to a client as a fact |
| `Inference_Tags` | the count disagrees with the body's `[INF]` marks, or a tag says what is inferred but not what would **confirm** it |
| `Accuracy_Basis` | never typed — computed from citation density, ERS mass, and how many cited sources support a challenged subcap |

`engine.narrative review` refuses a verdict from a section's own author, the renderer refuses an unreviewed section, and the three agents are **generated from `report_spec`** so a new section fails the build until it has an owner.

### 3 · The technographic scan had no owning agent (AUD-0154)

It was the union of whatever sixteen category researchers tripped over — which can never say what it did **not** look at. `technographic-scanner` works the four layers deliberately, earns each status from the evidence kind, and emits `search_requests` for connectors a subagent cannot reach rather than fabricating a detection. Its JSON is asserted against the app's own `parse_technographic_scan`.

### 4 · No routine started a DMA (AUD-0156)

Five Routines watched, rectified, refreshed and promoted; none began a run, so a client folder waited for somebody to notice it. `dma-assessment-intake` (`trig_018eeMRDobRQXPZ4aobjfUih`) prepares the binding and **stops at the AskUserQuestion** a headless firing cannot answer — that refusal is the correct outcome, because a run bound on a guess researches the wrong 851 cells to completion.

## Two more the audit surfaced

**AUD-0155 · cost.** Nothing knew what a run cost, so the $5/pillar ceiling was a hope. Measured: **$6.45 for six subcaps, 76% of it cache reads** — 130K re-read on each of 188 turns. A 690-cell engagement projects to **~$741 against a $20 target**. `engine/cost.py` prices it and states four levers with arithmetic attached; three are catalogue or measurement arithmetic, and the fourth is **labelled a placeholder** rather than dressed as a result. Levered: $12.46. Filed **MITIGATED, not DESIGNED_OUT** — the levers are not yet enforced by the harness. `engine.cost schedule` puts a 16-lane run at **97 minutes** against the 2-hour target.

**AUD-0157 · template adherence** was unverifiable: the template's identifier appeared nowhere in the plugin. `engine/template.py` diffs a local copy against `contract.SHEETS`, shape only, since the template's rows are placeholders by design. The **contract is authoritative**; the check exists to make divergence visible while somebody can still decide which side is wrong.

## Verification

- **1320 passed, 7 skipped.**
- 22 new tests for the report tier and the scan, 5 for the routines canon.
- `audit_coverage.py --strict`: **0 holes** (from 17).
- `stress_run_lifecycle.py`: 31/31.
- 98/98 scripts import clean, 0 broken refs, 0 taxonomy drift.

The ledger refused AUD-0156 until it had a check attached — that mechanism working.

A second commit fixes a performance defect this change introduced: the cross-register ERS pass landed on every `append_evidence`, costing 0.30s and a second save per banked row. It now scores inline on the append and reconciles at synthesis, where a second source actually changes a judgement.

author: milechy
body:
## 基本情報

- **Phase / タスク名**: プランゲートの fail-safe とゲート取り違えを固定する
- **Tier**: S（`src/**`。ただしプロダクションコードは1行も変えていません）

---

## 24h 自走由来チェック

24h 自走 CLI の生成ではありません（対話セッションからのオーケストレーション）。スキップ。

---

## 変更概要

**テスト3ファイルへの純追加のみ（377行追加・削除ゼロ）。プロダクションコードは1行も変えていません。**

昨日〜今日、プランゲート周りを大きく変更しました（`analytics` の Standard 降格と `conversion` との分割、`queryTenantPlanOrThrow` の新設）。その**壊れやすい箇所**を固定します。

---

## ★穴1: `queryTenantPlanOrThrow` が一度もテストされていなかった

新設した `queryTenantPlanOrThrow` は**既存テストに一切登場していませんでした**（`queryTenantPlan` は `getTenantPlan` 経由で間接検証されていたが、新設版はゼロ検証）。

この関数の存在理由は「**データが変 → `free_ad`／DBが壊れた → throw**」の区別です。どちらかに寄ると、**DB障害を403で覆い隠す元のバグに戻る**か、逆にデータ不備で500を返すようになります。両方向を固定しました。

| 入力 | 期待 |
|---|---|
| 既知5値 | そのまま返す |
| `plan` 列が null | throw せず `free_ad` |
| 未知の文字列（`"enterprise_trial"` / `"STANDARD"` / `" growth "` / `"typo-plan"`） | throw せず `free_ad` |
| 行が存在しない（`rows` 空） | throw せず `free_ad` |
| **クエリが例外** | **`free_ad` に丸めず throw** |

### ドリフト検知

`it.each` で同一入力を `queryTenantPlan` と `queryTenantPlanOrThrow` の**両方に流し、DB例外以外では常に同じ結論**であることをテーブル駆動で1箇所に固定しました。allowlist が2箇所に独立実装されている以上、片方だけプラン段を直して他方を取り残す事故は、この1本で検出できます。

---

## ★穴2: ゲート取り違え

`trends` / `evaluations` は**個別テストが皆無**でした。あわせて6エンドポイントをテーブルにまとめ、`standard` プラン1本で「**analytics系は全通過・conversion系は全403**」を一括検証します。

| ゲート | エンドポイント |
|---|---|
| `analytics`（Standard〜） | summary / trends / evaluations |
| `conversion`（Growth〜） | conversions / knowledge-attribution / rule-effect |

新しいエンドポイントが増えたときは、このテーブルに足すだけで取り違えを検出できます。

---

## ★穴3: 403 のエラー形と文言

- `error` フィールドは analytics / conversion **どちらの403でも完全一致**することを対比テストで固定。ここが割れると admin-ui の `isPlanUpgradeRequired` が効かず、**正常系の403が「読み込み失敗の赤帯」として表示されます**
- `message` は機能別に正しいこと（analytics側は "Standard" を含み "Growth" を含まない、conversion側はその逆）。**Standard開放後に「高度なAnalyticsはGrowth以上」と出る**という実際に起きた不具合の再発防止です

---

## ★穴4: 原価（`llm_usage`）の露出

- client_admin は **growth / enterprise どちらでも** `llm_usage` が null で PostHog も呼ばれない（**プランと原価開示は無関係**という設計の固定）
- レスポンス全体を**再帰走査**し、`cost` を含むキーが `llm_usage.cost_jpy` の1個だけであることを固定。将来フィールドが増えたときの紛れ込みに気づけます

---

## イレギュラー操作（自分で洗い出した分）

テストにしたもの:
- 403 を受けた後に `?tenant=` で他テナントを指定して再試行 → client_admin はゲートが JWT の `tenant_id` で判定するため**回避不可**（plan確認クエリの第2引数が JWT 由来であることまで確認）
- super_admin 自身の `app_metadata.tenant_id` が乗っていても、データ絞り込みは `?tenant` クエリが勝つ
- 同一テナントへの連続リクエストで毎回 plan確認クエリが走る（`checkAnalyticsPlanAccess` は 60秒TTLキャッシュを経由しないため、**プラン変更直後に古い判定を引きずらない**）

見送ったもの:
- 「super_admin の `?tenant=` と client_admin の JWT が食い違うとき、どちらが勝つか」は、1リクエストに認証コンテキストは1つで super_admin 時点でゲート自体がバイパスされるため**衝突は起きない**。意味のある形に言い換えてテスト化した
- プラン変更の実DB結合（即時反映）はモック構成では検証不能。TTLキャッシュ非経由という性質までを固定し、実DB結合はスコープ外
- 403連打でゲートを疲弊させる系は DoS 寄りで、プランゲートの正しさの検証ではない

---

## ★このテストが本当に壊れを捕まえることの実証

2種類の変異を注入して確認しました（いずれも確認後に復元）。

| 変異 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `queryTenantPlanOrThrow` がDB例外を握り潰す（**修正前のバグに戻す**） | 該当1件がピンポイントで失敗 |
| `/conversions` のゲートを `conversion` → `analytics` に取り違える | **8件が失敗**（テーブル駆動が3エンドポイント全てを捕捉） |

---

## 影響範囲

- [x] API スキーマ変更なし
- [x] DB migration なし
- [x] `.env` / secrets 変更なし
- [x] **プロダクションコードの変更ゼロ**

---

## テスト確認

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` — エラーなし
- 対象3ファイル — 166 tests 全通過

- [x] ローカルでテスト実行済み

---

## 残存リスク

- `queryTenantPlanOrThrow` と `queryTenantPlan` の allowlist が**コピペで2箇所に独立**している設計自体は変わっていません。3つ目の呼び出し元が増えれば同じ問題が起きます
- 原価の走査は**キー名に `cost` を含む場合のみ**検出。`margin` や生の数値で漏れるケースは捕まりません
- 実DBとの結合（プラン変更の即時反映）はモック構成では検証不能

author: zeroxm
body:
Closes #44.

Adds a **Safari Zone** slice to the main adventure wheel in Kanto, and first fixes the reason a second region-only slice couldn't be added safely.

## The blocker

The adventure wheel dispatched with `switch (index)`, and Area Zero was appended to the slice array only for generation 9 — so `case 17` meant Area Zero **because exactly one optional slice existed**. Adding a generation-1 slice would have made index 17 mean different things in different regions: a player landing on Find Fossil and getting Safari Zone.

## Slices are now data

`adventure-actions.ts` lists every slice, and `AdventureActionName` is **derived from that list**. The component maps names to outputs through a `Record<AdventureActionName, () => void>`, and dispatch is `this.handlers[this.actions[index].name]()`.

I checked both halves of the guarantee by deliberately breaking them:

| mistake | result |
| --- | --- |
| row added, handler forgotten | `TS2741: Property 'safariZone' is missing in type …` |
| handler for a row that doesn't exist | `TS2561: … 'safariZoneTypo' does not exist in …` |

Strategy expressed as data, matching `POKEMON_POOLS`, `CONSOLATION_PRIZES` and `formRules`. **Decorator was considered and rejected** — the gating axis is set membership (`generations: [1]`), which inheritance can't express without a class per combination.

The other five index-switch roulettes are untouched. None is generation-gated, so none has this bug.

## The wheel

Reuses `PokemonPoolRouletteComponent` as a sixth pool — **no new component**. Area Zero stayed bespoke because its list is generation-*independent*; Safari Zone's is gated to generation 1, which is exactly the pool shape.

**22 species**: the RBY + FRLG Safari Zone table minus the water encounters, which overlap too heavily with the generation 1 fishing wheel.

## Prizes improve as the run goes on

`PokemonPool` gains an optional `rareBoost`, so the seven prizes — Chansey, Kangaskhan, Scyther, Pinsir, Tauros, Dratini, Dragonair — **double in width once `currentRound >= 4`**, the threshold `catch-legendary-roulette` already uses for "past the fourth gym". Three of them have mega forms, so a late Safari trip is worth more than an early one.

⚠️ **The boost clones rather than assigns.** `getPokemonByIdArray` returns the **shared National Dex objects** — writing `.weight` on them would have left Chansey heavier on every other wheel and in the Pokédex for the rest of the session. There's a test asserting the dex entry is untouched.

## Testing

**344 → 368.** The 19 per-slice dispatch tests are what pay for the refactor: an index-based test could never have caught that three slices don't follow the `<name>Event` naming convention (`goStraight` → `doNothingEvent`, `teamRocket` → `teamRocketEncounterEvent`).

Verified in the running app, not just in Karma — the decisive check being that **index 17 fires `areaZeroEvent` in Paldea and `safariZoneEvent` in Kanto**, which is exactly what the old `case 17` could not do:

- Kanto: 18 slices, Safari Zone present, Area Zero absent — and the reverse in Paldea
- Landing on the slice opens the pool wheel titled "Which Safari Zone Pokémon?", all 22 species
- At round 0 every weight is 1; at round 4 the seven prizes are 2 and the National Dex entry for Chansey is still 1

Build 1.50 MB with no budget breached, `npm audit` clean including dev dependencies, all six locales at parity (2,210 keys).

### Worth checking by hand

- Play into Kanto and land on Safari Zone for real — my browser checks drove the component directly, so the wheel's own click path is the gap.
- Land on a few **other** slices in Kanto, Sinnoh and Paldea. That's the regression this refactor exists to prevent, and it's the thing I'd most want a second pair of eyes on.

body:
## Summary

Issue #2281: a job whose worker died mid-run (OOM kill, SIGKILL,
the 20m TimeoutStartSec on honeypot-sandbox-worker.service, power
loss) is moved into inbox/running/ but the process that would
move it back out never gets to run again. Nothing re-queues it, so
it sits there forever and status-export.py reports it as 'running'
indefinitely.

## Changes

`sandbox/worker.sh`: new `sweep_stranded_running()` function
called at startup, BEFORE the drain loop. It iterates
`inbox/running/` and any `.json` whose mtime is older than
`WORKER_STALE_RUNNING_SECS` (default 1800) is moved to
`inbox/failed/` with a one-line `.error` file explaining the
recovery. The threshold is configurable so operators can tune it
for their sample window.

The fix is local to worker.sh and does not touch the drain loop
or the service unit; the next drain picks up the moved jobs.

- Local gate (`.orchestrator/gate.sh HEAD all`) passes (GATE_FAIL=0).
- No AI-attribution strings in commit, PR body, or issue comment.

author: matiaspc
body:
## What it is

`DSConfetti` — a celebratory confetti burst you attach to any view and fire by changing a trigger value. When the trigger changes, a shower of paper strips, discs and triangles erupts from a configurable origin, arcs up and outward, tumbles under gravity with an edge-on "paper flip" flutter, and fades as it falls.

**UX problem it solves:** design systems are full of inputs and containers but rarely have a *reward* moment. Success beats — task completed, purchase confirmed, streak extended, level unlocked — feel flat without a bit of delight. `DSConfetti` gives every app a consistent, on-brand celebration in one line, without pulling in a third-party particle library.

## How it works

- Pure SwiftUI particle system: **`TimelineView(.animation)` + `Canvas`** (iOS 17 / macOS 14).
- Motion is **analytic** — each piece's position, spin and flutter are closed-form functions of elapsed time (`p = p₀ + v·t + ½g·t²`), so there's no per-frame integration state, it's deterministic, and it stays smooth at high piece counts.
- **Zero idle cost:** the `TimelineView` is only mounted while a burst is on screen. Each burst retires itself once its last piece has faded, and overlapping bursts are supported.
- Confetti is drawn in a **non-interactive overlay** (`allowsHitTesting(false)`) that fills the view's bounds, so taps pass straight through to your UI.

## Public API

```swift
func dsConfetti<Trigger: Equatable>(
    trigger: Trigger,
    intensity: DSConfettiIntensity = .medium,   // .light / .medium / .festive
    colors: [Color] = DSConfetti.defaultColors,  // vibrant DS palette
    origin: UnitPoint = .center,                 // e.g. .top to rain from above
    haptics: Bool = true
) -> some View
```

### Usage

```swift
@State private var celebrations = 0

VStack {
    DSButton("Complete") { celebrations += 1 }
}
.dsConfetti(trigger: celebrations, intensity: .festive)
```

## DS conventions

- ✅ **Tokens only** — colors from `DSColors.defaultPalette` (`DSConfetti.defaultColors` = primary/secondary/tertiary/warning/success/info); spacing/typography via `DSSpacing` / `.ds(...)` in the preview. No raw color/font literals in the public surface.
- ✅ **Haptics** — fires `DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(.success)` on each burst (toggleable).
- ✅ **Light/dark** — vibrant palette colors render over any content; `#Preview` shows both schemes.
- ✅ **Catalog** — new "Confetti" `section(...)` added to `ComponentCatalog.swift`.
- ✅ Naming/style — `DS`-prefixed types, `DS<Name>.swift`, doc-comment + `MARK` structure matching existing components (`DSRating`, `DSSegmentedControl`).

## Source / inspiration (attribution)

Pure-SwiftUI particle patterns from the iOS community:
- [Vortex (twostraws)](https://github.com/twostraws/Vortex) — iOS 17 SwiftUI particle systems incl. confetti
- [Hacking with Swift — "Special Effects with SwiftUI"](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/articles/246/special-effects-with-swiftui)
- [Designing a Dynamic Confetti Effect (TimelineView + Canvas)](https://medium.com/@jc_builds/swiftui-tutorials-designing-a-dynamic-confetti-effect-aa531c5adfb1)

## ⚠️ Manual verification needed

This was authored in a **Linux sandbox with no Swift/SwiftUI toolchain**, so it could not be compiled. Please verify in Xcode:

- [ ] Package builds (`DSConfetti.swift` compiles against iOS 17 / macOS 14)
- [ ] Open the `DSConfetti` `#Preview` — burst fires on button tap in **light** and **dark**
- [ ] Open `ComponentCatalog` → **Confetti** section fires a full-screen burst
- [ ] Motion feels good — pieces arc up, tumble, flutter edge-on, and fade cleanly
- [ ] Confirm success **haptic** fires on device
- [ ] Confirm confetti overlay does **not** block taps on underlying UI

## Summary
Found by the daily health check: `assets/i18n/*.json` — the files actually fetched at runtime (`loadDict()` does `fetch("assets/i18n/${lang}.json")` in `assets/i18n.js`) — were stale relative to the root `*.json` locale files, in two ways that are user-visible on `home.html`:

1. **Missing `home.lightbox.*` keys (all 5 locales).** The process lightbox added to `home.html` uses `data-i18n="home.lightbox.prev|next"` and JS `captionKey: "home.lightbox.c1|c2|c3"`, but those keys existed only in the root locale files. At runtime the captions resolved to `undefined` and prev/next fell back to English.
2. **Stale `home.story.text` / `home.story.watch` (all 5 locales)** — still described the removed 1:30 video ("Watch the Process") while the page markup and root JSON say gallery ("View the Gallery"). Switching language on `home.html` reverted the copy to the old wording.

Fix: copy the already-translated values from the root locale files into `assets/i18n/`. No new translations were authored; after this change each `assets/i18n/<loc>.json` is byte-identical to the corresponding root `<loc>.json`.

```diff
  "home": { "story": {
-   "watch": "Watch the Process"
+   "watch": "View the Gallery"
  },
+ "lightbox": { "prev": ..., "next": ..., "c1": ..., "c2": ..., "c3": ... }
```

## Health check results (nothing else to fix)
- **Build**: `docker run ... jekyll/builder:latest ... jekyll build --future` succeeds. Only note: `Configuration file: none` (no `_config.yml`), which is expected for this site.
- **Key parity**: 0 missing and 0 orphan keys in es/fr/it/pt vs `en.json`, both at the repo root and in `assets/i18n/`; all 10 files parse as valid JSON.
- **Broken references**: no local `href`/`src` pointing at a non-existent file across all 26 `*.html`, `sw.js` and `manifest.json`; no duplicate `id` attributes on any page; after this change, every `data-i18n*` key used in HTML/JS resolves in `en.json`.
- **Identical-to-English values (reported, not changed)**: es 110, fr 84, it 74, pt 84 — nearly all are prices/dates/metrics, proper nouns (`Elias Thorne`, `Via degli Ulivi, 42`), or brand/loanwords that are legitimately the same (`Concierge`, `Boutique`, `Total`, `Composition` in fr). A handful of real candidates for translation, left out because they are a brand/style decision: es `product.footer.{privacy,returns,lab_reports,sourcing_ethics,contact,the_journal}`, es/pt `*.footer.legal`, it `*.footer.privacy`, `product.specs.composition_text` (INCI ingredient list — arguably should stay Latin).

author: hynix666
body:
`03-apis-and-interfaces.md` said: *"`storage-local` **does** read-modify-write per append,
eleven times a run, and two concurrent runs there already race."*

Written down, never measured — and there was **no test file for the adapter at all**, which is
how prose describing a defect sat beside code that had it.

## What it actually costs

| concurrent appends | kept | lost | threw |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | **1** | 0 |
| 11 | 3 | **8** | 3 |
| 30 | 2 | **28** | 16 |

Silent at two. The throws were `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` raised from inside
`append` itself — `writeFile` truncates before writing, so a concurrent reader observes a
partial bundle. Losing revisions *and* corrupting reads, from one unguarded read-modify-write.

The doc also named the wrong race: two concurrent **runs** write different files. It is
concurrent appends to the **same** run that lose entries, and eviction across runs measured
clean.

## It compounded into permanent content loss

Sweep thirteen's reclamation computes its live set from what the bundles say. A wrecked bundle
reported zero surviving revisions, so all twelve retained bodies were reclaimed —
transient concurrency bug → permanently unreferenced content → swept → unrecoverable.

## And it exposed a hole in sweep thirteen's own guard

That guard required the run's stored refs to appear in the live set — and **`[].every()` is
true**, so an empty or unreadable bundle read as trustworthy and authorised the sweep. A guard
that passes when it learns nothing is not a guard. It now compares `retainedRefs`, held in
memory during the run, so a storage fault cannot empty the evidence it checks against.

## Three fixes, each mutation-proved

**Serialised appends**, scoped to the **directory** rather than the bundle: `append` also runs
`evict`, which reads every bundle and deletes the oldest. Keying on the path left the cross-run
case broken and, on Windows, loud — 7 appends threw `EPERM ... rename` while a reader in
`readAll` held the target open.

**Atomic writes** via temp-then-rename. Reverting this left every in-process test green, because
serialisation hides it — the property is cross-process, so it is tested with a real second
process. With `writeFile` restored: **9 of 2,057 foreign reads saw a partial file.**

**A Windows caveat, measured rather than assumed.** `rename` onto a path another process holds
open fails with `EPERM`, so a zero-gap reader makes every append fail. That is the correct
failure *direction* — loud, not silent — and the guarantee there is "never partial, possibly
refused" rather than "never partial, always written". `renameWithRetry` covers realistic readers.

## Verification

`npm run verify` → **exit 0**. 1,401 tests (was 1,393), 2,784 oracle verdicts, 9 boundaries.

author: danielaskdd
body:
## Description

During cache rebuild, a payload that looks like JSON but cannot be parsed is reported **twice** for a single failure:

1. `_process_json_extraction_result` logs `"<chunk>: JSON extraction result is empty or unrecoverable"`.
2. `_rebuild_from_extraction_result` then falls through to the delimiter parser, which logs `"<chunk>: Complete delimiter can not be found in extraction result"`.

The second message is not an independent finding. The delimiter is missing because the payload was never delimiter-formatted, which is a direct consequence of the failure already reported one line up. At WARNING level it makes one bad chunk look like two distinct problems, and points at a delimiter-format issue that does not exist.

This demotes that second message to DEBUG on that one path. The delimiter parser is unchanged for every other caller, and the rescue it performs is untouched — an empty JSON object with delimiter records appended still yields those records.

## Related Issues

Follows #3745 (merged), which fixed a different warning on the same function: a *valid* empty JSON extraction being misread as a parse failure. This PR has been merged up to it and reconciled — see the last commit and the note below.

## Changes Made

- `lightrag/operate.py`
  - `_process_extraction_result` takes `warn_on_missing_completion_delimiter: bool = True`. When False the missing-completion-delimiter finding goes to DEBUG instead of WARNING, so nothing is lost for diagnosis.
  - `_process_json_extraction_result` takes `parsed: dict | None = None`, letting a caller that has already recovered the payload hand it in instead of having it re-parsed. `None` is unambiguous as "not supplied" because `tolerant_load_json_dict` always returns a dict, so an unrecoverable payload still arrives as `{}`.
  - `_rebuild_from_extraction_result` parses once, uses that payload both for the #3745 acceptance test and for the demotion decision, and demotes only on the fall-through — which after #3745 only an unrecoverable payload can reach.
  - Net effect on the parse count for this path: `main` parses the payload twice (once inside the parser, once in #3745's acceptance condition); this PR parses it once.
  - The defaults keep the live extraction path (`operate.py:4134` and `4200`) and genuine delimiter payloads behaving exactly as before.
- `tests/extraction/test_rebuild_fallback_warning_dedup.py` (new, 4 tests)
  - An unparseable JSON-looking payload produces exactly one WARNING (the JSON one), with the delimiter finding still present at DEBUG.
  - A delimiter-formatted payload missing its terminator still WARNs — nothing else reported it, so it is the only signal there is.
  - A wrong-schema JSON payload never reaches the fallback at all, spying on `_process_extraction_result` to prove it. This is what makes the demotion safe to apply unconditionally, and is the thing that would have to be revisited if that early return were removed.
  - The rescue path still recovers delimiter records appended after an empty JSON object.
- `tests/extraction/test_rebuild_json_empty_fallback.py` (from #3745)
  - `test_rebuild_still_falls_back_on_unparseable_json_looking_text` asserted the delimiter finding at WARNING, which is exactly the message this PR moves. It keeps every assertion it made — the fall-through, the empty result, and the presence of the finding — and captures at DEBUG instead.

## Checklist

- [x] Changes tested locally
- [ ] Code reviewed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if necessary)
- [x] Unit tests added (if applicable)

## Additional Notes

**What's broken and how the fix works:** the two log sites have no knowledge of each other, so the fallback parser cannot tell "I am the first one to look at this payload" from "I am a rescue attempt after someone already reported a failure". The caller knows, so the decision is passed down from there rather than inferred at the log site.

**Review history worth reading:** the first version keyed the demotion off empty extraction results. Codex correctly pointed out that emptiness does not imply the JSON parser said anything — a payload that parses but carries the wrong schema (`{"answer": "no entities found"}`) extracts nothing in silence, so the demotion removed that chunk's *only* warning instead of deduplicating two. Fixed in 0b0c8b4 by tracking the parse outcome, and #3745 landing has since made that case return early anyway; the test now pins the early return.

**What this deliberately leaves alone:** #3745 already decided that a JSON payload accepted as a valid parse gets no delimiter warning. This PR does not revisit that; it only removes the doubled report on the unparseable path.

**Verification**

- `tests/extraction`: 265 passed, 7 failed. The 7 failures are identical on `main` (261 passed, 7 failed — the delta is exactly the 4 new tests) and come from missing spaCy models in this environment; `test_keyword_extraction_drivers.py` fails to collect for the same reason on both sides and was excluded.
- `tests/pipeline` and `tests/llm/test_vlm_json_escape_repair.py`: 694 passed. Together with `tests/extraction` this covers every test file referencing the changed symbols or log strings.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

**Not verified:** the live (non-cached) extraction path, which does not reach this fallback and is unaffected by the default arguments.

## Summary

- Cuando un trabajador tiene un reingreso aprobado en el mismo día, `iniciarReingreso()` sobreescribe `hora_entrada` con la nueva sesión y limpia `hora_salida`; solo `hora_entrada_inicial` conserva la primera apertura del día (migración `042_reingreso_nomina.sql`).
- La interfaz (mobile y web) mostraba `hora_entrada` directamente en las tarjetas/tablas de registros, por lo que un día con reintegro mostraba únicamente la última apertura y el último cierre, en vez de la primera apertura del día junto con el cierre final.
- Se agregó el helper `horaEntradaMostrada()` (mobile) que prioriza `hora_entrada_inicial` sobre `hora_entrada`, y se aplicó en todos los lugares que muestran la entrada del día: tarjeta de período, tab "Hoy", tarjeta de registro, vista semanal de asistencia y dashboard de asistencia del gestor. En el módulo web de nómina se agregó `hora_entrada_inicial` al tipo `Registro` y se usó el mismo fallback en la tabla y el detalle de período.
- La lógica de estado (jornada activa, tiempo transcurrido, alertas de "sin salida") sigue usando `hora_entrada` tal cual, ya que corresponde a la sesión actual/activa, no al valor mostrado como resumen del día.

author: aetherlogosprime-architect
body:
Found by surveying branches that were pushed and never proposed. Andrew saw fifty branches on the page and read it as finished work not being cleaned up; measured, only three of the last sixty merged branches were left standing, and thirty had never had a proposal opened at all. The stall is at the opening, not the closing. This is one of five of mine that merge cleanly — finished repairs that were simply never offered.

The change: a test guarding a hook had a ten-second timeout. That timeout is a HANG detector, not a performance budget, and the two were conflated. Spawning Git Bash on Windows is fast on an idle machine and slow on a loaded one — and the pre-push suite deliberately drops to a single worker when memory is low, which is exactly when the machine is most loaded. So the run that most needs the suite to be trustworthy is the run where a bare process spawn can exceed ten seconds, and the timeout then reads as "the hook misbehaved" when what happened was "the machine could not start bash in time."

Resized to catch a hook that never returns, which is the only thing this guard is for. A correct hook finishes in well under a second; a hung one never finishes. Nothing legitimate lives in between. The failure message now names a slow spawn as a slow spawn rather than letting it read as hook failure.

Same family as the rest of this week's findings: an instrument reporting confidently about something other than what it was asked. Draft until its stations are proven.

author: recregt
body:
## Summary
Replaces the hand-rolled exact/prefix/acronym/substring/fuzzy scoring in `SearchIndex::search` with `nucleo-matcher`'s optimized single-pass matcher, eliminating the per-keystroke, per-item `to_lowercase()` + `Vec<char>` rebuild that ran even when nothing changed between searches. Restructures scoring to build lightweight `(item, score, indices)` candidates first, sort and truncate to `limit`, and only then construct the full `SearchResult` (including its string clones) for the surviving top results instead of every match. Changes `AppItem::name`/`description` and `SearchResult::title`/`subtitle` from `String` to `Arc<str>` so cloning shared item data into a result is a refcount bump instead of a heap allocation. Also switches the release profile to `lto = "fat"` (dev/CI test and clippy steps are unaffected, since they don't use `--release`). All existing ranking behavior verified unchanged via the existing test suite (native and under Wine on the Windows target) and the existing `search_at_scale` benchmark.

author: strubio-ray
body:
Follow-up to #241. That PR documented the fifth custom manager as depending on a `ghcr.io` hostRule; that was incomplete, and the credential it named was wrong.

Two conditions must hold before the pin can resolve, neither in this repo:

1. The runner hostRule password must be the workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` — see `Rubio-Enterprises/.github-private#233`. GitHub documents only a **classic** PAT and the Actions token as GHCR credentials; a separately minted App installation token is documented nowhere and empirically returns **HTTP 403** on `HEAD /v2/.../manifests/main` despite the App holding `packages: read` (that permission governs the Packages REST API, not the OCI registry).
2. The package must grant read to the runner repository under **Manage Actions access** — *"only workflows running in repositories that are given read permission on that package can download the package."* No REST API exists for it; it is a manual per-package step.

Until both hold, the manager extracts the dep correctly and logs `Could not determine new digest` every run — the exact reason `mac-dev-playbook`'s three first-party managers looked configured while never updating a pin.

Docs-only. `tests.test_renovate_config` still 25/25; markdownlint clean under the org config.

| [fro-bot/agent](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent) | action | minor | `v0.105.1` → `v0.106.0` | [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/fro-bot/agent/badge)](https://securityscorecards.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/fro-bot/agent) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>fro-bot/agent (fro-bot/agent)</summary>

### [`v0.106.0`](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/releases/tag/v0.106.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/compare/v0.105.1...v0.106.0)

#### What's new

<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

This release extends brokered-push delivery with a path opt-in mechanism, more actionable failure comments, and two new read-side query surfaces that were previously write-only or Discord-only.

##### Features

Brokered-push delivery previously assumed the consumer repository kept deployable code in the same directory layout as this repo. Repos with code under paths like `apps/<name>/src/` would fail every delivery attempt even when all trust gates passed, with no clear indication of why. A new `brokered-push-extra-paths` action input accepts comma-separated path prefixes that widen the allowlist per consumer — the defaults are unchanged, so existing setups are byte-identical to before.

Protected surfaces (`.github/`, scripts, manifests, lockfiles, and Dockerfiles) are rejected by two independent enforcement layers regardless of any opt-in. Both consume a single canonical definition, so the parse-time check and the runtime validation inside `validateBrokeredPushFiles()` cannot drift apart. When a delivery does fail, the PR comment now names a specific cause (`failureClass` union) and lists up to ten repo-relative offending paths in a fenced block — fence-escape sequences and markdown-active characters are neutralized before rendering, so model-chosen path strings cannot become links or mentions. [#​1493](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1493)

Two capabilities that were configurable but not queryable by agents are now readable. The brokered-push allowlist is exposed as a `brokered-push-allowlist` action output: a JSON object (`defaultPaths`, `rootFiles`, `extraPrefixes`) serialized from the exact definitions enforcement uses, with a drift-pin test that feeds probe paths back through `validateBrokeredPushFiles()` to guarantee representation and behavior cannot disagree. The gateway's `POST /operator/dispatch` route mirrors the launch route's full gate stack (guard → rate limit → session token → validation → binding → denylist → authz) and returns every `DispatchOutcome` variant as `200 {outcome}` — HTTP status codes are reserved for transport failures only. Idempotency keys carry a SHA-256 payload fingerprint so retrying the same request replays correctly and reusing a key for a different repo or task rejects with 400 instead of silently replaying the wrong outcome. [#​1496](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1496)

<details><summary>Full changelog</summary>

#### [0.106.0](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/compare/v0.105.1...v0.106.0) (2026-08-29)

author: davecourtois
body:
Slice 1 of the governed-run receipt. **Not C5b** — C5 stays VOID and untouched. This is product architecture extracted from what C5 taught, and it grants nothing.

## Why

A governed run already knows who governed it, what it was based on, what candidate it produced, who reviewed it and how it ended. An external witness reconstructed all of that afterwards: 673 lines of apparatus that destroyed an expensive run when a 62-line ad-hoc parser met one event whose nested field was a string where its author assumed an object — a shape already sitting in the previous run's preserved log.

> **Never fabricate a specimen when a measured specimen already exists.**

## The schema, after four review rounds

```text
Completeness != Outcome                   VOID cannot be an Outcome; it is what a
                                          reader concludes about INCOMPLETE
UNKNOWN outcome                           representable, never COMPLETE
every fact carries Knownness              KNOWN / UNKNOWN / MALFORMED / UNSUPPORTED,
                                          membership read by enumeration
KNOWN requires a stated Source            everywhere, including inside Attempts
the zero Value is not evidence            an unset field cannot stand in for a
                                          recorded absence
candidate condition explicit              PRESENT -> all candidate facts KNOWN
                                          NONE    -> all explicitly UNKNOWN (an
                                                     instrument that cannot read the
                                                     thing may not claim it is absent)
                                          UNKNOWN -> never COMPLETE
review condition explicit                 ACCEPTED/REFUSED require reviewer evidence
delivery is measured                      DELIVERED / NOT_DELIVERED / UNKNOWN with a
                                          source, not a raw bool
the delivered attempt is bound exactly    same provider, decision AND reviewed digest
                                          as the receipt -- one measured fact must not
                                          support a different claim
decision vocabulary closed                accept / revise / escalate, bound to outcome
re-derivable facts verified               Verify recomputes; typed MismatchKind
                                          (DISAGREEMENT / UNRECOMPUTABLE /
                                          RECORDED_UNKNOWN / RECORDED_MALFORMED /
                                          RECORDED_UNSUPPORTED)
```

`ReviewDecision` mirrors `roles.Decision` rather than importing it — a serialization schema that borrows a live internal type changes meaning whenever that type does — and a test holds the two vocabularies equal in both directions.

## Boundaries held mechanically, not described

- **No admission.** `TestAReceiptCannotAdmitAnything`. The receipt reports evidence; it may not grant authority to itself.
- **No isolation.** Start/end isolation stays external — a governed process cannot be the sole witness that its own environment was isolated.
- **Legacy segregated.** `FromEvents` lives in `internal/runreceipt/legacy`, an import-guard test fails if anything outside it imports the adapter, a reconstruction can never be COMPLETE, and the adapter never infers (an earlier draft set `GovernorCommit` from `BaseCommit` — one fact, two claims).

## Corpus

Pinned baseline `C4.log` + `C5.log`, present and **sha256-checked**, plus discovery of every other `experiments/*/runs/*.log` — 38 logs today. Two different claims, deliberately separated:

- **All logs -> totality only.** Parser survives, states belong to their vocabularies, no structural assumptions.
- **Pinned baseline -> content regression.** Facts known to exist there must still be extracted.

That separation came from a real finding: `W1.void1-operator.log` is a void run with no binding revision, and the original assertion demanded a base commit from it. The parser was right; the test author was wrong.

## Review status, stated plainly

Phase 1 passed on the exact head `6335f61`. `Hosted adversarial review` **skipped** — the availability probe found `codex=false`, `gemini=false` (no provider key in this environment), so no independent automated reviewer looked at this PR. Mechanical checks passed; that is not the same as reviewed, and it is not clean by exhaustion.

`Sensei architectural gate` passed, but `internal/runreceipt` is a package the graph has never examined (`PREFLIGHT_STATUS_EMPTY`, zero anchors). That pass means "nothing governed was violated", not "this was governed".

## Next

Slice 2: direct governor emission — one emitted receipt per terminal run path, `Completeness()` exercised at the production boundary, and no `FromEvents` anywhere in it. Then exact candidate admission.

author: d-morrison
body:
Closes #746.

## The defect

`resolve_bullet_style()`'s candidate scan required whitespace **after** the marker, so CommonMark's empty list item — a bare marker on its own line — produced no candidate at all and the style fell through to the `-` default.

Reproduced against `main` before starting, with the fragment authored `*` so the target is visible:

| `NEWS.md` first bullet | fragment normalized to |
|---|---|
| `*` (bare marker) | `-` |
| `* ` (trailing space) | `*` |

Identical intent, opposite outcome, keyed on an invisible character that any whitespace-trimming editor removes.

## Scope: two sites, not one

The issue names only the candidate scan. `normalize_bullet_markers` carried the **same** assumption, and that half is the one that actually produces the MD004 flip — a fragment's bare marker kept its own character while every sibling was rewritten, leaving a `*` item in a `-`-styled file. Fixing only detection would close the issue with the damage intact one function away, so both are fixed. Flagging it rather than folding it in silently.

I swept for a third site: `[-*+]` appears at exactly those two places in this script.

## What review changed

The pre-push adversarial review found a **blocking defect in my first commit**, and it matters more than the original bug.

A bare `-` is an empty list item only where a list item can start. Under a paragraph line the identical text is a **setext heading underline**; a bare `*` or `+` there is lazy paragraph continuation. My widened patterns admitted all three, so a heading set the file's bullet style — and on the normalize side a fragment's heading underline was *rewritten into a bullet*, destroying content rather than merely misreading it.

Verified independently against CommonMark via `markdown-it`, which also corrected my first fix:

| input | parses as |
|---|---|
| `-` | list item |
| `Intro` / `-` | **`<h2>`, zero list items** |
| `Intro` / `` / `-` | list item |
| `- a` / `-` | **two list items** — a bare marker after a list item is a list item |

That last row broke the obvious "must follow a blank line" rule. Only the previous line separates the constructs, which a line-oriented matcher cannot see, so both sites moved from `grep`/`sed` to **one shared `awk` predicate**: a bare marker qualifies at start-of-file, after a blank line, or after another line that opens a list item.

Sharing the predicate means detection and normalization cannot drift apart. It also removed the one portability question the review raised and I could not settle — `$` inside an ERE group had `grep` precedent here but would have been this repo's first `sed -E` use, on a capability with no macOS CI leg.

## Verification

- **All 26 tests pass, including under `mawk 1.3.4 20240123`** — the exact build `CLAUDE.md` records as aborting on interval expressions. The awk program uses none; I checked rather than assuming, and ran the suite under it.
- **Tests 21, 22 confirmed to fail against `origin/main`**, with the baseline first checked for *absence* of the distinguishing symbol, per the stale-`HEAD~1` lesson.
- **Five aimed mutations**, each stated before running and each confirmed to break its named case: bare branch accepted unconditionally → 23; bare branch removed → 21; scan context dropped → 26; normalizer context dropped → 22; normalizer never rewrites → 11.

One mutation initially **survived**, and it was mis-aimed rather than a coverage gap — it targeted the scan while the only candidate test exercised the normalizer, which tracks its own context. Re-aiming it exposed genuinely uncovered logic, which is now Test 26. That path is reachable in exactly one shape: a bare marker in list context is normally preceded by a list item that already resolved the style, and a *skipped thematic break* is the sole exception.

## Known gap, documented rather than silently fixed

A **spaced** thematic break (`- - -`, `* * *`) inside a fragment is rewritten — `resolve_bullet_style` guards against it via `is_thematic_break`, but that guard was only ever wired into detection. Pre-existing and unchanged here; confirmed by running it rather than asserted. The review also correctly caught that my first commit's comment claimed such breaks *don't* match, which was false.

A bare marker after a list item's lazy continuation line is rejected. That errs toward the pre-fix behaviour (not normalized) rather than toward corruption (a heading rewritten), and tracking it needs real block parsing.

author: visualmoney
body:
`#59` 의 `SCHEDULING_SLACK` 처방이 `tests/integration/test_rate_limit_compliance.py` 에 오지 않은 것을 고칩니다. 상수를 `tests/timing.py` 로 빼 두 파일이 공유합니다.

## 재현이 안 됐습니다 — 그래서 쟀습니다

세 조건 26회 중 실패 0회입니다.

```text
idle                10회 0실패
--cov (CI 와 동일)    8회 0실패
--cov + CPU 8 포화    8회 0실패
```

추측으로 상한을 고르는 대신 CPU 16배 과부하에서 각 단언의 실제 여유를 쟀고, **그 측정이 계획을 두 번 바꿨습니다.**

| 단언 | 실측 최대 | 상한 | 터지려면 | 조치 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `t < 0.5` 버스트 | 0.0001s | 0.5 | 0.50s 지연 | **그대로** |
| `t < 2.5` 11-20번째 | 1.0622s | 2.5 | 1.44s 지연 | → `1.0 + SLACK` |
| `t < 3.5` 21-30번째 | 2.1133s | 3.5 | 1.39s 지연 | → `2.0 + SLACK` |
| `total <= 5.0` | 3.6535s | 5.0 | 1.35s 지연 | **그대로** |
| `elapsed < 0.1` | 0.0000s | 0.1 | 0.10s 지연 | **그대로** |
| `live_elapsed < 1.0` | 0.0002s | 1.0 | 1.00s 지연 | **그대로** |

### 취소한 것 1 — "즉시 통과" 상한에 여유 얹기

처음 계획은 모든 상한에 `SCHEDULING_SLACK`(2.0)을 얹는 것이었습니다. **얹었으면 세 검사를 지우는 것이었습니다** — 주기가 1.0인데 여유가 2.0이면 "즉시 통과"와 "한 주기 기다림"이 같은 판정을 받습니다. `assert elapsed < 0.1 + 2.0` 은 유량 제한이 통째로 사라져도 통과합니다.

> 상한에는 두 종류가 있습니다. **"N주기 기다렸는가"** 는 하한이 진짜 검사를 하므로 여유가 한 주기를 넘어도 됩니다. **"기다리지 않았는가"** 는 여유가 한 주기 이상이 되는 순간 아무것도 묻지 않게 됩니다.

### 취소한 것 2 — `total <= 5.0`

규칙(`기대값 + SLACK`)을 적용하면 `2.7 + 2.0 = 4.7` 로 **지금보다 좁아집니다.** 기계적으로 밀었으면 플레이크를 새로 만들 뻔했습니다.

## 실패 메시지

`all(제너레이터)` 는 이것만 남깁니다.

```text
E  assert False
E   +  where False = all(<generator object ... at 0x73f7f058dfc0>)
```

그 테스트에는 `all(...)` 이 **세 개**입니다. 어느 것인지도 안 나옵니다. 바뀐 뒤:

```text
E  AssertionError: 11-20번째(한 주기 대기): 5/10건이 [1.00, 3.00]초 밖입니다 —
   15번=3.053s, 16번=3.053s, 17번=3.053s, 18번=3.053s, 19번=3.053s
E  구간 전체: [1.051, 1.051, 1.051, 1.051, 1.051, 3.053, 3.053, 3.053, 3.053, 3.053]
```

20% 확률로 나는 실패는 **다시 재현시킬 수 없습니다.** 이 항목이 이 PR 에서 가치가 가장 큽니다.

## 되돌려 확인

| 무엇을 죽였나 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| `assert_band` 의 `out` 을 `[]` 로 고정 | 3건 실패 |
| 15번째 요청 앞에 `sleep(2.0)` | 위 메시지대로 실패 |
| `RateLimiter.acquire` → `return True` | **7건 실패** — 상한을 넓힌 대가로 잃은 것이 없습니다 |

## 덤으로 고친 것

`test_rate_limit_accuracy.py` 주석이 이렇게 적혀 있었습니다.

> ~~대기가 한 주기 더 늘어나는 회귀는 이 여유(2초)보다 크므로 상한이 여전히 잡는다~~

`1.0 < 2.0` 입니다. **한두 주기 과대 대기는 상한도 하한도 못 잡습니다.** 그 트레이드오프를 받는 이유(과소 대기만이 API 차단을 부릅니다)를 `tests/timing.py` 에 적었습니다.

## 테스트

```text
uv run pytest -m 'not requires_api and not performance' --cov
  1174 passed, 7 skipped, 47 deselected in 37.86s
  커버리지 92% (게이트 90)
```

## 남는 한계

**수정의 효과를 실패율로 보일 수 없습니다.** 이 머신에서 26/26 통과였으므로 "고친 뒤 N회 통과"는 아무것도 증명하지 않습니다. 보일 수 있는 것은 터지는 데 필요한 지연이 **1.44초 → 1.94초** 로 늘었다는 계산뿐입니다. 다음에 또 터지면 그때는 메시지가 실제 값을 알려줍니다.

일지: [`docs/dev_logs/2026-08-30_10_issue92_flake.md`](../blob/fix/issue92-rate-limit-flake/docs/dev_logs/2026-08-30_10_issue92_flake.md)

Closes #92

author: luismunozse
body:
## El bug

El navbar le ofrece **"Mi desempeño"** al rol TECNICO apuntando a `/tecnicos` (`navbar.tsx:74` y `:129`). El técnico hace clic y **vuelve al dashboard**.

No es un link mal puesto. La pantalla **existe completa**:

| Capa | Qué hace |
|---|---|
| `app/(dashboard)/tecnicos/page.tsx:11` | si el rol es TECNICO → `redirect('/tecnicos/<su-id>')` |
| `app/(dashboard)/tecnicos/[id]/page.tsx:67` | calcula `isSelf` / `canView` |
| ídem `:79` | si abre una ficha ajena, lo empuja a `/dashboard` |
| `GET /api/tecnicos/[id]` | va por `requireAdminOrSelf(id)` |
| ídem `:197,365` | renderiza "Mi desempeño" y "Mis comisiones" |

Nada de eso corría nunca. `/tecnicos` vivía en `RUTAS_ADMIN`, así que el middleware rebotaba al técnico **antes de la primera línea**. Era una feature terminada, con su scope bien resuelto en tres capas, muerta en producción.

## El fix

`/tecnicos` pasa a un bucket **ADMIN + TECNICO**. Es un gate grueso por ruta — el alcance real lo siguen decidiendo las tres capas de arriba, que ahora por fin se ejecutan.

El **VENDEDOR no entra**: no tiene pantalla propia ahí. Verificado que no existe self-view de vendedor, así que no toca lo que cerré en el #371.

## Dos cosas sobre los tests

**El test existente asertaba el bug.** `rutas-por-rol.test.ts` daba por correcto que al TECNICO se lo redirigiera de `/tecnicos`. Se corrige explicando por qué cambió, no se borra.

**`requireAdminOrSelf` no tenía ningún test**, y al abrir la ruta pasa a ser el guard que sostiene todo: es lo único que impide que un técnico lea la ficha —y las comisiones— de un compañero cambiando el id en la URL. Se agregan 7 casos.

Son tests de **caracterización**, no TDD: el guard ya funcionaba y nacieron en verde. Para que eso no sea una garantía vacía, **rompí el guard a propósito** (`if (false)`) y confirmé que 4 de los 7 se ponen en rojo; después restauré.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` → limpio

author: flying-coyote
body:
`PATTERNS` could not see **55 of the 61** open issues — two generator families no pattern carried: **49** `🤝 Community engagement triage` and **6** `⚠️ Expired Measurement Claims Detected`. Drain run 11 nonetheless logged *"Nothing left matching — the backlog is drained"*, because `remaining` measured **matched minus closed** and hit zero whenever the patterns saw nothing.

An all-clear that cannot distinguish *nothing left* from *nothing seen* — inside the instrument written to cure exactly that pathology.

## 1. Both families added

Verified against titles **fetched from the API**, not reconstructed: the warning sign is `U+26A0 U+FE0F`, and a pattern carrying a bare `U+26A0` matches nothing.

The new tests **extract the regexes from the workflow** rather than retyping them — a retyped copy would pass while the shipped pattern stayed broken, which is the same mistake one level up. Proven failure-capable: strip the `U+FE0F` and 5 of 47 checks fail.

Result: **60 of 61 matched**, standing issue correctly kept.

## 2. The completion notice reconciles against the repo

It now counts issues matching no pattern and reports **both readings** — the right outcome if they are human, a missing generator family if they are not — because this workflow matches on titles and cannot tell the two apart. Reporting the number and both readings is the honest output; asserting either verdict is not.

Both branches proven reachable: the default fixture's 54 human issues produce the reconciliation, and a bot-only fixture produces the all-clear. A check that could only ever say *"not drained"* would be as useless as the one that could only ever say *"drained"*.

## 3. The residue was never human

It was called **"55 human issues untouched"** in `PLAN.md`, in `.github/workflows/README.md:101`, and in the test fixture's 54 `Real human issue about N` entries. All 55 are `github-actions[bot]` output — verified by fetching them (`"Automatically created by source-monitoring workflow"`, `"Generated by: scripts/check-measurement-expiry.py"`).

**That mislabel is why the false all-clear was believed**: filed under "human", matching zero of them looked like success. The fixture encoded the same wrong belief, which is how the suite stayed green while the real drain was blind.

The workflow header also said **two** generators produced the backlog. It was four, and the two omitted are 55 of the 61 still open — the same mistake written twice, once in prose and once in the pattern list.

Both feeders are already deleted (`d9e484d`, `4875ed5`), so nothing refills these families: this is a one-time drain, not a recurring suppression.

## Also: the review job had no bound at all

`claude-review` passed **no `claude_args`** — no turn cap, no tool allowlist — so once the `@claude` path started working (#1007), the `author_association` gate was the only control on an agent holding `contents: write` and a live API key.

Added `--max-turns 30`, matching what the deleted source-update job used for a heavier task; the comment-only sibling's `15` is the in-repo evidence that `claude_args` is valid on this action version. A turn cap is **not** an authorization control and does not replace the gate — it bounds blast radius and spend.

`--allowedTools` deliberately **not** added: a review needs to read widely, and guessing the set risks silently truncating reviews. That half of the self-audit's recommendation stays open rather than guessed at.

## Verification

- `test-close-superseded-workflow.js` — **50/50** (was 44)
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors
- `--links` — 0 dangling, 0 root-relative, both lanes
- `check-measurement-expiry.py` — exit 0
- both workflows parse as YAML

## Remaining

**One `workflow_dispatch` apply run, which needs the operator** — Claude gets 403 on dispatch. After it, the expected end state is 6 open (the standing issue plus the 5 previously-matchable, if those are closed too).

author: davidchica-flit
body:
## Qué entrega

Eslabón **4 de 4 y último** del Feature [#11912](https://dev.azure.com/FlitDevOps/FLIT%20-%20FLITO/_workitems/edit/11912). Cierra el canal sobre el flujo de compra que ya existía.

### AC1 — ya se cumplía por construcción, y lo que se añade es la prueba

**No lleva código, y está bien que no lo lleve.** El gestor ya veía `solicitado` y `pagado` de los dos orígenes, y ya no veía los dos estados del canal:

- `condicionesCola()` no empuja **ni un filtro por `origen`** en la rama del gestor — solo `gestion_operaciones`, `proveedor_soat_id` y la lista de estados visibles;
- `FRONTERA_AUTOGESTION_SOAT` trae la rama `origen = 'cliente'` desde la #11914;
- `ESTADOS_SOAT_VISIBLES_GESTOR` es **lista blanca** desde la #11913, así que `pendiente_revision` y `rechazada` quedan fuera sin escribir nada.

Lo que aporta esta HU son tests que **miden SQL renderizado y el valor ligado a cada `$N`**, y que mueren si la lista blanca se vuelve negra o si la frontera pierde su rama. Verificado de forma independiente por `qa-agent` y `security-agent`; se dice así en vez de simular una implementación.

### AC2 — el Cliente descarga su póliza

`TIPOS_SOPORTE_VISIBLES_CLIENTE` deja de estar vacía. **La póliza y «la factura del proveedor» son la misma fila**: no existe un tipo `poliza` separado — el documento que sube el OCR es `factura_soat`, y el propio enunciado lo llama «la factura-póliza». Abrirla **es** el AC2.

- **Póliza**: visible solo con el SOAT en `pagado`.
- **Factura de venta**: visible en cualquier estado, y se argumenta: la única forma de que un `factura_venta` cuelgue de un `soat_id` es que lo subiera el propio Cliente (la del flujo de trámite cuelga de `flito_impuestos`, verificado recorriendo los cuatro escritores de esa columna). La necesita justo cuando **no** está pagada: al corregir un rechazo, «¿qué factura tengo cargada?» no tenía respuesta. Cierra una carga declarada de la #11914.
- Los soportes de origen interno siguen fuera y el comprobante PSE sigue gobernado por su allowlist de roles.
- El recorte por tipo va **al WHERE y también en memoria**, para conservar el criterio de la #11913 («no se lee lo que no se va a devolver») y para que la garantía no dependa del `where`, que el doble de drizzle ignora.
- **Allowlist del canal: cero entradas nuevas.** `GET /:id/soportes` ya estaba inscrita; el archivo baja por la ruta pública de token HMAC firmado.
- **Cero cambios en `apps/web`**: el visor de soportes ya renderizaba para este rol. Se **midió** con un spec Playwright temporal (sesión de Cliente → detalle → visor → petición a `/api/files`), que se borró después dejando el árbol limpio.

### AC3 — sin OCR no hay `pagado`

`POST /:id/factura` sigue siendo la única vía; no se añade carga manual de PDF y valor. El test cuenta los escritores de `pagado` y **declara la excepción que existe de verdad** —`reversar()` (RN-06), admin con motivo e historial, anterior a este Feature— en vez de afirmar una regla que el código no cumple.

## Cargas heredadas, cerradas

- `validarSolicitud` llama a `carreraPerdida()` en vez de duplicar su literal: el docblock del helper prometía «un solo sitio para que las tres digan lo mismo» y era falso en la letra.
- La aserción del parámetro en el test de aislamiento por compañía pasa a ser **posicional** (helper nuevo `sql-ligado.ts`): la forma anterior pasaba aunque `origen` se comparara contra otro valor, y la nueva **lanza** si la columna no aparece comparada, con lo que también caza al que borra la condición entera.
- El comentario de la #11913 que decía que la lista de soportes está vacía, reescrito.

## Gates

| Gate | Veredicto |
|---|---|
| `flit-code-review` | **OK** — SHA revisado `10b0d28` |
| `qa-agent` modo B | **PASS** — matriz AC→TC completa, 4/4 mutantes muertos |
| `security-agent` | **PASS** — 0 bloqueantes (auditó la reapertura de la lista que él mismo forzó a cerrar en la #11913) |
| `db-review-agent` | **no aplica** — el diff no toca `schema.ts` ni `migrations/` |
| `flit-ayuda-flito` | delta en `soat.md` |
| `ux-agent` | omit — extensión sin UI nueva: el visor de soportes existente resuelve el AC2 |
| `architecture-agent` | no aplica — el canal está decidido en ADR-0008 |

**Verificación real:** 6 archivos / 101 tests del WI · suite completa `apps/api` **350 archivos / 6776 pasados** · `build:api` y `typecheck -w apps/web` limpios · Playwright **100 pasados**.

## Notas

- **Decisión de producto elevada, no defecto:** la póliza que el Cliente descarga trae la **prima**, el mismo importe que la #11913 quitó de su DTO (`valorPagado`). El campo sigue fuera del JSON; el dato entra por el documento, y el AC2 ordena la descarga. Si el negocio no lo quiere, la salida no es otro filtro: es entregarle un documento distinto, y eso es alcance nuevo.
- La descarga **no** está gateada por `origen`: el AC dice «una solicitud de su compañía», y el Cliente ya veía en su cola los SOAT de origen trámite de su compañía desde la #11913.
- **Para una HU posterior:** la justificación escrita de por qué `/:id/soportes` no registra acceso PII quedó a medias — cierta del JSON, incompleta ahora que el PDF que baja una empresa tercera lleva placa y VIN. El evento sí queda registrado un salto antes (`GET /:id`), y la ausencia en la descarga es preexistente e idéntica para admin, proveedor y auditor.
- **Deuda preexistente cuyo radio de impacto crece:** al resolver una revisión OCR, Operaciones elige el SOAT a mano sin contrastar que la compañía del soporte coincida. Antes una resolución errónea entregaba la póliza equivocada a roles internos; ahora también a la empresa cliente de ese SOAT. Exige que un interno autorizado se equivoque.
- Autocrítica de `qa-agent` que conviene conservar: un caso de `gestor-ambos-origenes` pasa **vacuamente** bajo el mutante de la lista blanca (con la lista invertida la consulta ni se construye). El mutante muere en otros dos casos, así que no es hueco, pero ese caso no aporta detección por sí solo.

## Cadena

Eslabón **4 de 4** — **cierra el Feature #11912**. Nace de `develop` con la #11913 ([PR #247](https://github.com/flitsas/flito/pull/247)), la #11914 ([PR #248](https://github.com/flitsas/flito/pull/248)) y la #11915 ([PR #249](https://github.com/flitsas/flito/pull/249)) ya mergeadas y desplegadas en DEV con smoke M1 verde.

author: obiemunoz
body:
`mergePluginFailures` and `mergePluginNotices` in `packages/ts-migrate-server/src/migrate/index.ts` were the same loop written twice: for each group, look up an existing cause with `findCause`, union the file lists with `mergeFiles`, then either update the existing entry's `files` and `fileCount` or push a fresh entry.

They differed on exactly two axes. The first is the object pushed when no entry exists yet: failures push `pluginName`, `reason`, `ruleId`, `fileCount` and `files`, while notices also carry `hint` and `marked`. The second is that notices promote `existing.marked = existing.marked || group.marked` when an entry is already there, and failures have nothing to promote.

Both now sit on one `mergeFileNotices` helper, generic over the entry type, with a `build` closure for the first axis and an optional `onExisting` callback for the second. The generic is constrained to the fields the shared loop actually touches (`pluginName`, `reason`, `ruleId`, `files`, `fileCount`), which is the intersection of the two element types, so `MigrateResult['pluginFailures']` and `MigrateResult['pluginNotices']` both satisfy it directly. `build` returns `T`, so each call site builds its own full entry under its own element type and the extra fields never have to be described by the constraint. No `as` cast and no `any` anywhere in the fold, and `tsc` accepts writing `files` and `fileCount` through the generic.

The `marked` promotion still happens for notices only: it is passed as `mergePluginNotices`'s `onExisting`, `mergePluginFailures` passes no callback at all, and the comment about a later pass marking a site an earlier one only reported moved into the callback with it. Same entries in the same order with the same fields, same mutation of existing entries.

Built with `pnpm -r run build`, linted with `pnpm lint`, and ran the server suite from the repo root with `npx cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules npx jest packages/ts-migrate-server`: 9 suites and 117 tests pass, including `tests/commands/migrate/pluginNotices.test.ts`, which is unchanged.

author: mufflyt
body:
Appendix 1 already stated the mechanism —

> *a clinician who left practice before enumeration was routine has no registry record to be linked to*

— and then reported 66.2% as though the whole remainder were a limitation of matching. **The mechanism is testable**, because certification era and certification status vary independently.

## The test

If the shortfall were a name-matching failure, certifying before the registry existed would depress linkage for everyone who did so.

| ACTIVE certificants | n | linked |
|---|---|---|
| certified **before** NPPES enumeration opened | 4,173 | **84.4%** |
| certified **after** | 11,112 | **84.7%** |

**Three tenths of a point.** Certifying before the registry existed costs a practising midwife essentially nothing.

## So the era difference is confounding, not an era effect

The roster-wide gap — 66.5% vs 84.3% — is era confounded with *having left practice*. The shortfall concentrates where both conditions hold:

| pre-NPPES certificants | n | linked |
|---|---|---|
| DECEASED | 481 | **33.7%** |
| LAPSED | 4,707 | **55.4%** |
| RETIRED | 1,256 | 60.0% |
| **ACTIVE** | 4,173 | **84.4%** |

And of records where no candidate was found *at all*: **1,606** qualified before enumeration opened against **502** after.

## Why this changes the claim, not just the completeness number

A **matching shortfall** is a limitation of method: repairable in principle, direction unknown.

A **registry-coverage boundary** cannot be repaired from these data at all — the record was never created — and it falls almost entirely on people who had already left the workforce, which is the population a workforce estimate is not about.

This is the argument the ACTIVE-restricted bounds needed. They now rest on a mechanism rather than a caveat.

## Method notes

`NPPES_START` is the registry's own opening year, **not** a quantile of this roster. A data-driven cut would be circular, since what is being tested is whether the registry's start date explains the gap.

The producer refuses to write if no certification year parses — AMCB writes `MM/YYYY`, and parsing the year positionally returns `NA` for every row while still producing a table that looks valid.

It does **not** claim to measure whether any individual ever held an NPI. That is unobservable here.

## Discipline

- Every number generated; **ten registered as protected results**, so none can be typed into prose later
- The detect scaffold gained the artifact those keys resolve through — its *green* cases failed until it did, which is the scaffold reporting that the registry had outrun the fixture
- Declared in `REBUILD_ORDER` as a FROZEN consumer before T5 had to find it
- Artifact is aggregate; the person-level input stays gitignored

## Context

This came out of investigating whether the AMCB→NPI match rate could be improved. It cannot, by the route we expected: **both linkage paths already block against all 19 historical NPPES snapshots** (`match_amcb_to_npi.R:227`, `match_nppes.R:253-260`), so a former-name crosswalk adds nothing. That branch was discarded. This is what the investigation actually found.

## Summary

Ports staging's "Team access" admin-membership route (`/admin/members` — lets a club owner add/remove other admins), adapted for `main`'s password+MFA auth model since staging's version is built entirely on the passwordless auth system `main` doesn't have.

**Key adaptations (not a straight port):**
- Reuses `main`'s existing owner-only authorization pattern (`lib/authorization.ts` + the same shape as `lib/billing-route-auth.ts`) instead of inventing new auth-checking logic — added a `"membership"` capability alongside `"content"`/`"billing"`.
- The invite flow sends a password-recovery email (reusing `main`'s existing "Forgot your password?" flow) instead of staging's passwordless sign-in code, since a newly-invited admin needs an actual way to log in through `main`'s password-only login page.
- Re-added "Team access" to the sidebar, owner-only — Phase 2 deliberately left it out since the route didn't exist yet.

**This was reviewed (8-angle parallel review + verification pass) before pushing, per request.** Two real correctness bugs were found and fixed in `lib/owner-admin-membership.ts`:
1. An orphaned-Auth-identity leak: a lookup that could fail ran outside the rollback boundary, so a transient failure left a newly-created Auth user with no cleanup path.
2. A TOCTOU race in the rollback logic that could delete a concurrently-committed membership row under specific timing.

Both are covered by new regression tests (one of which was verified by temporarily reintroducing the bug and confirming the test actually catches it). 6 more lower-severity findings were fixed (error-code-to-HTTP-status mapping, misleading error message, missing error-message entries, a mislabeled unsafe function). 2 findings were deliberately left — full details in `HANDOFF.md`.

## What changed

The v0.0.2 session's hard requirement: the standings view now exists, and Fixtures ↔ Table are reachable from each other at all times.

- **Persistent tab nav** on both pages, matching the `Kickoff Standings.html` design reference: Oswald caps on a shared hairline, active tab in ink with a pitch-green inset underline. Routes are `/` (Fixtures) and `/?tab=table` (Table), deep-linkable with `&league=` (e.g. `/?tab=table&league=pl`).
- **Full Table view** built to the reference artboards (1a/1b/1c): zone bands in the calendar's own competition colours, expandable Zones & key legend with per-league tie-break rules, PPG column + games-in-hand callout and `+1` chips, lettered W/D/L form pips, next-fixture join with both clocks, per-row expansion on mobile, sortable full columns on desktop with a "Pos stays canonical" banner when sorted off points. All five leagues.
- **Standings sync**: `npm run sync` now also fetches the official league tables from ESPN's public standings API into a committed `src/data/standings.json` — the same generated-and-diffed, never-typed posture as fixtures. Rank moves are logged but never drive the exit code; the fixtures diff semantics are unchanged.
- **Supporting changes**: hand-authored 2026-27 zone/tie-break metadata in `competitions.ts` (England and Spain hold fifth UCL berths via the 2025-26 coefficients); IBM Plex Mono loaded for tabular numerals; `App.tsx` split into `FixturesPage` + `TablePage` under the shared shell (mechanical extraction, no behaviour change); fresh data snapshot from this session's sync.
- **Docs**: the session's audit, redesign directions, AI shortlist and hosting plan in `docs/v0.0.2-proposal.md`.

## Why

There was no way to get from the fixtures view to a standings view — the standings view didn't exist at all. The visual direction for it was already settled by the design artifact, so this ships that design against real, provenance-stamped data instead of placeholders.

## For the reviewer

- Position/points/records come from the provider's table, never recomputed locally — league order depends on per-competition tie-breakers (La Liga breaks level clubs on head-to-head first).
- Known deviations from the design reference, deliberate: Results tab noted as future (no Results view exists yet); Overall/Home/Away split deferred (the feed has no venue split); "Team detail →" buttons omitted (dead links until a team view exists); "matchday N of M" computed from most-played rather than an official round (ESPN exposes none).
