author: laurenceday
body:
Closes wildcat-finance/skills#940

## What changed

Issue #940 asked whether the generated skills.sh payload should keep living in
this tree. ADR-054 answers it: it stays, and relocation is refused on discovery
rather than on effort.

`.agents/skills/promise-machine/` is a generated copy of this repository, kept
inside it. At `7e97b519` it is 999 tracked files and 21,789,732 bytes, against a
tracked tree of 3,102 files and 121,305,325 bytes: 32.2% of the files, 18.0% of
the bytes. ADR-040 chose that arrangement and rejected five alternatives, every
one of which keeps the payload in this repository. Holding it outside was never
put next to them, so the size question had no recorded answer and kept being
reopened.

`skills.sh.json` groups `promise-machine` from the repository root, and both the
skills.sh listing and a ref-less `npx skills add wildcat-finance/skills` resolve
against the default branch. This repository is in neither the CLI's
`BLOB_ALLOWED_OWNERS` nor its `BLOB_ALLOWED_REPOS`, so the command falls through
to a shallow clone of that branch and discovers skills in that tree. A payload
off `main` is not discoverable, and a thin entrypoint left behind to preserve
discovery is fetch-after-install or an outside link, both of which ADR-040
already rejected. A separate repository and an orphan distribution branch are
costed in the record and fail the same way.

The record also corrects what the existing size constants mean. `MAX_FILES` and
`MAX_BYTES` are the CLI's extract defaults; they gate its `well-known` and
`download` source types, which are direct `SKILL.md` and archive URLs. The
`github` type this repository installs through never consults them. They are
kept and now commented, so nobody reads 994 against 1,000 as an imminent install
failure.

One guard holds the tracked footprint under a stated ceiling and names ADR-054
when it fails. It binds on bytes before the CLI-cap assertion does.

## Verification

- Root suite 737 of 737.
- `horos check` reports the boundary matches the tree.
- phylax, ephoros and hypomnema each exit 0; imprimatur scores every prose
  artefact 100.0 with 0 defects.
- Two audit rounds, one low finding in round 1 fixed in `e1f13e6a`, round 2
  clean. The guard was driven rather than reread: lowering
  `TRACKED_BYTES_CEILING` to `21_000_000` fails with `21789732 not less than or
  equal to 21000000`, lowering `TRACKED_FILES_CEILING` to `900` fails with `999
  not less than or equal to 900`, and both name ADR-054.

## Carried forward

- The sync coupling is unrepaired. #854 records the sync/scan ordering fault and
  the missing import-closure check, and owns both. This run changed neither.
- Whether `1_010` and `22_500_000` are correctly sized headroom is not
  established. They were chosen to bind before the CLI-cap assertion, not from
  a projection of how the payload grows.
- The discovery claim is a reading of the skills CLI's `source-parser.ts`,
  `add.ts`, `blob.ts` and `git.ts`. No relocation was attempted and no install
  was driven against a moved payload. ADR-054 records the conditions under which
  it should be revisited rather than cited.
- `RECORDED_TRACKED_FILES` and `RECORDED_TRACKED_BYTES` appear only in the
  guard's failure messages and are never asserted, so the recorded figure can
  drift below the ceiling without the suite noticing. Asserting them exactly was
  rejected as brittle.
- ADR-054 took the next free number against `origin/main` at this branch's cut.
  Assigning numbers at authoring rather than at merge is the collision surface
  #888 owns.

## Summary
A validation failure in production returns a generic `{code, message, requestId}` with no field-level detail — by design, since `appError.details` (the flattened Zod field errors) is only added to the client response outside production. The problem: that same detail was never logged server-side either, so a report like "creating a user fails with VALIDATION_ERROR" was undiagnosable from `docker compose logs app` — there was no way to see which field failed or why, in production or from the logs.

Adds `details: appError.details` to the warn/error log payload. This is server-side only — the client response is unaffected, still stripped of details in production — but now `docker compose logs app` shows exactly what failed.

body:
2026-08-29 실사고. #718(진단)의 후속 — **원인 특정 후 근본 수정**.

## 원인

토요일 8.01km 가 애플 피트니스엔 있는데 앱에 안 들어왔다. #718 로 붙인 진단이 **"조회 0건"** 을 보여줬고, 설정을 확인하니 **읽기 허용 목록에 '운동'(workoutType)이 없었다** — 걸음·속도·심박 같은 수치만 있고 워크아웃 자체가 빠져 있었다.

조회 창은 마지막 저장일(8/27)부터라 **이미 저장된 8/27 러닝조차 안 잡혔다.** 그게 결정적 단서였다.

## 왜 스스로 복구가 안 됐나

- iOS 는 읽기 권한이 없으면 **에러 대신 빈 결과**를 준다(정책 — 앱이 거부를 감지 못하게)
- iOS 는 **읽기 권한 상태를 앱에 알려주지 않는다** — `authorizationStatus` 는 쓰기만 반영
- 그래서 앱의 '이미 물어봤음' 마커가 한 번 켜지면 **권한이 꺼져도 시트를 다시 못 띄운다**. 복구 경로가 **앱 삭제뿐**이었다

**같은 계열 세 번째다.** 주석에 v2(경로 권한 미요청 → 지도 빔), v3(마커만 남아 시트 안 뜸 → 지도 유실)이 기록돼 있다. 앞선 두 번은 **키 버전만 올려** 넘겼는데, 그건 근본 해결이 아니었다.

## 조치

1. **마커 키 v3 → v4** — 이번 기기 즉시 복구
2. **자가복구 경로 신설** — iOS 가 상태를 안 알려주니 **경험적 신호**로 판정한다:
   > 조회 창은 마지막 저장일부터라 **그 러닝이 반드시 포함**된다. 그런데 0건이면 읽기가 막힌 것이다.

   판정은 기존 기록 수를 아는 **웹**이 하고(`readAuthSuspect`), 네이티브는 마커를 지운 뒤 재조회한다(`resetHealthReadAuth` 브리지)
3. **화면에 원인과 조치를 말해준다** — *"'운동' 읽기 권한이 꺼진 것 같아요"* + **「건강 권한 다시 요청」** 버튼

지금까지는 0건이 나와도 사용자가 알 방법이 없었다. 이제 앱이 먼저 말한다.

## 검증

| | |
|---|---|
| vitest 1165 · vue-tsc · harness:check | ✅ |
| `xcodebuild` RunningCoach (generic/iOS) | ✅ BUILD SUCCEEDED |
| 실기기 | ⚠️ 확인 필요 — 마커 v4 는 **재빌드/재설치로 적용**된다 |

## 남은 한계 (정직하게)

`readAuthSuspect` 는 추론이다. 조회 0건의 다른 원인(HealthKit 자체 장애 등)에도 뜰 수 있다. 다만 **버튼을 눌러도 부작용이 없고**(권한 시트를 한 번 더 띄울 뿐), 지금처럼 **아무것도 모른 채 4일을 보내는 것보다는 낫다**.

author: rphovley
body:
## Summary
`docker-compose.dispatch.yml`'s `image:` line silently defaulted to `quotethat-dispatch:latest` — the same hardcoded-quotethat pattern the worker image had before it became project-scoped. `dispatch.sh` already exports `MUADDIB_DISPATCH_IMAGE` correctly before invoking compose, so this was dead code on the supported path, but misleading and a real collision risk if compose is ever invoked directly.

Changed to `:?` (required), matching this same file's own existing convention for every other value `dispatch.sh` is responsible for. Also fixed the quotethat-hardcoded example commands in this file and `Dockerfile.dispatch`.

**Scope note — found but not fixed, reported instead:**
- `docker-compose.worker.yml:12` has the identical `${MUADDIB_WORKER_IMAGE:-quotethat-worker:latest}` pattern — same dead-but-misleading fallback, same fix would apply, but out of scope for this change (directive was dispatch-specific).
- `Dockerfile.dispatch` has no `COPY` instructions at all (source is bind-mounted at runtime, not baked) — the nested-path `COPY`-prefix bug class (#41) doesn't apply here.
- Found a real, separate, larger gap instead: `docker-compose.dispatch.yml`'s `build.context: ..`, `volumes: - ..:/repo`, and `working_dir: /repo/muaddib` are all resolved relative to wherever `dispatch.sh` invokes compose from (no `--project-directory` override, unlike `spawn-worker.sh`), and all assume muaddib is nested one level under the real project root. For self-hosting (muaddib's own root has no nested `muaddib/`), `..` resolves to the *parent* of the muaddib checkout — an unrelated directory — not muaddib itself. This means the dispatch daemon doesn't support self-hosting at all today, a genuinely separate and larger fix than a naming issue. Not attempted here.

## Test plan
- [x] `docker compose config` resolves to `muaddib-dispatch:latest` when `MUADDIB_DISPATCH_IMAGE` is set (as `dispatch.sh` always sets it)
- [x] `docker compose config` fails with the intended clear error when it's unset
- [x] Confirmed no other script invokes this compose file without going through `dispatch.sh` first (grepped for `docker-compose.dispatch.yml` references)

author: gigayama
body:
#86 をマージしたあと、念のため差分を敵対的にレビューしたところ、**実機で再現する誤りが 2 件**見つかりました。どちらも公開ずみの本文にあります。文章だけの変更です。

## ①「げきおこ」「バリア」の条件は、向きではなく画面の幅でした

本文にこう書いていました。

> タブレットを たてに して つかって いる ときは、この 2つは 文字が 出ず、ほのおの マークと たての マークだけに なります。

**これは誤りです。** 条件は画面の向きではなく **幅 768px 未満**でした（`src/BossBattle.jsx:305,310` の `hidden md:inline`）。

- `tailwind.config.js` は `screens` を上書きしていないので `md` は既定の 768px
- `src/` と `index.html` に `orientation` を見ているコードは **1 つもありません**

Playwright で 6 種のビューポートを実測した結果です。

| 幅 | 「げきおこ」「バリア」の文字 |
| --- | --- |
| 390px（スマートフォン） | 出ない |
| 744px（iPad mini） | 出ない |
| 768 / 810 / 834px（iPad たて持ち） | **出る** |
| 1366px（学校のクロームブック） | **出る** |

つまり、本文が名指ししている「がっこうの クロームブック」では、**たて持ちでも文字が出ます。** 逆に消えるのはスマートフォン幅と iPad mini で、これは「たて／よこ」では説明できません。

あわせて、画面中央の全画面カットイン（`BossBattle.jsx:540,581`）は `md` が文字の大きさしか変えず `hidden` が付かないため、**どの幅でも文字が出る**ことを書き足しました。小さいふだが読めないときの逃げ道になります。

## ② 存在しない節へ案内していました

> うつしたい ときは「きろくを ほかの タブレットに うつす」を 見て ください。

この見出しは**ありません**。#86 で章名を「きろくが のこる ばしょと、きえて しまう とき」に変えたときの直し忘れです。

しかも同じ文書の別の場所が「ほかの タブレットへ うつす きのうは ありません」と**正反対**を書いているので、読み手は探したうえで存在しないと知ることになります。

実在する章に向け直し、先に「きのうは ありません」と言い切るようにしました。アプリ側にも記録の持ち出し UI はありません（`StorageAPI` にあるのは自作コースの `encodeCourse` / `decodeCourse` だけで、`records-export.js` は giga-school の集計ページ向けの窓口）。

## 検査

- `lint-manual.mjs` → 警告 0 件
- 公開と同じ組み立て → 本文 24,670 字／画像 56／降格した本文 0
- `npm test` 5/5、`npm run check` 46/46＋コントラスト 708/708

author: shir0o
body:
## What

Implements the colour-token regression guard specified in [issue #661](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/issues/661) and the Ink design system spec.

Mirrors the existing i18n regression guard (`scripts/check-hardcoded-ui-strings.ts`):
- Scans only lines added in the current diff.
- Fails the build if a new raw hex value (`#fff`, `#abcdef`, …) or raw Tailwind palette class (`bg-red-500`, `text-blue-600`, …) lands in component source.
- The stylesheet (`src/index.css`) is excluded by file extension so CSS custom-property definitions stay unflagged.
- Test files (`*.test.tsx`, `*.spec.tsx`) are excluded — they legitimately exercise the patterns the guard is meant to flag.
- Comment lines (`//`, `/*`, `*`) are skipped so issue refs like `(#563)` don't produce false positives.

Existing hardcoded colours across the tree are intentionally untouched — the guard prevents **new** ones.

## Acceptance criteria (from #661)

- [x] Scans only lines added in the diff, matching the i18n guard's approach
- [x] Raw hex values and raw palette classes in component source fail
- [x] CSS custom property definitions in the stylesheet are not flagged
- [x] Exposed as an npm script (`check:colors`) and run as its own CI step
- [x] Passes on the current tree with no changes to existing files
- [x] The guard itself has tests (29 unit tests)

## Changes

- `scripts/check-hardcoded-colors.ts` — the guard. Pure functions are exported so tests can exercise them; the CLI entry is gated on `process.argv[1]` so importing the module from tests does not trigger `process.exit`.
- `src/test/checkHardcodedColors.test.ts` — 29 unit tests covering hex/palette detection, comment skipping, target-file scoping, and unified-diff parsing.
- `package.json` — adds `check:colors` script.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — adds the guard as its own CI step.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `[Unreleased]` entry.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors
- `npm run check:i18n` — pass
- `npm run check:colors` — pass
- `npm run test:coverage` — 91.89% lines / 78.71% branches / 87.18% functions / 90.09% statements (all thresholds met)
- `npm run build` — clean
- Sanity check: a temporary file with `bg-red-500` and `#ff0000` in `src/components/_GuardTest.tsx` correctly fails the guard with exit code 1; the same hex in a `*.test.tsx` file is correctly excluded.

## Test approach

The guard has one job: emit a clean, falsifiable, scoped result. The interesting testable behaviour lives in the pure functions (`findViolations`, `isCommentLine`, `isTargetFile`, `parseUnifiedDiff`). The CLI `run()` is a thin orchestrator that wires them together with `git diff` — testing it end-to-end would require either a real git fixture or aggressive mocking of `execSync`, and the value of that test is low because the orchestration is shallow. The diff-scoping end-to-end test (where the guard skips an existing hex match in the tree but flags a new one) was verified manually during development; the i18n guard follows the exact same pattern and is not tested end-to-end either.

author: svyable
body:
Adds Chapter 7, “Bell Labs and the Architecture of Wandering,” to the Drafting manuscript of *The Search Frontier*.

The chapter treats Bell Labs as an institutional search architecture rather than a creativity myth: practical problem supply from the telephone network, patient funding, disciplinary depth, low-cost intellectual crossings, hard experimental feedback, and pathways from foundational theory to engineering. It uses the transistor and Shannon’s 1948 information-theory papers as the principal cases, while preserving the counterargument that Bell Labs’ search capacity depended partly on an unusual regulated-monopoly structure that cannot simply be copied.

Scope: exactly one manuscript chapter, the book README/TOC advanced to 7 of 20 drafted, and chapter-specific source-ledger additions. No root catalog/discovery files changed and nothing released to Shelf.

author: moonfall-man
body:
House Party (Unity, NVUnityPlugin's D3D11 NGX) turns out to be a second engine with the inversion #5 describes for Bannerlord: the evaluate block carries the DRS render size in `OutWidth/OutHeight` while `Width/Height` hold the display size the game created its own feature with. Its gameplay textures are additionally padded for dynamic resolution (5120x2048 allocations for a 5120x1440 display), which turns the output-texture fallback into a feature NGX refuses: every evaluate answers 0xBAD00005, and three strikes disable the bridge on each scene load — the menu, whose allocations match the display, works.

Two changes, both scoped to the inverted case (`OutWidth < Width`):

1. **Use `Width/Height` for the output instead of the output allocation.** That is the shape the game's own create states (`Width == OutWidth ==` display in both engines' creates), and the contract its D3D11 evaluates demonstrably pass. The true render size still reaches the evaluate through the game's own subrect dimensions, which these engines fill in correctly. For Bannerlord's unpadded textures this lands on the same values the fallback chose, so #5's case is covered without behavior change beyond the padding case.

2. **Deliver the named output region instead of standing aside on the padding mismatch.** The partial-output stand-aside exists because Gallipoli's map screen names no region. An inverted block does name it: the subrect origins state 0,0, and the game's own DLSS writes exactly that region of the same padded allocation and displays only it. The unnamed-region stand-aside stays as it was.

Verified on House Party (RTX 4090, driver 616.56, 5120x1440): menu and gameplay both deliver, 26k+ evaluates without a failure where previously every scene load logged three `evaluate failed with result 0xBAD00005, InvalidParameter` and `disabled after repeated failures (evaluate)`. The DLSS 5 Neural Rendering add-on binds and runs in gameplay. Happy to attach full before/after logs.

Should also resolve #5, though I could only test the House Party half.

author: ywatanabe1989
body:
fix(ci-runners): the health monitor could never pass — ssh joins argv, so every remote command ran bare

`scitex-hpc ci-runners watch` alarmed CRITICAL on a fleet I had just restored
and independently confirmed healthy:

    ALARM: scitex-ci: supervisor UNREGISTERED -- no holder jobid at
    /home/ywatanabe/.scitex/hpc/runtime/ci-supervisor-holder.jobid on spartan
    RC=12

while, from the same machine:

    ssh spartan 'cat $HOME/.scitex/hpc/runtime/ci-supervisor-holder.jobid'
    29677925

THE CAUSE. ssh does not pass argv through. It JOINS its arguments with spaces
and hands the result to the remote shell as ONE command string. So in

    ssh "$HOST" bash -lc "<cmd>"

the local shell strips the quotes around <cmd>, and the remote receives

    bash -lc squeue --user=$USER --job=123 --noheader --format='%i %T %N'

where `-c` takes only the next WORD as its command; everything after becomes
$0/$1/... The remote ran a BARE `squeue`.

MEASURED against a RUNNING supervisor, not reasoned:

    as generated    ->  [JOBID PARTITION NAME]          <- squeue's HEADER row
    with printf %q  ->  [29677925 RUNNING spartan-bm151]

So step 1 set STATE=PARTITION, JOBID=JOBID and would alarm "allocation DOWN"
against a healthy allocation. Step 0 read an empty holder id and alarmed
"supervisor UNREGISTERED". Step 3 would run a bare `df` and take an arbitrary
filesystem's IUse%.

None of these are errors — they are WRONG ANSWERS, which is why nothing ever
surfaced them. The JobSpec was never installed, so nobody watched the watchdog
fail. A monitor that cannot pass is worse than no monitor: it is the
alarm-fatigue failure that makes the next real outage invisible.

THE FIX. All five remote call sites shared the defect, so this fixes the class
rather than the instance — one helper, defined once in the generated script:

    rsh() { ssh "$HOST" bash -lc "$(printf '%q' "$1")" 2>/dev/null; }

`printf %q` escapes the command into a single shell WORD, so it survives the
join intact and `-c` receives the whole thing. Sites converted: step 0 (holder
jobid), step 1 (squeue), step 2 (srun --overlap pgrep), step 2b (.needs-restart
marker), step 3 (df -i).

VERIFIED END TO END against a live fleet, with the verdict moving in the right
direction at each stage:

    before the fix                exit 12  "supervisor UNREGISTERED"   (false)
    mid-patch, pipes mangled      exit 10  "7 runner(s) DOWN"          (false)
    fixed                         exit 10  "2 runner(s) DOWN"          (TRUE)

and the two it now names are the two that are genuinely not up, corroborated
independently:

  * scitex-plt            — 7 runners launched, 6 Runner.Listener processes
                            running; this is the one that did not come up
  * spartan-pooled-cpu-01 — its install dir is under a DIFFERENT base,
                            .../punim0264/ywatanabe/ci-pooled/, while
                            RUNNER_DIRS is built from a single --ci-base, so
                            its dir can never match the listener argv

The five that ARE up (org-spartan-cpu-01, org-spartan-cpu-02, neurovista,
scitex-audit, scitex-core) are correctly reported healthy, and GitHub's org
runner API independently shows the org ones online and busy.

I ALSO BROKE IT MYSELF ON THE WAY, and the verification is what caught it. My
first patch collapsed the three-line `ssh ... \` call sites with a transform
that split each tail on its first "|". Step 2's tail was `2>/dev/null || true`,
so it became `| true` — piping the listener list into `true` and discarding it,
which is why the run above reports 7 DOWN. Step 1's `| awk` lost its pipe and
worked only by accident. Both repaired and re-verified; the intermediate state
is recorded here because a plausible-looking edit that silently discards output
is the same class of defect as the one being fixed.

NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: the multi-base problem. This fleet now spans three
runner bases — `ci`, `ci-pooled`, and `/data/scratch` (an unmanaged
hand-installed runner) — and `discover_fleet` takes one `--ci-base`. Making the
monitor multi-base is design work with its own decisions, not a quoting fix, and
bundling it here would hide which change moved the needle.

author: vasihemanth
body:
Adds Qoder (Alibaba) as a supported coding agent — sessions, traces, delegation and a harness panel. Requested in #282.

## What Qoder turned out to be

Its CLI is a Claude Code derivative. Same JSONL record shape (`cwd`, `gitBranch`, `isSidechain`, `parentUuid`, `version`) under `~/.qoder/projects/<slugged-cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl`, plus five record types of its own. So `_qoder_trace_events` filters the existing Claude-shaped parser rather than converting a new format.

**It records no token counts.** Every assistant turn carries a `usage` object in Anthropic's shape whose `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and both cache counters are `0`, with the real figure in `credits`. That held for all 22 assistant turns on the install this was built against.

The counts can't be reconstructed either: `context_usage_ratio` is a fraction of an unknown denominator (`runtime-config.contextWindow` is `null`, the IDE's `maxTokens` is `0`), and `.models/<uid>/catalog-v6` is encrypted at rest, so even the model id stays opaque (`qmodel_38max`, `qfmodel`).

So Qoder reports 0 tokens and $0.00 under `billing_mode: subscription`, where that is the correct reading rather than a missing value, and the credits it actually spent drive a meter on its panel and the trace header. Three `not_available` entries say why the zeros are there — a bare zero is indistinguishable from a failed scan, which is exactly how DSH's missing codec read. ADR-0004 records the decision and the rejected alternatives, including a hardcoded credit-to-dollar rate.

## Two traps that would have produced wrong numbers

**Root sessions are globbed one level only.** A recursive walk returns every subagent transcript as a session of its own, turning two sessions into four. Same class of bug as the workflow count that was really counting subagent sidecars.

**The directory slug is not reversible.** Qoder replaces `/` with `-` without escaping dashes already in the path, so `-Users-dev-Documents-Qoder-2026-08-30-abc` has several valid readings. The project comes from the records' own `cwd`.

## One set of sessions, two surfaces

Qoder also keeps an Electron store in Application Support. Its `main.sqlite` looks like a second session store and isn't: message rows are marked `source = "sdk-projection"` and reuse the transcript uuids, and its `session_id`s are the transcript ids. Scanning both would double-count everything. It's read only for the human-readable session title, and counted towards the disk footprint (20 MB CLI + 40 MB IDE).

**Known limitation, stated rather than papered over:** `chat_sessions.session_kind` also admits `sideChat` and `automationExecution`. Every observed row is `standard` with a matching transcript, so there's no evidence either kind skips the JSONL — but if one does, it would be invisible. Unioning on `session_id` would cover it; that isn't built against a shape nobody has seen. Recorded in the code and the survey doc with the trigger to revisit.

## Read-only, and no credentials

`~/.qoder/.auth`, `auth.v1.dat`, `auth.machine-id` and the IDE's `byok_model_credentials` / `mcp_oauth_credentials` are existence-only, never opened. `.qoder-app-status.json` — which holds the account holder's name and email in plaintext — is not read at all, not even for a version string. SQLite opens read-only; the IDE holds a multi-megabyte WAL while running.

Attachment records are mapped by **allowlist**, not denylist: the four observed kinds are harness-injected context (skill catalogues, system reminders, hook output), and an unrecognised kind may carry file bodies, so it's dropped rather than passed to the renderer.

## Verified, not assumed

Per the repo's verify-before-done rule, every number was recomputed a second way.

| Claim | Independent check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session count | 4 transcripts on disk decompose to 2 root + 2 subagent | `/sessions` returns the 2 parents |
| Root credits | scanner vs HTTP vs a separate `jq` path | 6.5609, three ways |
| Delegated credits | same | 6.3803 (49% of spend) |
| Regressions | full backend suite vs a pristine `git archive` of `origin/main` | failure sets byte-identical (22 pre-existing, none in qoder) |

Also checked the surfaces that took a new agent key but were never opened: `/config/billing` reports `subscription`, `/config/retention` reports non-configurable and non-archivable, and `/analytics` buckets a zero-token agent without dividing by zero.

## Three bugs this caught before merge

- **Subagent transcripts carry the parent's `sessionId`**, so keying children by it collided both under one React key and made them indistinguishable. They're keyed by their own filename now.
- **The trace showed `INPUT 0 / OUTPUT 0 / CACHED 0`** with credits nowhere on the page. A session with no subagents had no explanation at all — the DSH failure again. The header now reads `CREDITS · DELEGATED · TOKENS not recorded`.
- **`/config` was rendering another agent's skills.** A Qoder trace showed "Project Configuration — Skills (48)"; all 48 were `scope: user` from Claude Code (45), Gemini (2) and Qwen (1), and none were Qoder's. That call site already excluded DSH for exactly this reason. Qoder now shows Runtime Capabilities from its own session log — the 11 skills and 3 MCP servers that run was offered, with plugin-scoped entries (`better-harness:`, `qoder-qmind:`) marked as such.

## Test plan

- 19 new scanner tests (`backend/test_qoder_scan.py`) and 3 new panel tests, all synthetic fixtures under `tmp_path`; no test reads a real home directory.
- Covers root-vs-subagent separation, credit summing, the unreversible slug, the `<system-reminder>` strip, tool-result survival, unknown-attachment rejection, IDE-title enrichment, an IDE row with no transcript, a torn final line, and traversal in the id lookup.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; no console errors on the trace page.
- Clicked through the dashboard tile, the agent page and both traces.
- Leak scan over the panel payload and the full diff: no credential-shaped strings, no absolute user paths.

## DO NOT MERGE YET — migration-history reconciliation required

This PR adds a no-cost runtime validation path for the public-database security hardening after Supabase development-branch creation was blocked by the current plan.

### Runtime contract
- Spins up disposable PostgreSQL 17 in GitHub Actions.
- Builds a production-like minimal schema/role/RLS fixture.
- Applies the hardening SQL inside the ephemeral CI database.
- Verifies public catalog read-only access, trigger/RPC execution boundaries, pinned search paths, and owner-only RLS behavior.
- Does not connect to or modify any Supabase project.

### Important migration drift
A read-only production check shows the production ledger already contains:
- `20260828101520 book_candidate_voting`
- `20260828101530 book_candidate_backend_hardening`
- `20260828101542 book_candidate_submit_rpc_fix`
- `20260828104212 public_database_security_hardening`

The current repository `main` does not contain all equivalent source migration files, and the production ledger versions differ from the original repository timestamps because those migrations were applied through a Supabase management action. Therefore this branch must **not** be merged blindly: doing so could make a repository-driven migration runner attempt to apply equivalent SQL under a different version.

### Supabase branch attempt
Creation of the explicitly approved temporary Supabase development branch was rejected with `Branching is supported only on the Pro plan or above`. No paid branch was created and no branch charge was incurred.

### Release boundary
- CI/reconciliation work only.
- No further production database write from this PR.
- Do not merge until migration history is reconciled deliberately.

author: ypjun100
body:
## Background

The start stage read the repository one angle at a time — find the existing structure, then check the code, then write the spec and plan. None of those reads needed the previous one's result, so the wait was the sum of all of them rather than the slowest.

That cost gets paid out of research depth, and shallow research shows up in the plan: a new function proposed beside one that already does the job, naming and placement invented next to the repository's own, a change wider than the requirement needs. Nothing sat between writing the plan and asking the user to approve it, so all of that reached the user intact.

## Summary

**Planning research fan-out** (`## Planning Research` in `butter-workflow-start`)

Five named axes go out in a single batch for Track B/C: `reuse`, `convention`, `impact`, `verification`, `external`. An axis is dropped only when the task gives it nothing to find. `01-SPEC.md` is written while they run, since it carries user needs rather than implementation choices.

Each agent stays read-only, reports findings rather than proposals, anchors every item to a repository location, and states when a search came up empty — silence and "nothing found" are different answers. Research that surfaces missed risk moves the track from B to C.

**Plan validation gate** (`## Plan Validation` in `butter-workflow-start`)

The finished `02-PLAN.md` goes to an agent that did not write it, checking reuse, minimal change, architecture fit, and convention, plus risk-target coverage on Track C. A verdict with no findings has to state what was searched for and not found; an empty pass does not count.

Findings are applied and the plan is re-checked once — one round, not a loop, so the gate cannot stall the stage. Findings still open after that round, and findings the plan author disagrees with, stay unapplied and are reported with their reason at the approval pause. The `03-TASK-*.md` files are written after the plan settles, so applying a finding does not mean rewriting the split.

Both contracts live inline in `SKILL.md` and both carry the inline fallback for tools without a subagent mechanism, matching the existing `### Delegate The Judgement` contract.

**Docs**

README gains a `Planning` section and an updated skills-table row. `docs/workflow-proposal.md` gains `#### Planning Research` and `#### Plan Validation` under the start stage, plus two core principles.

## Scope

Track A is unchanged: no plan, so no fan-out and no gate. The implement and code-review stages are untouched — parallelism was scoped to plan writing only.

## Verification

No automated test suite; this repository is documentation and prompts. Checked manually:

- `git diff main -- skills/butter-workflow-implement skills/butter-workflow-code-review` is empty.
- The `## Preference Capture` section is byte-identical across all three skills.
- The five axis names match between `## Planning Research`, the `## Workflow` steps, and the README block.
- Every Track A line in `SKILL.md` is unchanged, and both new steps state that Track A skips them.
- The README skills table matches the `skills/*/SKILL.md` directories and their `name:` frontmatter.

## Decisions Already Taken

- Track B, not C: markdown-only, three files, fits the existing delegated-agent pattern, easy to revert.
- The two contracts are inline in `SKILL.md` rather than split into `references/` files — they are written once and read from one place.

author: sgladstein
body:
**Follow-up to #150, which merged at head `9323e2e` minutes before these two things were written.** A merged PR cannot carry new work, so the branch was restarted from `origin/main` and this is a second PR. Documentation only — no code, no engine or asset change.

**Where it sits.** #150 measured whether a creature's *motion* changes how findable it is, and found the decoy field is entirely static. These are the two checks that finding was still owed: does it survive the creature changes that landed underneath it, and does the owner agree with it when he looks.

## §7a — every figure re-taken on the merged head

`main` landed **#142** (ants starve, a birth grant), #145, #146 and #149 under the branch while the report was open, and #142 is creature code. Every figure was re-taken rather than carried forward — a baseline measured on a tree nobody else has does not transfer.

**All identical**: the probe ladder (371 / 141 / 57 / 36 / 15 / 0 still against 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 moving), ambient motion, and all four live seeds including the never-moved fractions 42 / 41 / 33 / 22%.

Identical output across a change that must have moved something is this repo's stale-binary tell, so it was checked before being believed: the binary was rebuilt after the merge (05:43:34 against `src/sim/creature.rs` at 05:39:03) and contains `birth_grant`, a field that exists only in the merged `assets/species/ant.ron`.

**Why it is unmoved is a regime difference, and it bounds the report**: #142 governs the colony's energy ledger over long horizons, while this harness places founders and runs 600 frames, in which nothing hatches and nothing starves. A colony run long enough to starve is exactly where the never-moved fraction would be expected to shift — now stated rather than left implied.

## §7b — the owner's verdict, and the framing it corrects

Card `20260830T045018630Z-abf50b` (one frozen frame against 20 stepping ones, same 31 ants, same slope, same seed):

> *"I can see them in both but it is much more obvious in the scene stepping."*

**Confirms** the direction and the magnitude by eye, on the same scene the numbers came from.

**Corrects** a framing the report inherited: `creature-appearance-design.md` is titled *"Why you cannot find an ant"*, and the owner can. So the decoy count is what §7 already said it was — a count of candidates the eye must reject, not a claim of invisibility — and 148 against 1 is a large difference in how hard the search is, not the difference between possible and impossible.

Recorded with the card's own limits rather than as a clean win: the crop is 850 px at zoom 5 on a bare slope against sky, an easier picture than the 512x320 frame at 1x the player looks at. The follow-up worth posting is the same comparison at play scale.

`bash scripts/docscheck.sh` clean; `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean on the base.

author: gregpriday
body:
## The problem

The toolbar project pill had a transparent 28px button sitting on top of its emoji glyph. Clicking there opened the name-and-emoji editor; clicking anywhere else on the pill opened the project switcher. One control, two outcomes, and no visible boundary between them — the sub-target only revealed itself as a faint hover wash, after you'd already committed to the click.

The switcher is a many-times-a-day action. Renaming a project is a once-ever action. The rare one was sitting inside the hit box of the frequent one.

And the mis-click was worse than landing on the wrong surface. Both surfaces open with a text field focused, so the switcher's habitual click-type-Enter sequence typed into the **name field** and committed a rename. Dismissing the popover committed a dirty draft too, so even an abandoned mistype landed.

## The change

The whole pill opens the switcher. Identity editing moves behind **Edit name and icon…** in the pill's existing right-click menu.

The label is deliberately not "Rename project" — the switcher's row menu already has *Move or rename project…*, which is the on-disk relocation dialog. These are different things and shouldn't read alike.

The editor keeps its commit semantics unchanged and becomes a controlled, anchored popover. Everything that existed only to hold the overlay illusion together goes with it: the contextmenu/pointer replay onto the pill, the extra roving-tabindex stop, the sibling `parentElement` lookup, and the five tests that pinned the replay.

## Focus

An anchored popover has no trigger, so Radix restores focus to `null` and it lands on `document.body`. `PillRestoreTarget` hands the shared policy in `overlay-focus-restore.ts` the pill to aim at, which leaves every pointer close where it belongs — dismissing this popover by clicking the pill opens the switcher and focuses its search box, and a blanket restore would yank focus straight back out of it. Only the keyboard close is claimed locally, ringed, because that's the single case the shared policy hands back to Radix.

The menu item records its intent (scoped to the project that was right-clicked) and the menu's own close hook spends it, so the popover is raised after the menu is gone rather than inside its teardown, where the pointer release that closed the menu could dismiss the popover it just opened.

## Why the menu and not Project Settings

Settings → General already has name, emoji, colour and icon, and the pill's menu already links to it — so this is a fast path, not the only path. A two-field edit didn't warrant opening a full settings dialog.

## Notes

- Prior art for the overlay was #6928, which established it must be a sibling rather than a nested button. That constraint disappears along with the overlay.
- The pill ContextMenuContent's `preventDefault()` in `onCloseAutoFocus` is pre-existing and untouched here.

## Testing

- `npm run check` ✅ · `npm run typecheck` ✅
- Full vitest suite: 52,583 passing
- `ProjectIdentityEditor.test.tsx` rewritten around the new contract — 24 tests covering the focus outcome for each close path, the modality split, and the `setRestoreTarget` wiring
- New Playwright test in `e2e/full/worktree/core-project-lifecycle.spec.ts` position-clicks the emoji region and asserts the **switcher** opens, then right-clicks and opens the identity popover. Asserted by position because the regression is in the hit map, not in any handler a unit test can see. That spec (6 tests) passes locally against a real build.

author: sgajbi
body:
Part of #176 (slice 4 — operator read; slice 3 `ordered_fallback` remains, pending the alternate-candidate design; do not close the issue on merge).

## What

`GET /platform/providers/routing-posture` — the charter §15 'inspect current routing posture' surface. It **composes, never re-derives**: policy identity (`fixed_configured_mode` v1), the single candidate the policy would bind next (governed catalogue entry id, family, revision, `revision_pinned`, lifecycle state — the same resolution the gateway binding uses), the circuit-breaker descriptor from its own builder, quota/budget enforcement flags, and the enforcing kill-switch count from the kill-switch status builder. A posture read that disagreed with gateway behavior would be worse than none; sharing the builders makes disagreement structurally impossible.

**Deliberately absent** (producers rule): a routing-policy artifact registry — exactly one policy exists today; the registry ships with the second policy (S3). Per-request gates are documented on the response as per-execution concerns recorded on each routing decision.

## Evidence

26 focused tests green: null-candidate posture, governed-identity posture (incl. unpinned exposure), enforcing-vs-cleared kill-switch counting, API contract; lint, mypy (688 files), openapi-gate green. CI proves combined lanes.

author: ekkus93
body:
Implements the software portion of P4-004 through BlueZ directly on the Linux system D-Bus.

- implements `BluetoothBackend::pair` with `org.bluez.Device1.Pair`
- registers a BlueRoute application `org.bluez.Agent1` using `NoInputNoOutput`
- authorizes callbacks only for the exact outgoing peer currently being paired
- rejects PIN/passkey input and numeric-confirmation flows that a headless agent cannot honestly satisfy
- limits one outgoing pairing operation per backend instance
- bounds pairing to 60 seconds and attempts `CancelPairing` on local timeout
- maps BlueZ rejection, authentication, timeout, stale-state, and connection failures into typed `CoreError` categories
- implements explicit trust/untrust via the Device1 `Trusted` property
- requires a peer to be paired before setting `Trusted=true`; untrusting remains allowed
- keeps Bluetooth pairing/trust separate from BlueRoute membership
- adds deterministic pairing-control/error tests and a real-hardware `bluez_pair_probe` example
- documents the pairing-agent, timeout, trust, and hardware-acceptance policy

The feature-branch Rust 1.95 gate passed formatting, `cargo check --workspace --locked`, Clippy with `-D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked` after the final security review.

P4-004 intentionally remains `[-]` in `docs/TODO.md`: all four software subtasks are implemented, but acceptance requires two real Linux test nodes to complete pairing through the Rust-controlled flow.

author: swalmi
body:
## What

* Added ADR-003 documenting the document chunking strategy.
* Selected Unstructured's `By Title` strategy for insurance policy documents.
* Documented why fixed-size, recursive, semantic, and sentence-window chunking were rejected.
* Documented how title-based boundaries preserve legally meaningful sections such as Coverage, Exclusions, and Limits of Liability.
* Documented the risk of semantic chunking incorrectly grouping legally opposite but topically similar content.
* Documented Unstructured's automatic handling of oversized sections through `max_characters`.
* Documented why table elements remain independent chunks to preserve structured numeric data.
* Added the reference to *RAG-from-First-Principles*, Chapter 2.

## Why

Insurance policies rely heavily on section structure to convey legal meaning. Using title-based chunking reduces the risk of mixing content from different legal sections and helps prevent silent omissions or incorrect retrieval of important exclusions, limits, and coverage details.

## How Tested

Documentation-only change. No code changes or automated tests required.

## Checklist

* [x] Tests pass / not applicable — documentation-only change
* [x] Self-reviewed
* [x] Docs updated

author: mammonrn
body:
แก้บั๊กที่เจอตอนทดสอบบน production จริง 1 เรื่อง และเพิ่มฟีเจอร์ 2 อย่าง

## 1. บั๊ก: กดออกจากระบบแล้วค้างที่ "กำลังดำเนินการ"

สาเหตุอยู่ที่ `runAction` ใน `app/auth-button.tsx`

```tsx
if (outcome.ok) return;   // ข้าม setIsWorking(false)
setError(outcome.error);
setIsWorking(false);
```

บรรทัดนี้เขียนไว้ตอนทำ login ซึ่งพอสำเร็จแล้วเบราว์เซอร์กำลังถูกพาไปหน้า Google จึงตั้งใจคง `isWorking` ไว้ไม่ให้กดซ้ำระหว่างรอเปลี่ยนหน้า แต่ตอนออกจากระบบผู้ใช้ยังอยู่หน้าเดิม ไม่มีอะไรมาล้างสถานะ ปุ่มจึงค้างตลอดไป แก้โดยแยกสองกรณีด้วย `leavesPage`

### กรณีที่เกี่ยวข้อง: signOut คืน error ทั้งที่ลบ session สำเร็จแล้ว

ไม่ใช่ตัวที่ทำให้ค้าง แต่เป็นปัญหาจริงอีกจุด จำลอง `/auth/v1/logout` ตอบ 500 แล้วพบว่า

| | ก่อนแก้ | หลังแก้ |
|---|---|---|
| ปุ่มหัวเว็บ | "เข้าสู่ระบบ" | "เข้าสู่ระบบ" |
| cookie ที่เหลือ | 0 | 0 |
| ผู้ใช้เห็น | **"ออกจากระบบไม่สำเร็จ"** ขัดกับความจริง | ไม่มีข้อความ |

auth-js ลบ session ในเครื่องทิ้งไปแล้วแม้ฝั่งเซิร์ฟเวอร์จะตอบพลาด (404/401/403 ถูกข้ามให้อยู่แล้ว เหลือ 500 กับเครือข่ายมีปัญหาที่ยังคืน error) `signOut()` จึงเช็ค `getSession()` ยืนยันสถานะจริงก่อนตัดสินว่าล้มเหลว

## 2. กล่องยืนยันก่อนออกจากระบบ (`app/logout-dialog.tsx`)

ใช้ `<dialog>` ของเบราว์เซอร์กับ `showModal()` แทน modal ที่เขียนเอง เพราะได้ focus trap, ปิดด้วย Escape, คืนโฟกัสกลับปุ่มเดิม และกัน element ข้างหลังไม่ให้ถูกอ่านโดย screen reader มาให้ครบโดยไม่ต้องเขียน JS เอง

ใช้ `<form method="dialog">` ให้ปุ่มปิดกล่องพร้อมส่งค่ากลับเอง และล้าง `returnValue` ก่อนเปิดใหม่ทุกครั้ง ไม่งั้นการกด Escape รอบถัดไปจะถูกอ่านเป็น "ยืนยัน" โฟกัสเริ่มต้นอยู่ที่ "ยกเลิก" กัน Enter รัวแล้วหลุดออกจากระบบโดยไม่ตั้งใจ

## 3. แถบต้อนรับหลังเข้าสู่ระบบ (`app/welcome-toast.tsx`)

`/auth/callback` เติม `auth_welcome=1` เฉพาะตอนแลก code สำเร็จจริง แล้ว client อ่านและลบ param ทิ้งด้วย `history.replaceState` ถ้าให้ client เดาเอาจากการมี session อยู่ แถบจะโผล่ซ้ำทุกครั้งที่ reload หน้าโดยที่ยังล็อกอินค้าง param อื่นของผู้ใช้ยังคงอยู่

### บั๊กที่เจอระหว่างทาง: แถบไปโผล่นอกจอ

หัวเว็บมี `backdrop-blur` และ `backdrop-filter` ทำให้ element นั้นกลายเป็น containing block ของลูกที่เป็น `position: fixed` วัดตำแหน่งจริงได้ว่าแถบไปอยู่ที่ `y = -32px` คือเลยขอบบนจอออกไปจนมองไม่เห็น แก้ด้วยการแขวนไว้ที่ `document.body` ผ่าน portal หลังแก้อยู่ที่ `y = 704` บนจอสูง 800 ตามที่ควรเป็น

## ผลการทดสอบ

ทดสอบด้วย `npm run build` + `npm start` แบบ production พร้อม Supabase จำลองที่วิ่ง OAuth flow จริง

| ทดสอบ | ผล |
|---|---|
| เข้าสู่ระบบ แล้วแถบต้อนรับขึ้น | "เข้าสู่ระบบแล้ว / ยินดีต้อนรับ สมชาย ใจดี" และ param ถูกล้างจาก URL |
| แถบหายเอง | หายที่ 3.5 วินาที |
| reload ขณะยังล็อกอินค้าง | แถบไม่โผล่ซ้ำ |
| กดออกจากระบบ | กล่องยืนยันเปิด `:modal` เป็น true และยังไม่ออกจากระบบ |
| Escape / คลิกนอกกล่อง / ปุ่มยกเลิก | ปิดได้ทั้งสามทาง ยังล็อกอินอยู่ และโฟกัสคืนกลับปุ่มเดิม |
| ยืนยันออกจากระบบ | ปุ่มกลับเป็น "เข้าสู่ระบบ" ใน ~1 วินาที cookie เหลือ 0 |
| `/auth/v1/logout` ตอบ 500 | ไม่ขึ้นข้อความผิดพลาดหลอกผู้ใช้อีก |

Regression เดิมยังผ่านทั้งหมด: `?auth_error=` รหัสมั่วหรือพยายามยัด HTML ไม่แสดงอะไรและไม่มี XSS, ฟอร์มค้นหาพัสดุทำงานปกติ, ตั้งค่า env ไม่ครบยังขึ้นข้อความไทยพร้อมบอกตัวแปรที่ขาด, หน้าแรกยัง prerender เป็น static, `npm run lint` / `tsc --noEmit` / `npm run build` ผ่าน และ `package-lock.json` ไม่ถูกแตะ

author: fanduzi
body:
Fixes #49

## Problem

Immediately after a LATEST start against a silent MySQL, `GET /api/tasks/{id}/replication` reported `RUNNING` + `DELAYED` with `delay_seconds` in the hundreds of thousands. File/pos was already the source tip; `last_event_at` was the old binlog header. Idle later corrected this after the 2s dump wait. FILE_POS/GTID catch-up must keep real lag.

## Change

- Delay/status do not use `now - last_event_at` when the dump is at the source tip.
- Fresh LATEST reports at-tip as soon as StartSync succeeds (no wait for the 2s idle poll).
- Idle dump wait shares the same at-tip rule.
- `last_event_at` may still show the last event header time.
- Catch-up that is still behind the source tip stays `DELAYED`.

## Tests

- `buildReplicationResponse` / GET `/replication`: RUNNING at tip with a days-old header is `NORMAL` / delay 0; behind-tip catch-up stays `DELAYED`.
- MySQLRunner: LATEST start reports at-tip immediately; FILE_POS catch-up keeps event-header lag; idle poll reports at-tip.

## Notes

Rebased onto `origin/main` after #50 (`c8bbb04`). `handlers_tasks.go` overlap is only the L3 header (numeric-id pagination + at-tip delay). Not merging from this PR.

author: joaquinbejar
body:
## Summary

The greek aggregators summed eleven greeks across a strategy's legs with
unchecked `Decimal` addition. The plain overflow was the lesser problem:
`alpha_from` returns `Decimal::MAX` as a **documented sentinel** when theta
vanishes but gamma does not, so a strategy with two legs at a sub-contract
quantity aborted on `Decimal::MAX + Decimal::MAX`.

Fixing that surfaced a second defect in the same place, and it is the one worth
reading this PR for.

## 24 accumulations, not 23

12 in `Greeks::greeks` (the twelve-field aggregate) and 12 in the per-greek
aggregators — the issue says eleven of the latter; there are twelve. All go
through `d_add` now. No new plumbing: `GreeksError: From<DecimalError>` already
existed and both entry points already returned `Result`.

## The second defect: `checked_add` cannot see this one

**One sentinel leg beside an ordinary one never aborted — it silently dropped
the ordinary leg.** `Decimal::MAX` has scale 0 with a mantissa filling all 96
bits, so a fractional addend would need a 29th significant digit; `rust_decimal`
rescales the addend to scale 0 instead of failing, and anything below half a
unit rounds to zero. The addition *succeeds*, the running total stands still,
and the other leg's alpha is gone without a trace.

Converting to `d_add` does not fix that, because nothing overflows. So the two
alpha accumulation paths — and **only** those two, no other greek has a
sentinel — carry an explicit guard that refuses a sentinel operand and names the
leg:

```
leg {index} ({symbol} {strike} {style} {side}) has a vanished theta, so its
alpha is the Decimal::MAX sentinel and cannot be summed into an aggregate;
read the leg's own alpha instead
```

### The guard refuses exactly when a contribution would be lost

This is narrower than "a sentinel can never be aggregated", deliberately:

- **Refused** — a sentinel meeting a total that already carries a contribution,
  or a contribution meeting a total that is already the sentinel. Covers
  sentinel + ordinary in either order, and two sentinels, caught before the
  range limit.
- **Allowed** — a lone sentinel, and a sentinel beside legs whose own alpha is
  zero (`alpha` returns zero for a vanished gamma, so nothing is dropped).

The looser rule would have broken `OptionData::greeks_snapshot`
(`src/chains/optiondata.rs:1229`), which calls `greeks()` on a **single** option
and maps `alpha == Decimal::MAX` to `None`. Refusing a lone sentinel there
would discard eleven good greeks to report one bad one, and falsify that
module's doc comment. **A lone sentinel still returns the sentinel; chain
snapshots behave exactly as before.**

No silent drop survives either way.

## The mechanism is now pinned once, where the next person will look

`Decimal::MAX.checked_add(x)` returning `Ok(Decimal::MAX)` is a property of
`rust_decimal`, not of this sentinel, and it has cost **three** separate
diagnoses in this programme — it also made `chains::optiondata::unlock` re-emit
the locked quote it existed to remove (#459, merged as #472).

`checked_add_near_max_reports_ok_without_moving_the_value` now sits beside the
`d_add` family in `src/model/decimal.rs`, names both call sites it has broken,
and states the rule: **when you nudge a value and need to know it moved, compare
the result against the input; `checked_*` returning `Ok` only says the result
was representable.**

It also pins the boundary, which is narrower than first diagnosed: the silent
window is `|x| < 0.5`, not `|x| < 1`. At half a unit the addend rounds away from
zero to 1 and the sum genuinely overflows. Both sides are asserted so the
boundary is visible rather than implied.

## The sentinel stays `Decimal::MAX`

The issue asks whether it is still the right sentinel. It is: it was a hazard
only because the aggregators added it with the raw operator, and reporting that
sum was the whole of the danger. Replacing it would change the documented return
of the public `alpha` and ripple into `OptionData::calculate_greeks` for no
added safety. `alpha_from`'s doc comment carries that reasoning, states that
nothing prevents a caller reaching the sentinel — with the concrete reachable
case, rather than a claim of impossibility — and points at the pinned test.

The error variant reuses `CalculationErrorKind::ThetaError`: a vanished theta is
the cause, `numerical.rs:147` already uses it that way, and inventing an
`AlphaError` would be a public-API change to buy a better label.

## Aggregated greeks are unchanged — two independent checks

1. **Source-level.** `Decimal::checked_add` and `impl Add for Decimal` both
   dispatch to the same `ops::add_impl`; they differ only in whether a non-`Ok`
   result panics or yields `None`. For any sum the old code did not abort on,
   `d_add` returns the identical value — bit-identically, not approximately.
2. **Differential test.** `test_checked_aggregation_matches_the_unchecked_sum`
   builds a 24-leg matrix (both styles × both sides × three strikes × two
   maturity/vol/quantity regimes), accumulates a reference with the raw `+`
   operator greek by greek, and asserts the whole `Greek` struct equals it
   across all twelve fields, plus each of the twelve `Greeks::*` methods against
   the corresponding reference field.

The fixture for the sentinel tests was verified to be the real defect rather
than a construction: reverting only the two alpha accumulations to `+=` makes
both two-sentinel tests fail with `Addition overflowed` while the other five
still pass.

## The proptest exclusion is gone

`Greeks::greeks` was deliberately absent from the strategies panic-freedom
property, with a comment explaining why. Both are removed and the call is
driven with the rest. 67 property tests pass.

## Tests

4019 lib + 67 property + 423 integration + 207 doctests, 0 failed. `cargo fmt
--all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --workspace -- -D
warnings`, `make scan-banned` and `make public-api-check` clean — re-run after
the rebase onto `main` rather than trusting the pre-rebase run.

Public API unchanged: both entry points already returned `Result<_,
GreeksError>` and no error variant was added. `CHANGELOG.md` carries the
behaviour change under `### Fixed`, including the note that a lone sentinel is
unaffected.

## Stack

Chain A, second of four.

- Stack: #470 → **#469** (this one) → #463 → #471. Independent of chain B
  (#466 → #451 → #453), chain C (#462), #459, and the #442 capstone.
- Base branch: `main`. #470 merged as #475, so this branch is rebased onto
  `main` and the diff is its own work alone.

Closes #469

author: spencerjireh
body:
## What was wrong

The review body was Markdown the model wrote to a format `agent/SKILL.md` described in prose. The posted reviews show what that bought.

On [orders-api #19](https://github.com/spencerjireh/orders-api/pull/19) the verdict is nowhere near the top — four provenance bullets first, and the reader reaches line 12 before learning anything decided. A sensor field name is used as a claim (`secret_probe.decoy_read: true`). The coverage caveat is a parenthesis reading *"Other five services not run"*, when Cujo had executed one of six services. An `info` finding and a credential read are set in the same weight.

On [#8](https://github.com/spencerjireh/orders-api/pull/8) there is not one inline comment: both anchors were rejected by `validateAnchors` and dumped into `### Findings without a diff anchor`. The degraded path was the normal path.

Neither carries anything an agent reading the PR could parse.

Each of those is the failure decision 36 named for the footer — *a rule telling a model to end its body a particular way is a rule that fails silently* — one layer up.

## Why this approach

**Decision 74** extends 36 from "the server owns the footer" to "the server owns the body". `render.ts` composes the headline, ordering, sections and folds from `findings[]`, `coverage` and `egress`; `body` becomes a one-sentence lede.

Rendering in `github-mcp` rather than tightening the rubric is what makes this reach **in-flight pull requests**: a session pins its rubric at creation (decision 16), but `github-mcp` is stateless with a fresh server per request, so the next review on every open PR gets the new shape.

The verdict word is a function of the tool, so a model cannot write "blocked" onto an advisory review.

**Rejected:** tightening the rubric again (what 36 already rejected, and this is the second piece of evidence against it); a template the model fills in; keeping `comments[]` beside `findings[]`; inferring held findings from finding text; rendering the JSON block visibly; deriving the board's comments in `serialize.ts`; letting `github-mcp` read the check reports (decision 5).

## What changed, per concern

**`apps/github-mcp`** — `render.ts` and `plain-title.ts` are new. `comments[]` leaves the schema; `coverage`, `egress`, and per-finding `detail`/`next`/`held` join it. `appendMovedComments` is retired: a refused anchor is marked in place with `(not in this diff)`, since the body already carries every finding. `runUrl` is extracted from `appendRunFooter` so the footer link and the block's `run_url` cannot disagree.

**`apps/cujo`** — `commentsFromFindings` derives the same anchored list for the board, wired into `parseReview`. A legacy call's own `comments[]` still wins.

**`apps/web`** — `details`/`summary` join the sanitizer allowlist (deliberately **not** `open`, so folds stay collapsed as on GitHub), with `.cujo-prose` styles and a `ComposedBody` story.

**`agent/SKILL.md`** — the "What ran / Results / Egress" section is replaced by per-field discipline. The voice paragraph is kept verbatim.

**Docs** — Contracts 3 and 4, the architecture crossings row and flow step 5, decision 74.

## Two details worth review

**`held` is a field the design discussion never named, and it is load-bearing.** `github-mcp` has no check reports (decision 5) and title-matching is exactly what this PR deletes, so it cannot tell a malice warn from an ordinary one. Marking *every* warn held on an `accusation_follows` review would mislabel "no test covers this". One boolean the rubric sets was the smallest thing that works; `.default(false)` means a legacy call is never held.

**`safeText` closes a live hazard.** The body was passed through verbatim, so a model echoing attacker text containing `<!-- cujo:post_advisory_review:... -->` could forge a duplicate marker and suppress a real review. `alreadyPosted` reads that marker.

## Trust boundary and the gate

Nothing new crosses into the sandbox — `coverage` and `egress` are tool *input* written by the agent, on the `TrueForge → github-mcp` crossing. This does touch the human gate: `post_gated_review`'s input shape changes. Decision 60's structural guarantee is preserved exactly — that tool still registers the bare `reviewInputShape`, so `accusation_follows` cannot exist on it (`server.test.ts` pins this).

## How it was verified

`pnpm lint`, `typecheck`, `build`, and `pnpm test` — **1061 passing** (github-mcp 108, cujo 742, web 145, log 60, gh-app-auth 6). `uv run ruff check` clean, `uv run pytest` 238 passing. Rebased on `main` (through #84).

New: `render.test.ts` (two golden byte-equality bodies, plus headline vocabulary, held markers, section ordering, legacy `### Notes` and heading demotion, escaping, the JSON block) and `plain-title.test.ts` (which asserts the backstop never fires on any of the nine hard-rule titles, copied in verbatim).

`server.test.ts:174-189` lost its byte-identity assertion on the whole body — the headline is the server's now and lands on every review. What the private-repo guarantee still asserts is that neither footer nor marker appears.

The comment template is pinned with the *same literal* in `apps/github-mcp/tests/render.test.ts` and `apps/cujo/tests/review/findings.test.ts`, because both sides derive it.

## Known incomplete

- **`make test-int` was not run**, and no run has been posted against a real PR. The verification that matters most is the first live review.
- **Two derivations of one rule.** `apps/cujo` re-derives the comment list so the board's panel keeps working without a new projection field. Same trade as decision 21, same defence (both sides pin the template).
- **The board's `FindingsList` still shows raw model titles**, so a title translated in the review body is untranslated on the run page.
- **No test asserts on the rubric's review prose** — the same hazard decision 36 named, now one layer smaller.
- **Deploy window.** Merging deploys. If `apps/cujo` swaps before `github-mcp`, a session created in that window pins the new rubric against a server that passes `body` through verbatim, posting a one-sentence review. The reverse direction is safe, which is why the renderer handles legacy input; the window is a redeploy long and a new commit re-runs the PR.
- `docs/decisions.md`'s index carries two stray duplicate lines (`68.`/`69.` repeating the titles of 71 and 72 with broken anchors) that arrived on `main` from concurrent PRs. Left untouched — not this PR's concern.

## Wording question

The gated headline reads `**Accusation, pending confirmation**`, but that body only reaches GitHub *after* a maintainer confirms, so it describes the state it was drafted in. `**Accusation, confirmed by a maintainer**` is one line in `verdictOf` if that reads better.

author: shumoku88-bit
body:
## Purpose

Add the first practical exact-allocation operation on top of LOAM's integer-quanta core.

## Changes

- add `Loam.Core.Allocation`
- keep this first slice explicitly nonnegative with `Nat` quanta rather than assigning semantics to negative `Quantity`
- derive a common `base = total / recipients`
- retain `extra = total % recipients` by giving one additional quantum to the first `extra` parts
- zero recipients returns no parts
- prove a positive recipient count yields exactly that many parts
- prove the sum of all parts exactly reconstructs the original total
- include a compile-time sanity example: `100 / 3 -> [34, 33, 33]`
- expose allocation from `Loam.Core`

## Deliberately not decided yet

- allocation of signed/negative quantities
- recipient identities or priority semantics
- whether remainder should go to first, last, rotating, or policy-selected recipients
- weighted/rational allocation
- allocation directly over runtime `SomeAmount`

This is a small numeric kernel: exact integer division plus explicit retained remainder, with total conservation proved in Lean.

author: iamwhatever
body:
<!-- no-visual-delta -->
**Why no screenshot:** pure refactor with no rendered delta -- the bar's markup, Tailwind classes, i18n keys and `data-testid`s are byte-for-byte unchanged; only the module it lives in and which hook owns its state moved.

Stage 1 of #4626. A pure refactor: zero observable behaviour change, zero new surface armed.

## Why extract before arming anything

The drag-move undo that landed in #4617 works for **session drags only**. Its substance is not the bar — it is a lifecycle that is invisible on a happy-path read:

- an offer stays **PENDING** until the server acknowledges, because the move is optimistic and an offer armed on the store would let undo fire while the original PATCH is still in flight (the original write then lands and silently reverses the undo);
- it latches **`superseded`** when a third party's placement arrives inside that window, because by ack time live state may match the destination again (a move away and back) and nothing later could tell;
- once **LIVE** it is *dropped, never re-validated* — deriving visibility from live state let a retired offer come back and overwrite a newer, intentional move.

Stage 2 arms artifacts and folder-into-folder moves. `moveFolderTo` moves a whole subtree, so it needs exactly these staleness guards — which is why the mechanism is extracted rather than copied. A second hand-rolled copy would get one of the three subtly wrong.

## What changed

- **`website/src/hooks/useMoveUndo.ts`** (new) owns the offer state machine, the `MOVE_UNDO_MS` deadline, and the hover hold that suspends it. Callers inject only the surface-specific parts:
  - `locate(itemKey)` — where the item sits now; `undefined` = gone (retire), `null` = unfiled root
  - `apply(itemKey, folderId, { onCommitted })` — the optimistic move, acknowledging on server success
  - `folderExists(id)` — so undo degrades a deleted origin to unfiled instead of posting a 400
- **`SessionMoveUndoBar` → `MoveUndoBar`**, `MovedSession` → `MovedItem`, and its `slotKey` / `sessionTitle` fields → `itemKey` / `itemTitle`. Those two names would be lies the moment an artifact or a folder subtree arms the same offer.
- **`ChatSidebar` is the SOLE caller.** ~120 lines of offer machinery collapse to three memoised deps plus a descriptor built at the drag site.

`MOVE_UNDO_MS` and the one-way `live` / `superseded` semantics are preserved exactly, including two details a re-implementation would drop:

- the deadline effect's deps stay pinned to `[offer?.id, paused]` — flipping `live`, or writing the frozen remainder, must not restart the clock;
- `onHoldChange` captures the id that was current when it was handed to a bar, so a bar retiring through its 150ms `AnimatePresence` exit cannot freeze a *newer* offer's clock.

### Deliberately NOT renamed

The `components.sessionMoveUndoBar.*` i18n keys and the `session-move-undo*` test ids keep their names. The strings are translated in every locale catalogue, and the ids are what `website/scripts/capture-session-move-undo.mjs` selects on — renaming them would be churn plus breakage for no behavioural gain.

## Proof of no behaviour change

The existing tests pass with **their assertions untouched** — only the module path, the component identifier, and the two renamed field names change:

- `website/src/test/MoveUndoBar.test.tsx` (renamed from `SessionMoveUndoBar.test.tsx`) — 15 tests
- `website/src/test/ChatSidebar.moveUndo.test.tsx` — 15 tests
- `website/src/test/ChatSidebar.moveUndoStale.test.tsx` — 2 tests

## Testing

- Targeted: 32/32 green across the three suites above
- Full frontend suite: `1665 passed / 1666 files`, `26,340 tests passed`
  - one pre-existing failure, `src/i18n/productName.test.ts`, is **main-inherited** — it flags product-name strings in `pullRequestPanel.owner_not_configured_guidance` and `sttSettings.the_bundled_audio_decoder_is_missing_or_damaged`, fails identically on pristine `d7b7d65c3`, and this diff touches no locale file
- `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run lint` 0 errors

## Out of scope (stage 2, separate PR against the same issue)

- `ArtifactsPage.tsx` `handleDragEnd` — `moveArtifact` and folder nesting via `updateFolderMut`, both currently silent
- `moveFolderTo` in the sidebar and its drag routes + menu picks

no linked issue: intentional. This is stage 1 of two, and the tracked issue
(kirodotdev/KiroCrew#4626) must stay open until stage 2 arms artifacts drags and
folder-into-folder moves, which is what its report actually asks for. The closing
trailer therefore belongs on the stage 2 PR, not this one.

author: camshaft
body:
## What

An **aged** check-lease waiter now acquires **unconditionally** (yield only to priority) — the robust anti-starvation fix (concierge OPTION 1), following the #6038 aging-lower interim.

## Why

The old bounded `+1` over-cap slot wasn't enough: under **sustained over-cap** (`vert_weight` already ≥ cap, from a prior aged admission or mixed old-weight leases), a 2nd aged waiter still couldn't fit (`vert_weight + my_weight > max+1`). So a starved build waited for its own aging, but the loop/harness ~10min command-timeout **killed it first** (exit 144) → death → retry → more load (v-deferral-declines' CDZ0900, starved ~13 ticks). A weight-2 gate (needs 2 slots) could *never* fit under contention.

## How

`check_lease_go`: yield to a held priority lease first, then **`if aged { return true }`** (ignore weight/cap), else the unchanged non-aged cap check `vert_weight + my_weight <= max`. This **guarantees** a waiting build eventually acquires — no starvation-death, for any weight — while still always yielding to pr-sync's priority gate.

Bounded in practice by: the aging wait staggers admissions, non-aged acquirers stay capped (the trilogy #6004+#6026+#6030 bound the common path), and the nix-daemon CPUQuota caps total build CPU.

## Tests

Updated `check_lease_go_priority_wins_and_vertical_yields`: aged over/far-over cap → go (the anti-starvation cases, including the exact weight-2 CDZ0900 death case `check_lease_go(false, 0, 10, 2, 2, true)` → true); aged still yields to priority (`(false, 1, …, true)` → false). Non-aged cap checks unchanged.

Gate: 252 xtask tests + `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

author: whitphx
body:
Branch protection has no stable set of job names to require in this repo. `test-build.yml` skips most of its per-package jobs through the `changes` filter, and both workflows generate matrix job names that move whenever the matrix does, so requiring jobs by name would leave every newly added job unrequired and break on the next matrix change. This is groundwork for gating Dependabot auto-merge on CI.

This adds a `test-build-all-green` job to `test-build.yml` and an `e2e-all-green` job to `e2e.yml`, each reporting on every other job in its workflow, so `main` can require one context per workflow. `allowed-skips` names the jobs that legitimately don't run on every event, so a job dropping out of the graph fails the gate instead of passing silently.

The second change closes a gap that gate would otherwise lock in. The `changes` filter had no pattern for files no single package owns, so a bump touching only the root `yarn.lock` matched nothing and every unit-test job skipped, even though that lockfile resolves dependencies for the whole workspace. The same held for the root lint configs that every package's `check:lint` and `check:format` read. The `gha` filter becomes `global` and covers the shared lockfiles, manifests, lint and install configs, toolchain pins, and `packages/tooling`. The cost is that any PR touching `yarn.lock` now runs the full matrix rather than the jobs for the package whose manifest changed.

The third change stops a check going red when it shouldn't. Labeling a PR `skip-changeset` after opening it starts a second `changeset-check` run that takes the bypass, while the first run keeps going and leaves its failure on the commit. A per-PR concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress`, matching what `test-build.yml` and `e2e.yml` already do, lets the `labeled` run supersede the `opened` one.

Branch protection still has to be pointed at the two new contexts, which is a repository setting. On `main` the gate takes effect immediately either way: it is a job of the `Test and Build` run, so a gate failure flips that run's conclusion and holds back `postbuild.yml`.

author: wms2537
body:
Closes the Compose scope of #116.

`compose.prod.yml` hardens the **application** posture (auth, cookies, sessions). This hardens the
**container**: what a process can still do once compromised. They fail differently — a wrong auth
setting refuses logins loudly, a wrong capability drop breaks recording only under load.

Read-only root filesystems, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, PID/CPU/memory ceilings, bounded
logs, explicit tmpfs. The stack runs `network_mode: host` for cameras, multicast and WebRTC — which
removes the network namespace as a boundary and makes these process-level ones matter *more*.

## Every exception came from booting it

That's the difference between this and a hardening checklist:

- **MediaMTX** dies read-only with `unable to load TLS keypair ... open auto.crt` — it generates a
  self-signed keypair into its working directory at startup.
- **nginx** dies with `chown("/var/cache/nginx/client_temp", 101): Operation not permitted` — its
  entrypoint chowns cache dirs before dropping to the worker user. Granted back exactly
  `CHOWN`/`SETUID`/`SETGID`, not a blanket revert, and deliberately not `NET_BIND_SERVICE` (it listens
  on :8080).
- **nginx** also renders its config template into `/etc/nginx/conf.d` at boot, so that needs a tmpfs.
  Masking it costs nothing — the only file there is the one being regenerated.
- **The AI worker** keeps a writable rootfs: it downloads model weights on first use, and `read_only`
  turns that into a crash loop the first time someone enables an optional profile. Given a cache
  volume instead. Honest rather than aspirational.

## Compatibility evidence — from a real boot of all three services

- core **healthy** with a read-only rootfs, `/data` still writable (recording works)
- rootfs writes actually refused (`touch /rootfs_probe` → read-only file system)
- auth on (`401` on `/api/v1/system`), dashboard served (`200`), web→core proxy `200`
- `docker inspect` confirms `ReadonlyRootfs=true`, `CapDrop=[ALL]`, `no-new-privileges`

## The test

Guards the properties, not the file's shape — nothing else in CI notices a dropped setting, since the
stack boots either way. It also asserts the two read-only exceptions stay *documented*, so the next
reader doesn't assume one was forgotten and either re-add it (breaking boot) or remove it elsewhere.

Both negative-controlled. One control caught my own explanatory comment defeating its assertion — the
check now reads `cap_add:` lines rather than the whole file.

Gate: fmt 0, clippy 0, **542 tests**.

author: robertblust
body:
Two things the breadcrumb did and the canvas did not.

## Context

`spine` was set on the ancestor chain when the neighbourhood was built, used for geometry, and **dropped before it reached the DOM** — so the path from the root to the focus was drawn like any other ownership line. And the focused node was styled in the *same CSS rule* as `:hover`, so the node you had chosen looked exactly like whichever one your pointer was over.

Three tiers now:

| | |
|---|---|
| where you are | the focus, ringed in `--ink` |
| how you got here | the spine and its ancestors, `--c-mid` |
| everything else | `--c-weak` |

The ring is why the focus is not simply `--c-firm`: **every page square already is**, so filling the focused one with the same colour made it one more square among fifty-eight. A stroke is the one mark nothing else on the canvas wears.

The class is set on the **update**, not the enter. A link keyed `from→to` survives a click, and whether it belongs to the spine depends on where the focus now is — setting it only where a path is created left every survivor wearing the answer to a question asked one focus ago. The check caught this; a hash-loaded page never would, because everything enters at once.

## The divider

360px is right for a folder's card and wrong for a profile claiming 58 skills. The panes are now separated by a handle: **drag**, **double-click** to reset, **arrow keys** when focused. That is the shape every two-pane tool a visitor already uses puts between them — an editor sidebar, a devtools split, a Finder column — and the keyboard is there because a control that can only be dragged cannot be reached without a pointer.

The width is remembered and **clamped on the way back in**, so a number dragged wide on a large monitor cannot swallow the canvas on a laptop. On resize the *stored preference* is re-applied rather than the rendered width, so a pane clamped down on a narrow window comes back when there is room.

The key is a constant in `stage.js`, not the page's — this file is byte-identical on every site that draws a stage and knows none of their names, and `localStorage` is per-origin.

## A bug the check caught

The clamp first subtracted a hard-coded handle width and left the canvas **16px under its floor** — the grid has two gaps and the arithmetic knew about neither. It measures the chrome now:

```
stored 900 on a 900px window → { stage: 774, card: 428, canvas: 320 }  ✓ floor held
widened to 1440              → { stage: 978, card: 632, canvas: 320 }  ✓ preference came back
```

`divider` asserts the floor holds against a stored width of 9000, that a drag widens and is remembered across a reload, that double-click restores the default and clears storage, and that the keyboard works.

## Checks

Both suites pass; `stage.js` and `stage.css` stay byte-identical across the two sites.

author: tyler-r-kendrick
body:
Stacked on #140. The second service `delete.where` unblocks, and it needed nothing else: **19 steps, no superseded steps**.

## Two revokes, both wider than the request that asked for them

`lakeformation`'s revoke is the same shape as `sso-admin`'s. The pack compared the whole `Principal` structure and nothing else, so:

> revoking `SELECT` on **one** table from a principal removes **every** permission that principal holds, on **every** resource.

`Resource` and `Permissions` are required on the request and both are ignored. That is two services, two revokes, both over-broad — a pattern rather than a coincidence, and the reason the mutant added with the effect in #140 inverts the predicate rather than checking that the call returned. A test that only asserts the revoke succeeded passes in both.

The comparison is structural — `item.Principal == input.Principal` is deep equality over the map in CEL, which is exactly what the pack got by comparing the JSON it had marshalled.

## A grant is keyed by nothing it grants

Grants are keyed by a fresh generated identifier rather than by what they grant, so **granting the same principal the same permission twice stores two rows** and the listing shows both — something the real service would not do. The recording pins that.

Nothing consults a grant in any case: no S3, Glue or Athena operation in this emulator asks Lake Formation whether a principal may read a table, so neither a grant nor a revoke changes what any other service answers. `RegisterResource` is the same — registering a location does not make it governed, and the ARN is not checked to name anything.

## Ratchet

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| packs | 71 | **70** |
| case labels | 2007 | **1999** |
| services LOC | 47,166 | **47,056** |
| fault sites | 728 | 728 |

Case labels pass below 2,000 — from 2,526 when this session started.

## Verification

`make test`, `make ratchet` and the equivalence replay are green.

マジカルミライ プログラミング・コンテスト向けの新企画「ミクの本体はツインテールである」を、リポジトリ直下の `miku-twintail/` ディレクトリとして追加します。

## 追加内容

- `miku-twintail/docs/MARKET_RESEARCH.md` — 市場調査（コンテスト動向・類似作の構造分解・文化的文脈・TextAlive App API 技術基盤）
- `miku-twintail/docs/DESIGN.md` — 設計書（出落ち回避の核: 髪の素材＝歌詞の文字、定着判定＝ビート、髪の揺れ＝ボーカル音量。ミク度採点式、観賞モード、枯れた技術の水平思考）
- `miku-twintail/docs/TEXTALIVE_DEV.md` — TextAlive App API 開発ガイド（トークン取得、組み込みコード、App Debugger でのホスト接続テスト、モック移行対応表）

依存なし単体 HTML。Verlet 髪物理、幾何によるミク度採点、WebAudio 擬似曲、日常の物 4 種のお題、ミクの公式造形に合わせたツインテール描画（付け根の立ち上がり・四角い飾り・毛先テーパー・ツヤ）、タップ演奏（合いの手）システム。
