author: monkopedia-coder
body:
`TlsAcceptor.accept` ended in a broad `catch (e: Exception)` that refiled whatever it caught as `TunnelError.TlsHandshakeFailed`, with no cancellation rethrow ahead of it. On the JVM that clause catches cancellation too — `java.util.concurrent.CancellationException extends java.lang.IllegalStateException` — so every ordinary teardown (service shutdown, scope cancellation, a `withTimeout` expiring, a client going away mid-connect) came back out of `accept` as a domain **failure**, and `TunnelForegroundService.kt:250-257`'s untyped `catch (e: Exception)` filed it through `crashReporter.logCaughtException`. A routine cancelled handshake was landing as a non-fatal crash report — lifecycle noise in exactly the channel #616 / #626 / #630 / #643 spent a week making meaningful.

`Closes #644.`

## Red before, green after

The test is the point of this issue: #643 already added a cancellation test that is **green against unmodified `main`**, because it asserts only "not `UnhandledTlsState`" plus "a `CancellationException` appears somewhere in the `cause` chain" — both already true of the wrapped `TlsHandshakeFailed`. That test is doing a different, real job (it pins the classify-after-write ordering) and is left untouched. The new tests assert the thrown **type**.

Verbatim, `:core:tunnel:jvmTest --tests 'com.rousecontext.tunnel.TlsAcceptCancellationTest'` against `88de3ddf` with **only the test file added**, no production change:

```
TlsAcceptCancellationTest[jvm] > cancellation raised during the handshake propagates as cancellation()[jvm] FAILED
    org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError at TlsAcceptCancellationTest.kt:101
TlsAcceptCancellationTest[jvm] > a withTimeout around accept surfaces the timeout, not a handshake failure()[jvm] FAILED
    org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError at TlsAcceptCancellationTest.kt:76

3 tests completed, 2 failed
```

with, from the JUnit XML:

```
AssertionFailedError: accept must rethrow cancellation, not wrap it -- got
  com.rousecontext.tunnel.TunnelError$TlsHandshakeFailed: TLS handshake failed
AssertionFailedError: the timeout's own cancellation must reach the caller, got
  com.rousecontext.tunnel.TunnelError$TlsHandshakeFailed: TLS handshake failed
```

The third test in the same class — `an ordinary handshake failure is still reported as TlsHandshakeFailed` — was **green in that same run**, before any production change. Both directions, one run: a fix that turned real handshake failures into cancellation would have failed it.

## The second instance of the same defect

`TunnelClientImpl.connect` had the identical shape and is fixed here too. It parks in `opened.await()`; its broad catch turned a scope teardown at that moment into `TunnelError.ConnectionFailed`, which went out through *two* channels — thrown to `TunnelForegroundService.connectToRelay`'s untyped catch (crash-reported) **and** published on `errors`. Red-before, same method (only the `catch (e: CancellationException)` clause removed from the final code):

```
AssertionFailedError: connect must rethrow cancellation, not wrap it -- got
  com.rousecontext.tunnel.TunnelError$ConnectionFailed: Failed to connect: tunnel scope torn down mid-connect
AssertionFailedError: the caller's own cancellation must reach it, got
  com.rousecontext.tunnel.TunnelError$ConnectionFailed: Failed to connect: Timed out waiting for 500 ms
```

The three failure paths out of `connect` now share `abandonConnect`, so the cancellation path **still** closes the inbound queue and moves the state machine to `DISCONNECTED` — neither call suspends, so both are safe in a cancelled coroutine, and leaving the client at `CONNECTING` would strand it. Only the error *report* is dropped, and the test pins both halves. (The extraction also keeps `connect` under detekt's `LongMethod` ceiling.)

### No `docs/ux-decisions.md` entry, and why that is a fact rather than a reading

The `connect` half means a cancelled connect no longer publishes on `errors`, which looks like it could touch `.claude/rules/ux-changes.md`'s *"whether an error is shown at all"*. It does not, and this is determinable rather than a judgement call: **`TunnelClient.errors` has no production collector anywhere in the repo.** Declared at `TunnelClient.kt:19`, emitted at `TunnelClientImpl.kt:200,205`, collected by nothing — no ViewModel, no service, no bridge.

Measured with a positive control, so the empty result is a real read and not a broken search (non-test, `*.kt`, whole repo):

```
CONTROL  incomingSessions  -> 8 references, incl. 2 real collectors
                               (TunnelForegroundService.kt:247, TunnelSessionManager.kt:47)
QUERY    .errors           -> 0
```

An error that is not shown either way cannot have its visibility changed, so that bullet is not engaged and no decision-log entry is included. The crash report at the service boundary is the consequence that actually lands.

The second commit on this branch corrects two kdocs from the first that had asserted the opposite — that the `errors` publication "surfaces to the user". Behaviour is unchanged; only the stated reason is, and the measurement is now recorded in the source so the next reader does not re-derive it from the same wrong starting point.

(Separately: a public `SharedFlow<TunnelError>` with zero collectors is itself a signal that exists and cannot be heard — the same family as everything else in this run. Pre-existing, out of scope here, and being filed separately; deliberately untouched by this PR.)

## Ablation

Each production change reverted independently, full `:core:tunnel:jvmTest` each time:

| ablation | result |
|---|---|
| revert `TlsAcceptor.accept` only | `225 tests completed, 2 failed` — exactly `TlsAcceptCancellationTest`'s two cancellation tests |
| revert `TunnelClientImpl.connect` cancellation clause only | `225 tests completed, 2 failed` — exactly `TunnelClientConnectCancellationTest`'s two |
| neither reverted | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 225 |

In both ablations the ordinary-failure tests stayed green, including `an ordinary handshake failure is still reported as TlsHandshakeFailed` and `TunnelClientImplTest`'s existing `ConnectionFailed` coverage. Nothing else moved in either direction.

### #643's ordering invariant is undisturbed

The classify-after-write ordering (a produced `close_notify` reaches the peer; a cancellation from the transport write wins over classification) is untouched — this change only adds a clause to the outer `catch` in `accept`. Its two pinning tests, verified individually from the JUnit XML on the merge head:

```
PASS handshake wrap reporting CLOSED fails the accept, and not as a defect
PASS cancellation during the handshake write is not reclassified as a defect
```

plus all of `TlsAcceptorWrapStatusTest`, including `cancellation during the underlying write is not reported as a defect`.

## Module sweep

`:core:tunnel` and `:core:bridge` were swept for the same shape — a broad `catch (Exception)` with no cancellation rethrow ahead of it. **Both** spellings were searched: a grep for `catch (e: CancellationException)` alone misses `catch (e: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException)`, which is how the two correct sites in this very file could look absent. This PR normalises all three sites in `TlsAcceptor.kt` to the imported short name so the next sweep finds them with one grep.

**Fixed here** — cancellation escaping as a *thrown* `TunnelError` into the crash-reporting boundary:

- `TlsAcceptor.kt:86` — `accept` → `TlsHandshakeFailed`. #644's subject.
- `TunnelClientImpl.kt:199` — `connect` → `ConnectionFailed`, thrown **and** published on `errors`.

**Found, filed as #646, deliberately not fixed here** — cancellation converted into a *returned result* rather than a thrown error. Same rule violation, different blast radius, and each needs its own decision about what the caller should see:

- `CtLogMonitor.check` (×3) → `SecurityCheckResult.Warning`, a user-visible security warning for a check that was

author: pharanyx-labs
body:
Thirteen syscall handlers had no test that ran them. The argument for reaching twelve of them was already written in `.github/syscall-coverage.yml` three times over; nobody had asked it of the whole list.

**65 → 78 of 91.**

## The structural fact

An `SC_NONE` dispatch row means there *is* no central capability check: the authority depends on which object the caller names, so it is tested inside the handler. The body is therefore reachable from ring 3 by a task holding nothing, and a probe proving the call says no is a probe that ran it.

That argument promoted `SYS_GET_LINE` (2026-08-24), the device family (2026-08-28) and S52's capability trio (2026-08-29), each written into the manifest as *"the same structural reason"*. Twelve of the 26 `uncovered` entries were also `SC_NONE`. `captest` section 13 enters them: 19 checks over twelve handlers.

## The manifest had drifted in its reasons while enforcing itself perfectly on its numbers

Its entries described why each call's **success** path was not reached — no `CAP_UNTYPED` to retype a frame from, no pipeline in the session, login reads its password elsewhere. All true; none about whether the body runs, which is the distinction the file's own header says it exists to preserve. Two were also false:

- `captest` **holds** a `CAP_UNTYPED` and retypes from it in its own section 9.
- `SYS_FRAME_PAGES`' entry said the slot-3 capability was *"refused before the handler body would report anything"* — its row admits every caller.

The four counts those sentences surrounded were gated by `doc-claims` and correct throughout. The reasoning was not gated and was wrong.

## The thirteenth was a gap in the workload, not the kernel

`SYS_FS_INODE_FREE` is gated on `CAP_ENCRYPTED_STORAGE`, which `fs_server` holds and calls on its unlink path — one shell command away from running on every session boot, and nothing had issued it. `session_test.py` now runs `rm`, asserting with `stat` that the name stops resolving rather than trusting `rm`'s own success message.

## What was tried and failed

The first draft probed `SYS_READ` through **fd 0** and hung the gate for the full 40s timeout with no marker. `SYS_GET_LINE` is covered by a refusal and looks identical from the dispatch table — but `h_get_line` tests `CAP_CONSOLE` inside the handler, where `h_read`'s fd 0 branch tests no authority at all and its only early return is `console_hw_owned()`, false in this image. The probe reads fd 3 instead, asserting the retired **[H-3]** ramfs door still answers `SYS_ERR_NOSYS` — a branch nothing had checked since it was shut.

## Where the technique stops

Two `SC_NONE` handlers were deliberately **not** promoted, and stating why is the point — without a boundary the argument is a licence to promote anything.

- `SYS_GET_PASS` blocks; it has no non-blocking branch.
- `SYS_SHLIB_INFO` would enter a body that returns at its first line, because `shlib_active()` is false in every tracked image.

**"The body was entered" stops being coverage when the body is one branch of a feature compiled out.**

## Falsification

`SYSCOV_PROBES_ABSENT=1` compiles section 13 out. `make smoke-syscall-coverage-control` requires the checker to name **exactly** the twelve — failing on more or fewer, not merely on a red gate.

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| `make smoke-syscall-coverage` | `handler entered (measured): 78` = `declared covered: 78` |
| `make smoke-syscall-coverage-control` | `CONTROL PASS: section 13 removed, and the coverage gate names exactly its twelve` |
| `tools/check_base_gate_reddens.sh SYSCOV_PROBES_ABSENT` | RED — its 31st `-D` pair |

Both arms rebuild and reboot all three workloads though the flag changes only `captest`: running one arm leaves the other two transcripts missing, the checker then also names the eight syscalls only the modules session enters, and the gate reddens with the defect contributing nothing. **Without the arm, a promotion the probes earned is indistinguishable from one that was free all along.**

The arm runs as a **step in the existing `syscall-coverage` job**, not a job of its own, so it adds no required context and needs no ruleset sync (**[C-6]**).

## Also

- Syscall 46 (`SYS_REGISTER_STORAGE_BACKEND`), retired because registering a userspace block backend meant the kernel calling ring-3 function pointers from ring 0, is checked to still fail closed for the first time. Its reason had described the mechanism as though it existed.
- `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` §1.8's closing paragraph nominated the pipe family and `SYS_STDIO_INFO` as the two cheap gaps *"worth doing next"* and called the `uncovered` reasons *"hypotheses this manifest has not measured"*. #179 had closed both halves. Both phrasings, and the two false manifest reasons, are now in the `forbidden:` ratchet.

**Invariant preserved:** S25 — which syscalls a test actually exercises is measured, not assumed. That row asserted the property against a stale constant (`not that it is 83`) and now names none.

## Summary

Upgrades zod from 3.25.x to 4.4.3. Required a co-bump of `@hookform/resolvers` (3.x doesn't support zod 4; 5.9.1 does).

zod 4 introduces 3 breaking API renames in `src/schemas/habitSchema.ts`:
- `errorMap: () => ({ message })` → `error: () => string`
- `required_error` + `invalid_type_error` unified into single `error: (issue) => string`

`@hookform/resolvers` 3.x calls into zod 3 directly and doesn't understand zod 4's error shape — `NewHabitWizard` and friends got back empty error objects, so `trigger('name')` on empty input silently passed. Bumping to 5.9.1 (supports `zod ^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`) fixes this.

author: robertblust
body:
Two things the breadcrumb did and the canvas did not.

## Context

`spine` was set on the ancestor chain when the neighbourhood was built, used for geometry, and **dropped before it reached the DOM** — so the path from the root to the focus was drawn like any other ownership line. And the focused node was styled in the *same CSS rule* as `:hover`, so the node you had chosen looked exactly like whichever one your pointer was over.

Three tiers now:

| | |
|---|---|
| where you are | the focus, ringed in `--ink` |
| how you got here | the spine and its ancestors, `--c-mid` |
| everything else | `--c-weak` |

The ring is why the focus is not simply `--c-firm`: **every page square already is**, so filling the focused one with the same colour made it one more square among fifty-eight. A stroke is the one mark nothing else on the canvas wears.

The class is set on the **update**, not the enter. A link keyed `from→to` survives a click, and whether it belongs to the spine depends on where the focus now is — setting it only where a path is created left every survivor wearing the answer to a question asked one focus ago. The check caught this; a hash-loaded page never would, because everything enters at once.

## The divider

360px is right for a folder's card and wrong for a profile claiming 58 skills. The panes are now separated by a handle: **drag**, **double-click** to reset, **arrow keys** when focused. That is the shape every two-pane tool a visitor already uses puts between them — an editor sidebar, a devtools split, a Finder column — and the keyboard is there because a control that can only be dragged cannot be reached without a pointer.

The width is remembered and **clamped on the way back in**, so a number dragged wide on a large monitor cannot swallow the canvas on a laptop. On resize the *stored preference* is re-applied rather than the rendered width, so a pane clamped down on a narrow window comes back when there is room.

The key is a constant in `stage.js`, not the page's — this file is byte-identical on every site that draws a stage and knows none of their names, and `localStorage` is per-origin.

## A bug the check caught

The clamp first subtracted a hard-coded handle width and left the canvas **16px under its floor** — the grid has two gaps and the arithmetic knew about neither. It measures the chrome now:

```
stored 900 on a 900px window → { stage: 774, card: 428, canvas: 320 }  ✓ floor held
widened to 1440              → { stage: 978, card: 632, canvas: 320 }  ✓ preference came back
```

`divider` asserts the floor holds against a stored width of 9000, that a drag widens and is remembered across a reload, that double-click restores the default and clears storage, and that the keyboard works.

## Checks

Both suites pass; `stage.js` and `stage.css` stay byte-identical across the two sites.

author: tmchow
body: ## Intent Printed CLIs were failing ordinary sequential commands with exit 5 / `rate limited: endpoint class … exhausted after N attempts` after a small number of retries, instead of waiting for the politeness budget to refill. Sniffed prints also emitted `--rate-limit` default `2` (and some prints `0`) while `client.RateLimitAuto` is `-1`. Closes #3959 ## Approach Two generator sites, confirmed on current main: 1. After the existing server-driven 429 / Retry-After retry policy is exhausted (`maxRetries > 0`), safe-to-replay requests now block until the local politeness budget refills, bounded by the command context / `--timeout`. Unsafe writes, RetryBudget exhaustion, and harness fail-fast (`clientMaxRetries() == 0` under verify/dogfood) still return `RateLimitedError`. Short `--timeout` fails with `timed out waiting … for rate-limit budget to refill`, not a hang and not a generic rate-limit exhaustion error. 2. The emitted `--rate-limit` default is `client.RateLimitAuto` unless the spec sets `default_rate_limit` / `x-pp-default-rate-limit`. Sniffed vs documented specs are one rule. Server-driven 429 / Retry-After calculation, max retries, and RetryBudget are unchanged. ## Scope Primary area: generator templates (`client.go.tmpl`, `root.go.tmpl`) and the matching generated-output contract. Why this belongs in this repo: every future printed CLI inherits the limiter failure mode and the contradictory `--rate-limit` default. ## Risk Generated `internal/client/client.go` and `internal/cli/root.go` change on next print. 429 retry counts, Retry-After parsing, mutation no-replay, and verify/dogfood fail-fast are unchanged. author: danieljhkim
body:
## Task

DANI-10094 — Remove speculative store metadata fields: --scope, --owner, --task-id

### Description

## Problem

`monodev checkout -n` and `monodev store update` accept `--scope global|component`, `--description`, `--owner`, and `--task-id`. Of these, only `--description` earns its place. `--owner` and `--task-id` are speculative enterprise/integration metadata that nobody fills in on a single-user local tool and that nothing in the codebase reads to make a decision. `--scope` is worse than unused: it forces a taxonomy decision on the user at store-creation time, before they have any idea what the distinction will mean for them.

## Why It Matters

Every flag on the creation path is a decision the user must make on day one, and creation is the moment where abandonment is most likely. Reducing `checkout -n` to a name plus an optional description makes the first-run experience one obvious step. Unused fields also carry ongoing cost: they appear in `store describe` output, in the persisted schema, in the remote persistence manifest, and in every test that constructs a store.

## Scope

- Drop `--owner` and `--task-id` from the CLI surface entirely.
- Drop `--scope` from the CLI surface. Determine from `internal/engine/scope_test.go` and the scoped-store code whether scope currently drives any behavior; if it does, document what is lost and either keep the behavior under an internal default or file a follow-up before removing.
- Keep `--description`.
- Remove the corresponding fields from the persisted store schema, or retain them as ignored-on-read for backward compatibility with already-written store files — pick one and state the choice in the schema code. Existing local stores must not become unreadable.
- Update `store describe`, `store ls`, and JSON output to stop emitting the removed fields.

## Constraints / Notes

- Pre-1.0, per CHANGELOG: "Backward compatibility is not guaranteed prior to 1.0." Breaking the flag surface is acceptable; silently corrupting or refusing to read an existing store on disk is not.
- A removed flag should produce a clear error naming the removal, not a generic cobra "unknown flag" message, for at least one release.

### Acceptance Criteria

- `monodev checkout -n foo --owner bar` exits non-zero with an error that names the flag as removed rather than a bare unknown-flag message.
- `monodev checkout -n foo --description 'x'` still works and the description appears in `monodev store describe foo`.
- A store file written by the current release before this change is still readable by the new binary, covered by a testdata fixture loaded in a test.
- `monodev store describe --json` output contains no owner, taskId, or scope keys.
- `make lint`, `make test`, and `make test-integration` pass.

## Execution Summary

<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

Outcome: success
Changes:
- Dropped `--owner`, `--task-id`, and `--scope` from `checkout -n`, `store update`, `store ls`, and `store rm`. Root `FlagErrorFunc` rewrites cobra unknown-flag errors to `flag --X has been removed` for one release.
- Kept `--description` on create and update.
- Removed persisted `StoreMeta` fields `owner`, `taskId`, and `scope`. Choice (stated in `schema.go`): drop from the struct; `encoding/json` ignores unknown keys, so existing `meta.json` files stay readable and extra keys are omitted on the next write. Fixture `internal/stores/testdata/legacy_meta.json` is loaded through `FileStoreRepo.LoadMeta`.
- `store describe` and `store ls` (text and JSON) no longer emit owner, taskId, or scope. Location scope remains an internal routing field (`json:"-"`).
- Scope still drives store location internally via `defaultScope()` (component after `monodev init`, else global). Ambiguous IDs now prefer component instead of requiring `--scope`.
- Lost CLI ability: forcing a global store after `monodev init`. Documented in CHANGELOG and `docs/worktrees.md`.
- `NewStoreMeta` is now `NewStoreMeta(name, createdAt)`; callers updated to compile.
- Extra: `migrateWorkspaceRecord` now copies Repo/WorkspacePath/AbsolutePath onto the in-memory workspace so the existing engine identity test matches the persisted migrate.
Assessment: Acceptance criteria covered by unit tests (removed-flag error, description round-trip, describe JSON keys, legacy fixture load). `make test` and `make test-integration` passed. System `make lint` cannot load the Go 1.27 config with homebrew golangci-lint 2.12.2 (built with go1.26); re-ran with CI-pinned golangci-lint v2.13.1 (go1.27): 0 issues.
Strategic decisions: ignore-on-read by removing fields rather than keeping dead json tags; keep location routing under the existing default rather than filing a follow-up before dropping `--scope`.
Design weaknesses / risks:
- Severity: medium. After `monodev init`, there is no CLI way to create a global shared store.
- Mitigation: documented; creating the store before init still lands in `~/.monodev/stores/`.

</details>

## Validation

- Not reported

## Branch Freshness

- Base ref: `origin/main`
- Head ref: `orbit/DANI-10094-6a93c344`
- Behind base: 0
- Ahead of base: 1

author: bogdaniel
body:
A **read-only** evidence-retention audit, the bounded issue it produced ([#241](https://github.com/zenchron-dynamics/zenchron-foundry/issues/241)), and the machine-readable 535→723 reconciliation.

Nothing was rebuilt, no SBOM regenerated, no workflow dispatched, no artifact created or deleted, no retention setting changed. The only GitHub calls were `GET`.

## The headline finding

**The 40 SBOM documents for `7061caaf` were never stored, and their absence is not an expiry.** At that revision `stage-and-authorize.yml` had no SBOM step at all — the only occurrence of the word is `sbom: false` — and the step was added eight days later by `5275c1f` (#236). The documents were produced by a local buildless audit lane on 2026-08-27, 86 MB, gitignored, discarded with the lane.

**The accepted run's artifacts are still live.** 41 of 42, expiring 2026-11-18. Both the authorization record and all twenty child artifacts were downloaded during this audit; they contain no `sbom/` directory and no SPDX or CycloneDX document, exactly as `sbom: false` implies.

This corrects the repository's own audit record, which states that record "was a 30-day workflow artifact and has expired". It is a 90-day artifact and it has not expired. Nobody had queried the retention API before asserting the expiry — the same failure mode the audit is about.

## The seven questions

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| where stored | nowhere; never a workflow output at that revision |
| configured retention | **90 days** (repo max 90), `retention-days` unset on every evidence upload; policy requires **2555** + immutable |
| why unavailable | never retained — not expiry |
| checksums / producer / subjects | **fully preserved**; only the bytes are gone |
| do future runs store SBOM bytes durably | bytes yes, durably **no** — a 90-day artifact; `generate-evidence-bundle.sh` is invoked by no workflow |
| can authorization complete with retention < governance period | **yes** — nothing checks |
| is expiry detected | **no** — nothing queries `expires_at` for artifacts |

**No durable, tested retention contract exists**, so one bounded issue was filed rather than a contract invented here. The historical loss cannot be repaired retroactively and **reopening #120 is not appropriate**.

## The reconciliation

Every finding now **carries** its obligation class and, where it is about one component, that component — rather than having them regexed back out of diagnostic prose.

| obligation class | findings |
|---|---|
| `licence-determination` | 470 |
| `corresponding-source` | 162 |
| `licence-review` | 65 |
| `copyright-notice` | 24 |
| `file-component-disposition` | 1 *(project-scoped)* |
| `publication-authority` | 1 *(project-scoped)* |
| **total** | **723** |

535 implicated components · 721 component-scoped findings · 0 orphaned · 2 project-scoped. Total in **both** directions or the producer refuses. Two sabotages: an orphaned finding and a duplicated component.

Currently all 535 carry findings, so the zero-finding disposition path is exercised only by fixtures — the record says so rather than implying coverage from silence.

---

## Security-sensitive change checklist

**blast-radius** — the notice producer gains a reconciliation step and two refusal codes; `policies/repository-material.yaml` gains four audit paths. If the reconciliation is wrong the producer refuses with `NB-RECONCILIATION-*` and no candidate passes; it cannot fail open, because the mapping is asserted total in both directions before the verdict is computed.

**fail-direction** — both new codes fail CLOSED and both paths were executed: a finding naming a component outside the implicated set refuses as an orphan, and a component listed twice refuses rather than reconciling. The audit itself changes no control, so it has no fail direction to get wrong.

**not-vacuous** — the reconciliation is proved against the real 535/723 measurement, not a fixture, and the two sabotages are shown to refuse. The audit's central claim was verified by *downloading the artifacts said to be expired* and finding them live — which is what turned a repeated assumption into a corrected fact.

**control-plane** — none required by this PR. #241 will need one (durable storage outside GitHub artifacts), and that is why it is an issue rather than a change here.

**reversibility** — `git revert` restores the previous behaviour. The audit records are inert documents; the producer change adds an emitted artifact and two codes and removes nothing.

**external-review** — no. Read-only measurement plus a reconciliation. It reaches no legal conclusion, changes no policy decision, and grants nothing. It does report that a governance control is unimplemented, which is filed as #241 rather than asserted as compliant.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [ghcr.io/alam00000/bentopdf-simple](https://redirect.github.com/alam00000/bentopdf) | patch | `2.8.7` → `2.8.8` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>alam00000/bentopdf (ghcr.io/alam00000/bentopdf-simple)</summary>

### [`v2.8.8`](https://redirect.github.com/alam00000/bentopdf/releases/tag/v2.8.8): Text Editing In BentoPDF! and many more - v2.8.8

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/alam00000/bentopdf/compare/v2.8.7...v2.8.8)

#### Dad Joke Of the Release

What do you call a bee that can't make up its mind? A maybe 🤣

### The Biggest Release of BentoPDF yet!

**This is the biggest release of BentoPDF**. BentoPDF can now edit text, image, shapes in BentoPDF and there are two new engines **Kura** and **Hyper Compress**. Detailed Explanation is below.

#### PDF Text Editing

BentoPDF can now edit the actual text inside a PDF.  You can click any paragraph and type. Text reflows live, fonts and styling are preserved, and everything runs entirely in your browser, as always.

- **Edit in place** with live reflow, real font matching, and word wrap that follows the original layout
- **Full styling**: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript, subscript, font family and size, text colour, outline colour and width, character and line spacing
- **Paragraph control**: left / centre / right / justify alignment, bulleted and numbered lists with indent levels, and left-to-right and right-to-left text
- **Find & replace** across the document, plus **spell-check** with a personal dictionary and per-language switching
- **Images**: add, replace in place, or export a PNG, edit it in any app, and have your saved changes re import automatically
- **Objects**: align, distribute, rotate, flip, duplicate, and reorder front to back. Even commercial software like Apryse and Nutrient do not support this
- **Accessibility**: alt text for tagged PDFs, and reading-order text export
- Undo / redo, document properties, page navigation, zoom presets

This was arguably the hardest feature I had built so far. Given the complex nature of PDFs and the different ways it can be produced, you might encounter certain bugs.

##### Note

Local fonts access is only available on chromium based browsers such as Chrome and Edge. Other browsers have a limitation of not having the font access API.

### Hyper Compress is the best open source PDF compression engine

[hyper.bentopdf.com](https://hyper.bentopdf.com) · [github.com/alam00000/bentopdf-hyper-compress](https://redirect.github.com/alam00000/bentopdf-hyper-compress)

Hyper is a High fidelity, content preserving PDF compressor that preserves PDF conformance.

- **Monotonic**: Hyper never returns a larger file. If compression does not save space, you get the original back untouched. This makes it useful for workflows so you can have a predicctable output.
- **True lossless mode**, with no quality loss
- **Verified output**: transformations that can affect visual fidelity are checked and rolled back when a page cannot be reproduced faithfully. **0.39% corruption rate, the lowest of any engine measured**
- **Benchmarked** against Ghostscript, MuPDF and qpdf across 2,104 real-world PDFs and 27,352 engine runs, with fidelity measured by an independent renderer:

| Tier     | Hyper                  | Ghostscript   | MuPDF         | qpdf         |
| -------- | ---------------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------ |
| Lossless | **22.4% @​ SSIM 1.000** | 21.1% @​ 0.997 | 4.7% @​ 1.000  | 6.3% @​ 1.000 |
| 300 dpi  | **52.3% @​ 1.000**      | 19.1% @​ 0.996 | 14.0% @​ 1.000 | n/a          |
| 150 dpi  | **58.2% @​ 0.999**      | 42.4% @​ 0.994 | 19.4% @​ 1.000 | n/a          |
| 72 dpi   | **64.8% @​ 0.996**      | 53.9% @​ 0.990 | 28.0% @​ 0.999 | n/a          |

- Ships as a CLI, Node SDK, C API, self-hosted service, and a WebAssembly build for the browser

#### Kura is a PDF standards and preflight engine

[kura.bentopdf.com](https://kura.bentopdf.com) · [github.com/alam00000/bentopdf-kura](https://redirect.github.com/alam00000/bentopdf-kura)

Kura turns everyday PDFs into archival, print and accessible ones, from a single engine.

- **Supports every standard**: all 11 PDF/A levels, PDF/UA-1 and UA-2, PDF/X-1a through X-6, PDF/E-1 and PDF/VT, plus Factur-X, ZUGFeRD, XRechnung and Order-X e-invoices
- **Print preflight built in**: 396 bundled profiles covering hairlines, rich black, image resolution, overprint, transparency, page boxes, fonts and colour, with repairs where a repair exists, and your own profiles in JSON or the XML dialect you already use
- **Validates clean**: 0 red on the veraPDF corpus, Isartor 204/204, BFO 34/34, Ghent Output Suite 5.0 69/69, PDF/UA Reference Suite 10/10, Cal Poly PDF/VT 24/24
- **Proven on real files**: 30,677 real-world PDFs converted, **zero crashes**, zero timeouts, 0.05 s median
- Also Ships as a CLI, C library, npm package, Docker image, and a WebAssembly build that runs entirely in the browser

##### Note

Both Kura and Hyper are not yet integrated into BentoPDF. I need to do some further tests and optimizations after which they will be ready to be integrated. However they are stable and you can try them out

author: netecazo
body:
## Why

`npm audit` goes from **21 high severity advisories to zero**.

The 14.2 line could not fix them. Their vulnerable range ran to `16.3.0-preview.10`, so the patch only exists in 16.x — which is why `npm audit fix` kept proposing a breaking major. That is the entire reason for this upgrade.

## Breaking changes handled

**Async request APIs.** `cookies()` returns a promise in Next 15+, so `supabaseServer()` becomes `async` and its **20 call sites** now await it.

**Async route params.** `params` is a promise for dynamic segments, destructured at the top of each handler in the four affected routes: the automation detail page, the inbound webhook, the automation `PATCH`/`DELETE` pair, and the approvals endpoint.

**`next lint` was removed** in Next 16; the lint script now calls `eslint` directly.

**`tsconfig.json` was rewritten by Next's own build** — `jsx: preserve` → `react-jsx`, `.next/dev/types` added to `include`, and the JSON reformatted with expanded arrays. That is Next's automatic config migration, not a hand edit. It makes the diff look bigger than it is.

## Verification

Beyond the build, I started the production server and exercised every route:

| Route | Result |
|---|---|
| `/`, `/about`, `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/security`, `/login` | 200 |
| `/dashboard` | 307 → login, so the auth middleware still gates correctly |
| Server log | clean, no errors |

Content spot-checks held: the homepage still carries the corrected copy ("real results coming soon", "Slack connects today"), and Terms still carry Florida governing law. `tsc --noEmit` clean. 11/11 crypto tests pass. `npm audit`: **0 vulnerabilities**.

## Before merging

This is a framework major on a live site, which is why it is a branch rather than a push to `main`.

Since the Vercel project is not linked to GitHub, there is no automatic preview for this branch. To get one, run `npx vercel` (without `--prod`) from a checkout of `next-16` and click through the preview URL before merging.

Also note, unrelated to this branch but required before the next production deploy: `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `CRON_SECRET` must be set in Vercel, or Slack connections throw and the scheduler returns 503. Both fail closed by design.

author: nos-tromo
body:
Play a job's original recording inside the app, and seek to it from any timestamped row.

## Backend — a capability URL

`GET /jobs/{id}/media` authorizes with a per-job token in the URL rather than the request principal, because a `<video>`/`<audio>` element cannot attach the trusted identity header. The token is minted at job creation, handed out only on the owner-scoped snapshot, kept off the job listing, compared with `compare_digest`, and revoked when the job is deleted. Every failure is a `404` — never `403` — so a wrong token cannot probe which jobs exist.

`FileResponse` answers `Range` with `206`, which is what lets the player seek without refetching, and the nginx location passes the header through.

Consequence worth naming: an upload now has to outlive the pipeline that consumed it. That is load-bearing rather than incidental, and `docs/architecture.md` says so.

## Frontend — the player

- A slide-in `MediaPanel` over `<video>`/`<audio>`, mounted once in the `Shell` and driven by a small zustand store, so any row can open or seek it.
- `TimeCell` makes each timestamp in the transcript and the visual-context tabs a seek control.
- The media URL resolves against the SPA sub-path, so it works under `/nextext/`.

## Icons over text

The last commit swaps the three text controls in the job row for the icons `@infra/ui` v0.17.0 exports (nos-tromo/infra-ui#54): `PlayButton` opens the player, `DisclosureButton` shows/hides results — which also gives that toggle the `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` wiring the plain button never had — and `StatusIcon` replaces the status word. No i18n change: every label moves from visible text to the marker's accessible name and tooltip, so screen readers and hover still get the wording, and the row stops reflowing as translated words change length.

## Notes

- Releases **v1.7.0** — the tag is minted on merge.
- `make verify` and `make test` both green; 218 frontend tests, plus new backend coverage in `tests/test_api/test_media.py` and an nginx-config test.

author: huyplb
body:
Handlers now take Fastify's own `FastifyRequest` / `FastifyReply`. The wrapper in between them and the framework is gone.

## Why

It was scaffolding from removing Express: an interface of our own, plus an adapter object translating Fastify to it, so ~80 handlers could keep their Express-shaped signatures instead of being rewritten in the same change. That was the right call then. With Express gone it only costs:

- Roughly 80% of it was pure renaming — Fastify already has `status()`, `statusCode`, `redirect()`, `removeHeader()`.
- Anything it did not expose had to be punched through it. That is how streamed responses came to drop every header, security headers included.
- It had started leaking: `respond.ts` had grown a `FastifyLikeReply` beside it.

## What is left

The two things Fastify genuinely does not do for us, in the new `platform/http/reply.ts`: cookies, and taking over the socket for a stream (`hijack` + flushing the headers Fastify has collected, which is what keeps the security headers on an NDJSON response).

`fastify-bind.ts` goes from 193 lines to 58.

## Also removed while in here

- **`api/security-headers.ts`** — a middleware wrapper over the header policy with no callers; the server applies the policy from an `onRequest` hook. Its test was asserting against a hand-rolled response fake shaped like nothing that ships, so the header cases move to the policy itself and the hook gets a live assertion in `http-contract.test.ts`.
- **One of two identical declarations of the auth fields.** `AuthedRequest` is now declared once, in the platform layer, so `rate-limit.ts` can read `userId` without casting for it and without importing from a feature.

## A bug this caught

Cookie behaviour is now tested over a real reply rather than by calling the serializer directly. That immediately caught a bug the refactor introduced: Fastify's `header()` already accumulates `set-cookie` rather than replacing it, so the manual accumulation carried over from the Express-era helper sent every cookie twice over. The SSO callback sets two cookies on one response, so this would have shipped.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `npx vitest run` — 2940 passed, 0 failed
- `npx eslint .` — 0 errors
- `npm run build -w @foxschema/web` succeeds
- `api/http-contract.test.ts` (80 routes against a real listener) is the regression net for the transport swap and stays green
- The two new assertions were A/B'd against a deliberately broken implementation to confirm they fail when they should

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches every API handler, session/SSO cookies, streaming migrations, and idempotency—behavior should be equivalent but regressions would affect auth and write paths broadly.
> 
> **Overview**
> Removes the Express-era **HttpRequest/HttpResponse** adapter so routes and guards use **`AppRequest`** (typed `FastifyRequest`) and **`FastifyReply`** directly. **`fastify-bind`** no longer wraps requests/replies; handlers call **`send`**, **`header`**, and **`status`** on Fastify’s API. Shared behavior that Fastify does not cover moves into **`platform/http/reply`**: **`setCookie`/`clearCookie`**, **`headerOf`/`pathOf`**, and **`streamWrite`/`streamEnd`** (hijack + flush headers so NDJSON streams keep security headers).
> 
> The unused **`api/security-headers`** middleware is deleted; the Fastify **`onRequest`** hook still applies **`securityHeadersFor(pathOf(req))`**. Policy tests live in **`security-headers-core.test.ts`**, with a new live check in **`http-contract.test.ts`**. **`AuthedRequest`** is defined once in **`platform/http/types`** for guards like rate limiting. Idempotency and error helpers are updated to hook **`res.send`** and **`res.raw`** lifecycle events. Cookie tests now run against a real reply (catching duplicate **`Set-Cookie`** accumulation).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f9d2b36eb39427f485b7f8fa43e12c1be573dad0. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: caspernieuwenhuizen
body:
Closes #3105

Re-cut of #3188 onto current `main`. Same two commits, conflicts resolved
against the five leak fixes that have since landed. **Based on `main`, not
stacked.**

Slice 2 of 5 for #3017. Eight Pro features gain a gate and leave
`config/license_gate_pending.php`: `match_analysis`, `match_prep`,
`match_execution`, `tournaments`, `tournaments_auto_balance`, `training`,
`exercises`, `media`. The pending list drops from 28 entries to 20.

## The four conflicts, and how they were resolved

All four are this slice's plan gate meeting my own #3151 scoping fix in the
same methods. **Both belong, in that order: permission first, then
entitlement.** That is the order the rest of this epic already uses, and it
matters — someone who does not coach the team should get the permission
answer, not an upgrade pitch for a plan that would not let them in either.

**`MatchPrepRestController`** — the two `prep_id`-keyed role routes. `main`
has `permission_callback => can_edit_role` (#3151's scope check, which
resolves the activity behind the prep); the pick has
`callback => self::gate( … )` (the plan gate). Kept both: the permission
callback runs first and answers `403`, the plan gate runs inside the callback
and answers `402`. Neither was dropped for the other.

**`FrontendMatchPrepView::render()`** — `main` has #3151's
`ActivityTeamScope::coversTeam()` refusal, which **returns**; the pick sets
`$plan_locked`. The scope refusal stays first and the plan flag follows it, so
an out-of-scope coach never reaches the upgrade panel. Commented in place so
the ordering is not re-derived by the next reader.

**`docs/match-execution.md`** + **`docs/nl_NL/`** — `main` has #3151's
"the match must belong to a team you coach … refused (`403`)" paragraph; the
pick appends an "On your plan" section. Both kept, plus one linking sentence
noting that a plan refusal is a different answer carrying `402`. That is
`license-and-account.md`'s "not on your plan ≠ not allowed" distinction said
where a reader of the REST list will hit it.

## Everything else is unchanged from #3188

The shape: each controller carries one private `gate()` wrapper over slice
1's `LicenseGate::enforceWriteRest()`, applied to **every** route rather than
only the mutating ones — the helper decides from the verb, so wrapping a
`GET` is a no-op, and "wrap everything" is a rule a reviewer checks by
looking.

Two deliberate exceptions:

- **`tournaments_auto_balance`** uses `enforceFeatureRest()` on the auto-plan
  route alone. No auto-balance record to keep readable, only an action; the
  tournament around it stays on Standard. The button renders disabled in
  place with `UpgradePanel::lockedTitle()`.
- **`media`** gates the two upload routes and nothing else. `DELETE` and the
  retention decisions are how a club removes a child's photo; refusing those
  over a billing state turns a plan question into a data-protection one.

Surfaces render locked, never hidden. Where the feature has stored records
the read stays with the panel above it; where it has none to keep (the live
console, a training run, a CSV import) it locks whole.

`FeatureMapGateCoverageTest::isGated()` learns slice 1's two enforcement
helpers and matches up to the feature literal rather than a closing paren —
without that a properly gated feature reads as ungated, which is the failure
mode that teaches people to edit the pending list instead of the code.
`LicenseRefusalShapeTest::test_this_slice_gates_nothing` is retired: correct
while slice 1 landed alone, wrong the moment slice 2 gates `match_analysis`.

## Verified on this re-cut

- `check-docs`, `check-changelog-snippets`, `check-module-toggles`,
  `check-mobile-classes`, `check-po-duplicates` all pass.
- `php -l` clean on every changed file; PHPStan clean across the touched
  modules.
- The `.po` diff against `main` is **4 lines** — the single `Edit tournament`
  entry with its Dutch, nothing relocated by `i18n-sync` duplicated.
- All eight features gated, no stale pending entries, pending list at 20.

Supersedes #3188.

## Wizard plan

Exemption — (a): not a record-creation flow.

- The nav button container switches from a fixed `space-x-2` row to `flex flex-wrap gap-2`, so the buttons themselves can also wrap onto their own line(s) rather than overflowing horizontally.

This is additive to PR #16's earlier header work (wordmark sizing at the mobile breakpoint, consistent button sizing) — that made the individual pieces smaller and more uniform, this makes the row itself resilient when they still don't all fit on one line (e.g. the admin nav case with two extra pill buttons).

author: maifeeulasad
body:
Closes #28.

## What was wrong

`handleExport` read from `visibleRows`, populated with the most recent page response. So **"Export CSV" on page 3 of a 500-row table wrote ten rows** — under a menu label implying the whole dataset. Silent, plausible-looking, wrong output.

`exportAllData` already existed in `utils/exportData.ts` and was exported from the barrel. It was never wired to the UI.

## The fix

Export now goes through the data source's `listAll`, **reusing the filters and sort from the last request** so it exports what the user is actually looking at, minus the pagination.

`listAll` is optional on `CrudDataSource` — a source over an unbounded remote collection has no safe way to honour it — so the menu degrades to the visible page rather than failing.

## The labels changed, deliberately

```
Export CSV          →   Export all as CSV
                        Export page as CSV   (when all is unavailable)
```

The old wording is exactly what made the bug invisible. The menu now states which it will do.

`exportScope: 'page'` opts out explicitly where fetching everything would be expensive.

## Also

- A failed export reports through `onError` and a toast instead of writing an empty file
- Menu entries disable while an export is in flight

## Tests

Five new cases: full-set export calls `listAll`; labels match the effective scope; a source without `listAll` degrades to page scope and says so; `exportScope: 'page'` is honoured even when `listAll` exists; a failing `listAll` surfaces an error rather than an empty file.

## Verification

```
pnpm lint    0 problems
pnpm test    232 passed  (was 227)
coverage     passes at the raised thresholds
```

author: ihudak
body:
The remaining class from **F31's addendum**. It was already proven by measurement — it did not need a recurrence.

## The defect

F31's addendum injected four kinds of damage into an **unmutated** tree. Each scored `KILLED | exit+failline` — the tier reporting kills with **no mutation present at all**.

A false KILL inflates the coverage claim exactly as a false green does, and unlike a survivor it is **owed no ledger entry**, so nothing downstream ever questions it.

## The guard

`falsify_verdict` now probes the scratch at the moment a kill is about to be recorded, and scores `UNPROVEN | …+artefact` when it cannot hold a file — a natural fourth channel beside `timeout`, `scaffold` and `signal`.

**It writes a token and reads it back**, because the two filesystem shapes fail differently and only one is visible to an existence check:

| | ENOSPC shape |
|---|---|
| HFS+ | fails at `open()` → artefact **absent** |
| **APFS** | `cat > f` succeeds → artefact **exists and is empty** (17 of 30 measured) |

The field report matches the second, and `[[ -e ]]`/`[[ -r ]]` are both true for it — which is why F31's first guard never fired. `df` is deliberately not used: APFS reported ~1.8 MB free while writes were already coming back empty.

Sampled on the **KILLED path only**, for the addendum's own reasons: an end-of-run probe passes because the scratch removal frees the exhausted space two lines earlier (6 of 16 measured), and a SURVIVED verdict observed nothing failing, so there is nothing to misattribute.

## Demonstrated failing, and the APFS shape reproduced on Linux

`tests/test-falsify-artefact-guard.sh` uses **`/dev/full`** — a write that returns ENOSPC and reads back empty. That is the APFS shape exactly, with no root, no loopback mount and nothing left behind. The test asserts that premise before relying on it.

Against the previous `run.sh` the broken-scratch case scores **`KILLED|exit+failline`** — the addendum's exact signature.

## Guarded against overreach

A verdict guard that fires too widely is worse than the defect, so the test also pins:

- a **healthy** scratch still scores `KILLED`
- a `SURVIVED` verdict is **untouched** by a broken scratch
- `FR_SCRATCH` **unset** behaves exactly as before — every existing hermetic caller
- the probe **leaves no file behind** (it runs once per kill, hundreds of times per corpus run)

## Measured unchanged where it must be

Whole corpus after the change: **548 mutants, 538 KILLED, 10 SURVIVED, 0 UNPROVEN**, ledger clean, 0 problems — identical to before. The guard adds no false unprovens on a healthy machine.

Hermetic suite **75/75**; shellcheck and dialect lint clean.

## Not yet validated on APFS — F31 stays open

The mechanism was observed on macOS; `/dev/full` is a Linux stand-in for it. A macOS run is needed to confirm the probe sees the real thing, and F31 is deliberately left open until then.

author: prestomation
body: ## What changed Home Keeper used **mirror** for three different things, and the vocabulary had already drifted half-way to "sync" on its own: | Concept | Called in code | Called in the UI | |---|---|---| | Profile-filtered tasks pushed to an external `todo.*` list | `task_mirror.py` / `task_mirror_sync.py` | "Sync to a to-do list", "Two-way sync" | | Auto-buy reminders pushed to a shopping list | `shopping.py` / `shopping_sync.py` | "Shopping list" | | `device_class: problem` sensors turned into tasks | `problem_tasks.py` / `problem_sync.py` | "Problem sensor sync" | So the panel said *"Sync to a to-do list"* over i18n keys named `mirror.*`, the profile field was literally `sync`, the CSS was `.hk-sync-group`, the docs-site slug was already `todo-sync` — while the Python underneath was `TaskMirrorSync`. Meanwhile `settings.sync_off` (problem sensors) read *"Problem sensors are not mirrored"*: the two features had swapped each other's word. **Sync** is now the single word for "kept in step with something outside Home Keeper", on every surface and in all sixteen languages. ### The feature rename - `task_mirror.py` / `task_mirror_sync.py` → **`todo_list.py` / `todo_list_sync.py`**, preserving the repo's `NAME.py` (pure planner) / `NAME_sync.py` (HA-aware driver) convention. A literal `mirror`→`sync` swap would have produced `task_sync_sync.py` and `class TaskSyncSync`, because `_sync` already means "the driver half". - `TaskMirrorSync` → `TodoListSync` (beside `ShoppingListSync`, `ProblemSensorSync`); `TaskMirrorPlan` → `TodoListPlan`; `mirror_key` → `sync_key`; `desired_by_mirror` → `desired_by_sync`. The record a plan is built from *is* a profile, so `mirrors`/`mirror` became `synced`/`profile` rather than colliding with the `sync` block a profile already carries. - `ORIGIN_TODO_MIRROR` → `ORIGIN_TODO_SYNC`, value `home_keeper_todo_sync`. - Storage key `task_mirror_items` → `todo_list_items`, **no migration**. The feature shipped in 0.18.0, and an emptied bookkeeping self-heals without duplicating: `plan_sync`'s phase 2 looks for an open line with the same summary and adopts it instead of adding a second one — a path that exists precisely for bookkeeping that was lost. - i18n namespace `mirror.*` → `todo_sync.*` across all 16 locales, including the string-concatenated `t('todo_sync.' + s.name)` lookup in `panel.ts` that builds three field labels and that a key-by-key grep would have missed. ### User-visible prose Every string that said "mirror" now says "sync" — for the to-do list sync, the shopping list and problem sensors alike — in `services.yaml`, `strings.json`, `translations/*.json` and the frontend locales, English **and** the fifteen translations (each using its own language's sync verb rather than its mirror verb). ### Left alone on purpose Ordinary English "mirrors"/"mirroring" in internal comments about unrelated things (`limits.ts` mirrors `const.py`, the Settings tab mirrors the options flow), the shipped CHANGELOG sections, `docs/*_PLAN.md` scratch docs, and the two historical DOM ids `#hk-task-mirrors` / `#hk-mirror-add` that a test asserts are *absent* — renaming those would stop the guard guarding anything. `ha-integration-template` needs no changes: all ten of its "mirror" hits are ordinary English in comments. ## Screenshots The Settings tab, with the reworded copy on all three cards: A profile's **Sync to a to-do list** group — the three field labels here come from the concatenated `todo_sync.*` lookup, so this shot is what proves that rename landed: The synced chores on the household's own list, proving the renamed storage key and origin marker work end to end: Settings on a narrow screen: ## Verification Run locally, all green: | Tier | Result | |---|---| | `pytest tests/unit` | 1533 passed | | `npx vitest run` | 758 passed (26 files) — incl. i18n parity + untranslated-leak guard | | `bash ci/e2e-up.sh` (Playwright) | 196 passed | | `bash ci/test-python-integration.sh` (Docker) | 167 passed | | `bash ci/test-mutation-python.sh` | **98.97%** (574/580), threshold 80% | | `bash ci/test-mutation-frontend.sh` | no mutable TypeScript changed | | `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` | clean | | `vale` | 0 hits on lines this PR changes (40 pre-existing, all on untouched lines) | | `ci/check-changelog-release-gap.py` | clean | `mypy` could not run here — Home Assistant won't `pip install` in this sandbox (a native wheel fails to build). `mypy --follow-imports=skip` over the two renamed modules is clean; CI runs the real check. The Docker tier is the meaningful one for the persisted rename: `test_todo_list_sync.py` exercises the renamed `todo_list_items` key and `origin: home_keeper_todo_sync` against a real HA container. ## Checklist - [x] Tests run locally (`pytest tests/unit -v`, `bash ci/test-frontend.sh`) - [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated — no issue references, so no `(Fixes #N)` - [x] Panel UI changed → current screenshots committed under `docs/images/` and embedded above with an HTML img tag - [ ] New user-facing UI surface → n/a, no new surface; the tour needs no new step - [x] Version bumped to `0.19.0b5` (`manifest.json` + `const.py`) — required because `v0.19.0b4` is already tagged. No `preview-release` label: terminology change, not a new feature.

author: wukong2468
body:
Introduce a binary on-disk cache that persists parsed translation results, so consecutive launches skip re-parsing large translation files.

- Add TranslationCache with a custom binary format (magic header, version, SHA256 checksum, signature, length-prefixed UTF-8 strings) for faster read/write than JSON.
- Cache is keyed by a signature computed from translation file path, size and last-modified time; any change invalidates the cache and triggers a full re-parse.
- Cache files live under BepInEx\cache\JustAnotherTranslator and are distinguished per loader.
- Validate integrity: magic, version, signature and payload checksum are verified on load; corrupted/outdated caches automatically rebuild.
- Wire the cache into AsyncTranslationLoader.LoadFilesThreadFunc, skipping parsing on a cache hit and persisting the cache after a successful parse.
- Add per-path timing logs (cache load vs direct parse) in milliseconds for developer benchmarking.

Performance: Publish Precision Participant-Cap vs CPU Budget Table

author: ali0600
body:
Docs only. M28 will make fights hold more than one foe; this is the research pass that has to land first, per the rule at the top of `GENRE_CONVENTIONS.md` — if a surface's section is thin, thicken it *before* building, because the research is the deliverable.

## What it found

**"Fights are solo" was never a convention we were honouring.** Dragon Quest I is the only reference that fights one at a time. Every other game in the set — FF1, DQ2, Chrono Trigger, EarthBound, Super Mario RPG — fields authored formations. So this milestone retires a scope line rather than abandoning a divergence, and the M13 entry that recorded "encounters are visible, presses are timed, and the fight was solo" now says which two of those three survive.

**The best find pays for the last milestone.** FF1's infamous "Ineffective" — aiming at an enemy that died earlier in the round and wasting the turn, the game's most complained-about behaviour — happens *because* FF1 enters all four commands before the round resolves. It is a consequence of command-all-then-resolve, not of per-enemy targeting. M27.1 replaced that round shape on play-test feedback, so the gap between choosing and striking no longer exists and the whole failure mode is unreachable here. No retarget rule, no dead-target message, no tests for either.

**SMRPG answered a question M27 had to leave open.** §7a said it could not verify whether the classics skip a cursor with one legal target. Super Mario RPG asks which enemy "if there is more than one" — so the skip is attested, and the foe cursor can mirror the ally cursor exactly, which is what keeps every fight already shipped pressing the same keys.

**Groups and multi-target magic arrive together.** DQ1 has no group spells because it has no groups; DQ2 introduces both in the same release and shapes its spell list by target. So a spell's target shape becomes data rather than a runtime cursor — which is what this repo's own backlog nominated.

**One body names a formation** (SMRPG's 512 ROM formations, CT's set encounter points), rather than adjacent bodies merging. EarthBound's merge is attested and refused, and its manual says why: "**occasionally**, other nearby enemies may join in on the fight". Occasionally is a roll, and composition would then depend on where a wandering NPC happened to stand — the objection M13 raised against step-counter encounters, arriving through a different door.

## The one loud divergence, recorded as one

**No reference game shows enemy HP.** FF1 lists enemy names in their own box and spends its four HP boxes on the party; DQ2's window shows names and how many are still standing; EarthBound and Chrono Trigger show nothing; SMRPG makes it a *reward* — Mallow's Psychopath spends a whole turn to read one enemy's remaining health. Five to zero.

This template has drawn a numeric `name hp/max` bar for its single foe since M13, and you have been playing it that way ever since. So the choice was between extending a shipped divergence consistently and removing something you already read. **Bars per foe** (your call), recorded as a deliberate divergence with the genre's own answer deferred behind a deliberately small hook — it lives in one caption function and one build branch.

## Also in here

- Both backlog revisit hooks ("a targeting step for ENEMIES", "multi-enemy fights") struck through and pointed at the M28 entries.
- A new backlog item the research surfaced: **a boss with minions as a fight *shape*** — SMRPG's Mack summons his bodyguards back and leaves the field until they are cleared, which is a rule about the encounter rather than about any enemy in it. Formations ship; that does not.
- The determinism note: the two seeded streams stay two, drawn in foe order, so a one-foe fight draws exactly the sequence it drew before. A per-foe stream was rejected — foe 0 would need the bare label, an index-zero special case whose only observable effect is the compatibility itself.

`tools/check.sh` green (docs-only, so it rides the `check-docs` stand-in). Every claim names the game it came from; where two sources disagree — DQ2's Firebane being group or all — the section says so.

author: ryceg
body:
> Supersedes this PR's first revision, which made lockdown per-tenant. That was the wrong call and the reasoning behind it was wrong too — see "Why the first revision was wrong" below.

## Nocturne already always requires authentication

There is nothing for a site-wide lockdown setting to add.

- The default-deny `FallbackPolicy` (`AuthorizationConfiguration.cs`) requires a non-empty `PermissionTrie` on every endpoint without an explicit authorization attribute.
- `AuthenticationMiddleware:240` grants the anonymous Public subject's permissions **only** when `IsShareAccess()` is true.

So on a bare tenant host an unauthenticated caller resolves an empty trie and is denied, with no setting involved. Anonymous read exists only on a deliberately-minted `{token}.share.{base-domain}` host.

## What the setting actually did

It gated the `[AllowAnonymous]` surface that `IsPublicRoute` did not allowlist. That allowlist covers `/api/v4/auth/`, `/api/auth/oidc/`, `/api/oauth/`, `/api/v4/oauth/` and `/api/v4/local/` — but **not** `/api/auth/passkey/*` or `/api/auth/totp/*`.

Enabling lockdown did not make a tenant private. It made a tenant **unable to sign in**. #1024's own merged tests assert exactly this: `/api/auth/passkey/login/options` → 401 under lockdown.

A setting that cannot help and can only brick a tenant is not worth keeping, let alone exposing.

## Two settings, both dead

| | `Security:RequireAuthentication` | `SecuritySettings.RequireAuthForPublicAccess` |
|---|---|---|
| Enforced? | Yes | **No — read by nothing** |
| Scope | **Process-global** (`IConfiguration`) | Per tenant |
| Settable? | **Nowhere** — no appsettings, compose, `.env` or doc | UI settings API |

The global one has been unset since the original `64bbeeb31 v4 api` commit.

## Removed

- `Middleware/SiteSecurityMiddleware.cs` and its `Program.cs` registration
- `Filters/SiteSecurityFilter.cs` — read `HttpContext.Items["SiteLockdownEnabled"]`, the only other reference to which was itself, registered nowhere. Its doc comment claimed it was what respected `[AllowAnonymous]` — exactly the backstop a reviewer would assume covers the middleware. It never ran.
- The whole inert `SecuritySettings` section: `RequireAuthForPublicAccess` and the equally unread `HideGlucoseInFavicon`
- The web twin: `requiresSignIn`, `isPublicRoute`, `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`, and the `requireAuthentication` plumbing through `hooks.server.ts`, `app.d.ts` and the settings store

## Kept

- **The status probe.** It shared the deleted handler, but its `catch` is what drives the setup / recovery / unresolvable-host redirects. The handler is renamed for what it actually does now.
- **`requireAuthentication` in the status document**, hardcoded `false` — it is part of the Nightscout-compatible payload a legacy client parses. The V1 and V3 status golden files are unchanged and still pass, which is the check on that.
- `STATIC_ASSET_PREFIXES`, still used by the probe's skip list.

## Why the first revision was wrong

It kept the per-tenant setting and wired it up, on the reasoning that migrating Nightscout users expect `AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied`. That analogy does not hold: Nightscout's default was **public-readable**, Nocturne's is already deny. The baseline was never checked before the design was chosen, and the proposed follow-up — a UI toggle — would have shipped users a self-lockout button.

## Verification

- `Nocturne.API.Tests`: **6120 passed, 0 failed**. Full solution builds clean.
- Web: `vitest` green; `pnpm check` **53 errors, 0 in any file touched here** (57 before — the 4 closed were the settings-store references to the deleted type).
- The one failing web test, `appearance-store.ssr`, **fails identically on `origin/main`** — verified by checking out main in the same worktree.

## Note

This deletes the code #1024 added three commits ago. That fix was correct for the mechanism as it stood; the mechanism is what turned out not to be worth having.

author: atrawog
body:
## Summary

This plugin serves `kind: distro` and validates an authored `distro:` body against its
**own** self-contained `#DistroInput` before dispatching. That duplication is sanctioned —
the plugin schema must compile standalone while spec's `#Distro` must generate Go — but it
means the two can **drift**, and when they do the failure is actively misleading: charly's
core accepts a field and this plugin rejects it with

```
#DistroInput.disk_layout: field not allowed
```

which reads like the field does not exist anywhere.

Two fields were missing:

| Field | Added to spec in | Consequence of the gap |
|---|---|---|
| `installer` | [spec#71](https://github.com/opencharly/spec/pull/71) | **already drifted** — an authored `installer:` block has been rejected here since that landed |
| `disk_layout` | [spec#72](https://github.com/opencharly/spec/pull/72) | surfaced this: a charly build carrying an omarchy distro entity failed to validate |

### Every file in the diff

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `candy/plugin-distro/schema/distro.cue` | `#DsDiskLayout`, `#DsSubvolume`, `#DsInstaller`, `#DsInstallerFile` added; `disk_layout?` and `installer?` wired into `#DistroInput` |
| `candy/plugin-distro/schema_parity_test.go` | **new** — the drift guard and a dangling-reference guard |

### How this stops recurring

The parity test compares `#DistroInput`'s **top-level field set** against the set spec's
`#Distro` authorises, so the next omission fails *here, next to the fix* rather than in a
consumer's build log.

Inner defs are deliberately **not** compared: they differ in name (`#DsBootloader` vs
`#Bootloader`) and carry no `@go` annotations, so comparing them would be noise. What
matters is that every field a distro entity can author is authorable here.

The `want` list is a literal rather than something read from the `spec` module. Importing
spec to check the standalone schema would defeat the property being checked — this def
exists precisely so the plugin compiles without it.

## How tested

```
$ go test -count=1 ./...
ok  	github.com/opencharly/plugin-distro/candy/plugin-distro	0.005s
?   	github.com/opencharly/plugin-distro/candy/plugin-distro/cmd/serve	[no test files]
?   	github.com/opencharly/plugin-distro/candy/plugin-distro/params	[no test files]
```

**The guard was verified to discriminate, not merely to pass.** Deleting the `disk_layout`
line reproduces the exact failure this PR fixes, with a readable diff:

```
$ python3 -c "…remove the disk_layout line…"
$ go test -count=1 -run TestDistroInputCovers ./...
--- FAIL: TestDistroInputCoversEverySpecDistroField (0.00s)
    schema_parity_test.go:44: #DistroInput fields drifted from spec's #Distro.
         got: [alpine_bootstrap base_user bootloader bootstrap debootstrap dnf format inherit_packages inherits installer pacstrap version workaround]
        want: [alpine_bootstrap base_user bootloader bootstrap debootstrap disk_layout dnf format inherit_packages inherits installer pacstrap version workaround]
```

The line was then restored and the suite re-run green. A test that cannot fail is not a
gate, and this one was made to fail on purpose before being trusted.

The originating symptom is also reproducible: `charly box validate` in the charly repo,
with an omarchy distro entity carrying `disk_layout:`, reported

```
node "omarchy": plugin kind:distro: plugin_input fails #DistroInput:
#DistroInput.disk_layout: field not allowed
```

which is what sent me here.

## Rulebook compliance

- **R0 — skills first.** `/charly-internals:git-workflow`; the sanctioned
  spec-def/plugin-input duplication was read before a third copy was considered.
- **R1 — RCA every anomaly.** The `field not allowed` error was root-caused to schema
  drift rather than treated as "the field is unsupported". Chasing it turned up a
  **second, older** instance (`installer`) that nothing had reported, and both are fixed
  here — not deferred as out of scope.
- **R2 — finish the whole cutover.** Both missing fields, all four supporting defs, and
  the guard that prevents a third, land together.
- **R3 — no duplication.** This is the *sanctioned* duplication, not new duplication: the
  plugin input def must compile standalone. The guard is what makes carrying two copies
  safe, which is the honest answer to "why is this allowed to be duplicated at all".
- **R4 — no workarounds.** The field is added to the schema that rejects it. Loosening
  `#DistroInput` to an open struct would have silenced this and every future typo with it.
- **R5 — delete legacy completely.** `N/A — purely additive; nothing is removed or
  renamed.`
- **R6 — preserve user work and Git safety.** Feature branch off current `main`, PR-only,
  no force-push, no direct push to `main`, no hook bypass.
- **R7 — prove behavior, not compilation.** The guard is proven by making it fail, and the
  fix is proven by the originating `charly box validate` error going away.
- **R8 — preserve emitted artifacts.** `N/A — no generated artifact in this repo.`
- **R9 — binary equals source.** `go test -count=1` from this worktree.
- **R10 — fresh disposable proof.** `N/A — no bed in this repo. Its gate is the unit suite
  on the final tree.`
- **ADE — spec-is-the-test.** Every claim the new defs make is asserted by the two guards.
- **RDD — prove high-risk assumptions before editing.** The assumption that this def was
  in step with spec was false, and testing it is what found the older `installer` gap.
- **SDD — schema-driven design.** Schema-only change, mirroring the core defs.
- **Concurrency mandate.** `N/A — no roster.`

## Change classification

- **Change class:** CUE schema (plugin input def) + tests. No Go behaviour change.
- **Verification gate:** `go test -count=1 ./...`, plus a deliberate negative run showing
  the guard fails on drift.
- **Attribution tier:** fully tested and validated — the rejection this fixes was
  reproduced, the fix removes it, and the guard was proven to catch a regression.

*Assisted-by: Claude Code claude-opus-5[1m] (fully tested and validated)*

## Summary

Closes #622.

Makes the configuration-reference maintenance tests safe in published package sources, where repository-only `docs/` and `examples/` are intentionally absent. Source-workspace detection now honors Cargo's `.cargo_vcs_info.json` package marker and only reads repository authorities in a real checkout.

Corrects the check reference semantics: `time-complement` is enabled by default but remains `NotApplicable` until a sync group declares a time-complement policy; `constant-nonunit-scale` is the only built-in opt-in check. A parser-bounded maintenance test derives the opt-in set directly from `all_checks().enabled_by_default()`.

## Validation

- Full `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER= just gates` passed at exact HEAD `1ee9831e6a34792989a6a5ca83fc6062f5b86730`, including package relocation and 203 animation-pack validator tests.
- Focused configuration-reference and package-layout tests, clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass at that head.
- Independent Codex and Claude audits approve that exact head after Claude caught and verified the packaged-test regression fix.
- Every required hosted check passed at that exact head, including Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, docs/package, coverage, Pages preview, MSRV, animation-pack, typo, and conventional policy checks.

## Scope

No runtime check behavior, schema, or default is changed; this fixes documentation and the maintenance tests that bind it to existing implementation authority.

author: alexey-milovidov
body:
Reverts https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117128, re-landing https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115584 together with the use-after-free fix it needs.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115584
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/116103
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117128
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111017


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):

Fix a heap-use-after-free in the query pipeline executor. When a processor removed itself from a running pipeline, graph edges could be freed while pointers to them were still queued for processing in another executor thread.


### Description

This is `#115584` re-landed, with `#116103` merged in, because `#115584` on its own reopens a `heap-use-after-free` in the executor.

`ExecutingGraph::updateNode` keeps pending edge updates in a work list local to its own frame, filled under only a shared lock on `nodes_mutex`, so several frames hold private lists at once. `updateNode` releases that lock at two points, and a frame parked at either one can resume and dereference an `Edge` that another frame freed meanwhile. `#111017` fixed only the same-frame case, by scrubbing the removing frame's own list; it cannot reach the lists of other frames.

`#115584` did not introduce the race, but it widened it considerably: removal is deferred into `removeReadyGroups`, which any frame may call at either of those two points, so removals became both far more frequent and reachable from more call sites. In bucket `STID 2837-40ba` over the 60 days before the revert, the 5 occurrences preceding `#115584` are all `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, while the 8 following it span 6 jobs and reached `master`:

https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=9593cfadad22b8112fd28a6fbabece49cade9890&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29

That `master` failure is cross-thread and shows the exact path `#116103` closes: `T462` frees a removed node's edges in `removeReadyGroups` -> `removePendingGroup` -> `removeNode` -> `~Node`, while `T552` pops one of them and reads `auto & node = *edge->to;`.

`#116103` fixes it by retention rather than by tracking frames: `retireAffectedEdges` moves every edge of a removed node into a list that lives as long as the graph, points it at a permanently `Finished` stand-in node, and runs before the node is erased. A queued pointer therefore stays valid, and `updateNode` skips a `Finished` node without reaching its processor.

The merge is exact — this branch is `master` with `#115584` restored plus `#116103`'s three touched files byte-identical to that pull request, which was green apart from the unrelated `Not-ready Set` flake tracked as https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619.

author: kojiro5150
body:
## Purpose

Continue **Store Parity & Restart Durability** by making restart recovery explicitly distinguish durable semantic continuity from source-backed records that must be revalidated.

## Architectural finding

The existing constructors make an important trust consequence explicit:

- user-authored assertions/preferences/plans/commitments/decisions can persist as historical user continuity;
- model-authored inferences/recommendations/open questions can persist only as low-trust model continuity;
- facts and governed-source plans/commitments/decisions cannot be recreated as trusted records from a database row alone because their `GovernedEvidence`/`GovernedProvenance` brands are intentionally non-rehydratable.

This PR encodes that distinction instead of weakening `PERSISTENCE-TRUST-01`.

## Changes

- adds `recoverOperatingPictureRecordHistoryAfterRestart(...)`
- classifies every persisted version as one of:
  - `recoverable_user_continuity`
  - `recoverable_model_continuity`
  - `requires_source_revalidation`
- records exact reasons for governed fact/plan/commitment/decision revalidation
- preserves durable not-found/provider/integrity rejection unchanged
- fails closed if recovered head identity does not match the durable head
- returns only low-trust persisted versions plus recovery disposition; it does not construct `OperatingPictureRecord`

## Proving tests

- user-authored history survives restart as historical semantic continuity
- model-authored material survives only as low-trust model continuity
- persisted facts require source revalidation
- governed plan/commitment/decision records require source revalidation
- durable not-found/rejection is preserved
- head mismatch fails closed
- compile-time regression proves recovered continuity cannot be assigned to `OperatingPictureRecord`, `GovernedEvidence`, or `AuthorityEvidence`

## Explicit non-goals

- no trust rehydration
- no automatic repopulation of the high-trust in-memory store
- no provider reacquisition yet
- no model retrieval
- no automatic chat-memory capture
- no embeddings
- no proactive behaviour

This is the classifier required before any safe restart reintegration can be attempted.
