author: shoutcape
body:
## Problem

`treeman branch` and `treeman review` fetched every API page, built one big string, and only then started `fzf`. Against `payloadcms/payload` (649 remote branches, 663 open PRs) both showed nothing at all for several seconds. Practically all of that was serialized network round trips — local `git` and row rendering were under 10 ms.

## Results

Measured live under a pty in `~/github/payload`, before vs. after in the same harness:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `branch` — picker on screen | 3.90 s (blank) | **0.03 s** |
| `branch` — first rows | 3.90 s | **0.59 s** |
| `branch` — complete list | 3.90 s | **2.56 s** |
| `review` — picker on screen | 3.57 s (blank) | **0.03 s** |
| `review` — first rows | 3.57 s | **0.54 s** |
| `review` — complete list | 3.57 s | 3.49 s |
| GitHub branch list (7 pages) | 2.9 s | **1.10 s** |

`ESC` cancels cleanly throughout. Before the change `fzf` did not appear on screen until everything had been fetched. `review`'s completion time is unchanged: its GraphQL cursor pagination is inherently serial, so streaming moves when rows appear, not when the list finishes.

*(An earlier revision of this description quoted 4.16 s → 1.20 s for `branch`. Those came from a pty harness that did not answer fzf's cursor-position query, which stalled it ~0.5 s on both sides. The table above is measured with that fixed; the before/after ratio is unaffected.)*

## Changes

### 1. Parallel REST pagination

`internal/forge/paginate.go` reads page 1 with `gh api --include`, takes the final page number from the `Link: rel="last"` header, then requests pages 2..N concurrently (bounded at 8) while still delivering them to the callback in page order. Endpoints with no `rel="last"` fall back to walking `next` one page at a time. It fails loudly on a response with no header block rather than treating a bare JSON body as a single page, since silently returning page 1 of N would truncate the branch list.

### 2. Streaming picker

`runStreamingPicker` starts `fzf` against an `os.Pipe` and writes rows as the producer emits them. `consumerClosed` treats `fzf` closing stdin on selection as "done", not as a failure. `BranchListPages` and `PRListPages` hand out one API page at a time; `BranchList` and `PRList` become thin accumulating wrappers, so existing callers are unchanged.

### 3. Painting the picker before any row arrives

Starting `fzf` early was not enough on its own. `fzf` paints nothing while `--select-1` or `--exit-0` is set, because either flag can make it exit before it has shown a UI, so it will not draw a frame it might immediately tear down. With rows arriving at 1.20 s, `fzf` painted at 0.025 s with neither flag and at 1.29 s with either one.

Both flags are now dropped when no query is given, and the two outcomes they covered are settled once the row stream ends: no rows cancels the picker, exactly one row selects it. Those are the only results they can produce without a query. With a query they are kept, since only `fzf` can tell how many rows match it. `switch` and `delete` are unaffected — their lists are complete before `fzf` starts, so there is no wait to shorten.

This also replaces `Kill` with `SIGTERM` when TreeMan ends `fzf` itself. `fzf` restores the terminal when asked to terminate but cannot when killed, which left the cursor hidden for every line printed afterwards — reachable on the pre-existing producer-error path too.

The one behaviour change: with no query and exactly one available result, the picker now appears briefly instead of not at all.

### 4. Per-branch PR lookup for `treeman branch`

The branch list was no longer the bottleneck — the MR/PR column was. It came from the whole open-PR list, so no row could render until that query had been walked.

`internal/forge/branchpr.go` asks each branch for its own open PR instead. One ref lookup per branch would be far too slow, so refs are batched and the batches run concurrently, feeding rows in as the REST branch list is still paginating. A preview query returns the alphabetically first refs with their PRs in one round trip, which is what puts rows on screen before the list has been fetched at all; GitHub orders refs and REST branches identically, so the preview is a prefix of the first page and duplicates drop out cleanly. A failed preview costs only the head start.

Constants were measured rather than guessed (payload, 649 branches):

| batch / concurrency | first batch | complete |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100 refs × 7 | 1.10 s | 2.97 s |
| 50 refs × 13 | 0.96 s | 1.58 s |
| **25 refs × 16** (chosen) | **0.71 s** | **1.68 s** |

A GraphQL query costs 1 rate-limit point regardless of batch size, out of 5000/hour, so the extra queries are not a practical constraint.

## This also fixes a wrong PR column

Joining the open-PR list on head ref name alone attributed a **fork's** PR to a same-named branch in this repository. In payload:

- `3.x`, `codex/hierarchy-delete-strategy`, `fix/autosave-overwrites-link-modal` each showed a PR number belonging to someone's fork
- `feat/mongoose-custom-id-type` showed the fork's #15522 instead of the repository's own #17273

A ref's `associatedPullRequests` never returns a PR that is not its own head — verified across all 649 branches, zero non-head results.

## Alternatives measured and rejected

- **REST for the PR list.** Parallel REST pagination of `pulls` came in at 3.10 s against GraphQL's 3.35 s, but with the first page at 1.36 s instead of 0.62 s and ~13 MB downloaded. An earlier shell-only estimate of 1.9 s did not include decoding and was wrong.
- **A combined GraphQL `refs` + `associatedPullRequests` query, paginated.** 1.83 s per page and cursor pagination is serial, so 7 pages would take ~12.8 s. Note this is the measurement that made the per-ref approach look unaffordable; it measures the *serial* cost, and concurrency collapses it.

## Notes and limitations

GitLab keeps the existing fetch-then-render path: `glab` is not installed on the machine this was developed on, so a parallel version could not be verified. It still works, it just does not get the speedup.

Batches still in flight when the picker closes are left to finish rather than blocking the caller, so `ESC` stays instant; batches that have not started are abandoned.

## Verification

```bash
go vet ./...
go test -race ./...
make build && script -qec "./smoke-test.sh" /dev/null   # needs a TTY
```

All pass, including under `-race` — which caught a genuine bug where in-flight goroutines outlived the call and still read package state. The smoke test's mock `gh` now emits response headers for `--include` and answers the preview and per-ref batch queries, matching the real CLI.

body:
Clears the runner warning that all five actions target `node20`, a runtime GitHub is retiring. The runner currently force-upgrades them to Node 24 at execution time — it works, but it is an unsupported path that eventually becomes a hard failure.

| Action | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | v4 | **v7** |
| `docker/login-action` | v3 | **v4** |
| `docker/metadata-action` | v5 | **v6** |
| `docker/setup-buildx-action` | v3 | **v4** |
| `docker/build-push-action` | v6 | **v7** |

Verified each target declares `runs.using: node24` and each current pin declares `node20`.

These majors exist *specifically* for the runtime change — `checkout@v5` moved to node24, and each `docker/*` bump is headlined "Node 24 as default runtime". Requirement is Actions Runner ≥ v2.327.1, which `ubuntu-latest` already exceeds (it is what forces Node 24 today).

**Only behavioural change across the span:** `checkout@v7` blocks fork-PR checkout for `pull_request_target` / `workflow_run`. This workflow triggers only on `push` to `main` and `workflow_dispatch`, so it is unaffected.

body:
## Scope

Small prerequisite before the profile editor UI: the scanner must know the canonical tracked-instrument id/state from the backend instead of relying on its session-local `saved` flag.

### Adds
- `getTrackedInstruments()` mobile read service for canonical `GET /api/v1/tracked-instruments`
- scanner loads canonical tracked instruments alongside scanner results
- `Seurannassa` is derived from persisted instrument + market identity
- successful `trackInstrument(...)` updates the in-memory canonical collection with the backend-returned row
- transient UI state is now only `saving | error`; there is no local `saved` truth
- focused source regressions

### Why this comes before profile UI
The profile API is keyed by canonical `tracked_instrument_id`. The app must first have the persisted tracked-instrument row/id available in the scanner before a minimal profile editor can be attached without guessing identity.

### Boundary
No tracking-profile UI yet. No calendar changes. No tracked event, Strategy, Risk, Broker, PAPER/LIVE, trading-task, backend, or schema changes.

author: phongleo1107
body:
Nothing in this codebase had downloaded a repository or parsed one outside a test. app/analysis/pipeline.py is the code path that does: it sends the credential-free request github.py builds, streams the response into archive.py, applies is_secret_path to every yielded path, picks a grammar by extension, and calls extract_imports — all on one frozen Deadline per request, threaded into both consumers and asserted by object identity so a stage that quietly built its own from ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT_S is caught.

The SHA return channel is an out-parameter, not a changed tuple (ADR-011). archive.py keeps yielding (path, content); ArchiveInfo carries the commit SHA and the skip counts. The tempting third option — a generator return value read from StopIteration — is delivered only on exhaustion, and the pipeline stops at MAX_SOURCE_FILES without draining, so it would be empty in exactly the case that needs it. An out-parameter is filled the moment the first member establishes the root, so it survives an early break; a test pins that after a single next().

iter_raw(), not iter_bytes(). httpx transparently decodes a Content-Encoding before the caller sees a byte — measured, 52 wire bytes become 1700 decoded. Every budget in archive.py is defined on wire bytes: MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES bounds bandwidth, and the compression-ratio guard's denominator is meant to be what was actually transferred. This is a deliberate deviation from the plan of record and is pinned behaviourally rather than argued.

A configured GITHUB_TOKEN was an exfiltration proxy. RepoMetadata.private had been parsed and validated since the client landed and had no consumer. The 403/404 collapse hides whether a private repo exists; it does not help when the operator's token can actually read one, because GitHub then answers 200 and the preflight succeeds. Refused now, with the same opaque error. New SECURITY.md row.

MAX_SOURCE_FILES is the parse cap and is not archive.py's 50 000-member cap: different limits at different layers, exceeding one rejects the archive and exceeding the other sets truncated. It is checked after the filters so 3000 images cannot exhaust the budget for source, and it breaks rather than continues so the rest of the download is abandoned. A test exists only to prove the two caps cannot be conflated.

The deadline still cannot preempt a parse or a query already running (ADR-010). A frozen-clock test pins that the file being parsed when the budget expires runs to completion and the run aborts on the next one. No test or docstring here implies otherwise.

Output is a content-free RepositoryAnalysis (ADR-012): loc and bytes are measured while the content is in hand precisely so nothing downstream holds it, and resolution targets exactly this file set so an edge cannot point at a non-node. No resolution, no sorting, no graph.

33 controls mutation-tested one deletion at a time; 32 caught. The survivor, closing(members), is annotated as redundant while closing(response) and CPython refcounting both hold. Two of the five first-pass survivors were defects in the tests — the close assertion drained the stream, where httpx closes it anyway, and download_request() could be swapped for a bare build_request because create_client() sets no Authorization default (ADR-009 working) — and one was a false claim in a comment: the root regex does not depend on greedy backtracking, since under fullmatch greedy and lazy agree on every input. All three fixed.

1065 tests, ruff and mypy --strict clean. Everything still runs against respx and in-process tarballs; nothing has been fetched from GitHub itself.

author: ijustwantedmycheeeeese
body:
## Summary
Third and final PR of the trigger-engine plan (engine core + ETB [#35] → death [#36] → **attack**).

- `fireAttackTriggers(lobby, card)` -- same shape as the ETB/death firers, hooked in `declareAttackers` once `lobby.combat.attackers` is committed.
- **Combat-sequencing fix**, the real substance of this PR: an attack trigger has to resolve *before* combat damage, not after, or an effect like a pump-on-attack counter lands too late to matter for that combat. `declareAttackers`/`declareBlockers` already only call `resolveCombatDamage` immediately when there's genuinely nothing left to block with (both gated on `stack.length === 0` at entry) -- so `resolveStackTop`'s existing tail just needed one added check: when the stack drains to empty, if `lobby.combat.step` is still `"damage"`, resolve it there instead of at the original declare-time call site. No new state needed -- an earlier draft of this plan used a dedicated `awaitingDamage` flag, dropped after review found it could fire damage while a defender's block declaration was still legitimately pending (since `combat.step` already encodes the right condition for free).
- Two seed abilities, oracle text confirmed via a direct Scryfall search rather than guessing from memory (most real \"attacks\" triggers target *another* creature, e.g. Mentor, which is out of this vocabulary's scope by design -- took several search attempts to find genuinely self-only ones): **Library Larcenist** (draw a card on attack) and **Ezio, Brash Novice** (+1/+1 counter on attack, base 1/1 -- picked specifically because it's a clean, unambiguous way to prove the sequencing fix: if the counter doesn't land before damage, Ezio deals 1 damage, not 2).
- No client changes -- #35's generic ability-vs-spell Stack rendering already covers attack triggers too.

## Test plan
- [x] Scripted `socket.io-client` test, 6 assertions: an attack trigger (Library Larcenist) lands on the stack and combat damage genuinely does NOT resolve while it's pending; the draw effect resolves correctly; combat damage then resolves automatically once the stack drains (no separate action needed); **the sequencing proof** -- Ezio (base 1/1) dealt exactly 2 combat damage, confirmed only possible if its own +1/+1 counter landed before damage was computed for that same combat.
- [x] Full regression: re-ran all three trigger-engine test suites (ETB from #35, death from #36, attack from this PR) together after this change -- 18 of 19 assertions passed cleanly; the one flake was the *unrelated* ETB-PR's disconnect/reconnect timing test, which is timing-sensitive under back-to-back suite execution in this dev environment (confirmed via re-running it standalone, cleanly, multiple times) -- not a regression from this PR's combat.step change, which can't logically affect an ETB-only scenario (combat.step never becomes `"damage"` there).

author: clofour
body:
## Summary

This is a behavior-preserving structural cleanup of the areas that had begun accumulating too many responsibilities.

- split control-plane models, node/job/catalog concerns, reconciliation, execution, reload, and persistence compatibility into focused files
- move legacy allocation decoding/encoding out of the live `Allocation` model and into the state boundary while preserving old persisted records and compatibility status output
- document and enforce a single server/allocation lock ordering; execution snapshots server state before I/O rather than reacquiring the server lock under an allocation lock
- split agent durability/recovery, allocation execution, heartbeat/orphan reconciliation, and status callbacks; publish allocation snapshots instead of exposing partially mutated shared objects
- move the `trellis-node` application lifecycle into `internal/nodeapp`, leaving `cmd/trellis-node` as CLI/configuration wiring
- introduce named types for finite job-spec values (`Runtime`, `NetworkMode`, `HealthCheckType`) without typing open-ended label/constraint keys
- expand lifecycle tests to cover the complete transition matrix and legacy mapping
- split the dashboard job form into transport schema, form model/conversion, field editors, and panel orchestration
- preserve unsupported job-spec fields while editing in the dashboard instead of rebuilding only the currently editable subset
- align the dashboard health-check type with the orchestrator's `script` value

## Design constraints

The refactor intentionally avoids repository/service/interface layers that would add Kubernetes-style or enterprise-style abstraction without reducing coupling. Trellis keeps the same focused resource model and public API shape.

## Compatibility

Persisted allocations written with legacy `name`, `revision`, `Task`, and `status` fields are translated at load time. New records continue to emit compatibility projections for older readers/clients.

## Validation

The existing orchestrator build/lint/test and UI lint workflows are expected to validate this PR. Additional table-driven lifecycle and persistence compatibility tests are included.

author: w3bray
body:
Documento em relatividade geral que separa as duas proposições que a expressão "viagem no tempo" costuma confundir, e trata cada uma com o rigor que ela comporta.

| | Afirmação | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Teorema I** | Ir a um instante arbitrariamente distante no futuro gastando tempo próprio arbitrariamente curto | **Demonstrado** — e medido |
| **Teorema II** | As equações de Einstein admitem soluções exatas com curvas fechadas de tipo tempo | **Demonstrado como teorema** (Gödel, 1949); realizabilidade física em aberto |

## O que o documento cobre

**Teorema I** é provado de forma construtiva, via movimento hiperbólico a 1 g: a integração exata de `t(τ) = (c/a) sinh(aτ/c)`, a tabela de tempo próprio contra tempo coordenado (10 anos de bordo ↔ 14 736 anos na Terra), o custo em combustível pela equação do foguete relativístico, e a verificação experimental — múons no anel do CERN, Hafele–Keating, a correção de +38,50 µs/dia do GPS, os relógios ópticos do NIST a 33 cm de distância, e os 21,5 ms que Gennady Padalka acumulou na ISS.

**Teorema II** é provado exibindo a demonstração de Gödel: a mudança de sinal de `g_φφ` na métrica exata e o raio crítico `arcsinh(1) = ln(1+√2)`. Segue com o catálogo de soluções com CTCs, a construção de Morris–Thorne–Yurtsever passo a passo, os dois obstáculos que realmente restam (energia negativa e proteção cronológica) e as duas resoluções do paradoxo do avô — Echeverría–Klinkhammer–Thorne no caso clássico, e o teorema de ponto fixo de Deutsch, que sai de Brouwer, no quântico.

O documento é explícito sobre onde a demonstração para: não num paradoxo lógico, mas numa lacuna aberta na gravitação quântica.

## Arquivos

- `prova/viagem-no-tempo.html` — o documento. Não carrega nenhum script em tempo de execução: as 135 equações vão embutidas como SVG e os três diagramas são desenhados em canvas a partir das mesmas fórmulas do texto, nenhum é ilustrativo.
- `prova/calculos.py` — reproduz cada número citado usando apenas a biblioteca padrão, de modo que toda afirmação quantitativa do texto seja conferível linha a linha.
- `prova/build-math.js` — pré-renderiza a matemática. Idempotente, e guarda o TeX em `data-tex`, então o arquivo gerado é a própria fonte e não é preciso manter um segundo arquivo.

## Verificação

Todos os valores saem de `prova/calculos.py`. A página foi renderizada no Chromium e conferida em:

- ambos os temas, e nos três estados de tema (sistema sem stamp, e override explícito por `data-theme` nos dois sentidos) — contraste de corpo 15,3:1 e 16,1:1;
- 1280 px e 390 px — sem overflow horizontal do documento; tabelas e equações largas rolam dentro do próprio contêiner, com indicação visual de que rolam;
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` — quadro estático, sem loop de animação;
- sem erros de console.

Um detalhe do diagrama de Gödel que vale registrar: os cones são desenhados com φ reescalado por `sinh r · cosh r`, o que põe as bordas nulas em `1 ± √2 tanh r`. Em `r = 0` isso dá exatamente ±45°, e a borda inferior cruza a horizontal precisamente em `r_c`. Qualquer reescala positiva de φ preserva esse cruzamento, então o fato exato sobrevive à conveniência gráfica.

author: jonahsnider[bot]
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm11/pnpm)) | [`12.0.0` → `12.1.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/12.0.0/12.1.0) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/12.1.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/12.0.0/12.1.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.1.0): pnpm 12.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.0.0...v12.1.0)

#### Minor Changes

- `pnpm login` and `pnpm adduser` now record the granted token in the global `config.yaml`, under the `_auth` setting, with `--scope`'s scope routed to that registry under `registries`. `pnpm logout` removes it from there, and still from an `auth.ini` an earlier version wrote. Tokens already in `auth.ini` keep working.

- A `scope` set in a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is now ignored, with a warning naming where to set it instead. `pnpm login` records the scope as a `@scope:registry` route in the machine-global `auth.ini`, which outranks `~/.npmrc` in every project — so a repository-committed file could redirect a scope such as `@acme` for all of a user's other projects after one routine login. Use `--scope`, the `PNPM_CONFIG_SCOPE` environment variable, or the global config file instead [#​13557](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13557).

- Verified remote build artifacts are persisted in the shared store with their signed origin metadata. Later installs reverify the artifact against current trust, policy, platform, and source before reuse, while invalid remote variants are quarantined per channel ([pnpm/pnpm#13771](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13771)).

- Persist completed recursive tasks so `--resume-from` skips exactly the work that passed during a matching interrupted or failed `pnpm -r run` / `pnpm -r exec` invocation. When no compatible state exists, pnpm retains its graph-based resume behavior.

- Workspace install, rebuild, pack, publish, stage, and lifecycle work now starts as soon as its dependencies finish instead of waiting for an unrelated topological group.

- Added per-task concurrency limits to workspace task orchestration. Set `tasks.<name>.concurrency` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to limit how many instances of that task may run across workspace projects at once:

  ```yaml
  tasks:
    build:
      concurrency: 2
  ```

- `sideEffectsCache` now declares the whole of how a package's build output is reused — whether one is restored, whether one is saved, and the remote tier that shares it between machines:

  ```yaml
  sideEffectsCache:
    read: true
    write: true
    remote:
      org: acme
      packages: ['native-addon']
  ```

  `sideEffectsCache: true`, `sideEffectsCacheReadonly`, `remoteSideEffectsCache`, and its `organization` field all keep working. Where a field is set under both spellings the one above wins; where it is set under only one, it is kept.

  Two behaviors change, both bringing this CLI in line with what the Rust one already did: `sideEffectsCacheReadonly: true` now blocks writing to the cache, and setting it alongside `sideEffectsCache: false` gives a read-only view rather than switching the cache off entirely. A cache can also be declared write-only now, to populate one the run does not read.

- Workspace task orchestration ([pnpm/rfcs#23](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/23)). `pnpm -r run` and `pnpm -r exec` now schedule per task instead of in topological chunks: a task starts as soon as the tasks it depends on have finished, so a project no longer waits for unrelated projects that happen to share its chunk.

  A new `tasks` section in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` declares what a task depends on, using the `^` convention:

  ```yaml
  tasks:
    build:
      dependsOn: ['^build']
    test:
      dependsOn: ['build']
    lint: {}
  ```

  `^name` means the named task in each of the project's workspace dependencies; a bare `name` means the task in the same project; an entry with no `dependsOn` declares an empty dependency list. A task with no entry behaves as `dependsOn: ['^<its own name>']`, which is exactly what the previous chunked ordering implied — an unconfigured workspace gets the scheduler improvement and nothing else changes meaning. A project without the script is reported skipped and passes its edges through to its own dependencies, so a scriptless package does not sever a chain.

  Also part of this change:

  - A dependency cycle among the tasks of a run is now an error naming the participating tasks (`ERR_PNPM_TASK_CYCLE`) instead of silently running in an arbitrary order. Setting `ignoreWorkspaceCycles: true` downgrades the error to a warning: the cycle's tasks run in an arbitrary order relative to each other.
  - `--resume-from` now skips exactly the transitive dependencies of the anchor package; work unrelated to the anchor still runs.
  - Under `--no-bail`, tasks whose dependencies failed are reported as skipped, not failed, and do not add to the exit code.
  - With `--bail` (the default), the first failure still ends the run at once and nothing new is dispatched — including scripts already queued behind the concurrency limit.
  - `pnpm -r run --dry-run <script>` prints the task graph that would execute without running anything (including skipping the `verifyDepsBeforeRun` check); `--json` emits the tasks and their resolved dependency edges.
  - Output is inherited rather than piped only when at most one script can ever be in flight (`--workspace-concurrency=1`, or the graph forces the scripts to run one after another).

- Added macOS and Windows x64 and arm64 support to remote shared build artifacts [pnpm/pnpm#13771](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13771).

- Generalized the experimental shared-artifact protocol so candidates and signed payloads identify a discriminated subject. Dependency side effects use package and source-integrity subjects, while workspace tasks use project and task subjects.

  This changes shared-artifact request bodies and signed payloads. A pnpr server and its clients have to be on matching versions.

#### Patch Changes

- An `_auth` entry in the global config file no longer decides which registry packages come from when something else says. A `registry` or `registries` declared in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global config now wins over the route inferred from a stored credential, which still applies where nothing else declares one. The `pnpm_config__auth` environment variable is unchanged: it stays the way to point a CI runner at a mandated proxy, and still overrides what a repository declares.

- Fixed `pnpm deploy --legacy` to exclude dependencies that are only reachable from unselected workspace projects after `pnpm fetch`.

- Fixed dependency-verification install logs corrupting `pnpm exec` output and ignoring `--silent` [pnpm/pnpm#14197](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14197).

- `pnpm clean` / `pnpm purge` run from a workspace subdirectory now remove each project's own `node_modules` instead of emptying the workspace root's for every project [#​14239](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14239). A custom `modulesDir` is resolved against each project directory too.

- `pnpm dlx <pkg>@catalog:` now resolves the specifier through the calling workspace's catalogs instead of failing with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC` [#​14294](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14294).

- Fixed `pnpm doctor` reporting a version that does not match `pnpm --version` [pnpm/pnpm#14225](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14225).

- Pacquet now strips exactly one

author: venkateshboyapati
body:
## Summary

Env-gated scale harness under `apps/api/tests/scale/` that runs the **real** engine
(`UniversalTransferEngine.execute_tracked`) across every ordered pair of the five relational
engines (including same-engine pairs) × 4 sync modes × 5 schema shapes, and proves each cell from a
**separate driver connection**: `COUNT(*)` + an order-independent checksum over the mapped
projection, compared against a checksum computed independently from the fixture generator. Every
data cell runs twice to assert second-run semantics (overwrite N, append 2N, incremental N, upsert N).

```bash
cd apps/api
DATAFLOW_SCALE_MATRIX=1 PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.scale.run_matrix --rows 100000 \
  --out /tmp/matrix.json --markdown /tmp/matrix.md
```

Measured, full grid, all five engines live, **200 rows** (no result here is scaled up from a
smaller run): **pass = 168, fail = 57, skip = 0** of 225 cells. All 45 blocking cells
(`dest_exists_narrower`, G13, G14) refused and left the destination at 0 rows. The Oracle ↔
PostgreSQL sub-grid is **36/36 green** after the fixes below. Per-route table, per-column skip
reasons, and the grouped open failures are in `docs/SCALE_MATRIX_SQL.md`.

The harness declares no second type map. `dest_exists_compatible` is built from what
`services.schema_introspect` reads on the source, passed through the canonical inventor
`services.type_system.ddl_type` — i.e. the table create-new would have stamped:

```python
# tests/scale/matrix.py
dst.create_table(dst_table, columns, source_types=cache.source_types(src, columns))
# tests/scale/fixture.invented_ddl_for -> services.type_system.ddl_type
```

Otherwise a hand-written PostgreSQL `DATE` against an Oracle `DATE` source (which carries a
time-of-day, so the product reads `TIMESTAMP(0)`) reads as a harness bug when the engine was right
to refuse.

### Defects fixed, each in its one canonical owner

- **Oracle `TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE` read as NTZ** — SQLAlchemy carries Oracle TSLTZ
  awareness on `local_timezone` and leaves `timezone` False, so `_logical_type_from_sa` stamped
  `timestamp_ntz` and the writer quarantined every aware value the column exists to hold
  (pg→oracle `upsert`/`full_refresh_append` refused 200/200 rows; now pass with matching
  checksums). `connectors/generic_sql.py`:
  ```python
  if getattr(col_type, "local_timezone", False):
      return "timestamp_ltz"
  ```
- **Oracle string invention defaulted to BYTE width** — `VARCHAR(64)` became `VARCHAR2(64 BYTE)`,
  a real shrink for CJK; only a source that itself declared BYTE keeps byte semantics.
  `services/type_system.py`.
- **Oracle native `JSON` unrecognised by reflection** (`NullType`), so the document went out on the
  container/string wire and `{"i": 0}` arrived as `{"i": "0"}` — registered an Oracle JSON type in
  `ischema_names`. `connectors/generic_sql.py`.
- **JSON documents lost numeric polarity** — `default=json_default` renders `Decimal` as a JSON
  *string* (right for a DECIMAL column on the string wire, wrong inside a document python-oracledb
  decoded from OSON). Added a document-specific serializer; the scalar DECIMAL contract is
  unchanged. `services/value_serializer.py`, plus MariaDB's `UNSIGNED INTEGER` number spelling in
  `services/json_polarity.py`.
- `NVARCHAR2` missed by the national-carrier check during destination invention; Oracle explicit
  `NUMBER(1,0)` widened through generic 64-bit inference (`flag → DECIMAL(19,0)` overflow); SQL
  Server UUID stamped `VARCHAR(36)` instead of `UNIQUEIDENTIFIER`. `services/type_system.py`.
- SQL Server `trust_server_certificate` dropped on the read path (writer connected, introspection
  reported unreachable). `src/transfer/connector_dispatch.py`, `batch_readers.py`,
  `adapters_introspect.py`.
- SQL Server `DATETIMEOFFSET` reflected as NTZ; `NVARCHAR/NCHAR/NTEXT` classified as Latin-1
  (quarantined all CJK/emoji into a column that holds them); pyodbc short rowcount on
  all-or-nothing batches; BIGINT reflection collapsing to int4 bounds; Oracle identifier folding
  (`ORA-00942` on quoted lower-case lookup). `connectors/generic_sql.py`,
  `services/encoding_capacity.py`, `services/schema_introspect.py`.

### Open, not worked around

57 failing cells, grouped by root cause in the evidence doc — the largest groups are (a) SQL Server
destination invention choosing `VARCHAR` for a Unicode-capable source column, then correctly
refusing `U+8A9E`; (b) `* → sqlite` treating `UUID → TEXT` as a fidelity collapse when TEXT is the
wider carrier; (c) invented MySQL DDL emitting a `CHARACTER SET ... COLLATE` clause the server
rejects (`1064`); (d) cross-engine collation carry picking a weaker collation than the source, so
the gate refuses the product's own invented destination.

### Not proven yet

**No 100K run has completed.** Every measured route is under the 2,000 rows/sec bar (106–406
rows/sec; largest completed single run is 20,000 rows pg→pg at 406 rows/sec), so the 225-cell grid
at 100K is ~40h of wall clock. The grid above is a real 200-row run; nothing is extrapolated.
Slow-route profiling is end-to-end elapsed only, with no per-stage breakdown yet.

Caveat that changes how two failure groups read: the compose "MySQL 8" service on this box reports
**MariaDB**, and two repo tests fail on it identically on the base branch.

Math input in the chat lesson panel** — `ChatInputPanel` now imports the shared `FormulaComposer` with a pill toggle button and popup, matching the pattern already used in `FreeResponseQuestion` and the main `ChatInterface`. Students can compose math visually and insert as `$…$` at the caret.
- **11. Free-response false-negatives** — `validate-answer` route grows a `latexToPlain()` normalizer that strips `$…$`/`$$…$$` delimiters and expands `\frac{a}{b}`, `\sqrt{n}`, `^{n}`, `_{n}`, `\cdot`, `\times`, `\div`, `\pm`, and common Greek letters into plain-text forms. A new `latex-plain` match tier compares the normalized student and accepted answers so a keyboard-composed `$\frac{1}{2}$` matches a hand-typed `1/2`. The numeric matcher also now strips `$` so `$5$` compares to `5`. Semantic (LLM) fallback still fires for anything the deterministic tiers miss.

## Summary

Fixes the stage-2 rollout blocker from #5163. Migration `0126` backfills `mcp_tool_calls.decision_operator_id` and then drops the legacy `denial_reason` column. The backfill queues events for the deferred `ctrg_haku_0009_call_has_principal` constraint trigger as well as the attribution foreign key; PostgreSQL rejects the subsequent `ALTER TABLE` while either has pending trigger events.

The migration now runs `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE` before the validation checks and column drop, flushing both deferred constraint classes in the same transaction.

The merged #5246 image was published successfully, but production migration pod `haku-console-migration-b9fwv` still failed with `cannot ALTER TABLE "mcp_tool_calls" because it has pending trigger events` at `DROP COLUMN denial_reason`. The Deployment remains on the previous healthy revision until this fix rolls.

One migration file only; no cluster manifests or production data were changed.

author: markamccorkle
body:
Closes #1205. Wave 1 of #1204.

## The bug

With `knowledge.enabled: true` and `auto_scaffold: true`, this workspace has not produced a knowledge base at its root since **#390** — hundreds of runs later, `.nightgauge/knowledge/features/` still ended at `390-`.

The scaffold *did* run. The issue-pickup skill called `nightgauge knowledge scaffold`, which resolved its root with a bare `os.Getwd()`. On the scheduler path the stage's cwd is the run's **worktree**, so the PRD and decisions landed in `<worktree>/.nightgauge/knowledge/` — gitignored — and `knowledge_path` was patched into the worktree's `issue-N.json`. When the worktree was reclaimed after merge, the knowledge base went with it, and every later reader (feature-dev's "read `knowledge_path/PRD.md`" rule, `/nightgauge:retro`'s outcome append, the sidebar) found nothing.

## The fix

The scaffold moves into the **Go pickup path**, which already knows the canonical root. `config.MainCheckoutRoot` (#410) is the resolver: root resolution needs `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and needs to be the same answer every time — not something a skill gets right by convention. The skill's ~100-line bash block, including its `grep -A5 "^knowledge:"` config parsing, is deleted. **One path, not two.**

`knowledge_path` is stamped **absolute**, into whichever context file `execution.IssueContextCandidates` finds (#994) — on a worktree-isolated run that is inside the worktree. Absolute because the stages read it from the worktree while the sidebar and retro read it from the root, and only an absolute path is correct from both; both TypeScript readers already accept either form. The rewrite is atomic (temp + rename, #1210) and patches one field rather than replacing the document.

## `auto_scaffold` had no reader in Go at all

Adds `KnowledgeConfig.IsAutoScaffold()`, gated by `Enabled` for the same reason `IsTelemetryEnabled` is (ADR-005): a project that opted out of the KB must not get directories written into its tree by a nested flag it never looked at.

Its struct comment claimed *"defaults to false"* while `docs/KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md`, the `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` table and the SDK's own reader all treat unset as **on** — a contradiction that could never surface, because no resolver existed to be wrong. The docs' table wins.

## Also fixed in the same step

`knowledge workspace-init` (the skill's Step 8.3.5) had the same cwd exposure — it walked up for the workspace marker starting from the worktree. Canonicalized, and moved into the same Go step.

Config is now read from the **canonical** root rather than the passed root: in the dogfood shape the scheduler's own root *is* a worktree, which can carry a stale config or none at all.

## Tests

The fixtures build a **real linked worktree**. Against two unrelated temp directories the broken and fixed code are indistinguishable, because the difference is entirely in what `--git-common-dir` reports.

- `internal/orchestrator/knowledge_scaffold_pickup_test.go` (new, 5 tests): lands at the canonical root and **not** in the worktree; stamps an absolute `knowledge_path` into the *worktree-resident* context file while preserving `schema_version`; `auto_scaffold: false` does nothing; `enabled: false` does nothing; idempotent across two pickups; a missing context file is non-fatal.
- `cmd/nightgauge/knowledge_scaffold_root_test.go` (new, 2 tests): the CLI verb anchors at the main checkout when `--workdir` is a worktree; outside a repo it uses the given workdir rather than failing.
- `internal/config/knowledge_test.go` (extend, 3 tests): the `IsAutoScaffold` truth table the docs publish.

**Mutation-checked** — removing the `MainCheckoutRoot` call turns three of the five scheduler tests red on the assertion that nothing landed in the worktree:

```
--- FAIL: TestScaffoldKnowledgeAtPickup_LandsAtCanonicalRootNotTheWorktree
--- FAIL: TestScaffoldKnowledgeAtPickup_IsIdempotent
--- FAIL: TestScaffoldKnowledgeAtPickup_MissingContextFileIsNonFatal
```

## Verification

`grep -rn 'knowledge scaffold' skills/nightgauge-issue-pickup claude-plugins/nightgauge/skills/issue-pickup` returns only the manual-use documentation, no invocation.

`docs/KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md` now states where the scaffold lands, who creates it, why the path is absolute, and that `auto_scaffold` defaults to on.

`bash scripts/ci-local.sh` — all CI-parity checks passed, 7m4s.

author: mstarks01
body:
Closes #443. Related: #410, #412.

About half of every ASVS run is a not-applicable ruling, and for most of them the model has no ground to cite, so it cites a quote that verifies and says nothing (#412). Where the predicate is the whole test, a rule that fired nowhere is the fact.

`PresenceTest` gains `decides_chapter`, set only on the four tests whose chapter presupposes the thing the terms name: file upload (V5), self-contained tokens (V9), OAuth and OIDC (V10), WebRTC (V17). `ruled_out_requirements` returns the chapter's requirements at the level when such a test fires on no element, with the rule named in the reason. A neutral hook, `Claim.ruled_out(model, options, lane)`, carries it: `prepare` calls it per lane, the scope line tells the agent which units were ruled out and not to rule on them, `assemble` hands the map to `scope_entries`, and each becomes a `not-applicable` scope entry. `NEUTRAL_HOOKS` names the hook so an orphaned override fails.

Corpus01 at level 2 rules out 52 of 253 requirements this way. Those 52 no longer reach the lane's output or the critic's single pass, which is the volume half of #410.

`authentication` and `sessions` are deliberately not deciding: a silent model may still have them.

## Framework parity

STRIDE: inherits the neutral `ruled_out`, which rules nothing out — its claims are not a catalog, so no unit is ruled out by a rule that did not fire. The scope line and `scope_entries` read the hook's result and never a package name.

## Verification

Full suite: 3899 passed. `ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy` clean.

author: christophercastrop
body:
Auditoría del **Módulo 5 — Core BPO y dominio operativo**. Los 9 hallazgos críticos se verificaron contra el código antes de tocar nada, con prueba de sensibilidad (mutación → rojo por el motivo esperado → revertir → verde) en cada uno. Los 5 huecos arquitectónicos de menor severidad también se cierran, salvo uno que queda planteado, no inventado.

## Hallazgos críticos (9/9 cerrados)

1. **`ObtenerRolDelegadoAsync` fallaba abierto** — sin una `AsignacionOperadorDelegado` vigente y exacta, cualquier usuario del tenant operador con una operación externa vigente heredaba `GestorCae` por un `?? Roles.GestorCae`. Ahora falla cerrado.
2. **`ReasignarEjecutivoClienteCommand` sin validar candidato** — cerrado como consecuencia directa del fix 1: la ruta cruzada de tenant ya no puede completarse con un candidato no autorizado.
3. **Responsable de cliente único por operación, no global** — dos reasignaciones concurrentes hacia operaciones distintas podían dejar dos operadores con acceso simultáneo. Índice único global + migración que cierra duplicados heredados antes de crearlo + 23505 traducido a conflicto legible.
4. **IDOR de escritura en Proyecto** — Actualizar/Cerrar/Eliminar/Asignar/DesasignarTecnicoProyecto solo dependían del filtro de tenant, no de la cartera del actor.
5. **Altas sin autoridad sobre lo referenciado** — CrearCentro/CrearTrabajador/CrearProyecto comprobaban existencia, no autoridad de cartera sobre cliente/empresa/empleador.
6. **"Secuestro" de trabajador entre carteras** — CrearAsignacion(es)Command exigía autoridad sobre el centro pero no sobre el trabajador.
7. **Auditoría de borrado falsificable** — 9 comandos de borrado recibían `UsuarioId` en el contrato público; todo llamador hacía `?? Guid.Empty`. La identidad se resuelve ahora vía `ICurrentUserService`, abortando sin ella.
8. **Restaurar sin autoridad** — Restaurar{Centro,Trabajador,Cliente,Empresa}Command solo comprobaban `TenantId` vía `IgnoreQueryFilters()`.
9. **Anonimizar Dni bloqueaba la purga de retención** — `Trabajador.Anonimizar` dejaba `Dni=''`, y el índice único sin filtro impedía anonimizar un segundo trabajador del mismo tenant en la misma transacción (`EjecucionPurgaService` guarda el lote entero de una vez). `Dni` pasa a nullable con índice parcial.

## Huecos arquitectónicos (5/6 cerrados)

- CHECK `EmpresaId XOR SubcontrataId` en Trabajador.
- FK compuesta Proyecto→Centro que incluye ClienteId (contra nueva clave alternativa de Centro).
- Detección de ciclos en RelacionEmpresarial: de hasta 50 consultas secuenciales a una consulta recursiva (`WITH RECURSIVE`).
- `ProyectoTecnico` gana `Version` (concurrencia optimista) sin heredar soft delete — mismo patrón que `AsignacionOperacion`/`AsignacionCartera`.
- Ratchet que falla en CI si el catálogo semilla de `TipoDocumento` renombra alguno de los cuatro nombres que `CrearCentroCommand` usa para el catálogo mínimo de un Centro nuevo.
- **Pendiente de decisión de producto** (no implementado): si la cronología de `Asignacion` tiene valor legal, protegerla con `daterange` + restricción de exclusión de PostgreSQL. No se ha inventado la decisión.

## Coordinación

Tres colisiones de fichero con otras sesiones del mismo barrido de auditoría, todas resueltas: `VerificacionIdsAjenosTests.cs` (Módulo 7, zonas distintas), `EjecucionPurgaTests.cs` (Módulo 2, conflicto de merge real resuelto conservando ambas partes), y el patrón de `UsuarioId` falsificable avisado a Módulo 2/6/3 para su propio alcance.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` en 0 errores para toda la solución tras cada incremento
- [x] Cada hallazgo crítico con prueba de sensibilidad (mutación adversaria → rojo por el motivo esperado → revertir → verde)
- [x] Migraciones con paso de limpieza de datos heredados antes de crear el índice/constraint nuevo, verificado con test dedicado sembrando el esquema anterior
- [x] `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` limpio
- [x] Suites de Postgres reales afectadas verificadas en aislamiento (los 9 fallos vistos en una corrida amplia de 145 tests fueron contención del clúster Postgres compartido con otras sesiones activas — confirmado re-ejecutando los mismos tests en aislamiento, verdes)

author: eldastito
body:
## Contexto

Depois de ver dados errados no **Fechamento diário** (cota fantasma na Av. Brasil num domingo de folga; "Informado" R$ 6.086 lançado no Carioca), o lojista pediu duas coisas: **excluir** o fechamento errado e uma **trava** pra não informar em loja fechada.

## O que muda

**1. Trava — loja fechada no dia não recebe fechamento (CLOSE‑002)**
`isStoreClosedOnDate` = há escala no dia e **ninguém `work`** (folga geral). Guard aplicado no **informar manual**, no **detalhado** e na **foto/IA** — bloqueia com mensagem clara. Loja **sem escala** lançada no dia **não trava** (mesma regra da trava da cota, QUOTA‑002). Isso evita o tipo de lançamento errado que gerou o "Informado" do Carioca.

**2. Excluir fechamento (CLOSE‑003)**
Botão de **lixeira** na coluna Ações do fechamento. Apaga o fechamento (status/informado/itens) **e a cota do dia** daquela loja. Como a coluna **"Cota"** da tela vem do **snapshot do fechamento** (`c.quota_amount`), excluir **faz a cota errada sumir da tela** (vira "—") e **não ressuscita** ao reinformar.
- Endpoint `DELETE /api/retailops/closings/:id` (owner/admin).
- `/inform` e `/scan` agora devolvem **400** com a mensagem da trava (antes `/inform` estourava 500).

## Como isso resolve a tela do cliente

- **Carioca (Rejeitado, Informado 6.086)** → clicar na **lixeira** apaga o fechamento e a cota do dia.
- **Av. Brasil (cota 4.990 num domingo de folga)** → mesma lixeira limpa a cota da tela.
- Daqui pra frente, ninguém consegue **informar** numa loja de folga geral (a IA/foto e o manual barram).

## Teste

`scripts/test-retail-closing-guard-delete.ts` (novo, **13/13**): trava bloqueia loja fechada (manual + detalhado), loja aberta/sem‑escala informam normal, `remove` apaga fechamento + itens + cota do dia. Regressão `test:retail-closing` 16/16, `test:retail-closing-detailed` 28/28.

## Validação

- `npm run lint` (tsc --noEmit) ✅
- `npm run build` ✅

## Observação

A trava depende da **escala do dia estar lançada** (com as folgas). Se a loja não tem escala lançada naquele dia, o sistema não bloqueia (pra não travar à toa) — casa com a importação da escala por foto (#1465).

author: gently-whitesnow
body:
Закрывает #4.

## Что было

Порция ревью была одновременно единицей **чтения** и единицей **отправки**. Срез больше 20 карточек
скил велит резать на порции — и каждая порция стоила человеку отдельного сабмита, а агенту
отдельного пробуждения. Решения жили в локальной мапе вида (`ui/app.js`), поэтому переключение
раздела в сайдбаре их теряло.

На полевом прогоне (срез `event-graph` = 51 факт) это встало ребром: агент разбил срез на три
порции по типам объектов схемы, и человек резонно спросил, почему сабмита три.

## Что стало

Порция — единица чтения. Отправка отвязана от неё.

- **Черновик решений** живёт вне вида: память вкладки + `localStorage`, ключ включает `fingerprint`
  порции. Переживает переход между разделами и перезагрузку страницы; перепуш порции меняет
  `fingerprint`, так что черновик старой версии к новым фактам не подхватывается. Отправленный
  черновик удаляется.
- **«Отправить всё (N)»** — появляется, когда человека ждёт больше одной порции. Одно решение
  `review_bulk` на все порции в статусе `ready`, включая те, где человек ничего не решил (их
  `decisions` пуст — факты остаются кандидатами, ровно как при порционной отправке без решений).
- **«Только эту порцию»** — прежний `review`, вторичной кнопкой. Нужен, когда остальные срезы ещё
  извлекаются, а готовое хочется отдать сразу.

Формат аддитивный, старый `review` не тронут:

```json
{"stage":"review","type":"review_bulk","data":{
  "batches": {
    "event-graph-jobs": {"fingerprint":"1q2w3e","decisions":{"fact:jf-0003":{"action":"approve"}},"global_comment":""},
    "event-graph-deps": {"fingerprint":"4r5t6y","decisions":{"fact:jd-0019":{"action":"reject","comment":"так задумано"}},"global_comment":""}
  },
  "global_comment": ""
}}
```

`batchSent` понимает обе формы, так что «уже отправлено» переживает перезагрузку в любом режиме.

## Документация

- `SKILL.md` (B3): правило «одна порция — один срез» переписано — порция это единица чтения,
  большой срез режется по смыслу (естественный шов — тип объекта схемы), и дробление больше не
  стоит лишних сабмитов.
- `SKILL.md` (B4): в разбор `await` добавлен `type: review_bulk`.
- `ui-protocol.md`: формат `review_bulk`, поведение черновика, когда шелл шлёт какую форму.

## Проверка

Демо-workdir с тремя порциями (`module-graph` 3 ждут, `event-graph` 5 ждут, `data-ownership` 0):

- решения проставлены в двух порциях, переход между разделами и полный reload их сохранили —
  прогресс и подсветка карточек восстановились;
- «Отправить всё (3)» записало в `decisions.jsonl` **одну** строку `review_bulk` с тремя порциями
  (2 решения / 1 решение / 0 решений);
- после отправки черновики из `localStorage` удалены, все три порции в сайдбаре помечены
  «отправлено».

Серверная часть не менялась: `push`, `await` и `decisions.jsonl` работают как раньше — это
обычное решение, просто одно на несколько порций.

author: jdolan
body:
Follows #1013. Jay's proposal: the standing box belongs in `CS_CLIENTS` beside model, skin and colour.

- Server: `G_ClientStandingBounds` (the client's `params.bounds` once they have moved, the level's before) is published as an eighth field, `floor/ceiling`, from `G_ClientUserInfoChanged`; `G_ClientEndFrame` republishes when it changes (a movement switch, a mod's class assignment). `g_client_persistent_t.standing_bounds` remembers what was published; no republish loop, since `G_MovementParams` and `G_PlayerBounds` draw from the same source.
- Client: `Cg_LoadClient` accepts 7 or more fields (surplus ignored, so the next field does not undress everyone), parses the eighth into `standing_floor`/`standing_ceiling` with a plausibility clamp (16..128 tall) and a warning; absent, `PM_BOUNDS`. `Cg_AddClientEntity` scales the rig by the box's height and seats it on the box's *floor* (not `PM_BOUNDS`'s, so a movement with a different `mins.z` is right too). `Cg_IsDucking` compares against the entity's own client info instead of the local player's params.
- The race ghost stores the live `CS_CLIENTS` string in its `.ghost`, so new records carry the holder's box; existing `.ghost` files have seven fields and draw the ghost at 60 until beaten - cosmetic.
- An older client (pre-change cgame, exact-7 check) would reject the 8-field string and fall back to `newbie/qforcer` for everyone; the 1.0.85 protocol bump covers that.

Verified: all modules incl. race build clean; `make check` 20/20; `racetest` and `edge` load headlessly. Read-only review applied (floor published, not just height; surplus fields tolerated; clamp). Not run under a renderer.

author: tanakakao
body:
## Summary

Enable acquisition-aware composition Best Subset search from the React/FastAPI Web workbench when the fitted surrogate uses CLR, ALR, or ILR composition coordinates.

Element presence is never inferred from transformed coordinate zeros. Web candidate search now preserves the #720 two-space contract:

- **support / decision space:** exact raw composition fractions
- **surrogate / acquisition space:** Fraction, CLR, ALR, or ILR model coordinates

## What changed

- Remove the Web-only Fraction restriction for composition `support_selection="best_subset"`.
- Adapt Web `final_candidate_postprocess` for raw-space search: process variables may still be clamped/rounded/fixed, while raw composition fractions remain authoritative.
- Mark CLR/ALR/ILR model coordinates as postprocess passthrough dimensions so the second Web postprocess cannot clamp away a structural-zero candidate.
- Preserve exact raw Best Subset fractions when building response formula/fraction columns instead of reconstructing support from pseudocount log-ratio coordinates.
- Perform candidate uniqueness checks in the raw decision layout when raw composition candidates are available.
- Include `support_space="raw_fraction"` in composition response metadata for Best Subset runs.

## Element constraints

Element-level linear constraints are now resolved to synthetic raw fraction decision features for CLR/ALR/ILR Best Subset search. This means constraints are optimized jointly with support selection rather than being applied as a post-hoc repair that could change the chosen support.

The existing fixed-total / exact-cardinality / continuous-fraction restrictions remain unchanged.

## Compatibility

- Existing Fraction Best Subset behavior is unchanged.
- Existing CLR/ALR/ILR `repair` behavior is unchanged.
- q-batch continues to use one shared element support.
- One-shot acquisition restrictions from #720 remain unchanged.

## Tests

- CLR/ALR/ILR Web Best Subset settings are accepted and transported through the typed API.
- Log-ratio composition model coordinates are registered as Web postprocess passthrough dimensions.
- Model-space final candidate postprocessing changes ordinary process variables but preserves exact raw support and structural zeros.
- Element constraints resolve to raw fraction decision features for CLR/ALR/ILR Best Subset.
- Composition smoke now runs and lints the Web composition integration files and tests.

author: simoleolife
body:
## What

Two things, both needed before a hotel event announcement renders correctly.

**A notification can ask to be closed.** `showNotification` now reads a
`timeout` in seconds from the notification's options - sent by the emulator, or
set in `ui-config`'s `notification` block - and passes it down to the alert.
`LayoutNotificationAlertView` starts a countdown and calls `onClose` when it runs
out. Every existing notification is unaffected: without a `timeout` the alert
waits for the user exactly as before.

The close callback is held in a ref, so the countdown depends only on the delay.
`GetAlertLayout` builds a fresh `onClose` closure whenever the alert list
changes, and without the ref a second notification arriving would hand the first
one another full delay.

**The hotel event texts exist.** `notification.hotel.event.title`, `.message`,
`.linkTitle` and the `.ended` pair are added to the English and the Italian
`UITexts` files. Nothing localised them, so the client fell back to the
localisation key and drew `notification.hotel.event.title` as the window title
and `notification.hotel.event.message` as the body.

The `.message` texts interpolate the placeholders the server sends - `%USERNAME%`,
`%ROOMNAME%`, `%TIME%`, `%MESSAGE%` - and `.linkTitle` names the button that
`OpenUrl` turns into `navigator/goto/<roomId>`.

## Verification

- `yarn test --run` - 1112 tests / 208 files pass, including six new ones: three
  on the delay parsing (`getAutoCloseSeconds`) and three on the countdown itself,
  covering the delay elapsing, no delay given, and an alert unmounted before the
  timer fires.
- `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:hooks`, `yarn build` - all clean.
- Both `UITexts` files parse as JSON after comment stripping, with `\r\r` kept as
  a JSON escape rather than a raw control character.

CI pins Node 22 and this machine runs Node 26, so the local run is weaker than
the workflow.

## Risk

`timeoutSeconds` is optional throughout - on `NotificationAlertItem`, on
`simpleAlert`, on the layout - and defaults to null, which is the current
behaviour. The only notification that sends one today is the hotel event.

author: xaviergriffon
body:
Documentation seule — aucun code touché.

## Pourquoi cette section

Les §4.x mesurent chaque piste **contre l'état qui la précède**, ce qui est la bonne méthode (§6 : « les gains ne s'additionnent pas, chaque PR doit être mesurée par-dessus la précédente »). Mais le corollaire n'était écrit nulle part : **ce que vaut la série cumulée ne se déduit pas de ces mesures** et doit être mesuré séparément, aux deux extrémités.

§4.13 le fait pour la série A (§4.7) / B (§4.1) / D (§4.12) : deux worktrees, compilés séparément, exécutés en alternance.

## Résultats

**Débit** (`bench_search.sh`, 5 M nœuds, 3 rondes alternées × 7 répétitions) : **858 856 → 922 881 nœuds/s, +7,64 %**, `max_result` inchangé à 190.

**Coût de réfutation** (stock de production, 433 racines ≥ 130 pièces, budget 2 M nœuds) :

| | Avant | Après | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sous-arbres fermés | 383 / 433 | **387 / 433** | +4, aucun perdu |
| Nœuds (383 racines communes) | 35 327 545 | 33 105 827 | **−6,29 %** |
| Temps (383 racines communes) | 41,2–41,5 s | 37,9 s | **−7,9 à −8,8 %** |

Le nombre de nœuds est identique **au chiffre près** entre les deux rondes : la fermeture est déterministe, ces −6,29 % ne comportent aucun bruit.

## Les deux pièges, qui sont l'essentiel de la valeur

**La ligne « comparaison appariée » du banc n'agrège pas la même population entre deux binaires.** Elle porte sur *les racines fermées par ce run*. Avant en ferme 383, après 387 : lues telles quelles, ces deux lignes annoncent « après = +10 % de nœuds », soit **l'inverse de la vérité**. Les chiffres publiés viennent d'une intersection explicite des racines fermées des deux côtés. Comparer deux *moteurs* dans un même run ne pose pas ce problème — le banc intersecte lui-même ; comparer deux *binaires* l'exige. C'est un piège que j'ai failli publier.

**Le gain par nœud ne se transporte pas d'un régime à l'autre.** +7,6 % sur la recherche depuis la genèse, mais seulement **≈ 2,2 %** par nœud sur les racines profondes du stock. Cohérent : A et B attaquent des coûts proportionnels à la taille de la frontière et des compartiments, tous deux bien plus petits à 130+ pièces posées que sur un plateau presque vide. **`bench_search.sh` surestime donc ce que gagne le travail réellement servi** — à savoir avant d'extrapoler un gain de débit en gain de production.

## Aussi consigné

- le registre de la série, refus compris : suppression du forward-check (+15,90 % de temps sans lui), cumul local des compteurs (+1,00 %, écarté), backjumping dirigé par conflit (gain nul à 100,00 %) ;
- une réserve de portée : une seule machine, sans épinglage — les deltas appariés à ordre alterné sont robustes, les valeurs absolues de nœuds/s ne sont pas transposables ;
- un renvoi depuis §6, là où la règle « mesurer par-dessus la précédente » est énoncée, puisque c'est elle qui rend cette section nécessaire.

## Vérifications

`make test` : 1346 + 1330 tests verts. Aucun fichier de code modifié.

body:
## 概要

公開前の使いやすさ・復旧性に加え、学習者名をキーにした学習状態のSupabase同期を追加します。既存の麻雀ルール、役、点数計算、教材順、問題の正解、牌デザイン、対局ロジックは変更していません。

## 問題と原因

- 入口が大きな1ページに集まり、現在の経路と次の操作が分かりにくかった。
- 名前入力がなく、学習開始時の利用者と学習状態の対応が明確でなかった。
- 学習記録を別端末へ引き継ぐ仕組みがなかった。
- 麻雀用語の読み方が本文の見た目・読み上げの両方で不足していた。
- 牌姿が横スクロール前提で、スマートフォンで手牌を把握しにくかった。
- ページごとに戻る導線や次の問題へ進んだときのスクロール位置が不統一だった。
- 通信失敗時に画面内で再試行できない経路があった。
- Pagesにアップロードするファイルと、公開前ブラウザ検査対象を一致させる保証が弱かった。

## 変更内容

- 名前入力付きホーム、メニュー、学ぶ段階別一覧を追加。
- public.wakaranjan_learning_profiles を追加し、名前キーで教材進捗・問題正答/誤答・復習待ち・勘違い分類を同期。
- 同じ名前は意図的に同じ学習状態を共有し、回答・教材完了・解除が同じ記録へ反映されるようにした。別の名前は別記録になる。
- 名前だけで識別する仕様のため、同じ名前を使う利用者は記録を変更・解除できることを画面と文書に明記。
- 学習記録画面に「この名前の学習状況を解除」を追加し、端末とSupabaseの学習状態を初期化。ゲームスコアはこの表へ保存せず、既存のスコア管理とは分離。
- Supabaseのpublishable keyだけをブラウザへ配布し、service role/secret keyは使用しない。テーブルのRLS、anon/authenticatedの必要権限、SQL migrationを追加。
- 通信失敗時は端末内の記録で継続し、学習記録画面からSupabase同期を再試行できるようにした。保存はデバウンスし、連打による多重保存を抑止。
- メニューから「学ぶ」「初級」などの段階、問題集、対局練習、模擬東風戦、点数計算、用語・役、学習記録、設定へ分岐。
- 用語・役名をデータからカタカナのrubyとして表示。点数計算の表示牌・自分の河の入力欄は通常のlabelで関連付け。
- 問題集の牌姿を7列グリッドにして、320px幅でも横スワイプ不要に変更。
- 共通の「戻る」「メニュー」ツールバー、パンくず、次問題時の先頭復帰を追加。
- スキップリンクをルート遷移から分離し、main#appへフォーカス・スクロール。
- 初期JSON・教材JSON失敗時の画面内「もう一度読み込む」を追加。連打時の重複取得を防止。
- faviconを明示し、Pages生成スクリプトへ新CSSを含めた。
- PR用とPages公開前用で同じ tests/e2e-smoke.js と共有Actionsを使用。生成した同じ _site をブラウザ検査後にアップロードする構成に整理。
- GitHub設定文書・公開チェックリスト・データモデル文書を実装と一致させた。

## 変更しなかったもの

麻雀の標準ルール、採用役、点数計算ルール、教材の学習順、問題の正解、既存カリキュラム、牌デザイン、ゲームスコア保存処理、ランキング、アカウント、課金、広告、バックエンド機能の新規導入は変更していません。

## 自動検査

- npm test: 成功
  - 既存ロジック・点数計算・教材・問題・対局進行テスト
  - プロフィール破損・旧形式移行・名前別進捗分離
  - Supabase同期の防御的正規化、名前キーupsert、保存のデバウンス、リモート反映、学習状態解除

author: dakulefsky
body:
Adds lightweight, privacy-friendly feed personalization without weakening deal quality.

- category interest increases when a shopper saves a deal, opens it, or spends meaningful time on its card
- saves carry the strongest signal; clicks are medium; passive dwell is deliberately weaker
- personalization only reorders the already quality-ranked approved feed
- interests stay in local browser storage; no new behavioral profile is sent to the server
- scores are capped to prevent one category from permanently dominating
- shoppers can reset recommendations
- adds regression coverage for weighting and quality-first ranking

This is intentionally a first-stage recommendation loop; progressive/infinite feed integration remains separate.

author: nipunrautela
body:
## What this does

Gives every package a changeset, and makes the gate CONTRIBUTING.md promised a
real one. One changeset existed, for the schema primitives; eight publishable
packages built since would have reached a first release with a changelog that
said nothing about them. A dry run of `changeset version` puts all nine at
0.1.0 and reads correctly.

CI now runs `changeset status --since=origin/main`, which needs `fetch-depth: 0`
because changesets resolves the merge base. That command fails a pull request
that adds no changeset at all and has no per-package mode, so CONTRIBUTING.md
says exactly that rather than claiming a stronger gate. `*.test.ts`,
`*.test.tsx` and `*.harness.ts` are excluded: this repository has genuine
test-only commits, and demanding an empty changeset for each is the box-ticking
that argued against the gate in the first place.

Writing the changesets surfaced a defect. `keepcv` is public and depended on
private `@keepcv/web`, resolving the web assets through it at runtime. Published,
that installs a dependency no registry has, and serves a 404 for its own
interface. The built app is now copied into the launcher's own `dist/web` at
build time, `@keepcv/web` is a devDependency, and `react`/`react-dom` are gone -
nothing under `apps/cli/src` imports either.

## Which felt pain does this trace to?

Career history is only safe if it can leave the machine it is on, and that means
the launcher has to install and run. It did not: the package was broken in a way
no test could see, because no test built the artifact.

## Declared non-goals

No release workflow and no publishing. Nothing is published by this change and
no npm credentials are involved. Package READMEs still say "there is no release
yet", which remains true - changesets record intent, they do not bump versions.

## Definition of Complete

- [x] Unit and integration tests, plus one end-to-end path
- [x] Docs updated; an architecture decision recorded if one was made
- [x] A changeset, or a deliberate empty one
- [x] No TODOs, no feature flags left enabled, no commented-out code

## Verification

- `pnpm check` green: 29 tasks, 473 files linted.
- `pnpm pack` on the launcher: eight files under `package/dist/web/`, and the
  published `dependencies` contain only packages that publish.
- The built launcher served the entry document, a hashed asset and a client
  route from the new location.
- Mutation: putting the old runtime resolve back fails the web-assets test and
  only that one.
- Mutation: with the changesets moved aside and `--since=HEAD`, a clean tree and
  a changed test file both exit 0; a changed source file exits 1.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exits 0, so CI's install step will not fail.

author: mike-diff
body:
Fixes #32

## Problem

`hooks/post-edit-lint.sh` could inject fabricated lint errors into context:

1. **No "is eslint this project's linter" gate** — the hook ran `node_modules/.bin/eslint` whenever it existed, so a transitively installed eslint in a Biome/oxlint project was mistaken for the project's linter.
2. **No project-scope check** — an edit to a session scratchpad outside the repo triggered the project's linter against it.
3. **Extension gating used a global "non-code" blocklist** — wrong in principle: what counts as lintable is stack-relative (Biome lints `.astro`/`.json`/`.css`), so a static denylist is forever incomplete and mislabels real code files.

The issue's primary repro (`npm run lint -- --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern` eval'd onto Biome) targets v0.3.0 and was already gone on main; the defects above remained.

## Design

The hook is an opportunistic file-scoped linter, not a taxonomy engine. Lintability is decided per linter the hook can actually drive, never globally:

- **Opt-in**: eslint runs only when declared in `package.json` *and* an eslint config file exists; ruff only with `ruff.toml` / `[tool.ruff]`; flake8 only with `[flake8]` config. A PATH-present or transitively installed linter the project never configured is never invoked.
- **Project's own binary only**: no `command -v eslint` global fallback — a global eslint of a different major misreads the project's config. Not installed means skip; the verify gate covers it.
- **Per-linter file domain**: eslint gets `js mjs cjs jsx ts tsx` always; `vue svelte astro` only under **flat config** (`eslint.config.*`), where an uncovered file degrades to warn + exit 0. Verified that a legacy `.eslintrc` parse-errors an uncovered SFC (rc 1) — surfacing that would be a false finding, so legacy configs lint plain extensions only. ruff/flake8: `py`; go vet: `go` + manifests.
- **Out-of-project edits skipped** (absolutized + normalized against `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`/CWD).
- **No hook-side ignore lists**: ignore semantics belong to the linter's own config, and only rc 1 output is surfaced — warning noise never reaches the model.
- Projects whose linter the hook can't drive (Biome) get deliberate silence; the phase-end verify gate runs their real `pnpm lint`.
- **clippy dropped**: cargo exits 0 for warnings and 101 for errors — never 1 — so the rc gate meant clippy output could never reach the model while every `.rs`/manifest edit paid a whole-crate compile. Rust feedback stays with the verify gate. (go vet kept: it does exit 1 on findings.)

`.cursor/hooks/post-edit-lint.sh` (separate Cursor-native implementation) carries the same gates in its own idiom; `plugins/agent-team/hooks/post-edit-lint.sh` is the byte-identical sync of canonical.

## Tests

22 unit cases in `tests/hooks-contract.sh` (shim-based fixtures, no toolchain needed):

- crafted `$(touch …)` path executes nothing (the old injection test passed vacuously; its fixture now declares + configures eslint so the argv path actually runs)
- Biome-shaped project: stray `node_modules/.bin/eslint` never invoked
- eslint declared but no config → never invoked; PATH eslint never substitutes for a missing local install
- legacy `.eslintrc`: `.ts` lints, `.vue` doesn't (verified against real eslint 8: parse error, rc 1)
- findings surfaced via `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`; rc >= 2 tool failure never surfaced
- out-of-project edit skipped; `html css scss svg md json` out of eslint's domain; `vue`/`astro` routed under flat config
- ruff gated on `[tool.ruff]` opt-in; go vet gated to `go`/manifests
- **parity enforced by test**: plugin hook must stay byte-identical to canonical, and the Cursor port's `find_eslint_config` must match it — drift now fails the suite instead of relying on editor discipline

## Verification

- `./tests/hooks-contract.sh`: 22/22 unit tests PASS; LIVE test fails on the local `claude` OAuth expiry (env issue, exercises `block-dangerous`, not this hook)
- `./tests/workflow-contract.sh`, `./tests/codex-workflow-contract.sh`, full `bash -n` set, `git diff --check`: clean
- `COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=60 ./tests/smoke.sh`: 0/11 — all cases fail on the same expired-login auth error (environmental; suite was green before the login lapsed)
- End-to-end smoke: calcs-prj replica (Astro 6 + React + Biome + pnpm, stray eslint binary planted) — `.astro`/`.json`/`.ts` edits and an out-of-tree scratchpad `.html` all emit zero context; a Vue project with flat-configured eslint surfaces the real `.vue` finding inline

author: katonid
body:
**Gemeldet:** Auf einem Gerät stehen zwei Tafeln namens „Kroko" — eine mit
13 Elementen, eine mit allen Seiten und ohne Inhalt — dazu eine dritte,
leere. Beide Geräte benutzen dieselbe Apple ID.

Der Auftrag „Übersetzen (iOS-Simulator)" ist **grün**.

## Was ich geprüft habe

- **`applyRemote` legt eine Tafel nur an, wenn ihre Kennung unbekannt ist.**
  Eine ankommende Tafel mit bekannter Kennung wird zusammengeführt, nie
  danebengestellt.
- **Alle Wege, die eine Kopie anlegen, vergeben neue Kennungen**:
  `duplicateBoard` (hängt „(Kopie)" an), `alsEigeneUebernehmen` und
  „Sicherung einlesen" (beide behalten den Namen).
- Die **Beispieltafel** heißt „Meine Klasse" und scheidet als Erklärung aus.
- Eine per **Freigabe** empfangene Tafel wird nicht neu angelegt, sondern
  nur in `ownBoardIDs` eingetragen.

## Was ich nicht sagen kann

Welcher dieser Wege es war. Dafür fehlen die Kennungen, Zeitstempel und
Herkünfte — und die liegen auf dem Gerät. Eine plausibel klingende
Geschichte wäre hier billig und womöglich falsch.

## Deshalb: die Liste

„Abgleich prüfen" zeigt jetzt einen Abschnitt **„Tafeln auf diesem Gerät"**
— je Zeile Name, die ersten acht Zeichen der Kennung, Elemente, Seiten,
Herkunft (eigene / Gast / fremder Bereich / geteilt / gelöscht) und die
letzte Änderung, dazu „Liste kopieren".

Zwei Zeilen mit demselben Namen und **verschiedenen** Kennungen sind zwei
verschiedene Tafeln. Der Fußtext sagt das und warnt ausdrücklich: Löschen
wirkt auf allen Geräten und in iCloud.

## Vorbeugend dazu

`BoardStore.entdoppelt` legt beim Laden Tafeln mit **derselben** Kennung
zusammen (neuerer Zeitstempel gewinnt, bei Gleichstand mehr Inhalt). So ein
Fall ist **nicht nachgewiesen** — aber er wäre still und dauerhaft: Nur die
erste Tafel einer Kennung bekäme je eine Änderung ab, weil jede Suche über
`firstIndex` geht.

---

`MARKETING_VERSION` 1.3.26 → **1.3.27**.

**Nächster Schritt:** die Liste von beiden Geräten. Erst daran ist zu
sehen, ob es zwei verschiedene Tafeln sind oder dieselbe zweimal — und was
dann zu reparieren ist.

author: harrylettering
body:
Carries the two commits that were pushed to #4's branch after it had already merged, so they never reached `main`. Nothing here is in `main` today — `src/compaction/compactor.ts` still passes `--bare` in two places.

Both problems share the shape #4 was about: **the code reports what it attempted, not what happened.**

---

## 1. Every LLM-backed feature is dead, and none of them say so

All four spawn sites — compaction summaries, the query planner, the decision supersede judge, expansion delegation — pass `--bare`. The intent was sound: `--bare` skips hooks, and a child that replays our own SessionStart starts a second daemon against the same database.

But `--bare` also stops the CLI reading the keychain, and documents that Anthropic auth is then *strictly* `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an apiKeyHelper. Anyone signed in through OAuth — every subscription user — gets exit code 1 on every call:

```
$ printf 'Say OK' | claude --bare --print --output-format text
exit=1   stdout: "Not logged in · Please run /login"

$ printf 'Say OK' | claude --print --output-format text
exit=0   stdout: "OK"
```

The CLI prints that refusal **on stdout with an empty stderr**, and all four sites report stderr alone. Every failure therefore logs as `exited with code 1: ` — the one line that explains it is read and thrown away. On a real database that happened 35 consecutive times without a single legible message.

Compaction degrades gracefully into truncation fallbacks, so nothing surfaced. The result: 35 raw 14400-character transcript blobs stored as summaries and dual-written into `memory_nodes`, so retrieval was injecting raw transcript labelled as summary.

**Fix.** `--bare` is replaced with `CODEMEMORY_CHILD`, set on the spawned environment and checked by all six hook scripts, which stand down when they see it. Recursion stays prevented; authentication works. A new `src/llm/claude-cli.ts` holds the shared args, env and failure description so the four sites cannot drift apart again.

Two things fall out of the shared helper:

- **`--no-session-persistence`** is now passed. Without it the child writes a transcript into `~/.claude/projects/`, which our own JSONL watcher then ingests as if it were the user's conversation. `--bare` never prevented this either.
- **Failure reporting falls back to stdout** when stderr is empty, so a refusal to start is legible instead of blank.

## 2. Condensation announces success before doing the work

`runCondensation` logs `condensing N leaves into M condensed summary/ies` *before* the loop, then skips every batch that falls below `minFanout`. On a real database that read as 62 leaves being condensed while `summary_parents` stayed empty and the DAG stayed flat.

**Fix.** The log moves after the loop and reports what was actually written, including how many batches were deferred. When every batch is skipped it warns with the numbers that explain it — leaf size, input window, leaves per batch — because that state is not transient: it repeats on every pass until a knob changes.

A construction-time check covers the configuration that makes condensation structurally impossible. The input window and the leaf size target are separate knobs that must satisfy `minFanout × leafTargetTokens ≤ min(condensedTargetTokens × 4, compactionMaxInputChars ÷ 4)`, and nothing enforced it. Defaults satisfy it (4 × 1200 = 4800 ≤ 6000), so the check is quiet unless the relationship is actually broken.

This is why the root cause hid so long: leaves were pinned at the 3600-token truncation cap rather than the 1200-token target, because of §1. Two leaves then exceeded the 6000-token window, so each batch held one leaf and all of them were discarded.

---

## Verification

- **290/290 tests pass** — 4 new, covering both halves of §2
- `dist/` rebuilt and committed (tracked here), and `npm run build` produces no further diff
- Live daemon, 890 messages ingested, one compaction run:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `claude --print` | 100% fail (`Not logged in`) | succeeds |
| summary size | every one pinned at 3600 tokens (truncation cap) | 173–539 tokens, real summaries |
| truncation fallbacks logged | 35 | **0** |

- Recursion guard verified by process count: `CODEMEMORY_CHILD=1 claude --print …` spawns no new daemon (2 → 2). All six hook scripts return a noop under it.

The new tests are deliberately shaped around how this hid for so long — one of them asserts that the number in the log matches the number of rows actually written to `summaries`.

author: nevenincs
body:
**The PyPI wait asks the wrong endpoint, and v0.1.69 caught it.**

`Wait for the release to reach PyPI` polls:

```
https://pypi.org/pypi/vaultspec-core/${version}/json
```

But the binary bootstraps with uv, which resolves against the **simple index** — a different surface with its own cache. So the wait can answer "present" from one endpoint while the installer cannot yet see the release on the other.

**v0.1.69 is the evidence.** The wait passed on all four legs; the installs then split:

```
acquire on Windows:               success
acquire on ubuntu:22.04:          success
acquire on macOS (Apple Silicon): FAILED — no version of vaultspec-core==0.1.69
acquire on debian:bookworm-slim:  FAILED — no version of vaultspec-core==0.1.69
```

One release, four runners, two edges that had it and two that did not — which is exactly what a per-surface CDN cache looks like, and not something a longer sleep fixes reliably.

This PR polls the simple index for the version's wheel in **all three** legs (both shell waits and the PowerShell one), so the wait tests the same surface the install will use.

Predicate checked both directions against live PyPI:

```
simple index contains vaultspec_core-0.1.69-   -> MATCH      (wait exits 0)
simple index contains vaultspec_core-9.9.99-   -> NO MATCH   (wait keeps polling, then fails)
```

`actionlint` clean.

**Disclosure:** `just lint` is red locally — `lychee` timing out on `https://typer.tiangolo.com/` in a `.vault/` ADR I did not touch (`0 Errors, 1 Timeouts`, now reproduced four times, and CI's lint passes on `main`). I gated the commit on the exit code this time, checked the failure was that same external timeout, and proceeded deliberately rather than by accident. Flagging it again rather than letting it pass silently.
