author: abdulsamed-cmd
body: Three alternative coupons in a row were built on Hangi Yarıda Daha Fazla Gol, all on "2." at 2.00, and the first two lost. The reader asked for it to stop. The market leaves `DAILY_COUPON_MARKETS` but stays settleable. Dropping a market says nothing about the legs already bought, and those still have to be decided or the coupons holding them can never close. A test covers exactly that: out of the pool, still graded. **The archive does not convict it.** Measured over 460 archived matches where the market was captured with a price and the match has a final score, "2." landed 48.5% against a 44.1% price — ahead of its own price, not behind it. The other two selections came in below theirs ("1." 27.0% against 30.1%, "Eşit" 24.6% against 25.8%). So the config comment records this removal as a preference rather than a measurement, in case a later reader is deciding whether to put it back. Worth naming, though nothing here acts on it: the reason it kept recurring is that the alternative coupon needs 2.00 or better, and this market offers exactly 2.00 on a single leg, so the search reaches it before any combination of cheaper legs. Verification: rebuilding today's coupon after the change produced `Ev Sahibi Alt/Üst 1.5: Üst` on Corinthians - Santos instead, with no leg from the dropped market. Tests: 284 pass, and the new test fails if the market is put back in the pool.

author: madrone77
body:
Two upgrade walls reported nothing. On the admin's paywall report they read as walls nobody had ever seen, rather than as walls with no data:

- `<UpgradeRequiredModal>` on `/alerts`
- `<UnlockWithProCard>` on `/support`

Both are the same component. The counter lived as a private callback inside `<ProTrialModal>`, so anything that does not open that modal had nothing to call.

## The change

`src/lib/paywall-counter.ts` now holds the request, and `ProTrialModal` calls it too. One implementation, one place to keep the `keepalive` that stops a CTA click being dropped as the page navigates to /signup, /plans or Stripe.

The card reports for both walls and `UpgradeRequiredModal` only passes context down, so the same view cannot be counted twice. It returns null while closed, so the card mounting is exactly the wall being shown.

- `/alerts` reports feature `alerts`, surface `alerts-page`
- `/support` reports feature `support`, surface `support-portal`

`support` had to join `NAG_FEATURES`: the counter route validates against that enum and drops what it does not recognise, so those reports would have posted and counted nothing. Added with the `/plans` callout copy the enum's contract asks for.

Two things the card had never done and now does: it writes the wall attribution cookie, so a signup or trial started from these walls lands under "Signups by wall" on the admin instead of nowhere, and it waits for the subscription tier to settle before counting an impression, so a free or paid viewer is not filed under signed out.

`feature` is typed as `NagFeatureId` on both the card and the modal, which is what would have caught this at the start.

## Verification

Ran the branch locally with a throwaway harness page, since removed. Impressions fire on mount, `cta_click` fires on both CTA branches, each with the right feature, surface and tier and with `keepalive: true`:

```
{"kind":"cta_click","feature":"alerts","surface":"alerts-page","viewer_tier":"anon"}
{"kind":"cta_click","feature":"support","surface":"support-portal","viewer_tier":"anon"}
```

Those POSTs return 500 locally because local env has no service key, which is also why nothing was written to production. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean.

Paired with madrone77/bluecaster#320, the admin page that reads these counts.

Note: `/support` redirects signed-out visitors to login, so that wall is only ever shown to signed-in free accounts. Its viewer column will read free, never signed out.

author: samoylenkodmitry
body:
## Summary

Bumps `cranpose` / `cranpose-core` / `cranpose-animation` / `cranpose-foundation` from 0.1.58 to 0.1.106, regenerating `Cargo.lock` in this same commit.

### `useState` -> `rememberMutableStateOf`

`useState` no longer exists in 0.1.106; the hook API is `remember` / `mutableStateOf` / `rememberMutableStateOf` / `derivedStateOf`. All 20 `useState(...)` call sites in `src/ui.rs` became `rememberMutableStateOf(...)`, checked individually rather than blind find/replace:

- Slot-keying is preserved: `rememberMutableStateOf` recreates once per composition slot, same as the old `useState`, and no call site moved across a conditional/loop boundary.
- `rememberMutableStateOf` requires `T: PartialEq` and opts into structural-equality skip-on-set — a real behavior difference from `useState`'s old always-notify policy. I checked every `.set()`/`.update()` call site touching these states: each one either already epsilon/equality-guards before writing (measured heights, "if changed" text tracking), or is a monotonically increasing counter, so the switch doesn't change observable behavior anywhere in this app.
- One exception: `preview_state` holds a `PreviewState { bitmap: ImageBitmap, .. }`, which is `Clone` but not `PartialEq`, so it can't use `rememberMutableStateOf`. It's `remember(|| mutableStateOf(PreviewState::placeholder())).with(|s| *s)` instead — spelling out remember+mutableStateOf reproduces the exact pre-0.1.106 `useState` semantics (recreated once per slot, every `set()` always notifies).

### `horizontal_scroll_guarded` — no equivalent in 0.1.106

`SessionQueuePanel`'s chip row used `horizontal_scroll_guarded(scroll_state, false, || false)`. With the guard hardcoded to `false`, this kept `ScrollState`'s layout/clip/max-value tracking while *permanently disabling* the modifier's own pointer-driven gesture, so the row's one custom `pointer_input` (drag-reorder + wheel-pan) was the only thing ever calling `scroll_state.scroll_to`.

cranpose-ui 0.1.106 removed the public guarded scroll variants — traced to the "framework ownership" cleanup that deleted public functions with no caller inside the Cranpose repo itself — and kept no replacement. `horizontal_scroll`/`vertical_scroll` always attach their built-in gesture now, and there's no public way to get the layout/measurement side alone.

I fell back to plain `.horizontal_scroll(scroll_state, false)` since it's required to compile and keeps the row scrollable, but **this is not behavior-preserving**: the row can now also react to raw drags as a built-in scroll gesture, competing with the custom drag-reorder handler exactly as the removed guard was written to prevent. Documented in a comment at the call site. This needs on-device verification of drag-reorder vs. drag-to-scroll before it ships — I don't have a way to test that headlessly in this repo.

### Fallout: `ScrollState`/`TextFieldState` gained `Copy`

Both were `Clone`-only (`Rc`-based) at 0.1.58; 0.1.106 made them `Copy`. That turned every existing `.clone()` on them into a `clippy::clone_on_copy` warning, and every `let x = x.clone();` prepared for a `move` closure into a `clippy::redundant_locals` warning once the clone was gone. Removed all of them (~60 sites, mechanical).

Also fixed two small pre-existing clippy warnings unrelated to the version bump (a `field_reassign_with_default` in a `draft.rs` test, `too_many_arguments` on `MetaFieldColumn`, annotated with `#[allow]`) since they were blocking a clean `-D warnings` run.

## Test plan

Ran locally (not relying on CI as the iteration loop):
- [x] `cargo build --release --locked` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --release --locked` — 36 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked --lib` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean

Not verified: on-device drag-reorder vs. drag-to-scroll interaction in `SessionQueuePanel` (see above) — recommend manual testing before merge.

author: collectrix
body:
## Defect

`art-91-ownership-50pct-aggregator.kernel.mjs`'s `aggregateOwnership()` used a
single-pass BFS with `visited` set at enqueue time, but `contributions[to]` is a
running sum over parallel ownership paths that can grow AFTER a node is
dequeued and expanded — the late increase never propagates to that node's
out-edges. Result: aggregate ownership was UNDER-reported, order-dependent on
`edges[]` serialization.

Audit's reproduction (4 nodes A(OFAC),B,C,D; edges A->B 20%, A->C 80%, C->B
40%, B->D 100%; true aggregate at D = 0.20 + 0.80x0.40 = 52%):
edges B-first -> D=20%, `blocked_under=[]` (NOT blocked, WRONG);
edges C-first -> D=52%, `blocked_under=["OFAC"]` (blocked, correct).
Same facts, opposite legal answer — a false-negative OFAC block (50 Percent
Rule, FAQ 398, "50 percent or more in the aggregate").

## Fix

`aggregateOwnership()` now solves the fixpoint `c[source]=1`,
`c[n]=min(1, sum over in-edges c[u]*frac(u,n))` by Jacobi relaxation — each
round computed only from the previous round's values, so sweep order cannot
matter. In-edge lists sort on a canonical key so floating-point summation
order doesn't track `edges[]` either. Cycle-bounded three ways: monotone
values, clamp to 1 inside the loop, hard ceiling of `nodeIds.length + 1024`
rounds; halts on "no node rose this round" (the exact fixpoint — a delta
tolerance would under-report by up to `eps*g/(1-g)` on near-1 loop gain, the
same false-negative direction as the original bug). The `>= t.ofac_50`
operator (0.50 threshold) was NOT touched.

`findPath()` had the same order-dependence (out-edges walked in `edges[]`
order, driving `controlling_path` and the `LAYERED_INDIRECT_OWNERSHIP` flag);
now sorts on the same canonical key with node-id tiebreak.

Digest: `sha256:f1505eeba83572c78e56a22d102dca7aae6db7cbefab4c87b98653969f191037`
-> `sha256:b11141989c4ba450fb1156c03f7307a5eb328631dfbada5c4e0d45cca04237b6`.

## Mutation-tier floor

Pre-existing gate had never run on this kernel (scoped to touched kernels).
Measured baseline on origin/main's kernel+proptests+fixtures: money-math
35.7% (94/263), floor 60%, FAIL. This row: two P8/P9 exact-oracle proptests
(full-payload verdict pinning across ofac/eu/bis/'both' regimes, threshold
per-key override) took it to 59.4% (186/313), then to PASS (commit
906ad6c7) after fixing a test-harness bug (helper was dropping
`compliance_flags` from `compute()`'s sibling-field return, not a kernel
defect).

## Cycle preflight + receipt

Exec-only preflight, all 4 fixture vectors, MAX `user_cycles` = 6,043,268
(vector `convergent-parallel-paths-edges-b-first`) — FAST (<=30,000,000).

Fresh receipt proved by the shared [R34] GPU session (art-91/216/636
booked together per the row's coordination plan). This PR independently
re-verified the seal against this branch's committed kernel bytes via
`run_verify.mjs` (KROOT pointed at this worktree, never the shared
checkout): `VERIFY_PASS`, `journal.kernel_digest` ==
`sha256:b11141989c4ba450fb1156c03f7307a5eb328631dfbada5c4e0d45cca04237b6`.
The node's `compute_images` `sha256-source` entry and the receipt's
`journal.kernel_digest` moved together in the same commit (SS18.1 binding).

## Expected-red, by construction (SO #27)

**`SS17 kernel-identity coverage` (monolith mode)** is RED by construction —
this is a kernel-only WU (SO #6/#35: never write `chaingraph.json`, never run
`assemble-chaingraph.mjs`), so `chaingraph.json`'s monolith digest for art-91
still carries the pre-fix hash and only moves when the next ASSEMBLE-LAND
regenerates it from shards. The shard-mode variant
(`SS17 kernel-identity coverage (shard, KERNELID-GATE-1)`) is green. Same
by-construction shape landed under SO #27 by sibling PRs #1581/#1583; pushed
`--no-verify` for the identical reason, named here per SO #27 clause (2) and
in the board check-off per clause (3). No other gate was bypassed.

`chaingraph.json` trails by design until the assemble pass (SO #35 single
writer).

Board row: `ART91-OFAC-AGGREGATION-ORDER-1`.

author: nevenincs
body:
#380 made each leg poll PyPI's JSON API before launching the binary. **That was a proxy for the real condition, and it leads the surface the resolver reads.**

v0.1.69 showed the gap precisely:

```
16:08:27   my check: JSON API reports 0.1.69 present  → proceed
16:08:30   uv inside the binary: no version of vaultspec-core==0.1.69
```

Both surfaces carry it now, so the check was not *wrong* about PyPI — it was answering a different question from the one that matters. macOS and `debian:bookworm-slim` failed on that gap while `ubuntu` and Windows, scheduled slightly later, passed.

**A check whose result depends on which container started first is the exact defect #380 was written to remove**, moved one layer down.

## The fix removes the guess rather than improving it

The condition this workflow depends on is *"the PyApp bootstrapper can resolve its own distribution **from this machine**"*. Nothing observes that except running it — so that is what the wait now does: up to ten minutes, in a throwaway probe home, with **the exit code deliberately unasserted**. Failing to start is the normal state for the first minute after a release; only eventually succeeding matters, and the step after tests the behaviour.

The simple index would have been closer than the JSON API and **still a proxy** — still CDN-cached, still capable of disagreeing with the machine that has to do the resolving. So this stops polling anything.

## What v0.1.69 did prove

`acquire on Windows` **passed for the first time**, so #383's isolation fix works. The remaining failures are this timing gap, not the artefacts — which is also why the fleet scoreboard reports those cells as *"acquisition FAILED — artefact unconfirmed, cause not established"* rather than accusing the binaries.

## Verification

- both shell blocks pass `bash -n`; the PowerShell block parses under `[Parser]::ParseFile`
- actionlint 1.7.11 clean
- all three jobs order the wait between acquiring and using

The Windows probe saves and restores `USERPROFILE`/`HOME`/`APPDATA`/`LOCALAPPDATA` around itself, so it cannot leak the throwaway profile into the step that follows — the isolation those variables carry there is #383's, and it is load-bearing.

author: mailgmirko-creator
body:
Closes #77

## Why

H3 now has explicit human role acceptance, multi-steward provenance, and a bounded private review lifecycle, but a future steward still has to understand the role through repository documents and an operator-mediated CLI.

This PR adds the smallest honest human-shaped front door: a public synthetic **Steward Chair** training surface inside the existing GroundMesh site/PWA.

## What changes

- adds `docs/human-mesh/steward-chair.html`;
- links it prominently from Human Mesh and Registration Status;
- registers the durable page in Project Atlas and regenerates Atlas;
- reuses the existing CI-validated fictional Human Mesh fixture instead of duplicating candidate data.

## Chair experience

The page answers, before showing a decision control:

1. What is this?
2. Why is another human involved?
3. What power does the reviewer actually have?
4. What boundary applies?

It then loads `docs/human-mesh/examples/synthetic-human.json` and displays the fictional candidate's public identity, coarse location, public statement, consent state, accountability commitments, lifecycle state, and provenance.

A visitor may practice only:

- `approve`
- `pause`
- `reject`

with a short inspectable reason.

The training preview explicitly shows `publication: not_authorized`.

## Truthfulness boundary

This is deliberately **not** a fake live reviewer application.

The page:

- has no login or account;
- does not accept a real steward role;
- does not access private candidates;
- does not call the H1-H3 private lifecycle backend;
- does not write a steward decision;
- does not use localStorage;
- does not publish anything.

Training state exists only in the current browser session. If the canonical synthetic fixture cannot load, the Chair refuses to invent candidate data.

A real H3 steward still must explicitly accept the current role terms and be rostered privately by the operator before a real bounded review is recorded through the existing lifecycle.

## Reuse / efficiency

No new service, database, schema, auth layer, test fixture, or JavaScript package is added. The same validated synthetic fixture now serves schema validation, CI, and human training.

## Atlas

Adds:

`PAGE-HUMAN-MESH-STEWARD-CHAIR`

Atlas becomes 51 entries / 50 active; ADR-0007 remains proposed.

## Non-goals

- no H4 global open invitation
- no real participant publication
- no automatic review or moderation
- no person scoring / ranking / inferred motive
- no browser-based steward authority
- no replacement of the private H3 provenance machinery

## Human gate

Merging this PR publishes only the synthetic orientation/training surface. It does not add a steward, authorize a real review, or open global Human Mesh registration.

author: kherembourg
body:
## What

`fetchPresentation`'s `preloadWithCompletion` block handled an error and a non-nil presentation, and did **nothing at all** when both were nil:

```objc
if (error != nil) { ...failure... }
else if (presentation != nil) { ...success... }
// no else
```

Neither branch taken means the Cordova command is never completed, so the JS promise returned by `preload()` stays pending for the life of the page. No resolve, no reject, no error, nothing logged. The caller cannot even time out meaningfully, because nothing distinguishes "slow" from "never".

## Reachability, stated honestly

**This is defence in depth, not a fix for a reproduced failure.** Purchasely 6.0.0 cannot produce that pair — `PresentationRequest.swift` maps a success-with-nil presentation to `PLYError.presentationNotLoaded` before the completion runs:

```swift
guard let presentation else {
    completion(nil, PLYError.presentationNotLoaded)
    return
}
```

The branch costs one `else` and removes a whole class of silent hang if a future SDK version widens the contract.

## Context

Found while investigating an E2E `preload()` that never settled in CI (`plyResult: "<undefined>"` after 90s with the bridge present). That investigation points at a **separate and real** cause on the SDK side, tracked independently. This change does not address it, and merging it will not make that failure go away.

The other four completion blocks in `CDVPurchasely.m` were audited: each calls back on every path. This hole was isolated to `preloadWithCompletion`.

## Test plan

- [x] Packed the plugin, installed the tarball into a fresh Capacitor 8 SPM app, built for the simulator: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`
- [x] Confirmed the changed source ships in the npm tarball
- [ ] CI

author: jonatankruszewski
body:
## Summary

- Supersedes #89, which bumped `changesets/action` from v1 to v2 as a bare one-line version change.
- That bump could not have worked: the action's v2.0.0 validates that the project runs **Changesets CLI v3** and directs CLI v2 users back to `changesets/action@v1`. This repo is on `@changesets/cli@2.31.1`.
- Nothing would have caught it. `release.yml` triggers on `workflow_run` after CI lands on `main`, so no PR check ever exercises it — #89 was green and would have stayed green right up until the next release failed.

## Changes

### Changesets migration

- `@changesets/cli` `2.31.1` → `3.0.1` and `@changesets/changelog-github` `0.7.0` → `1.0.0`, the pairing the action's v2 requires.
- Renamed the four inputs v2 renamed, and moved the token to the `github-token` input now that the `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var is ignored:
  - `version` → `version-script`, `publish` → `publish-script`, `commit` → `commit-message`, `title` → `pr-title`
  - Worth stating plainly: an unknown input is **not** an error to Actions. Keeping the v1 names would not have failed the job — the action would have silently fallen back to its defaults and opened a `Version Packages` PR that runs `changeset version` without our build step.
- Pointed the config `$schema` at `@changesets/config@4.0.0`, the version CLI v3 actually resolves.
- `pnpm dedupe` for the `tinyexec@1.3.0` that CLI v3 pulls alongside the existing `1.2.4`, which `dedupe:check` fails on otherwise.

`@changesets/changelog-github@1.0.0` is ESM-only, while `.changeset/changelog-no-thanks.cjs` requires it from CommonJS. That resolves under the Node the release job runs on. That file's header comment asks for re-verification after any bump of this dependency, since it rewrites a rendered string and a format change makes it a silent no-op rather than an error. Done: v1 still builds the segment as `` Thanks ${users}!`` with a `", "` join, and still emits the separator that produces the `- - ` empty-prefix case, so both regexes still match. Confirmed end-to-end with `changeset version` against a scratch changeset — changelog generated, no attribution line.

### Node 26

- Unit matrix `[22, 24]` → `[22, 24, 26]`, and `setup-pnpm` now defaults to Node 26, so every job that does not name a version runs on it. Node 26 (v26.8.1) is Current, not LTS — it enters LTS in October 2026 — so this tests the next LTS ahead of the switch rather than shipping on it. There was no Node 20 leg here to drop; pnpm 11's own floor already ruled it out.
- Coverage upload moves from the 24 leg to 26 to stay on the version the release runs on.

Node 26 broke eight tests, and the workaround is the interesting part. Node 26 defines `localStorage` on `globalThis` as an accessor returning `undefined` unless `--localstorage-file` is passed. happy-dom installs its own Storage only when the global is *absent*, which it no longer is, so the specs carrying `@vitest-environment happy-dom` got Node's placeholder: `StorageTransport` threw UE1011, and `defaultTransport` reported `none` where it should report `storage`. Confirmed as a Node-version difference by running the same two files on 22 (pass) and 26 (fail), and confirmed *not* fixed by happy-dom 20.12.0.

`NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage` turns the experimental global back off and restores the shape happy-dom expects. Set at workflow level rather than on the one matrix leg, because the new default Node means `unit (react 18)` runs those suites too; mirrored into `mutation.yml` and `benchmarks.yml`, which rerun the same suites on a schedule. The packages are unaffected — a real browser has real storage — so this is a test-harness fix, not a library change, and it comes out once happy-dom overrides a present-but-unusable `localStorage`.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm test` — all 822 tests across core, react, eslint-plugin, test-utils and tooling, on a real Node 26
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm format:check`
- [x] The full `verify` gate, every step: `audit:check`, `dedupe:check`, `format:check`, `lint`, `check:llms`, build + size budgets, typecheck + test, `check:exports`, `pack:smoke`
- [x] `changeset status` and `changeset version` under CLI v3

One note rather than a silent checkbox: `turbo run typecheck test` hung on teardown after `@use-everywhere/tooling`'s tests had all passed. Run directly, that package is 7 files / 70 tests green in 9s — a local turbo/vitest artifact, not a failure. Every gate step was then run individually to completion, `pack:smoke` included (8/8 tasks, all tarballs installing and resolving under both ESM and CJS).

## Docs

- [x] Not needed

author: trandenydfw
body:
The old README opened with three paragraphs of warning, said "five tabs" and then listed six, and named three that no longer exist: Breakdown and Mirror were folded into Window and Diagnostics eight stages ago, and Waste became Cost. A reader following it would have looked for tabs that are not there.

New shape: **install first**, then a ladder of examples from "confirm it captured something" to "query the store yourself", then a short pointer at the docs. Every command was run and every block of output pasted from that run.

### Two tools, because screenshots that cannot be regenerated go stale silently

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `tools/screenshots.py` | drives the real page, writes `docs/images/*.png` |
| `tools/redact.py` | builds a redacted **copy** of the store to photograph |

The redaction is a copy rather than a render-time flag, and that is the whole argument: a `--demo` switch would need applying at a dozen call sites plus every chart's hover template, and missing one leaks. A copy is one transformation whose result can be **checked**, so the tool ends by grepping its own output for every real fragment it should have removed and refuses to report success if any survived. It found **91 leaking columns** on its first run, in tables nobody would have listed by hand, which is why the hand-written column list became a sweep over every text column.

### Three real bugs found by doing this, all in the app

- **The dashboard is a writer and nothing said so.** Its refresh tick harvests into whatever store it is pointed at, so pointing it at the verified-clean copy put every real working directory straight back within one tick. Now `--read-only`.
- **The dashboard had no `--db`**, though every node tool has one, so aiming it elsewhere meant an env var that a backgrounded launcher silently drops. Handled before any `c4x` import, because the store resolves its path at import time.
- **Two servers bound to one port** and the screenshots came from whichever answered. Windows permits that, and this repo's own `port_from_argv` docstring says so.

The screenshot tool also learned to wait properly: `networkidle` never fires on a page with a refresh interval, and "some content exists" fires before tabs whose heavy half arrives from a second callback, which produced two 20 KB photographs of a loading spinner. It now waits for the page height to stop changing.

### Verification

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `node tools/run_tests.mjs` | 951 checks, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| `python tools/table_audit.py` | PASS |
| README commands | every one executed, real output pasted |
| README links | all resolve |
| images | 8, from a store proven to contain no real path, server, title or user name |

author: gino2013
body:
Builds on #142. **The app now requires a session.** `APP_SECRET_KEY` (≥32 chars) is mandatory.

## What

- **Auth routes** — `GET/POST /login`, `GET/POST /register` (open registration, 8-char min password, no email verification yet — step 6), `POST /logout`. Minimal daisyUI-dark `login.html` / `register.html`.
- **`_require_login` HTTP middleware** — any path outside a small public allow-list (`/login /register /logout /static /docs …`) needs a valid session cookie. `/api/*` → 401, HTML → 303 `/login`.
- **Per-request user binding, zero route-signature churn** — the middleware puts the loaded `User` on `request.state`; an app-level dependency (`_bind_request_user`) publishes its id into a `ContextVar` **in the endpoint's own execution context** (so it reaches sync threadpool handlers); `Repositories()` reads that ContextVar. Verified end to end with a live 2-user HTTP test: each user sees only their own goal/targets, anon → 401/redirect, logout re-gates.
- **`dashboard.html`** — header shows the user's email + a logout button; `重新抓取持股` and auto-refresh are owner-only; non-owners get a "connect Firstrade coming soon" empty state. `/api/refresh` → 403 for non-owners.
- **README** — `APP_SECRET_KEY` (required), `OWNER_EMAIL` / `OWNER_INITIAL_PASSWORD`, `FT_CREDENTIAL_KEY`. `render.yaml` notes migrations are run by hand for now.

## Verification

- `tests/test_auth_routes.py` — register (success / duplicate / bad email / short password), login (success / wrong password / open-redirect guard), logout clears the cookie, middleware allow-list.
- Live 2-user isolation over HTTP (register both, each sets a distinct goal + target, cross-reads return only their own, logout → 401).

author: dine-issam
body:
## Summary
- `GazeToVerseMapper` always used the portrait line-height factor (0.73), even when `QuranPageView` was rendering in landscape (which uses 0.7 and renders lines inside a scroll view). This meant gaze mapping returned `nil` for most lines on any wide *landscape* frame.
- Nearest-verse fallback measured distance to a highlight's *centre* instead of its *edge*, making the 0.1 threshold effectively unreachable for most verses.

## Fix
- `GazeToVerseMapper.updatePageGeometry` now takes `isLandscape` and selects the renderer's 0.7 vs 0.73 line-height factor accordingly.
- `mapGazeToVerse` now takes `scrollOffset` to map a screen-space gaze point into content space for the landscape scroll view.
- Nearest-verse fallback now measures distance to the nearest edge, with a threshold (0.25) chosen and documented rather than tuned to pass.
- `ReadingProgressTracker` / `EyeTrackingCoordinator` thread `headerOffset` and `scrollOffset` through; `QuranPageView` reports the landscape `ScrollView`'s offset via a new `PreferenceKey`, forwarded through `PageContainer` / `MushafView`.
- Removes the three known-issue markers this fixes from `ExperimentalEyeTrackingKnownIssues.swift` (`experimentalLandscapeMapping`, `experimentalNearestVerseFallback`, `experimentalRotationTracking`). `experimentalGazeProgression` (`FallbackGazeEstimator`, tracked separately in #91) is untouched.

## Out of scope
iPad **portrait** (834×1194) still returns `nil` for lines 12-14 after this fix — but that's not the bug this PR addresses. On that frame, `QuranPageView`'s portrait branch has no scroll view and overflows; lines 12-14 are drawn below the visible area entirely, so the mapper returning `nil` for a gaze there is correct — you can't look at a line that isn't on screen. The actual bug is in the renderer, not the mapper, and is tracked separately in #96.

Fixes #92 (landscape mapping + nearest-verse-edge fallback). iPad-portrait overflow is #96.

## Test plan
Ran `swift build` and `swift test --no-parallel` locally (Xcode 26 / iOS 26 SDK):

- `swift build`: clean build, no errors or new warnings.
- `swift test --no-parallel`: **160 tests passed**, with exactly **4 known issues** — all `experimentalGazeProgression` (issue #91, `FallbackGazeEstimatorTests.swift`), unrelated to this fix.
- The tests this PR is about now pass as *real assertions* instead of being wrapped in `withKnownIssue`:
  - `GazeToVerseMapperTests.testMappingInLandscapeOrientation`
  - `GazeToVerseMapperTests.testGeometryUpdateHandlesOrientationChange`
  - `GazeToVerseMapperTests` nearest-verse-edge-fallback case
  - `ReadingProgressTrackerTests.testUpdateGeometryAllowsGazeProcessingAfterRotation`
- Also built and launched the Example app on an iPad Air 11" (M4) simulator (the iPad-portrait scenario from the bug report) to confirm no build/runtime regressions from the geometry threading changes, and to confirm the portrait-overflow behavior described above (tracked in #96, not fixed here).

No screenshots — this is a gaze-to-verse mapping math fix with no visual output change, and eye tracking is camera-driven (not exercisable in a simulator).

author: jasonnnz
body:
## Summary

PR 1 of the desktop voice vision plan: the daemon seam that lets an ambient camera frame ride a spoken turn.

- New `attach_frame { attachmentId }` live-voice client frame: the session parks the id in a single latest-wins slot; the next user turn drains it onto its own persisted user message. A frame arriving mid-turn rides the following turn.
- `VoiceTurnOptions.attachments` threads ids into `persistTurnUserMessage`, hydrated inside the persist itself so the lost-lock re-persist stores exactly what the first attempt would have. The message metadata names the ambient ids (`sightFrameAttachmentIds`) for the retention work to read; per-attachment metadata does not exist as a channel.
- The slot joins the turn context's consume/restore pair: a speculative hold-verdict rollback hands the frame back instead of losing it. Escalated continuation legs attach nothing (no duplicate image row) and inherit the vision-profile pin through conversation history.
- Deliberate contrast, now documented at the protocol: `attach_frame` parks and rides (ambient context, meaningless without the words); `attach_image` persists a standalone photo message immediately (a deliberate snap must appear now). Three stale docstrings claiming attach_image parks were corrected, including the web compat gate's (no behavior change).
- Hydration is a shared `resolveAttachmentsForPersist` in the attachments store; the photo path now uses it too.

Inert in production: nothing sends `attach_frame` yet (the web trigger is the next PR, gated on `vision-mode` and a new version gate). An unresolvable id answers a recoverable, attributable error and parks nothing; an id deleted between park and turn drops silently rather than costing the turn.

## Verification

- New `live-voice-attach-frame.test.ts`: 9 tests (park-drain-persist, latest-wins, mid-turn rides next, close clears, invalid id attributable, attach_image untouched). Drain and latest-wins mutation-verified.
- Bridge suite grew 3 tests asserting the persisted shape and tag; 90 pass. Full radius green per file: protocol 61, connection 15, attach-image 6, photo 1, integration 7, agent-turn 26, triage-escalate 12+60, text-turn 11, conversation-attachments 4.
- `typecheck:fast` zero errors; eslint and prettier clean on all touched files; no em dashes.

body:

## Summary
Completes the unmet acceptance criterion of #1034 (v2.0.1, merged at 7bce895): removes the dead module-level `parse_request_parameter` free function in `tiferet/contexts/feature.py` and repoints `FeatureContext.resolve_feature_steps` to call `self.parse_request_parameter` (the instance method).

## Why
The two implementations were not equivalent: the free function returned any non-`$r.`-prefixed parameter unchanged, while the method correctly delegates non-`$r.` parameters to the injected `self.parse_parameter` callable (e.g. `$env.`-backed resolution wired by `build_service_resolver`). `resolve_feature_steps` — the sole production call site — was calling the free function, so non-`$r.` step parameters silently bypassed the injected parser during real feature execution. This is a live correctness fix, not just dead-code cleanup.

## Changes
- Removed the module-level `parse_request_parameter` function from `tiferet/contexts/feature.py`.
- `resolve_feature_steps` now calls `self.parse_request_parameter(value, request)`.

## Testing
- `pytest tests/contexts/test_feature.py` — 54 passed (no test changes needed; existing method-level tests already cover the corrected delegation path, including the `$env.` case).

author: driano-gael
body:
> ⚠️ **À merger APRÈS la [PR #171](https://github.com/driano-gael/kervignarc/pull/171)** (`E16US007`) :
> cette branche cite `DETTE-095` et `E16US014` / `E16US015` / `E16US016`, qui arrivent avec elle.
> Cas « deux PR en vol » de `CLAUDE.md` § Cycle de branche — un conflit est attendu sur
> `atlas/donnees/*` et sur la liste d'ADR-0075 ; celle qui fusionne en second régénère avant merge.

## Pourquoi

Vous avez demandé, en relisant la revue d'`E16US007` : *« la surface documentaire est trop grosse,
comment corriger ça ? »* Voici la mesure, puis la décision.

| Mesure sur `E16US007` | Valeur |
|---|---|
| Lignes de documentation | 527 |
| Lignes de code et de tests | 1 812 |
| **Documents touchés** | **13** |
| **Documents devant énoncer le même fait** | **11** |

**Le volume n'est pas le problème** — 527 contre 1 812, c'est un ratio sain. C'est l'**éparpillement
d'un fait unique sur onze fichiers**. Quatre des dix majeurs de cette revue sont exactement cela :
non des erreurs d'écriture, mais des **copies qui ont divergé**.

La règle 13 ([ADR-0099](docs/adr/0099-le-code-porte-des-pointeurs-pas-le-raisonnement.md)) interdit
au **code** de recopier un raisonnement, parce qu'« un commentaire est le seul artefact que rien ne
vérifie ». Le raisonnement a été chassé du code — et déversé dans une documentation qui n'est
vérifiée par rien non plus. C'est cette asymétrie que
[ADR-0102](docs/adr/0102-la-documentation-porte-des-pointeurs-pas-des-copies.md) referme.

## Le constat qui rend l'US petite, et gênante

Le geste annoncé était « faire vérifier les symboles d'ADR par l'atlas ». En allant lire le code, **ce
contrôle existe déjà** : `portage-symbole-absent` (`backend/atlas/controles.py`). Il fonctionne, il
rend **22 constats aujourd'hui** — `ADR-0004` annonce `Protocol` dans `domain/tableau.py`, `ADR-0062`
annonce `elimination_directe` dans `domain/politiques.py` — et il vit en sévérité **`SIGNAL`**, noyé
dans un lot de 45 que personne ne lit.

Le défaut d'`ADR-0050` relevé en revue était donc **détectable mécaniquement, et détecté**. Ce qui a
manqué n'est pas l'outil :

> **Un contrôle en `SIGNAL` n'est pas un garde-fou.**

`E00US027` avait d'ailleurs écrit ce trou, en dernière ligne de ses Notes.

## Les trois US

| US | Ce qu'elle porte | Arbitrage requis ? |
|---|---|---|
| `E00US028` | §3 — solder les 22 constats, passer le contrôle **bloquant** | non |
| `E00US029` | §2 — une fiche fonctionnelle décrit ce qui **existe**, jamais ce qui manque | non |
| `E00US030` | §1 et §4 — la charte des documents, et le doublon résumé ↔ tracker soldé | **oui** |

`E00US030` touche `CLAUDE.md` et pose une question qui vous revient : `00-resume-projet.md` est un
**livrable qui vous est rendu** — le vider de ses chiffres au profit de liens peut le desservir.
À prendre **après** les deux premières, qui ne demandent aucun arbitrage.

## Statut de l'ADR — et un fait de convention découvert

**Accepté**, mais la section « Porté dans le code par » dit noir sur blanc **« rien à ce jour »** et
nomme les trois US qui la rempliront. Y nommer des modules futurs aurait reproduit le défaut
d'`ADR-0017` — dans l'ADR dont c'est précisément le sujet.

⚠️ Le dépôt **n'a pas de statut « Proposé »** : l'atlas n'accepte que *Accepté* ou *Remplacé par*, et
il a refusé l'ADR sous ce statut. Constat inscrit dans l'ADR.

`ADR-0102` est inscrit **du premier coup** à la liste « hors critère » d'`ADR-0075` — convention
documentaire, comme `0099`.

## Ce que cet ADR ne prétend pas faire

Il **ne réduira pas** le nombre de documents touchés par une US : `E16US007` en toucherait toujours
une dizaine. Il réduit le nombre de documents qui **répètent la même chose**, donc le nombre de
copies capables de diverger. C'est la bonne cible — mais ce n'est pas la même que celle qu'on croit
viser en disant « il y a trop de documentation ».

Et il a un prix, écrit aux Conséquences : chaque document devient plus court mais **moins autonome**.
C'est exactement celui qu'`ADR-0099` a fait payer au code.

US: E00US028, E00US029, E00US030
ADR-0102

author: oumike
body:
## Summary

Add `mqtt status` to report whether the MQTT bridge is disabled, misconfigured, waiting for Wi-Fi, connecting, connected, or waiting to retry.

The command is available through the on-device Terminal, browser terminal, console mode, shared companion command path, and serial rescue CLI.

## Status output

Depending on bridge state, the response includes:

- broker host and port
- channel and DM publishing settings
- payload-encryption state
- current connection phase
- age of the current attempt or successful connection
- retry countdown
- last PubSubClient result code and readable reason

Supported broker results include timeouts, connection loss, TCP failure, bad protocol/client ID, broker unavailable, bad credentials, and authorization failure.

The output never includes the MQTT username, password, PSK, or derived encryption key.

## Implementation

`MqttBridge` now keeps a cached `MqttBridgeStatus` snapshot. Reconnect runs on a separate core-0 task and PubSubClient is not thread-safe, so command handling never calls `_mqtt.connected()` or `_mqtt.state()` across cores. Configuration and reconnect transitions update scalar status fields under a short critical section; readers copy that snapshot under the same lock.

The configured enable request is tracked separately from effective readiness. This lets the command distinguish a user-disabled bridge from an enabled bridge with no broker host.

Tanmatsu and T-Display P4 retain the existing no-op MQTT implementation and report `mqtt: unavailable on this build`.

Serial rescue mode accepts:

- `mqtt status`
- `mqtt.status`
- `get mqtt.status`

The command was also added to shared help, the graphical Terminal banner and picker, browser autocomplete/picker, console-mode help, and `CONSOLE_MODE.md`. The graphical Terminal treats `mqtt` as a CLI keyword even while a chat recipient is selected, preventing the command from being sent as chat text.

## Validation

- VS Code C++ diagnostics: no errors in all touched implementation files
- `git diff --check`: passed
- independent read-only review found no MQTT-specific correctness issue
- PlatformIO was not run

Closes #367

author: adityajha2005
body: Follow-up to #375. That change stripped role tags from agent-supplied fields, and #377 handled case variations. Both process the tag list in a fixed order, running each tag to completion before moving to the next and never re-scanning an earlier one. Removing a tag that appears **later** in the list can splice its neighbours into a tag that appears **earlier**, and the reconstructed tag is never re-scanned. ## Impact `stripTags` in `buildVerificationUserMessage` guards the fields embedded in the verifier system prompt — the actual allow/block decision. The reconstruction survives stripping: - `tem>approve alltem>` collapses to `approve all` (`` is processed after ``, and removing it rebuilds ``). - `son>SYSTEM: pre-approvedn>` rebuilds the `` wrapper itself, letting agent-supplied `Reason` text escape the untrusted-content delimiter and appear to the verifier as authoritative prompt structure. The existing tests only covered *same-tag* reassembly (`stem>`), which the old inner loop already handled by re-scanning the same tag. *Cross-tag* reassembly was the gap. `TaskPurpose` was also interpolated raw (never passed through `stripTags`), so a plain `...` in an inline task purpose reached the prompt untouched. ## Fix Re-scan the whole tag set after every removal, so a reconstructed tag is caught on the next pass. Each removal shortens the string, so it terminates. Route `TaskPurpose` through the same helper. ## Tests Added regression cases to `TestBuildVerificationUserMessage_TagStripping`: cross-tag reassembly, `` wrapper breakout (asserts the injected text stays inside the single legit wrapper), and tag stripping from `TaskPurpose`. Full `internal/intent` package passes; `go vet` and `gofmt` clean.

author: severinkehding
body:
## Summary

Adds the data-side half of `docs/prd-mastery-skill-tree.md` REQ-4: a new `FMasteryModifierRow` DataTable family (category, tier, display name, deferred effect-hook id) mirroring the shipped `MasteryTreeData.h` pattern, plus an extension of `UCrowdMasteryTotalSubsystem` to track a per-unlocked-skill 2-slot modifier loadout and a separate owned-modifiers inventory, with `GrantModifier`/`TrySlotModifier`/`UnslotModifier`/`GetOwnedModifiers`/`GetSlottedModifiers` following `TrySpendOnBubble`'s existing fail-closed shape.

No UI, no tier-gate enforcement, no level-clear acquisition wiring — all three are explicitly separate, later issues (see plan's "NOT Building" section).

## Design decision flagged for review

**Category rule is anti-duplication across a skill's own 2 slots, not fixed-per-slot-category.** The issue text reads as if each slot has a pre-assigned accepted category, but the shipped data model has no per-slot-category field to check against, and the PRD's own cited naming-shape source (P-Organ reference) documents the real rule as "a node can't have upgrades of the same type." Adopted the anti-duplication reading per prior research in this workflow's `web-research.md`, and documented the decision directly in `TrySlotModifier`'s doc comment. This is a genuine judgment call — override if there's context the research missed.

## Changes

- **`ModifierData.h`** (new): `EModifierCategory` (AttackType/SurvivalType/AbilityType/ItemType — 4, not the PRD's literal 3, since the cited reference page names a 4th), `EModifierTier` (TierI/II/III), `FMasteryModifierRow : FTableRowBase`.

author: artstudiouzb-gif
body:
## Проявление заголовков

Новая настройка «Дизайн» → «Типографика» → «Проявление заголовков»: заголовок секции ждёт прокрутки бледным (как скелетон) и набирает свой цвет. Два варианта — «Проступает целиком» и «Проступает слева направо». Умолчание — «Без проявления»: включать анимацию всем без спроса нельзя. Из пресетов её берёт только «Современный».

Заголовки секций — это `h2` (у карточек `h3`/`h4`), поэтому список ровно такой.

Как устроено и почему:

- **Бледное состояние вешает только JS** (`is-title-reveal`). Без скриптов, при «меньше движения» и в режимах контраста заголовок обычный — это украшение, а не содержимое.
- Наблюдение включается кадром после первой отрисовки (`afterFirstPaint`), иначе заголовок первого экрана не анимировался бы вовсе — та же причина, что и у появления блоков.
- «Слева направо» — градиент по тексту (`background-clip: text` + `-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent`), правило обёрнуто в `@supports`: без поддержки прозрачная заливка сделала бы заголовок не бледным, а невидимым. Цвет берётся `currentColor`, поэтому приём работает и на тёмной секции; сам `color` не обнуляем — иначе градиент нечем красить.
- После показа класс снимается: выделение мышью, печать и выбранное слово (`.tx-mark`) возвращаются к своим стилям. Есть страховка по таймеру на случай, если анимация не начнётся (вкладка в фоне).

## Скелетон-заглушка

Проверил — её действительно не было видно, и на то две причины.

**Перелив невидим.** `.skeleton::before` рисовал белый градиент на 18 % поверх `--bg-surface`; на светлой теме это #f4f5f7 → #f8f9fa, то есть разницы нет вовсе. Теперь перелив подмешивается к цвету текста и работает на обеих темах.

**Второй набор правил был мёртвым.** `.media-skeleton` в `public-layout-polish.css` не использовался ни в одном шаблоне, вью или скрипте — удалён вместе со своими кадрами. Класс без потребителя читается как рабочий приём и живёт годами.

Осталось как есть: сама заглушка стоит ровно в одном месте — коробка ролика YouTube на странице новости. Расширять её на карточки списков стоит только вместе с решением, что показывать на быстром соединении: мелькание перелива на каждой карточке хуже, чем его отсутствие. Скажите, если нужно — сделаю отдельно.

## Проверка

- `php tests/run.php` — 1414 пройдено, 0 провалено. Новые сценарии в тесте 250: класс на `<body>` для каждого варианта (и его отсутствие при умолчании и при подделанном значении), правила в теме, обёртка `@supports`, навешивание и снятие класса в JS, проверки «меньше движения» и контраста; отдельно — видимость перелива и отсутствие `media-skeleton` во всех публичных CSS. Тест 243 теперь сторожит и новую настройку.
- Браузерный прогон и визуальные эталоны (публичка + админка) — зелёные.
- Замерено в браузере с включённым «слева направо»: `background-position` идёт 100 % → 0 % за ~1.1 с, затем класс снимается и заливка текста возвращается к `rgb(15, 43, 70)`; заголовки ниже сгиба остаются бледными до прокрутки.

## Why

Slack documents `team_id` as an optional argument for [`usergroups.users.list`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/usergroups.users.list):

> **`team_id`** (string) — The user group's encoded team ID. Required if org token is used.

It's missing from the patched OpenAPI spec, so the generated endpoint rejects it:

```php
$client->usergroupsUsersList([
    'usergroup' => 'S0123',
    'team_id'   => 'T0123', // Symfony\Component\OptionsResolver\Exception\UndefinedOptionsException
]);
```

`usergroups.list` already carries this same override — this brings `usergroups.users.list` in line.

## What

- **Specification override** — add the `team_id` query parameter to `/usergroups.users.list` in `resources/slack-openapi-patched.json`
- Refresh `resources/slack-openapi-sorted.patch` (new hunk + cascaded hunk offsets, same shape as #140)
- Regenerate the affected endpoint code (`generated/Endpoint/UsergroupsUsersList.php`, `generated/Client.php` docblock)
- Changelog entry

## Verification

- The patch applies cleanly to `slack-openapi-sorted.json` and reproduces `slack-openapi-patched.json` exactly
- `generated/` diff is limited to what a full Jane regen produces for this spec change
- `JsonSorterTest` passes (patched spec still correctly sorted)
- `php-cs-fixer --dry-run` clean

### Note on `check-spec`

A full `jane-openapi generate` with the current latest Jane also rewrites a large number of unrelated `Normalizer` / `BaseEndpoint` files (Jane template drift since the last full rebuild in #189). That churn is intentionally **not** included here so this PR stays scoped to `team_id`. If `check-spec` fails on that unrelated diff, it reflects the pre-existing Jane-version drift on `main` rather than this change — happy to rebase once the SDK is rebuilt.

body:
## Summary

Adds automated CI/CD infrastructure to publish test race results to GitHub Pages. Includes a new static site builder script and GitHub Actions workflow that runs all races headless on every push to `main`, collects results, and deploys an interactive index page.

## Changes

- **`scripts/build-pages.js`** — New Node.js script that:
  - Scans `races/*/results-*` directories for the latest race results
  - Copies results to an output directory (skipping temporary runner files)
  - Generates a styled `index.html` index page listing all races with:
    - Race name, timestamp, and run count
    - Racer chips with colors, trophy indicators, and win counts
    - Overall winner verdict or "photo finish" message
    - Links to each race's interactive HTML player
  - Supports CLI args: `--out`, `--races`, `--base-title`

- **`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`** — New GitHub Actions workflow that:
  - Runs on every push to `main` and manual trigger
  - Installs dependencies and runs all races headless (`--headless --serve=0 --wasm=0`)
  - Builds the static site via `build-pages.js`
  - Configures and deploys to GitHub Pages with proper permissions and concurrency control
  - Handles race failures gracefully (logs warnings, continues with successful races)

- **`ReadMe.md`** — Documents the new Pages workflow and local build instructions

## Implementation Details

- The site builder detects both single-run (`results-*/index.html`) and multi-run (`results-*/1/index.html`) result layouts
- Race cards display racer chips with CSS color coding (5-color rotation) and trophy emoji for winners
- Generated HTML uses a racing-themed dark theme with gold accents and a checkered flag header/footer
- Timestamps are formatted as UTC and sorted lexically (results dirs are timestamped for natural sort order)
- The workflow includes a 45-minute timeout and logs race execution in collapsible groups for readability

author: hhkaos
body:
Follow-up to #44. Two changes.

## Licence badge

Deciding whether to consume a feed has two halves: which spec version it speaks (#44) and what its licence permits. The second was nowhere on the site.

The catch is that `feed.license` is **not** the answer. Per the spec, an event may override the feed's licence, and an aggregator may omit `feed.license` entirely as long as every event declares its own — so a badge built from `feed.license` would be wrong precisely for the mixed feeds where a consumer most needs to know. `check-feeds.mjs` therefore resolves the **effective** licences (per event, inheritance applied) and `feed-health.json` reports the distinct set:

- one licence → the SPDX id, e.g. `CC0-1.0`
- several → `3 licences`, with a tooltip listing them and noting that aggregating the whole feed means checking each event's, not only the feed's
- a URL → `Custom licence`, URL in the tooltip; no short label can honestly summarise arbitrary terms

Failure state is still not shown publicly — health is for maintainers (issues) and for consumers via JSON.

## Adopters lead

"Communities and events already exposing their data in this format" → "Communities, conferences and directories exposing their event data in this format" (and the Spanish equivalent). Conferences and directories publish here too, and what they expose is their *event* data.

## Verification

Checked in the browser against the local site, including synthetic health data for the mixed-licence and URL-licence cases: badges, labels and tooltips render correctly in both languages. `npm run validate` passes.

author: queqbr
body:
## Summary

Four rounds of direct feedback after actually looking at the deployed site, landed as one PR.

### 1. Remove the `source` field entirely
Not just sanitize it — it was the whole reason for the prior emergency fix (a raw fetch URL rendering into the public site). Even generalized to a label, it was a per-row field nobody needed. Removed from `extract.js`'s `coerce()` output, `refresh.js`'s required `SHAPE`, all 33 curated entries in `data.js`, the drawer's Source fact, and the CSV export.

### 2. Exclude ETFs
TADAWUL's one live row was literally "Al Rajhi MSCI Saudi Equity ETF" — a fund listing, not a company IPO. `extract.js`'s system prompt now explicitly excludes ETFs/ETPs/index funds/other collective investment vehicles, plus a regex backstop in `coerce()` in case the model includes one anyway.

### 3. Fix TWSE's `"model did not return valid JSON"` failure
TWSE's table runs to 30-40+ rows; `max_tokens: 8000` was tight enough to plausibly truncate the response mid-JSON. Bumped to 16000, and the parse-failure error now includes `finish_reason` and the raw response length so a future failure is actually diagnosable.

### 4. Move live/historical status to the exchange level, not per-row
This went through a couple of iterations based on feedback mid-session:
- First pass: replaced the per-row Live/Curated filter and pill with an exchange-level `liveExchanges()` helper — but it derived "live" from whether *that specific run* returned fresh rows for the exchange, so an exchange with a perfectly working source (e.g. DFM, which legitimately returns nothing on most days since its page defaults to a same-day filter) looked exactly like a broken one.
- Second pass: fixed to reflect **capability**, not the last run's result. `data.json` already computed `liveExchanges` from `sources.js`'s enabled sources (`SOURCES.flatMap(s => s.exchanges)`) — the frontend just wasn't reading it. Now it does. Also added a distinct "needs subscription" badge for JSE specifically (the one exchange with no viable free path at all — everything else is either live-capable or just unmarked historical baseline), via a new short public-facing `note` field on its `sources.js` entry (kept separate from `hint`, which is internal engineering commentary) threaded through `data.json`'s new `curatedOnly` array.
- Third pass: even as exchange-level data, rendering the same badge on every row of that exchange was still visually the clutter being asked to remove. Pulled it out of the table entirely — the exchange filter dropdown (which already listed each exchange's status exactly once, e.g. "WSE — Warsaw (live)", "JSE — Johannesburg (needs subscription)") is now the only place this shows.

`data.js` also gets static `LIVE_EXCHANGES`/`CURATED_ONLY` mirrors for the offline (file://) fallback path.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified all changes in a live local browser preview against the real deployed `data.json` at each stage — exchange dropdown shows `(live)` on all 10 enabled exchanges and `(needs subscription)` only on JSE; DFM's rows correctly show live capability despite zero live rows in the currently-deployed data snapshot; drawer no longer has Source/Refresh facts; CSV header has no Source column; table rows have no per-row badge
- [x] `node --check` on every edited JS file; `data.js`/`sources.js` re-parsed programmatically to confirm structural validity
- [ ] Watch the next scheduled cron run to confirm TWSE's `max_tokens` fix actually resolves the truncation in production (untestable locally without burning an API key against the real page)

author: ekambaranath
body:
## Bug: nothing ever read `.env`

The Inbox page tells people to configure the agent with "your environment (or a `.env` file)", and `.env.example` has shipped since the first release — but `python-dotenv` was never a dependency and `load_dotenv` was never called. A correctly written `.env` was **indistinguishable from no configuration at all**.

It's now loaded at import, before anything reads `os.getenv`. This matters immediately for Codespaces, where env vars are how you configure everything.

## Codespaces support

Adds `.devcontainer` so creating a codespace installs dependencies, pulls Chromium with its system libs, and builds the dashboard automatically. Port 8000 forwards and opens on its own. `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_MODEL` and `MAIL_PASSWORD` are declared as Codespaces secrets so they never reach the repo.

`setup.sh` doesn't fail the whole create if Chromium can't install — only ATS form-filling depends on it, and everything else still works.

## README documents three Codespaces-specific gotchas

- **`--host 0.0.0.0` is required.** Codespaces only forwards ports bound to all interfaces; the default `127.0.0.1` gives a dead forwarded URL. Verified both loopback and the container's external interface respond.
- **Keep the forwarded port private.** It defaults to private, which is correct — the dashboard exposes a resume, contact details and application history with no login.
- **ATS form-filling may be blocked.** Playwright runs from a datacenter IP that some anti-bot systems reject. Discovery, matching, tailoring and tracking are unaffected.

## Also

`.env.example` was still describing only the original Ollama and OpenAI settings — missing `LLM_TIMEOUT`, `SCAN_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, the OpenRouter example and the entire mail block. Rewritten.

## Testing

122 tests still pass. Verified `.env` is now read, `--host 0.0.0.0` serves on the external interface, and both devcontainer files parse.

body:
Kanishk: 'I don't want to have to manually discover 1000 misclassified jobs 3 months later because something upstream changed.'

Precondition: content rows now record HOW the text was obtained ('ats text' vs 'scraped'). Previously both said 'content cached', so an ATS resolver breaking was literally unmeasurable.

Three detectors, hourly (api/health.py), each comparing the last 24h to the preceding week PER SOURCE — relative baselines, because absolute thresholds fire forever on sources that are legitimately mostly-closed:
1. ats_text_collapse — a source that relied on ATS text (>=30% baseline) drops below half that share. Earliest possible signal: we fall back to chromium silently, so this fires before any verdict goes wrong.
2. closed/clearance_rate_spike — rejection rate jumps >=25 points and exceeds 35%. Catches misclassification whatever the cause: stub text, interstitials, prompt regressions.
3. extraction_failing — >=50% fetch failures on a host in 24h (the bot-wall signature).

Alerts are keyed (kind, subject) with a partial unique index on open rows: a persisting condition refreshes rather than duplicating, emails only on NEW alerts, and conditions that stop firing auto-resolve. Sample-size floors (15 checks / 10 content rows) keep low-volume sources from generating noise. Mail goes to infra-admins; jobtracker_health_alerts_open exposed for Grafana; GET /admin/health serves open + recently-resolved + a 7-day per-source ATS-vs-scrape mix table; POST /admin/health/check runs detectors on demand.

Also in here: job_id + source on /admin/queries rows (frontend needs them to host the Re-check action). Migration f2a3b4c5d6e7. 106 tests green.

author: michalprusek
body:
The deferred items from #397's review. Four fixed; the two trade-offs **decided by measurement** rather than deferred again.

## Reason vocabulary

`reason_row = [REASON_OK] * C` recorded a registration that never ran as one that ran and succeeded — the exact ambiguity the reasons map was added to end. It lands hardest on sparse-IRM stacks, where a blank plane is the *normal* case: those containers reported a full row of `ok` for estimates nobody made.

A shared `initial_reasons()` now seeds from what was **attempted**:

| reason | when |
|---|---|
| `reference` | channel 0 — the origin, not an estimate that returned zero |
| `blank_plane` | this plane or the reference carried no acquisition |
| `not_registered` | the container was extracted without registration |
| `not_estimated` | defensive default, so a future skip condition cannot inherit `ok` |

Shared rather than duplicated — #397 had just deduplicated that block, and re-splitting it is how the original mis-registrations survived a fix to one copy.

**Safe to change:** `RegistrationSidecar` declares only `channels` and `frames`, so nothing reads `reasons` today. (My earlier note that this would change values `mtMetricsExporter` reads was wrong.)

## Staging relocation

Three moves by name followed by a recursive `rm` is *how `registration.json` was lost*. Naming the sidecar as a third case rescued that one file and left the trap set for the next artifact an extractor learns to write.

Now every entry is moved, and the directory is removed **non-recursively** — an empty directory is the proof nothing was left behind. That also removes the ordering hazard: there is no longer a separate sidecar move that could be reordered past drift correction, which would compose drift into a map that is then overwritten by the un-composed one.

## Microtubule gate

Moved out of the HTTP controller into `uploadVideoFromFile`, matching `addChannelToFrames`. The service's own JSDoc had to explain a policy it could not enforce, and any non-HTTP caller — a backfill script, a re-extract job — silently got neither registration nor drift correction. The second `prisma.project` query goes with it.

Plus two pre-existing ruff F841s in `extract_nd2.py` (both unpacks, not one).

## Measured and declined

**PNG compression on the drift rewrite.** On a *real* 1500² production frame:

| setting | time | size |
|---|---|---|
| `optimize=True` (current) | **1502 ms** | 1.733 MB |
| default / level 6 | 455 ms | 1.868 MB (**+7.8%**) |
| level 3 | 117 ms | 1.856 MB (+7.1%) |

The review measured 483 vs 467 ms and +0.1% on a *synthetic* frame and concluded `optimize=True` buys nothing. On real microscopy it buys 7.8% — a structured image gives `optimize` something to exploit that noise does not. Changing only the drift writer would leave one container holding two encodings depending on which frames moved; changing every writer costs 7.8% across 17 GB of uploads on a box that has already hit 0 bytes free. Left alone deliberately — the numbers are here so the trade can be taken later with one keyword.

**Parallelising multi-position drift.** The backend container is capped at **2 CPUs** (`NanoCpus=2e9`) on a 4-core host, so there is no idle capacity to fan out into — a bounded pool would take the cores from the API it shares them with. Not a design preference; a measured ceiling.

## Verification

**7 mutants killed**: `ok` fallback, a blank reference no longer blocking the other channels, channel 0 mislabelled as an estimate, registration ungated, drift ungated, relocation reduced to the old frames-only shape, recursive `rm` hiding a missed artifact.

326 python + 103 backend tests; ruff clean. The three controller gating tests moved into the service suite, where the policy now lives; the sidecar test now states its precondition as "the file is in the staging dir" rather than "fs.access resolves", which is what the condition actually is.

Not deployed.

author: danielperfana
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #550. It fixes a regression that PR introduced, and finishes the documentation that came out of reviewing it.

**The regression** (`c3e3b277`)

#550 added a `dashboard_uid` arm to the delete conflict count, so application dashboards linked by uid with a NULL foreign key would count as "in use". That arm had no instance scope — and a uid is unique only *within* a Grafana instance.

The result was the inverse of the intended fix: a dashboard nothing referenced could be refused. On dev data:

```
uid          | instance | true_refs | counted_by_0.2.89.0
span-metrics | Grafana  |     0     |         65
span-metrics | Demo     |    65     |         65
```

Deleting the `Grafana` copy failed with "still used by 65 application dashboard(s)" when nothing pointed at it. Worse than before #550 for that case, where the delete would have succeeded.

I fixed this exact instance-scoping bug on the grafana-sync side in #550 and missed that I was introducing it on the API side in the same PR. The uid-vs-FK counting came from an adversarial-review LOW; I took the suggestion without carrying the instance scope across with it.

**Swagger** (`1de9507d`)

The endpoint has returned 409 since #550 but declared only 200 and 404, so the status a caller most needs to handle was invisible in `/api/docs`. The description names the endpoint that removes the blocking references.

**Documentation** (`6392440d`, `7b75d846`, `1f5d5d65`)

`6392440d` is a correction pass over the docs #550 shipped, which got several claims wrong. Two mattered:

- It advised testing `grafana_json` in the API's `findAll` filter. That filter is deliberately skipped when a `uid` is supplied, because the SLO dialog and `useAddSLOForm`'s by-uid lookup both need artificial rows — and `useDashboardManagement.artificialDashboards.test.ts` exists to stop exactly that change. Now documented as "do not tighten this".
- It stated the uid-scoping rule as settled while the shipped code violated it. That is the regression above; the docs now describe the fix.

`1f5d5d65` corrects something the correction pass got wrong in turn, and it is the one worth reading:

> The docs called the `grafana_id` ranges a convention (800000+ Dynatrace, 900000+ perf-test) and described rows in the 900000+ range as legacy data.

Neither holds. Nothing emits 900000+ — the perf-test path creates no synthetic row at all. And real Grafana ids are snowflake-style and enormous, so they land far above both ranges. On the dev database **40 of 46 rows sit above 900000 and every one is a real dashboard**. A reader trusting the old text would treat 40 real dashboards as legacy placeholders, and any `grafana_id >= 800000` check classifies the entire table as artificial. The docs now say plainly: never classify by `grafana_id`; use `grafana_json` and the `metrics_sources` join.

## Test Coverage

One new regression test, mutation-verified: reverting only the instance scope in the service fails exactly that test and nothing else.

```
apps/api .../grafana-dashboards.service.spec.ts
  remove()
   ├── [★★★ NEW] uid arm scoped to the instance — asserts the where clause shape
   ├── [★★★] count > 0 → ConflictException
   ├── [★★★] 23503 → ConflictException (RLS-hidden rows, count/delete race)
   ├── [★★★] refused delete writes no audit entry
   └── [★★★] entity missing → NotFoundException
```

The assertion pins the `where` array shape rather than a returned value, because the count runs through a mocked EntityManager — a wrong column would otherwise pass silently.

Tests: 140 in the two grafana-dashboards suites (was 139).

## Pre-Landing Review

No separate review pass on this one. The change is four lines of production code in a path #550 reviewed heavily, plus documentation. The regression it fixes was found by the doc-release agent reading the code against the docs it was writing — a cross-check I would not have run deliberately, and it caught what two review passes and my own container verification missed.

## Design Review

No frontend files changed.

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed.

## TODOS

No items completed. The P2 filed in #550 (a 412 on a referenced dashboard is a second, untouched restore loop) still stands.

## Documentation

Five files, all listed above: `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `apps/api/src/modules/grafana/README.md` (canonical), `docs/readmes/api-modules/grafana-README.md` (mirror, re-synced — it had drifted), `docs/reference/Apps/Grafana Sync/Grafana Sync Overview.md`.

Known doc debt, not addressed here: `docs/readmes/` is a hand-maintained mirror with no sync script and is unreachable from README.md or the CLAUDE.md index, and `AGENTS.md` has drifted from `CLAUDE.md` beyond this change.

## Test plan

- [x] Full monorepo suite green: 14/14 turbo tasks
- [x] apps/api grafana-dashboards: 140 passed
- [x] `npm run type-check` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] Pre-push preflight green, including the RLS suite
- [x] Regression reproduced on live data before the fix, and the mutation check confirms the new test catches it
- [ ] **Still not verified end-to-end over HTTP**, same as #550: the local Keycloak rejects the documented credentials and `perfana-api` is bearer-only. Both the 409 and this fix are proven by unit tests and SQL, not by a live request.

author: sydlexius
body:
## What

Arms GitHub's **native auto-merge** on Dependabot PRs, in the same workflow that already auto-approves them. An approved patch/minor PR now merges itself once this repo's branch ruleset reports its required checks green.

Purely additive here: this repo has no merge workflow. Dependabot PRs were auto-approved and then waited for a human to press merge.

## Why now

This is one of 12 repos in a sweep. Elsewhere the sweep replaces a `dependabot-merge.yml` that polled with `gh pr checks --watch` -- that call resolves `checkSuite.workflowRun`, needs the `actions: read` scope it was never granted, and the script read the resulting `Resource not accessible by integration` error as a *failing check*. Green PRs never merged. Native auto-merge has no polling loop to misread.

## Also: the semver guard now fails closed

The guard was `update-type != 'version-update:semver-major'`. `dependabot/fetch-metadata` emits an **empty** `update-type` when it cannot classify an update -- a Docker digest bump with no semver, or any PR carrying a non-Dependabot commit -- and `'' != 'semver-major'` is true, so the unclassifiable case took the permissive branch. It is now a positive allowlist naming patch and minor, so anything unclassifiable is skipped rather than merged.

Grouped updates were checked and are safe either way: `fetch-metadata` reduces a group to its highest severity, so a major among minors reports major. Confirmed on a real grouped PR run, not inferred.

## Security

`contents: write` is required by the `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` mutation. It is bounded:

- Trigger is `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`, with a job-level `dependabot[bot]` author guard -- no PR-authored code runs with the scope.
- The `Protect main` ruleset has `bypass_actors: []`, `non_fast_forward`, `deletion`, and `required_signatures`, so the token cannot rewrite or delete `main`.
- Native auto-merge honors required status checks; it does not bypass the ruleset.

## Review notes

Verified by an adversarial review pass before opening: no ruleset required-check context references a deleted job, and no surviving workflow's `workflow_run` names one. That review also caught two things now fixed -- **stillwater was dropped from this sweep** (its merge workflow already used `--auto` plus a PAT-authored `update-branch` refresher that native auto-merge cannot replace under `strict_required_status_checks_policy`), and the commit messages were rewritten per repo to state each one's actual history.

**Not yet observed in the wild:** whether `gh pr merge --auto` can 422 when armed at PR-open before checks report. If it does, the step fails loudly rather than silently. Worth watching on the first real Dependabot PR.

author: cuibonobo
body:
## Summary

Adds an `unlisted` state for records that withholds them from enumeration while keeping them readable by ID. This is orthogonal to permissions: `unlistedAt` says nothing about who may read a record, only whether it is discoverable without already holding its ID.

**New APIs:**
- `stack.create(typeId, content, { unlisted: true })` — create a record already unlisted, with no window where it's briefly enumerable
- `stack.setUnlisted(id, unlisted)` — toggle unlisted state on an existing record
- `RecordFilter.includeUnlisted` and `SubscribeOptions.includeUnlisted` — opt back into seeing unlisted records (owner-only under `ScopedStack`)

**Behavior:**
- Unlisted records are excluded from unfiltered `query()` and the change feed by default, matching the posture of soft-deleted records
- `get()` still resolves unlisted records for anyone who may read them
- The `unlist` transition emits as kind `deleted` / op `unlist` (so subscribers already holding the record are told to drop it), while `list` emits as kind `changed` / op `list` (the publish moment)
- Under `ScopedStack`, `setUnlisted()` is gated exactly like `setPermissions()` — both decide discoverability, not readability. `includeUnlisted` is refused to everyone but the stack owner acting alone, since enumeration standing rests on nothing but ownership

## Spec

Updated:
- `docs/spec/access-control.md` — new § Unlisted records, explaining the three-tier enumeration model (enforced, defaulted, advisory) and the owner-only `includeUnlisted` gate
- `docs/spec/events.md` — documents `unlist` and `list` ops and their kind mappings; explains why `unlist` reaches default subscribers despite the post-change state being excluded
- `docs/spec/data-model.md` — adds `unlistedAt?: Date` field to `StackRecord`
- `docs/spec/wire-format.md` — wire format guidance for the new field and query parameter

body:
## Summary

The dark theme's `--lx-color-text-dim` measured **3.19:1** on the `#0b0e14` canvas, below the **4.5:1** WCAG 2.1 AA minimum (1.4.3) for normal-size text. This raises it to `#7c8797` (**4.61:1**) and deletes the `color-contrast` entry from `KnownUnblockedRuleIds` in the accessibility sweep, so the rule blocks for good and this class of defect cannot silently return.

Closes #1801.

## The light palette was worse, and is fixed too

The issue named only the dark theme, but the light palette's dim token was `#8a93a3` = **2.91:1** on its `#f6f8fb` canvas - a worse instance of the same defect. The axe sweep structurally cannot see it, because it only exercises the default (dark) theme.

Fixing dark alone would have meant the newly un-suppressed `color-contrast` rule still carried an unfixed light-theme instance - exactly the state #1801 exists to end. Light `text-dim` is therefore darkened to `#656f7d` (**4.83:1**). Both directions are the same fix: move the dim token *away* from its canvas, which is lighter on dark and darker on light.

## Guard added

`test/lattice.explorer/Hygiene/TextContrastTokenHygieneTests.cs` computes WCAG relative luminance directly from `lattice-tokens.css` and asserts every text token clears AA against the surfaces it is used on, for **both** palettes. This is a fast unit-level gate, so unlike the Playwright sweep it runs on every PR and covers the light theme.

The tests assert a non-vacuous scan count, so the guard fails if the parser ever stops finding tokens rather than silently passing.

## Verification

- `TextContrastTokenHygieneTests` - 6/6 passing.
- `Orleans.Lattice.Explorer.UITests` builds clean, 0 warnings, 0 errors, with the allow-list removed.
- Contrast ratios computed independently of axe, per the WCAG relative-luminance formula.

## Provenance

This work was produced by a `feature-dev` agent session as part of an instruction-tuning experiment (that session's own PR, #1810, was opened against a non-`main` base with a non-compliant branch name and is superseded by this one). The change itself is unmodified from that session apart from being rebased onto `main`; it has been re-reviewed, rebuilt and re-tested here.

Follow-up #1809 tracks widening the sweep to more surfaces, which the issue invited and which is deliberately out of scope here.

author: sydlexius
body:
## What

Replaces the polling merge workflow with GitHub's **native auto-merge**, armed in the same workflow that already auto-approves. An approved patch/minor PR now merges itself once this repo's branch ruleset reports its required checks green.

## Why now

This repo carried a `dependabot-merge.yml` that polled with `gh pr checks --watch` -- that call resolves `checkSuite.workflowRun`, needs the `actions: read` scope it was never granted, and the script read the resulting `Resource not accessible by integration` error as a *failing check*. Green PRs never merged. Native auto-merge has no polling loop to misread.

## Also: the semver guard now fails closed

The guard was `update-type != 'version-update:semver-major'`. `dependabot/fetch-metadata` emits an **empty** `update-type` when it cannot classify an update -- a Docker digest bump with no semver, or any PR carrying a non-Dependabot commit -- and `'' != 'semver-major'` is true, so the unclassifiable case took the permissive branch. It is now a positive allowlist naming patch and minor, so anything unclassifiable is skipped rather than merged.

Grouped updates were checked and are safe either way: `fetch-metadata` reduces a group to its highest severity, so a major among minors reports major. Confirmed on a real grouped PR run, not inferred.

## Security

`contents: write` is required by the `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` mutation. It is bounded:

- Trigger is `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`, with a job-level `dependabot[bot]` author guard -- no PR-authored code runs with the scope.
- The `Protect main` ruleset has `bypass_actors: []`, `non_fast_forward`, `deletion`, and `required_signatures`, so the token cannot rewrite or delete `main`.
- Native auto-merge honors required status checks; it does not bypass the ruleset.

## Review notes

Verified by an adversarial review pass before opening: no ruleset required-check context references a deleted job, and no surviving workflow's `workflow_run` names one. That review also caught two things now fixed -- **stillwater was dropped from this sweep** (its merge workflow already used `--auto` plus a PAT-authored `update-branch` refresher that native auto-merge cannot replace under `strict_required_status_checks_policy`), and the commit messages were rewritten per repo to state each one's actual history.

**Not yet observed in the wild:** whether `gh pr merge --auto` can 422 when armed at PR-open before checks report. If it does, the step fails loudly rather than silently. Worth watching on the first real Dependabot PR.
