body:
El usuario reportó que conectar a un canal tardaba bastante. En `supabase/functions/tiktok-connect/index.ts` (el proxy WebSocket hacia Euler Stream) había dos cosas sumando demora innecesaria al camino crítico de "conectar":

1. Usaba el paquete npm `@supabase/supabase-js` solo para leer una fila de `api_secrets`. Cargar un paquete npm en un Edge Function de Deno tiene un costo de arranque en frío notable — se paga en cada conexión que le toca una instancia recién despertada. Se reemplaza por un `fetch()` directo a PostgREST, sin dependencias externas.

2. Se hacía `await getEulerStreamApiKey(...)` **antes** de aceptar el WebSocket del navegador — el navegador no veía el socket como "abierto" hasta que volvía esa consulta a la base. Ahora el WebSocket se acepta primero, y la key se pide en paralelo — recién se espera justo antes de necesitarla para abrir la conexión hacia Euler Stream.

La otra pata de la demora — cuánto tarda Euler Stream en resolver el canal contra TikTok — no depende de este proxy.

Ya deployado a producción (`tiktok-connect` v19).

author: lyxot
body:
## Problem

A tool confirmation card can name a different record than the one the tool is run with.

`tool_start` carries its arguments as a JSON object. The browser reads the SSE line with a single `JSON.parse`, which rounds any integer past 2^53, and the chat adapter rendered `JSON.stringify` of that already-rounded value into `argsText`, which the card prints verbatim. The backend executes the exact integer.

```text
wire:      {"id":9007199254740993}
card:      {"id":9007199254740992}
executed:   9007199254740993
```

Studio gates tool execution on an approval, so this is a confirmation-boundary defect rather than a cosmetic one: a user can approve one record id and have another acted on. The same rounded value is then persisted and replayed to the model, since stored replay prefers `argsText`.

Ordinary `int64` values are all above 2^53 — snowflake ids, unix timestamps in nanoseconds, 64-bit hashes — so this is not confined to contrived inputs.

## What changed

`tool_start` now also carries `arguments_text`, the backend's own canonical encoding of the same arguments, and the adapter renders that in preference to re-encoding what it parsed. `arguments` keeps its type and shape, so every existing consumer is untouched and an event without the new field still renders.

`as_assistant_tool_call` and the new field share one encoder, so the text a user approves and the text replayed to the model cannot drift apart. The loop that hand-builds cards for calls it announces but never runs carries the field too.

On the client the selection rule lives beside the existing replay helper in `tool-call-arguments.ts`. `tool_end` merges further arguments into a call, so the rule keeps the exact text only while nothing has actually merged in, and rebuilds it once something has — judged by whether the merge happened, not by comparing two lossy encodings, which can collide.

## Why not the alternatives

Sending the number as a string would reach every consumer of the event to fix a display defect. A BigInt-aware parser on the client changes the type of every number in every event, whose blast radius is the whole stream. Declining to type large integers upstream would hand a tool that declares `int64` a string for exactly the values it exists to receive.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest studio/backend/tests/ -k "tool_loop or tool_call or passthrough or truncated_and_budget" -q
npm test --prefix studio/frontend
```

1598 backend tests and 6007 frontend tests pass; `tsc -b` is clean and eslint on the changed file reports what the base branch reports.

Beyond the suites, the end-to-end claim was checked by feeding a real emitted SSE line through a real `node` `JSON.parse`: the card text is `{"id":9007199254740992}` before this change and `{"id":9007199254740993}` after. Every added test was mutation-checked — dropping the field from either emitter, encoding the wrong value, letting the two encoders drift, dropping the client preference, re-encoding when nothing merged, and unwiring either adapter branch each fail exactly the test that covers them.

author: jefrykurniaone
body:
## What ships

Chart infra for `spec:rally-insights` (#146), ticket #169. Recharts 3.8.0 exact pin (not range), shadcn chart component (`src/components/ui/chart.tsx`), Rally chart tokens wired in, `ChartFigure` — the one accessible wrapper #170/#171/#172 compose onto. No real chart data — infra only, per ticket scope.

**Recharts version + React 19 evidence.** `recharts@3.8.0` peerDependencies: `"react": "^16.8.0 || ^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0"` — via `npm view recharts@3.8.0 peerDependencies`, against installed `react@19.2.4`. `package.json` pins `"recharts": "3.8.0"` exact.

## Merge status

Branch was off `5839997`; merged `origin/main` after #149/#150/#151/#157 all landed. Merge commit `d5b5818`. Merge alone (no rebase), per instruction. One post-merge fix commit `98a33fa` — see below.

**Head SHA: `98a33fa`.**

## `Badge` deleted by #149 — swapped to `Chip`

#149 deleted `src/components/ui/badge.tsx` outright and shipped `src/components/ui/chip.tsx` (`label` required prop, `children` removed from the type — a chip cannot render with no text). `ChartFigure`'s empty state now renders `<Chip variant='neutral' label={chipLabel} />`, not `Badge`. Confirmed: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean against the new `Chip` contract, and the empty-state screenshot (light/dark, both already captured) shows the pill with its label — same visual family as before (`neutral` resolves to the Shells wash, same as the old `secondary` Badge did), just the correct component now. Fix commit `98a33fa`.

`ChartFigure` stays a plain Server Component — no `'use client'` added. Checked, not assumed: it takes every string as a prop and never reads the dictionary itself, same constraint `src/components/ui/empty-state.tsx` documents on `main` (a `'use client'` directive there would break a Server Component call site passing a `LucideIcon` reference as a prop). `ChartFigure` was already built that way before this was raised, so nothing changed here.

## Wrapper API — what #170/#171/#172 inherit

`src/components/charts/chart-figure.tsx`, `ChartFigure`:

```ts
interface ChartFigureValue { label: string; value: string }  // pre-formatted; wrapper never formats a number

interface ChartFigureProps {
  title: ReactNode;
  caption?: ReactNode;
  values: readonly ChartFigureValue[];   // empty array IS the empty-state trigger, no separate isEmpty flag
  valuesToggleLabel: string;             // disclosure summary text
  valuesListLabel: string;               // aria-label on the <ul>
  emptyChipLabel: string;                // passed to Chip's label prop
  emptyMessage: string;                  // the one sentence
  children: ReactNode;                   // a <ChartContainer> around BarChart/PieChart/LineChart, omitted when values is empty
  className?: string;
}
```

Decisions later tickets inherit:

- Empty derives from `values.length === 0`, not a separate flag — never a chart plus a contradictory `isEmpty`.
- Caller supplies every string (title, caption, empty copy, toggle/list labels) — wrapper has zero hardcoded copy. #170-172 own their own dictionary keys, can reuse `insights.*` for shared toggle/empty wording.
- Caller supplies pre-formatted value strings — no Rupiah/percentage formatting in the wrapper, keeps money/percentage logic in resolvers, not the view.
- `children` free-form — any Recharts tree, not just Bar/Pie/Line.

## Chart tokens, both themes

`board-materials.css` (#148) defines `--chart-1..5`; `globals.css`'s `@theme inline` re-exposes as `--color-chart-1..5`. `src/lib/chart-tokens.ts` names them (`CHART_COLORS`, `chartColor(i)`) — nothing hardcodes a hex:

| Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| `chart-1` (PBP Green) | `#3ED27E` | `#3ED27E` |
| `chart-2` (Purple) | `#6C4CF0` | `#B7A4F7` |
| `chart-3` (Orange) | `#E8701A` | `#F2A24A` |
| `chart-4` (Dark Red) | `#9E2B25` | `#F08078` |
| `chart-5` (Black Green / Lime) | `#0E1F17` | `#D8F25E` |

**Measured contrast** (committed `board-materials.css` values, WCAG formula from `theme-contrast.ts`):

| | vs card, light | vs card, dark |
|---|---|---|
| chart-1 | 1.96:1 | 7.54:1 |
| chart-2 | 5.34:1 | 6.80:1 |
| chart-3 | 3.10:1 | 7.06:1 |
| chart-4 | 7.43:1 | 5.67:1 |
| chart-5 | 17.11:1 | 11.80:1 |

**Chart-1 flag — not fixed here, tracked forward.** `chart-1` (PBP Green) on the light-theme card clears only 1.96:1, short of the 3:1 UI floor for a series mark. Real visibility problem for a light-theme bar or line drawn in chart-1 alone. Not a defect in this wrapper — DESIGN.md deliberately keeps chart colours out of `AA_PAIRS` ("colour is free for charts by decision"), and recolouring a shared token is outside this ticket's scope. Orchestrator is recording this against **#152** (finalises `DESIGN.md`, governs the token layer) and against **#170** and **#171** (first tickets to draw real series and hit it).

## Accessibility

- Text list is the accessibility contract. `ChartFigure` always renders `<details><summary>{toggleLabel}</summary><ul aria-label={listLabel}>...` — collapsed by default (toggled, not just visually-hidden), keyboard-operable via native `<details>`, no JS state.
- Empty state: `Chip variant='neutral' label={emptyChipLabel}` plus one sentence, in place of the chart.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: `src/hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts` (`useReducedMotion()`) — the hook #170-172 pass into Recharts' `isAnimationActive`. Not wired into a real chart here (no real chart drawn by this ticket); proven against the demo.

## Screenshots

Captured against a temporary demo (bar: dues collected/owed; donut: money by Activity; line: seats-filled trend; a 4th empty-state card), real committed `board-materials.css` tokens, both themes. Left in the session scratchpad, not the repo — orchestrator attaches them:

- `chart-demo-light.png` — bar (green/purple), donut (orange/dark-red/lime), line (green), empty-state chip, light theme.
- `chart-demo-dark.png` — same four cards, dark theme (bars purple-lit, donut orange/dark-red-lit/lime, line green).
- `chart-demo-dark-values-expanded.png` — text-list disclosure open, Rupiah value pairs matching the bar chart's six Billing Periods.

## Bundle delta vs baseline (44 JS chunks / 2,130,088 B; 1 CSS / 92,997 B, `main`@`363df8a`)

Re-measured after the merge, since the merged tree is a different starting point than what was measured pre-merge:

- JS: 44 chunks, 2,135,009 bytes — **+4,921 bytes**.
- CSS: 1 file, 92,602 bytes — **-395 bytes**.

This delta is the whole merged tree against the original baseline, not #169 in isolation — #148/#149/#150/#151/#157 all landed in between (mark-forms.css deleted, motion.css added, badge.tsx deleted, chip.tsx added, and more). Recharts itself still costs close to nothing: nothing on a real route imports `ChartFigure` or `chart.tsx` yet, so tree-shaking drops it from every shipped chunk. Real cost lands with #170/#171/#172.

## Demo removed

`src/app/_chart-demo-169.tsx` and the render/bundle scripts used for the screenshots were deleted before the first commit — never landed in git history. `git show --stat` on both `#169` commits shows only wrapper/token/hook/dictionary files.

## Gate — full re-run after merge

- `npm run lint` — clean, zero warnings.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npm test` — **489/29 passed**, matches the new post-merge baseline exactly (not the old 464/28 this ticket started against).
- `npm run build` — green.

author: surgeservicesllc
body:
The first `scope=services-crm` hosted dispatch (run 33329711983) **failed its own postflight**: "the CRM immutability grants are wrong". Root cause: the hosted database's default privileges GRANT ALL on every new table to `authenticated`, so `20260830000500`'s narrow timeline grants — the append-only audit-trail guarantee — shipped wide on hosted. A narrower grant on top of ALL narrows nothing. PGlite carries no default privileges, which is why every local suite stayed green; the postflight caught it exactly as designed.

## The fix

- **`20260830000600_crm_grant_narrowing.sql`**: revoke-then-grant on the four CRM tables — collapse whatever the defaults handed out, then state each exact capability set again (accounts: no delete; timeline: select+insert only). Idempotent; a no-op restatement on a fresh chain.
- **The `services-crm` scope step now applies both files** with both ledger repairs; its unchanged postflight is the proof of the final state.
- **The behavior suite now installs hosted-style default privileges immediately before the CRM migrations run** — windowed, because under the whole chain they contradict an earlier migration's own security-catalog assertion — so an immutability claim that relies on the *absence* of a grant fails locally the way it failed on hosted. This class of defect can no longer pass the local gate.

## Gates

services-crm-foundation behavior 6/6 green under the hosted-defaults emulation; runbook/workflow guards 15; hosted-grant + phase1e census suites green on the new chain (46 total in the combined run); lint zero warnings; `tsc --noEmit` clean. Runbook 185; sentinels swept to `20260830000600`.

After merge: re-dispatch `scope=services-crm` and confirm the postflight passes on hosted.

author: siebebaree
body:
Notchlet had no way to ship. The app had no icon (the imageset was empty), nothing built a release, and the Sparkle update feed pointed at a URL that 404s. Nobody could download it.

Now pushing a `vX.Y.Z` tag does the whole thing: archive with the Developer ID identity, notarize, publish the GitHub release and deploy the appcast to Pages. Roughly twelve minutes, no laptop involved.

## Notes for review

**Both notarization passes are deliberate.** Apple issues one ticket per artifact. Stapling the `.app` is what lets a Sparkle-installed copy pass Gatekeeper with no network; stapling the DMG is what stops the download itself being flagged.

**Version numbers come from CI.** Sparkle compares `CFBundleVersion`, not the marketing version, so a forgotten bump silently hides an update from everyone already running the app. The tag and the run number own both values, which removes the failure mode rather than documenting it.

**`hdiutil` rather than `create-dmg`.** `create-dmg` positions icons by driving Finder over AppleScript, which is a known flake source on headless runners. The `Applications` symlink is the only part of the layout that carries meaning. Worth revisiting if the DMG ever gets a designed background.

**The icon is generated, not hand-cut.** `Scripts/AppIcon.svg` is the website's icon with one change: a widened `viewBox` that insets the artwork to the macOS grid, where the rounded square fills 824 of a 1024 canvas. Shipped edge to edge it would be visibly the largest icon in the Dock. `Scripts/make-appicon.sh` renders the catalog through a single 1024 master, because asking `sips` for a small canvas directly drops the clipped background gradient and returns only the dark glass panel.

## Verified locally

Archive succeeds clean with the Developer ID identity, universal and hardened. Version injection from the command line produces the expected `CFBundleShortVersionString` and `CFBundleVersion`. The icon compiles to `AppIcon.icns` and renders correctly. The DMG builds, signs, timestamps and mounts with the app and the Applications symlink.

Not yet exercised: notarization and the appcast, which need the runner. Rehearse with a manual workflow run before the first tag.

author: srid
body:
## The residue this closes

olai integrates with two things that are not olai. Both were extracted into packages of their own
once — `@olai/kolu-client`, `@olai/kolu-ui`, `@olai/odu-client` — and both left a residue behind in
the packages that are supposed to know nothing about them:

- a `kolu.ts` in `@olai/chat`, and a `koluConfig.ts` + `claimants.ts` in `@olai/server`
- a named `wiring.kolu` slot with a `koluHalf(…)` call beside it, and a read-back closure handing a
  plugin its own members back by spelled key
- four `...koluMembers` spreads in the middle of the wire spec, and a re-export tail of 30
  appliance-named symbols on the one package every browser bundles
- a row per plugin member in the server's expose map
- a `padi/` folder and an `odu-ci/` folder in `@olai/web`
- one property key spelled at seven sites across four packages

That residue was never sloppiness. It was olai's own **judgement about an appliance** — what an
absent padi means, which vault file is kolu's, which property wears which face — and it had nowhere
to live that was neither the appliance nor the core. `packages/plugins` is that place, and it is the
only one.

## The mount: one generic door, and the framework already owned it

A plugin declares a **whole surface** in its own package, with its own member names on it. Core
composes it as a **sibling** under the plugin's name:

```
core       surface/outlines/get        ← byte-unchanged
kolu       surface/kolu/fleet/get      ← declared `fleet`, in @olai/plugin-kolu
odu        surface/odu/ci/get          ← declared `ci`,    in @olai/plugin-odu
```

No general package computes any of those addresses. `composeSurfaceContracts` re-walks each
sibling's spec at `surface/<key>/`, and the key is the plugin's own `name`.

**Core does not become a sibling.** That reading would have moved `surface://collections/documents`,
an address an MCP client already writes, plus every tag assertion in the suite. Core keeps
`implementSurface` and its three-segment tags; the plugins go through `implementSurfaces` and get
four; and the two ride ONE WIRE as a **rooted bundle**, which is the framework's own shape end to
end (juspay/kolu#2222): `mergeDisjointGroups` where a server composes, `exposeRootedFaces` where it
gates, `connectSurfaces`' `core` slot where a browser dials. The fusion is safe by construction — the
framework forbids a `/` inside a name, so a three-segment set and a four-segment set cannot intersect
— and it is **counted** anyway, because the merge underneath is a last-writer-wins `Map.set` and a
silently dropped tag is a member that answers nothing with nobody told.

olai spelled that merge, the face union and the whole client seam for itself for one PR window; the
refactor round below deleted all of it. `packages/plugins/src/mechanics.test.ts` is the standing lint
that it stays deleted.

## The kinds

`@olai/format` imports no plugin and now needs to know nothing about terminals either: its kind
vocabulary is a **parameter**, and the server assembles the table from the enabled manifests and
hands it down as data — the same move the vault walks already make.

The closed union kept its exhaustiveness, which was the thing worth protecting. `PropType` gained
**one** arm, `contributed`, and the two tables are keyed by the built-in kinds alone — so an eighth
built-in is still a type error in four places, and a contributed kind is an arm both switches must
handle rather than a `default` that swallows it.

**BUILT and ENABLED are different questions** and the vocabulary carries both: a declaration naming
a kind whose plugin is not running is *accepted* and behaves as plain text, where a word no plugin
ever contributed is refused with the legal ones named. So `--plugins` cannot make a vault's file
wrong, and a door cannot appear and disappear with a flag.

## The fence

`packages/plugins/src/fence.test.ts`, as **equalities per package** rather than filtered lists
asserted empty — a rotted pattern reports nothing found and passes, which is the failure mode two
sweeps in this repo already sat red for two days over. It reads four grammars (positional
specifiers, the runtime's own `scanImports`, CSS `@import`, and `workspace:*` in a manifest).
Mutation-tested: three planted violations, one per grammar, produced two named failures.

It is a bun test and not a shell script on purpose. Both old fences ended in
`rg … 2>/dev/null || true` over `packages/<name>/src`, and both halves are hazards — `ripgrep` is not
in the dev shell, so a machine without an ambient one gets a **green fence that never ran**; and
`packages/<name>/src` misses `packages/tests` entirely, which is how four product-tier `@kolu/*`
imports sat in its geometry harness with `just check` green.

The two per-plugin scripts are now **one** `scripts/check-hydrated-deps.sh`, taking the pin and its
manifest. Both `just` leg names are preserved, so the CI graph odu expands is unchanged.

It does **not** fail on prose. Prose that names a package is not a dependency, and a fence that
failed on a comment is one people learn to work around — `check-kolu-deps.sh`'s own ruling, kept.

## Enablement

`--plugins` is CLI/nix-only, the git-policy shape (#434): no settings file, no browser toggle,
preferences draws the rows read-only. `Flag.withDefault(null)` so *nobody said* stays
distinguishable from `--plugins=` typed out loud; the names derive from the registry so the flag's
own file spells none of them.

```
$ olai web docs --plugins=nope
olai web: --plugins names nope, which this build does not have. It was built with kolu, odu.
```

## Evidence

Against a real `olai web` on a real vault: **this host's actual padi**, and an odu coordinator
fixture standing on a real unix socket at the path the resolution rule computes from the lane's own
`pr-url` and `worktree`. Nothing is mocked at the app's edge.

Preferences names each plugin and says whether this serve runs it — read-only, naming where the
decision lives:

![prefs-plugin-rows-enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e017c2a6-3930-4d42-922a-ac5072fe0ee6)

A lane row's `terminal` property wearing kolu's door, live:

![terminal-door-enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0f6c68c-2399-4b49-be85-dd09f49302e2)

...and its `worktree` wearing odu's chip:

![ci-chip-enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5099b227-e1ae-46ad-8146-069622be037b)

The chip's press opens the run matrix:

![ci-matrix-open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06912985-c802-4ba3-99d2-414e494abd69)

**The same vault with `--plugins=`, both daemons still running.** The rows are still drawn, because a
disabled plugin is not an absent row — a roster that hid what was off would be a page you cannot
learn the flag from:

![prefs-plugin-rows-disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f9c7562-5d37-4d54-b0cc-e78f62a16bc7)

...and the lane draws the ordinary absent state. `terminal` and `worktree` are still there, still
greppable, still editable, drawing as the plain chips any undressed property draws:

![absent-state-disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f96b2a2a-beb6-47c3-95ad-535436457a1b)

**The evidence run earned its place: it found two defects the 4654-test suite could not.** Both are
invisible to a unit test and both look exactly like a working app in a quiet vault.

1. **Every plugin context was silently wrong.** `PluginsMounted` folded the mounts over
   `props.children`, so the page was *created* in the app's own owner before any provider existed —
   and Solid resolves a context against the owner a component was created under. A live serve logged
   `padi connected` and `odu run live` in the same second the tab drew the pill as `absent` and no
   chip at all; the clients *had* the data. Folding over thunks fixes it at the root.
2. **A disabled plugin still drew.** With `--plugins=` the terminal door rendered in its own "there
   is no padi" arm — a row complaining about a tool the operator delib

author: imm0r
body:
The last one still drawn over: `favourite_pins_container_frame` — the bookmarks panel.

## Not a measurement problem

The browser shows it as an ordinary element: child 15 of the world screen, `913 × 591` at `0,86`, flags `0x00502EF3` (visible), same parent as `header`. It measures, it reports itself showing, and it is nowhere near screen-sized. Every rule added so far says it should be kept out.

`ScreenRegion` capped the keep-out list at **sixteen** and silently stopped there.

Sixteen was far past what the HUD alone has parts — which is what it was set for. Then the atlas arrived with three sources at once (the HUD, the world screen's furniture, the panels beside it) and the honest count went to nearly thirty. **A cap that drops the tail is a cap that decides which parts of the interface are honoured by their position in a list**, and the bookmarks panel was at the end of it. Everything ahead of it worked, which is exactly what makes the symptom read as something else.

## The fix

- Cap is **64** — high enough that a real interface never reaches it.
- `ScreenRegion.Refused` counts what it turned away, and the readout says `(N REFUSED - past the cap of 64)`. The next one shouldn't cost a screenshot to find; this one did.
- **A rectangle with no area is not a refusal.** An off-screen panel or a torn read was never a rectangle the cap turned away, and counting those would make that line cry wolf on ordinary frames.

Costs at thirty keep-outs: the map's terrain quad redraws per free piece (~20, trivial); the atlas clips lines per segment, so 2000 segments × 30 rectangles of float comparisons, and `Clear` is one pass per label.

## Tests

3 new (2 rewritten), 2183 total green, zero warnings: past the cap is refused *and* said so about, thirty parts is nowhere near it, and a no-area rectangle does not count as refused.

author: karthiksundar2002
body:
Two cluster-reproducibility fixes for the nwm Table A runs. Without them a preempted run silently restarts from step 1 and then crawls on network-filesystem memmap reads, so the runs can't currently be reproduced or resumed off this clone.

## `impls/main.py` — resume continues the step counter

`--restore_epoch` restored the agent weights but the training loop still started at step 1, so a preempted run redid every step it had already completed. For nwm runs the loop now starts at `restore_epoch + 1`, and the sampling RNG is re-seeded to `seed + restore_epoch` so post-restart batches aren't a replay of the pre-restart draws.

```python
start_step = 1
if FLAGS.restore_path is not None:
    agent = restore_agent(agent, FLAGS.restore_path, FLAGS.restore_epoch)
    if use_nwm:
        start_step = FLAGS.restore_epoch + 1
        np.random.seed(FLAGS.seed + FLAGS.restore_epoch)
for i in tqdm.tqdm(range(start_step, FLAGS.train_steps + 1), ...):
```

Gated on `use_nwm`, so stock ogbench behaviour is unchanged.

## `impls/utils/nwm_data.py` — `NWM_MEMMAP=0` reads exports into RAM

The exports were unconditionally memmapped. Random memmap reads over the cluster's network filesystem run at ~1-2 it/s, roughly 10x slower than the update step itself. `NWM_MEMMAP=0` loads the arrays into RAM instead; the tok train split is ~11 GB, so jobs using it need their memory budgeted accordingly. Default (`1`) keeps the existing memmap path.

+11 / -4 across the two files.

author: iridiummaster
body:
## Summary

- Select the newest media-bearing user message in the active turn, so trailing user-role context injections do not hide an attachment.
- Use that same selected message for vision encoding, exact multimodal-token placement, Qwen M-RoPE construction, and LFM2 image segments.
- Preserve assistant-prefix continuation and assistant tool-call/result flows while treating ordinary assistant replies as durable turn boundaries.

## Problem

Agent clients can append project or system context as additional `user` messages after the human message. The vision path previously selected only the final user message. A request shaped like `user(image), user(context)` therefore decoded the image during JSON parsing but never encoded or inserted it into the prompt.

This was reproduced through DeepSeek Harness with Qwen3.8 Flash Next: the uploaded image was present in the request, but mlx-serve selected the trailing context message and generated a text-only prompt.

## Validation

- `zig build test -Dtest-filter=activeTurnMediaMessage`
- `zig build test -Dtest-filter=insertMultimodalTokens`
- `zig build test`
- `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`
- `bash -n tests/test_vision_prefix_cache.sh`
- Live Qwen3.8 Flash Next regression: the Harness-shaped request processed one image, inserted 484 vision tokens at the owning user turn, built Qwen M-RoPE, and correctly read `Grey Fox Tr / Waterfall Dr`.
- Text-only continuation did not re-encode the historical image.
- Autoreview reported no actionable findings.

## Scope

This change deliberately selects new media only from the active turn. Reconstructing historical multimodal placeholders on a later text-only turn is a separate pre-existing multi-message concern and is not claimed here.

author: benjarvis
body:
The NFS models grew up alongside one implementation. The SMB2 suite already guards against that drift by replaying its corpus at Samba; this does the same for NFS, replaying the generated NFSv3 and NFSv4 corpora against a real **NFS-Ganesha** server — a userspace implementation nobody consulted while writing the models. It is the first step of a larger effort to mine correctness knowledge from independent high-quality NFS servers and test suites (knfsd, pynfs) into the models.

### What's here — `harness/nfs/`, the NFS analog of `harness/samba/`

- **`nfs3_client.py` / `nfs4_client.py`** — a standalone, hand-rolled ONC-RPC + XDR NFSv3 and NFSv4.0/4.1/4.2 client. Revived from a retired in-tree chimera harness, relicensed MIT, and brought up to the current model (SECINFO, BIND_CONN_TO_SESSION, the RFC 7862 data ops, the wide-attribute GETATTR/VERIFY, the component-name and compound-tag sentinels). Shares no code with any server's marshalling.
- **`nfs4_replay.py` / `nfs3_replay.py`** — drive each trace's compounds on the wire, maintaining the ino/clientid/session/stateid indirections and the change-attribute consistency oracle, and compare every reply to what the model baked in. A capability the server lacks is a SKIP, never a failure.
- **`deviations.py` + `ganesha_deviations.py` / `knfsd_deviations.py`** — the same registry contract the Samba harness uses: a divergence that matches a recorded, cited entry is reconciled; an unrecorded one fails.
- **`run_nfs_mbt.sh`** — stands up rpcbind and a **fresh ganesha per trace** in a private netns (its own `/run`, its export a loop-mounted ext4 image), so a trace always starts from an empty root and no protocol state. knfsd (a KVM guest) is stubbed to SKIP until [kvm-test-base#12](https://github.com/chimera-nas/kvm-test-base/pull/12) ships `nfs-kernel-server`.

CI gets a `ganesha` job beside `samba`; CMake registers one ctest per batch under the `ganesha` label, guarded so a consumer does not inherit it.

### First findings (recorded, so the suite stays enumerable while they're triaged)

| id | verdict | what |
|----|---------|------|
| GD-1 | server | ganesha's change attribute is coarse `ctime`; two mutations in one clock tick report the same value (RFC 7530/8881 §5.8.1.4) |
| GD-2 / GN-1 | model | ACCESS returns only the bits meaningful for the object type; the model over-asserts the full requested mask (both ganesha and the reference server mask — a model fix pending a coordinated regenerate) |
| GD-3 | server | READLINK on a directory answers `NFS4ERR_INVAL` where RFC 7530 16.25.4 recommends `NFS4ERR_ISDIR` |

Triage of the remaining classes continues against this PR's CI runs (the harness is validated end-to-end locally against ganesha 6.5; the full matrix runs on the x86 ARC runners). **Not for merge yet** — this is the harness landing plus the first pass of findings.

Also folds in the merged `stepData` live-data flavor (#13) and the NLM unlock-within-range correction (#16) this corpus depends on.

author: kevinlourd
body:
Closes the rollout window opened in #3797. features-service **v0.153.0 is live in prod**, so `attributedOutcomes` is required on the wire and is now required here, matching the producer.

## The fallback is deleted, not kept

It derived the same answer by asking whether any lead row carried the key. That is fine while the producer sends every row, and it becomes actively wrong the moment it narrows server-side: a brand with a **live tracker and no lead having reached anything** receives zero rows, so the derivation reads *"nothing is attributed"* and the Leads page silently drops every outcome tab from a brand measuring outcomes perfectly well.

So the fallback would answer confidently and wrongly on **exactly the case the field exists for**. Throwing on a body that does not carry it is the honest answer; falling back is a silent wrong number.

## Verified in prod before making it required

Through the api-service gateway, brand `75d7e3e8`:

| call | bytes | leads | keys/row | `attributedOutcomes` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | 58,897 | 72 | 12 | all 7 |
| `?leads=full` | 10,899,958 | 9,854 | 36 | all 7 |

## Tests

Fixtures across four files carry the field, since a body without it is now shape rot. Two new cases:

- **the producer's list wins over a key present on a row** — every lead carries `signup: false` and the producer says it cannot attribute it; a key on a row is not a statement that it is measured
- **an absent field throws**, rather than falling back

Retired with the fallback: the case pinning the derived path's blind spot (`[]` for a body with no leads), which was the whole reason the served field exists.

**228 files / 2,999 tests green.** `tsc --noEmit` clean.

body:
## Objective

Keep catalog-meta Raft integration tests bounded but reliable through hosted Windows election stalls. Closes #4509.

## Context

The fixed-peer test exhausted its eight-second leader wait, and the backup/restore test reused a leader observation after a deliberately rejected log entry; both passed on unchanged-head reruns.

## Non-goals

- No production Raft behavior, configuration, or timeout-default changes.

## Design

- Raise the test harness condition deadline to 20 seconds.
- Reacquire the verified leader immediately before the post-rejection safe command.

## Scope

- Includes: two catalog-meta integration test files.

author: yibeichan
body:
Closes #325.

## The bug

`babs_check_setup` probes a hardcoded `<analysis>/inputs/data` before validating
the input datasets:

```python
temp_list = get_immediate_subdirectories(op.join(self.analysis_path, 'inputs/data'))
```

`babs init` clones each input dataset to its configured `path_in_babs`, so on any
project not using the default layout this raises a raw `FileNotFoundError` out of
`os.listdir` — not even the friendly `ValueError` on the line below, which only
fires for a directory that exists but is empty.

Since #369 this affects a layout **BABS itself generates**. The BIDS-study layout
puts inputs under `sourcedata/<name>`, so `babs init` writes:

```yaml
input_datasets:
  BIDS:
    path_in_babs: 'sourcedata/BIDS'
  NIDM:
    path_in_babs: 'sourcedata/NIDM'
```

and the resulting analysis directory has `sourcedata/{BIDS,NIDM}` and no `inputs/`
at all. `babs check-setup` cannot run on such a project, which means losing the
test-job and environment checks that do work — we currently skip check-setup
entirely on every run.

## The fix

The pre-check was already redundant. The per-dataset loop immediately below
resolves `in_ds.babs_project_analysis_path` and raises for a missing directory
or a non-DataLad dataset, using the configured path — so it covers everything
the hardcoded probe did, correctly.

The one condition the probe uniquely covered is "no input datasets configured",
which is a property of the config rather than of the filesystem. This PR checks
that directly and drops the path probe, so there is no second path-resolution
to keep in sync with `path_in_babs`.

`get_immediate_subdirectories` was imported here only for that call. It is now
unused within `babs/`, but its definition in `utils.py` is left in place — it is
public API and `tests/test_utils.py::test_get_immediate_subdirectories` covers it.

## Verification

Against a real BIDS-study-layout project (`path_in_babs: sourcedata/BIDS` and
`sourcedata/NIDM`), on `ea5d6f0`:

```
OLD pre-check: FileNotFoundError -> .../analysis/inputs/data
NEW pre-check: passes, 2 input dataset(s)
   BIDS   path_in_babs=sourcedata/BIDS   exists=True is_datalad=True
   NIDM   path_in_babs=sourcedata/NIDM   exists=True is_datalad=True
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on the changed file.

**On tests:** I did not add one. The existing `tests/test_check_setup.py` cases are
integration tests built on the `babs_project_*` fixtures and the simbids apptainer
image, which I can't run in my environment, and there is no study-layout fixture to
extend. Happy to add a regression test if you can point me at the fixture you'd want
it built on — a `path_in_babs`-varying project fixture would cover this directly.

author: tomguiz
body:
### One cause, two symptoms

Every email leaves through a Make scenario sending from **kiteforecast@outlook.com**. Microsoft suspends consumer accounts that send transactional mail in series — which is exactly what keeps happening to yours. Moving to a `hotmail.com` address would not have helped: same service, same policy.

It is also why the "What's new" test never arrived in Gmail. A consumer mailbox has no SPF or DKIM aligned to a domain you control, so Gmail files it as spam or drops it silently — Make accepted the send and reported success.

### What this adds

`_shared/mailer.ts`: template fetch (from `main`, same deploy story as Make), `[[placeholder]]` rendering including the dotted paths the reminder templates use (`[[session.wind_speed_peak_kn]]`), and a Resend send. `process-reminders` is wired to it.

### Merging this changes nothing

Without `RESEND_API_KEY`, `mailerReady()` is false and reminders keep leaving through Make exactly as before. **Setting the secret is the cutover. Clearing it is the rollback.** `email_log` records which route each email took, so you can see the switch happen.

A failed Resend send leaves the row unsent so the next run retries, rather than recording a delivery that never happened.

### What you need to do before it can be switched on

1. Create a Resend account (free tier is 3,000/month — you have 27 riders)
2. **Verify a domain.** This is the part that actually fixes deliverability, and it needs a domain you own — you are on `tomguiz.github.io` today, so this likely means buying one
3. Add the DNS records Resend gives you
4. `supabase secrets set RESEND_API_KEY=... MAIL_FROM='KiteForecast <hello@yourdomain>'`

Do not paste the key in chat — set it with the CLI.

### Notes

Env is read lazily rather than at import: reading `Deno.env` at module scope makes the pure rendering impossible to unit-test off Deno, and freezes the value at import time.

Subjects are copied verbatim from the Make scenario so the switch is invisible in an inbox. Both real reminder templates are rendered in the tests and asserted to leave no placeholder behind — shipping a literal `[[spot]]` to a rider is the failure mode worth pinning.

This covers reminders only. The other 17 Make modules (digest, what's-new, friend requests, spot claims) follow the same pattern once this one is proven in production.

408 unit tests passing.

author: thorstenhornung1
body:
Schritt 1 der Umsetzung — das Sicherheitsnetz, bevor die Domäne umgebaut wird
(§104 Schritt 1 und 2, Übersicht #67).

## Warum zuerst

Issue #16 verlangt für die TypeScript-Migration „keine fachlichen Änderungen“. Ohne einen
vorher existierenden Golden Master ist diese Zusage nicht überprüfbar, sondern nur
behauptbar. Die heutige Engine (`server/src/calc.js`) ist die einzige Quelle der Wahrheit für
die Betriebskostenabrechnung — sie wird hier eingefroren, bevor irgendetwas daneben entsteht.

## Was drin ist

**Kanon (#1).** Die 140 Invarianten aus den vier Spezifikationen stehen jetzt
dokumentübergreifend nummeriert in `CLAUDE.md`, dazu das Prioritätssystem F0/P0/C0/P1/P2/Step 20+
(§5, §108–§110), die PR-Checkliste (§73), die Lizenzprinzipien (§271.22–§271.24), die
Scope-Schlussentscheidung (§125–§127) und die Implementierungsreihenfolge (§104). `AGENTS.md`
verweist darauf statt zu duplizieren.

**Golden Master (#25, erste Hälfte).** Zehn Fixtures unter
`server/test/fixtures/settlement/`, je `db.json` + `expected.json` + `README.md` mit der
Handrechnung. Verglichen wird der Umfang aus §55, cent-genau und ohne Toleranz.

Die Erwartungswerte sind **strikt spec-first** hergeleitet — von Hand aus der Spezifikation
vorgerechnet, nicht aus dem Code abgelesen. **Alle zehn haben im ersten Durchlauf getroffen.**
Die Kernverteilung der Engine ist fachlich korrekt.

**Invariantentests (#26).** Zehn Eigenschaften, die für jede Eingabe gelten müssen.
Vier waren rot.

## Die drei behobenen Fehler

| | Befund | Wirkung |
|---|---|---|
| **B1** | Direktzuordnung auf eine nicht beteiligte Wohnung zählte den Anteil als verteilt, schrieb ihn aber niemandem gut | Der Betrag verschwand vollständig aus der Abrechnung — weder Mieter noch Vermieter |
| **B2** | Der Tie-Break der Restverteilung hing an der Eingabereihenfolge | Dieselben Daten, andere Sortierung → andere Abrechnung. Spätestens beim Wechsel auf SQLite/PostgreSQL backend-abhängige Ergebnisse (§271.26) |
| **B3** | Fehlende Verteilbasis blieb außerhalb des Verbrauchsschlüssels stumm | Ungepflegte Flächen ließen die gesamte Grundsteuer wortlos beim Vermieter landen (Invariante 20) |

Bewusst **nicht** behoben, sondern begründet als Baseline eingefroren: die fehlende
Summengarantie beim §35a-Lohnanteil (B4) und die zu niedrige Vorauszahlungsempfehlung bei
Teiljahren (B6). Beides sind Verhaltensänderungen mit Wirkung auf jede Abrechnung und
gehören nicht in einen PR, der das Netz spannt. Alles in
`docs/settlement-baseline-befunde.md`.

## Netzprobe

Ein Netz, das nicht nachweislich fängt, ist keins:

| Sabotage der Engine | rote Tests von 44 |
|---|---|
| Tageszählung ohne inklusive Endgrenze | 20 |
| Eigennutzung fälschlich in der Bezugsfläche | 7 |
| Restverteilung entfernt | 9 |
| `Math.floor` → `Math.round` in `largestRemainder` | **0** |

Die vierte blieb grün, weil das Largest-Remainder-Verfahren sich selbst korrigiert. Als
bekannte Grenze dokumentiert (B5), nicht mit einem konstruierten Fixture kaschiert.

**Gegenprobe mit den echten Daten:** Ergebnis vor und nach den Korrekturen identisch — keine
bestehende Abrechnung ändert sich.

## Prüfung vor Merge (§73)

- [x] unit tests · 44/44 grün (24 bestehende unverändert)
- [x] settlement regressions · 10 Golden Master
- [x] build (`tsc --noEmit` + vite)
- [ ] server/client typecheck, repository-, migrations-, accounting-, permission-Tests —
      **entfallen ausdrücklich**, die Ebenen existieren noch nicht (TypeScript ab #16,
      Repository ab #3)

## Nicht in diesem PR

TypeScript (#16), Monorepo (#17), Zod (#18), Prisma/SQLite (#20, #241), Repository (#21),
Importer (#24). Der „alt vs. neu“-Vergleich aus #25 kann erst laufen, wenn es ein „neu“ gibt
— dieser PR liefert die „alt“-Seite und den Vergleichsmechanismus.

Closes #1
Closes #26

author: nadavoked
body:
## מה השתנה

הכרעת נדב מ-2026-08-30 (#140): תחנת תלמיד **ומחשב בנייה** מגיעים ישר למסך
בחירה גלוי בין דיסק מקומי ל-ImageCtl — בלי ESC ובלי הגבלת זמן.

| מסלול | לפני | אחרי |
|---|---|---|
| `bad-schema` | דיסק, `hidden`, ‏2ש' | דיסק, `hidden`, **0ש'** |
| `unregistered` | דיסק, `hidden`, ‏2ש' | דיסק, `hidden`, **0ש'** |
| `task-assigned` / `session-joinable` | סוכן | ללא שינוי |
| `cloner-wait` | סוכן | ללא שינוי |
| `build` | תפריט גלוי, ‏15ש' | תפריט גלוי, **ללא טיימר** |
| `classroom` בלי משימה | מוסתר, ‏2ש', ‏ESC | **תפריט גלוי, ללא טיימר** |

טכנית: `timeout_style=menu` ו-`set timeout=-1`.

**תוספת מאוחרת מנדב** — *"אם אין MAC הוא לא אמור לקבל GRUB"*: המסלול
הלא-רשום עדיין המתין 2 שניות, למרות ש-`offer_recovery=False` אומר שאין שם
מה ללחוץ עליו. ירד ל-0, כלומר בדיוק מה ש-`render_local_only` נותן ל-MAC
פגום. ‏`bad-schema` זהה לו, מאותה סיבה.

## המחיר, במודע

`CLAUDE.md` — תרחיש ה-QA הראשון ("מחשב בלי משימה עולה מהדיסק תוך שניות",
הדגמה 3) **בוטל**, ומנוסח מחדש כהחלטה עם תאריך ונימוק. מה שנשאר קריטי
ונבדק: מכונה לא מזוהה עולה מיד בלי תפריט · שרת כבוי (‏PXE נכשל בקושחה,
לא עוברים דרך הקובץ שלנו) · `cloner` הולך ישר לסוכן.

## מה נעשה מיותר

- `ROLES_WITH_VISIBLE_MENU` — התפקיד כבר לא משנה איך המסך נראה.
- `GrubConfig.hidden_timeout` ו-`GrubConfig.menu_timeout` — אין מסלול
  שקורא אותם; שני הערכים נגזרים מההחלטה.
- `ESC_HINT` ו-#41 — אין יותר צוהר חבוי להודיע עליו.

## בקרה שלילית

`tests/test_visible_boot_menu.py` מול הקוד הלא-מתוקן (‏`git checkout -- boot/`
במעבדה): **6 נכשלו, 6 עברו** — כל הכישלונות `AssertionError` על ערכים
(`hidden` מול `menu`, ‏`15` מול `-1`, ‏`2` מול `0`), אף אחד לא ImportError.
ששת שעברו הם בדיוק השומרים שלא נגעתי בהם.

## בדיקות

מעבדת ה-VM (‏Debian 13 / Python 3.13), פעמיים: **1258 passed** בשתי
הריצות (‏317s ו-317s).

## דורש טיפול נפרד (לא נגעתי — מחוץ לבעלות)

- `docs/imagectl-spec.md` §9 — "המחשב עולה רגיל תוך שתי שניות, בלי לראות
  דבר" כבר לא נכון ל"מחשב בלי משימה". §8 תקין כמות שהוא.
- `docs/grub-generator.md` — שלושה מקטעים מתארים את הצוהר החבוי ואת
  `ESC_HINT` (שורות 60-80, ‏276, ‏285, ‏297).

closes #140

这是全库文档大修 C3 簇的 Grok 删除安全审计闸门,不是合同正文施工。对象是 PR #88(`codex/doc-overhaul-c3-contracts`)七个 spec 文件的 diff;产出是 `.memo/design/doc-overhaul-20260830/review-c3-grok.md`。五问中 ①③④⑤ 通过;② 回滚 `spec/system.md` 新 :101 分号后「保留实际来源」,恢复旧 :107「都不能自报为 human 或 workflow reducer」——A 类改正面句改了条件。本 PR 不改 `docs/design/spec/**`。

author: balizero1987
body:
Measures three things over a window of squash-merged PRs — correction-chain rate, time to merge, builder attribution — and publishes them as a dated section in `docs/factory/SEAT-MIX.md`, because a metric nobody reads is theater.

The correction rule is **file-overlap**, never the subject prefix alone: a `fix:` subject over an unrelated surface corrects nothing in the window, and counting it would pay contributors to relabel.

## The finding, and it is about the acceptance criterion itself

The first implementation sliced `commits[:i]` to mean "commits before i" while `git log` returns **newest-first**. Every reported "origin" was a commit from the *future* of the fix that supposedly corrected it:

```
fix    e952cd17  ct=1787403089  2026-08-22T12:51:29Z
origin 0c795f85  ct=1787409648  2026-08-22T14:40:48Z   ← 1h49m LATER
```

**26 chains before the cure, 21 after, ZERO (fix, origin) pairs in common.** The count *and* every individual attribution were wrong.

Now the part that matters. The spec asks the correction count to reproduce a hand-measured **27-of-200 within ±3** (band 24–30).

| version | chains | inside the band? |
|---|---|---|
| **broken** (inverted ordering) | 26 | **yes** |
| **correct** | 21 | no |

**An implementation can pass this acceptance criterion precisely by being wrong.** So the number is reported as measured and **not tuned toward 27**. The spec says so in its own words — "±3 agreement is not validation of the heuristic; report the number, don't claim it proves the method" — and tuning a measurement until it matches a hand count is Goodhart on the acceptance gate itself. If the band must be met, that is a ruling, not an implementation detail.

I found this by measuring the **output**, not by reading the code. Nothing in the source looks wrong.

## Bites

**Second acceptance probe passes cleanly** — builder attribution **117/118 = 99.2%** (≥80% required), across all three machines (`air-m5` 53, `nuzantara` 37, `mini-pro2` 27); time to MERGE median 0.51h, p90 3.70h.

**`--write` appended a real dated section to SEAT-MIX.md** (25 lines) matching the shape of the file's one existing dated block.

**The corpus is armed** in both lists `immune-enforcement.yml` needs — `scripts-tests-sweep` is `continue-on-error` and gates nothing, so a corpus resting on it is armed to nothing (W81). `actionlint` rc=0.

## Two cross-family refutations, in parallel, both DO-NOT-SHIP

Kimi K3 and Codex sol xhigh, same diff, same attack list, no sight of each other. **28 findings, overlapping on three.** Each caught things the other did not.

Cured: same-second ties rejected (a merge queue lands several commits in one second — sol cited a real pair, `20292599f3cd`/`679806e7f26a`, both `ct=1779164922`); **p90 returning the MINIMUM at n=2** (`[1h, 100h]` → "p90 1h"); a rate denominator that rewarded tuning its own noise filter; `gh --limit 1000` with no `merged:` search dropping the p90-defining tail; duplicate chains; a **real repo subject the fix-detector dropped** (`fix queue baseline census and public timing (#4047)` — verified `2184b00a63`, the only such subject in two months); `$` matching before a trailing newline; duplicated PR numbers counted twice; no `base:main` filter; a negative duration entering a latency distribution.

And one found by the pre-commit hook itself: **the tool generated markdown that fails this repo's formatter**, so every PR that ran `--write` would have been blocked by the report it had just published.

**Declared, not cured**: reverts are excluded (widening is a definitional question about the metric, not a bug fix); and the two windows — git local-tz committer date vs gh UTC `mergedAt` — are **stated in the published output** rather than blurred, with an explicit instruction not to compute a ratio across them. sol measured the gap on this window: 120 git commits vs 118 under UTC bounds.

## Verification

**36 tests. 19 mutants: 16 killed, 2 proven equivalent with the proof recorded, 1 proven DEAD and deleted** rather than kept as a guard that looks like a guard (a self-origin check that mutation showed unreachable — an origin must be a non-fix commit, and any duplicate of a fix is a fix).

Three mutants survived at first and **all three were my own vacuous tests**: one asserted only an exit code, one recomputed the module's rule inside the test instead of calling it, and one shelled out to `gh` — which would have gone red on a CI runner for the runner's auth state rather than for the code. The suite went 2.6s → 0.76s when that one was stubbed, which is itself the proof the call was there.

Bytecode disabled throughout (W121), `__pycache__` cleared per case, restored from a byte `cp` never `git checkout`. 149 tests green across this and the two neighbouring corpora. `ruff` clean. `evidence_pack_lint` clean, no notices.

**Workflow-class**: auto-merge deliberately NOT armed.

Ledger: #5319 (squad L, L04-PR2)

Descriptor identity checks reject path replacement before bytes are consumed. They do not make an attacker-controlled operating system trustworthy. Markdown encoding preserves text structure; it does not certify the text's truth.

author: clovenbradshaw-ctrl
body:
## Summary

- Found running real fetched Russian War and Peace prose against the omnilingual-reading question (companion work in `the-fold`/`live_priors` on this same branch): `discoverRelationVocab`'s `SURFACE_RE` locates a candidate surface with `\b(?:NAME)\b`, and JavaScript's `\b` is defined purely against ASCII `\w = [A-Za-z0-9_]` — no Unicode-aware mode exists, even under `/u` — so a surface written entirely in a non-Latin script (Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Armenian, ...) can never be located, regardless of recurrence.
- Two more plausible causes (Russian case declension fragmenting surfaces; French code-switch dominance in the specimen) were tested directly and refuted before finding the real cause.
- Fixed with one shared `bWord()` helper built from this file's own pre-existing Unicode word-character class, applied at all four `\b` call sites in the file (three not reached by the measured specimen, including the negation-detection regex this file's own header already documents building for injected non-English priors, e.g. Basque).
- Confirmed universal, not specimen-scoped: the identical fix independently closes the defect on two more unrelated scripts (Greek, Hebrew) with no further changes.
- Byte-identical for ASCII, pinned as a regression.

Full account: `native/READING-SPEC.md` S34.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test native/tests/relations.test.js` — 28/28 (5 new cases: the measured Cyrillic defect+fix, a declension-vs-boundary discriminating control, cross-script Greek/Hebrew generality, the non-English-negation-injection use case, an explicit ASCII byte-identical pin)
- [x] `node --test "native/conformance/*.test.mjs" "native/tests/*.test.js"` — 376/366/10, same 10 pre-existing failures (uninitialised `legacy-eoreader6.1` submodule in this checkout), zero regressions
- [x] `node --test native/conformance/reading-spec.test.mjs` — the S34 entry carries the required `**Generality:**` tag and passes the P71/S31 disclosure gate

## Amended 2026-08-31 — the same pipeline run against all 516 real UN UDHR translations, and three more real defects closed (S35-S38)

User direction after S34 landed: apply the same process to every UDHR translation this corpus holds ("more than a universal reading, we're looking for our blindspots"), then, once the blind spots were diagnosed by comparing the CONTENT of all 516 readings against each other: "fix the issues."

- **S35** — a comma glued directly to a name's own trailing edge was read as a run continuation, gluing two adjacent subjects into one bogus surface (e.g. "Pierre, Anna Pavlovna" → "Pierre Anna Pavlovna"). Fixed with a hard-break rule on punctuation glued flush against a token's own edge; plain whitespace between two capitalised tokens is untouched (pinned as a regression so an ordinary multi-word name still merges).
- **S36** — `Cased_Letter` (Unicode's `\p{Cased_Letter}`) answers "does this letter belong to a case category," not "does this material ever use its other member." Georgian's everyday alphabet is Unicode-lowercase-by-category with no working uppercase convention in ordinary use, so `scriptCoverage` read it as fully cased while `extractSurfaces` found zero real Georgian surfaces — every "candidate" was English front-matter debris. Closed with a third, parameter-free structural gap (`script_case_unused`): zero distinct sentences carrying a non-sentence-initial capitalised token. Confirmed the same class, not Georgian-specific, on Cherokee's traditional all-uppercase block and a plain lowercase-only Latin construction.
- **S37** — `capitalisationIsSignificant`'s normal (z-score) approximation to a one-sided binomial test. The triggering Czech specimen didn't actually flip between old and new (both refuse it) — the real defect, found by an exhaustive sweep of the function's whole practical domain rather than stopping at one specimen, was a systematic bias: 24 of 1,711 checked `(cap, lower)` pairs where the approximation wrongly called a split "significant" and the exact tail correctly refuses it, zero in the other direction. Replaced with an exact one-sided binomial tail computed in log-space (avoids both factorial overflow and `0.5^n` underflow, which hits IEEE double's smallest subnormal at n=1074).
- **S38** — a highly-inflected language fragments a bare name's own case forms into unrelated referents (Russian: "Кутузов"/"Кутузова"/"Кутузову", "Анна"/"Анне"/"Анны"). New `declension.js::createDeclensionFolder` mines suffix-transformation rules from UniMorph's real Russian noun paradigm table and checks them PAIRWISE against two actually-observed surfaces — never as a per-word canonical lemma, which would risk corrupting an already-nominative name (the dominant Russian genitive-plural pattern, "ов"→"", would turn "Кутузов" itself into "Кутуз" if applied blindly). Verified against real fetched Russian War and Peace: 38 correct merges, zero false ones, across a floor sweep from 10 to 200 kept rules. Same pass: `native/scripts/build-pos-prior.mjs` (new, language-general, zero per-language code) built real `POSPrior@1` files for English/Russian/Finnish from UD treebanks, closing a separate defect diagnosed in `live_priors` (its own POS-vocabulary gate had never actually loaded, for any language, because its import path pointed at this repo's empty `legacy-eoreader6.1` submodule).

### Test plan (this amendment)

- [x] `node --test native/tests/rich-referents.test.js` — 14/14 (S35's comma-glue fix + control, S37's flip specimen + positive control)
- [x] `node --test native/tests/declension.test.js` — 9/9, against the real committed `declension-rus.json` prior, including a full `discoverReferents` end-to-end case
- [x] `node --test native/tests/pos-prior.test.js` — 7/7, against all three real committed POS priors (English/Russian/Finnish), same unmodified classifier
- [x] `node --test native/conformance/reading-spec.test.mjs` — S35-S38 all carry the required `**Generality:**` tag
- [x] Full suite: 383/372/11 (S37) → 399/388/11 (S38), same 11 pre-existing failures by name throughout, zero regressions

author: neelamkhan123
body:
Two things a user could see but never change: which repos sit in their sidebar, and the blue everything was hardcoded to.

## Pin and remove

`tracked_repos` gains a `pinned` flag (migration `b3d71e4a9c02`) — per-tracker rather than per-repo, for the same reason that join table exists at all: one user pinning React says nothing about anyone else's list. `PATCH` and `DELETE /repos/{full_name}` act on it.

Delete removes only this user's own link, never the shared `Repo` row and its synced history, so re-adding is instant rather than a fresh sync. Both endpoints invalidate the same per-user overview cache prefix `add_repo` already does.

On the frontend the actions live in one `RepoActionsMenu`, reachable three ways:

- right-click anywhere on a sidebar row
- a dots button, revealed on hover and shown outright below `lg` (where there's no hover to reveal it with), also tab-reachable so the menu has a keyboard path
- the same menu beside the repo-detail heading

One menu behind all of them rather than a row of always-visible buttons — putting a delete affordance permanently beside a link you click constantly is how repos get removed by accident. Remove is confirmed, and navigates back to Overview if you just deleted the page you're on.

`repoNames` deliberately stays in add order: `repoColor` indexes into it, so a pinned-first list would reshuffle half the chart palette the moment anything got pinned. The sidebar reads a separately sorted `sidebarRepos`.

## Accent color

The folder icons, the commit heatmap, the merge-time bars and the percentile bars were four independently hardcoded blues. They're one `--accent` token now, picked from six hues in the account menu and stored alongside the theme — applied pre-paint in `index.html` the same way dark is, so there's no flash of the default. The heatmap's ramp is derived with `color-mix` rather than hardcoded `rgba()` triplets, which is what lets it follow the choice.

**One call worth a second opinion:** `--chart-1..8` is left alone on purpose. That's the *categorical* palette, copied from the library's `chartSeriesColors` and validated as a whole for contrast and color-vision separation, with repos assigned a slot by position. Re-pointing one member at an arbitrary user hue would break that separation and change what one repo's line means next to another's. The visible consequence: with violet picked, the folders and heatmap go violet but repo #1's trend line stays blue. Easy to change if the whole screen should move together.

## Testing

- Endpoints exercised end-to-end against the running API: add → list → pin → list → delete, plus 404s on delete and patch of an untracked repo. Migration applied and the column verified on the dev database.
- `npm run build` and `npm run lint` clean, apart from a pre-existing `react-refresh` error in `src/main.tsx` that also fails on `main`.
- `tests/test_health.py::test_overview_endpoint_responds` still fails with a 401 — pre-existing, the test predates the auth gate.
- Not yet eyeballed in the browser: the six accent hues in light and dark, and the dots button's size next to the `text-2xl` repo heading.

author: kablewithak
body:
## Summary

Adds the durable design boundary for the final 342-trajectory measured protected-review workflow.

This tranche defines how the 162 functional trajectories are reviewed without leaking treatment metadata, without post-result case selection, and without turning protected-evidence defects into model-quality failures.

## Decision

Adopts `FINAL_342_MEASURED_PROTECTED_REVIEW_DESIGN_V1`.

Key invariants:

- 162 planned functional trajectories receive 162 primary review assignment slots.
- The 180 runtime-microbenchmark trajectories do not receive human rubric assignments under this design.
- The frozen 25% independent double-review fraction is resolved conservatively to 41 secondary assignments.
- Secondary review is predeclared across 12 strata: planned condition × frozen expected terminal decision.
- Hamilton largest-remainder allocation produces 23 answer, 6 clarify, 6 escalate, and 6 refuse secondary assignments across A/B/C.
- Within-stratum selection is deterministic from the frozen seed and planned run identity.
- Observed model outcomes never influence sampling.
- No replacement case is permitted after execution.
- Review identity is opaque and per measured trajectory; primary and secondary assignment IDs are distinct.
- Reviewer-visible evidence excludes condition, route, worker, cache, latency, cost, run order, internal rendered prompts, and hidden expected-answer/claim-registry material.
- Protected capture occurs before candidate output is reduced to public-only metadata.
- A capture gap is `EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE`, not a model-quality failure; it cannot silently disappear and blocks quality non-inferiority/runtime-improvement claims.
- Protected raw material uses event-driven deletion after review, adjudication, analysis-input materialization, and public receipt verification.

## Files

- `src/auragateway/local_abc/final_342_measured_review_design_v1.py`
- `tests/unit/local_abc/test_final_342_measured_review_design_v1.py`
- `benchmarks/local_abc/auragateway_final_342_measured_review_design_v1.json`
- `docs/adr/2026-08-30-local-abc-final-342-measured-review-design-v1.md`

## Validation

Locally validated for this focused tranche:

- governed ZIP/file custody and exact four-path materialization
- Ruff formatter qualification on isolated copies with AST equality
- focused Ruff lint on qualified formatted bytes
- focused mypy
- focused pytest

author: yaseralnajjar
body:
Implements Milestone 9 of the schema-first SQL platform: the common runtime policies and the raw PostgreSQL provider runtime. Adds verified typestate pools, typed session reset, bounded LRU preparation, exact fetch contracts, consuming transactions, savepoints, fresh retry-safe replay, owned and borrowed streams, cancellation cleanup evidence, redacted SQLSTATE errors, wire codecs, and PostgreSQL 13-18 live qualification.

Focused validation passes: common and provider Rust tests, SQL contract and mutation suites, strict Clippy, formatting, file-size and maintainability guards, and the live PostgreSQL 13-18 runtime matrix. No compiler source changed, so full Sifr create-PR and merge gates are not applicable under the phase rule.

Known unrelated validation issue: the PostgreSQL compiler artifact checksum hashes the complete workspace Cargo manifests and lockfile, so adding this isolated runtime crate causes the existing compiler mutation case to report guest-source drift even though no compiler source or dependency changed. This remains owned by Milestone 18 artifact-authority hardening.

author: musharna
body:
First real-photograph run of `calibrate_scale_from_marker` and colour correction (CameraTrax card + kidney beans, X-Rite booth card, a card half-occluded by a leaf). Findings in `memory/dogfood_scale_color_2026-08-30.md`; each reproduced against the code before the fix.

**HIGH — the card was measured as a plant, and it silenced the guard that would have said so.** `color_correct=true` detected the card, corrected the colours, then measured the card: its warm chips merged into the largest object in the scene (254,571 px), so `multi_specimen` never fired (`major_object_count=1` — the eleven beans all read as minor beside it) and `measure()` returned a 727,848-px frame-spanning "plant"; the batch row came back `measured: true`. The detected card's region (chip extent padded by the median chip size) is now excluded from the mask before any diagnostics, in both `segment()` and `measure_images()`, with a `color_card_excluded` advisory. Empty-after-exclusion refuses as `empty_mask`. Verified on the same photo: the beans are now the eleven major objects and `multi_specimen` fires.

**LOW — `frame_clipping` blamed the specimen for background slivers.** Two 5-px-wide edge slivers declared eleven interior beans "cut off". Clipping now requires an edge-touching component comparable to the largest (≥ 0.25×); a mostly-out-of-frame plant still warns because its sliver IS the largest object.

**Verified working on the real photos (no change):** scale tool exact on ground-truthed chips (127 px measured vs 121–127 truth; two chips agree 0.5%; clip advisory fired on the one 2.4%-off crop), the full chip→px_per_mm→mm chain (20.7×10.6 mm kidney bean), loud per-image refusal of the occluded card.

Six tests new or updated, each watched red first. 310 tests. Release 1.6.0 (measured numbers change for card-in-frame scenes — that is the point).

author: ruhex
body:
Closes #341   # linkage only — the integration PR aggregates the keywords that actually close issues

## Problem
`SendKeepaliveAsync` was the one send path entering `_sendLock.WaitAsync(CancellationToken.None)`. If `Dispose` ran while another sender held the lock (a slow-peer send inside the #285 budget), the queued keepalive waiter was never released: `SemaphoreSlim.Dispose` does not wake waiters (verified directly with a standalone probe — a parked waiter stays `WaitingForActivation` forever), and the holder's `Release` in its finally is swallowed by `ObjectDisposedException`. `HoldTimerLoopAsync` never completed → `RunAsync` never returned → the session graph stayed rooted by the semaphore's waiter queue. Reachable via `BgpServer.StopAsync`'s dispose loop and session replacement.

## Root Cause
The lock wait had no teardown observation channel: the only wake sources were the holder's `Release` (swallowed post-Dispose) and the caller token (`None`).

## Fix
Race the wait against a dispose signal: a `TaskCompletionSource` (`RunContinuationsAsynchronously`) set at the top of `Dispose()` BEFORE `_sendLock.Dispose()`; a parked wait loses the `Task.WhenAny` and unwinds as "not sent" (the existing best-effort contract). The wait keeps the CALLER's token. Fast path: an uncontended `WaitAsync` completes synchronously (`IsCompletedSuccessfully`) and skips the `WhenAny` — keepalives on a healthy session allocate nothing extra.

**Design deviation from the issue's proposal (wait on `_cts.Token`):** that variant was implemented first and caught by the full suite going red — `RunEstablishedAsync` cancels `_cts` BEFORE `RunAsync`'s catch blocks send their best-effort NOTIFICATION, so binding the wait to `_cts.Token` silently suppressed every post-teardown NOTIFICATION (e.g. Bad Message Length on a malformed header — `InvalidHeaderLength_OnWire_TearsDownSession_With_MessageHeaderError` failed). The WhenAny+signal design fixes the hang without touching the post-cancel send semantics.

## Correctness
- The abandoned (losing) wait task stays parked in the disposed semaphore's queue, but `RunAsync` now completes and the whole session graph (semaphore included) becomes GC-collectable — the actual harm in #341 was the never-completing task, not the parked node.
- The signal fires only inside final `Dispose` (idempotent CAS), so there is no live-operation window where a queued wait could be abandoned while the semaphore still serves sends.
- Grace-token callers (`NotifyCeaseAsync`) get the same dispose protection via the signal.

## Regression Test
`Dispose_WhileSenderHoldsSendLock_RunAsyncCompletes` — gated `WriteAsync` parks a refresh as the lock holder, a keepalive tick queues behind it, `Dispose` fires mid-wait; asserts `RunAsync` completes within 5s. Pre-fix: 3/3 red (the 5s timeout elapses — the exact hang). Post-fix: 8/8 green + full suite 802/802. The fake connection's gated write now cancels on `Dispose`, mirroring the real transport aborting a pending write (without it the fake could pin the sending loop past Dispose — behavior production never has).

## Verification
- `dotnet format` / `dotnet build` (0 errors) / `dotnet test` **802/802**
- Regression class + `MalformedUpdateResilienceTests` (the regression detector) — 5/5 consecutive green runs

## RFC
None directly (lifecycle fix); preserves RFC 4271 §6.1/§6.3 NOTIFICATION delivery on teardown — the rejected first draft would have broken it.

## Behavior Change
None observable on a healthy session. A send queued behind the lock at Dispose now reports "not sent" instead of hanging the session task forever.

## Deviation from Issue Proposal
Yes — see Fix: `_cts.Token` wait replaced by WhenAny dispose-signal (the issue's suggestion suppressed post-cancel NOTIFICATIONs; verified by a red full-suite run).

author: dallanq
body:
## What this is

A doctrine claim in this repo turned out to be false, and eleven files were
repeating it. The measurement is here, the correction is here, and the
mechanism it was justifying is deleted.

**The claim:** *"a `disallowedTools:` deny binds even under `bypassPermissions`;
an omission from `tools:` alone is not."* It appears in CLAUDE.md, the
architecture guide, ADR-0004, ADR-0006, ADR-0011, two specs, the packaging test
and three agent bodies. Seven of them cite issue #695 for it. That issue is the
birkeland lane breach — it says nothing about `bypassPermissions`, denies, or
omissions. The citation chain never terminated in evidence.

**The measurement:** `make probe-agent-binding` (new) spawns a probe agent under
the exact hosted options — `real_agent.build_options`, so `bypassPermissions`,
staged agents, the real MCP server — and reads whether a tool call actually
landed, off the `tool_result` rather than the agent's prose. Six arms, three
frontmatter shapes × tool search off and on. Reproduced twice against Claude Code
2.1.251 and agent SDK 0.2.128:

```
arm               tool_search  verdict   probe line
probe-a-control   false        CALLED    PROBE_RESULT: CALLED 1751
probe-b-deny      false        BLOCKED   subagent could not be spawned
probe-c-omit      false        BLOCKED   PROBE_RESULT: ABSENT
probe-a-control   true         CALLED    PROBE_RESULT: CALLED 1751
probe-b-deny      true         BLOCKED   PROBE_RESULT: ABSENT
probe-c-omit      true         BLOCKED   PROBE_RESULT: ABSENT
```

Both bind. A tool merely omitted from `tools:` is absent from the agent, exactly
as a denied one is. So every deny we shipped was restating the line above it.

## What changed

**All five `disallowedTools:` blocks are deleted** — 83 lines of triple-spelled
YAML a reader had to check against the grant list to conclude nothing. To take a
capability away from an agent, leave it out of `tools:`. The regression a deny
insured against — someone adding the tool back — is caught by the permission
snapshot in `agent-tool-names.test.ts`, which fails on any change to an agent's
list.

**The eleven claim sites are corrected**, ADR-0004 and ADR-0006 amended in place
with new `Last updated` lines rather than a strikethrough.

**Two new guards in `agent-tool-names.test.ts`:**

- *never denies a tool it also grants* — the probe found that a deny is applied
  **before** the zero-tools spawn check. Arm B granted one tool under all three
  spellings plus `ToolSearch`, denied that same tool, and the runtime refused the
  agent outright: `would be spawned with zero tools — refusing. Its tools list
  resolved to nothing: unrecognized [ToolSearch]` — naming only the built-in,
  because the deny had already removed the three MCP entries. `image-reader`
  grants exactly one tool, so it is one entry from that shape.
- *ships no `disallowedTools:` block* — so re-adding one is a decision a reviewer
  sees rather than a reflex.

**`record-extractor still denies the broad writer` becomes `record-extractor
cannot reach the broad writer`**, asserting `research_append` is absent from
`tools:` — the thing that actually binds. Kept rather than folded into the
snapshot so a red suite names the ADR-0006 lane, not just "the surface moved".

## Proving the lints fail

Both, and then a third for vacuity:

1. Re-added an overlapping deny to `image-reader` → three cases fired
   (`never denies a tool it also grants`, `ships no disallowedTools block`,
   `denies exactly the pinned tools`). Reverted.
2. With no denies shipped, the per-agent overlap arm has nothing to fail on — a
   check that cannot fail reads as coverage. So the rule also has a **synthetic
   arm**. Stubbed `grantedAndDenied` to return `[]` and confirmed the synthetic
   arm catches it: *"the overlap rule no longer fires — the per-agent arm passes
   vacuously"*. Restored.

## One cost, accepted

`check_rubric_tool_drift.py` asks whether a tool named in an agent body appears
in either list, and `disallowedTools:` was doubling as the marker for a
deliberate "you do NOT have this tool" mention. Removing the denies takes that
marker away, so its agent-body warnings go **5 → 12**. It is warn-only and does
not block a build; the suppression mechanism it wants is already an open issue
(search the board for `check_rubric_tool_drift suppression`).

## Also in here

- `make probe-agent-binding` is landed as a dev script rather than left in a
  scratch directory: a correction that cites a measurement should ship the
  instrument. It is a live billed probe, not a CI check, and the architecture
  guide's "what nothing checks" says so — it closes the runtime-binding gap for
  the **hosted** options only; Cowork in either run mode still has no instrument
  but a live session.
- Two stale counts corrected in prose I was already editing: the plugin-agent
  count (6 → 5, after the Opus re-reader was retired) and `research_query`'s
  holders (three of six → three of five).
- Issue #1491 rewritten. Its deny step and its whole Part 2 are retired by this
  measurement; the narrow `evaluation_append` tool it asks for is untouched and
  is now the only fix it needs. While there, applied that issue's own 2026-08-09
  ruling that Part 3 was deleted — the body still carried a live instruction to
  delete `place_search` from `record-extractor`, which calls it 33×.

## Why no Cowork session

Cowork runs permission mode `default`, where the `tools:` allow-list is already
proven to bind — twice, live, on 2026-07-18 and in issue #1341. The only
environment where a deny could have been doing something the omission was not is
`bypassPermissions`, which is what the probe measures.

## Verification

```
make engine-test                   # 2719 passed
eval/harness unit suite            # 2927 passed
apps/server                        # 214 passed
make probe-agent-binding           # the six arms above, twice
```

Frontmatter changes arm the run-log gate — **`eval-cosmetic-skip`**, as agreed:
no agent's capability surface changes behaviourally, since every deleted deny
named a tool the agent already could not call.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01UfR42BF7uvDzZhdPBcPno3

author: pauseb
body:
쿠폰 도메인 로드맵의 **P10-A**. `promotion_meta` 쓰기를 커스텀 라우트 밖에서 **워크플로 훅 안으로** 옮겨,
쿠폰 생성이 반쯤 성공했을 때 「발급 정책 없는 활성 쿠폰」이 남는 경로(#488 `N7`)를 없앤다.

**마이그레이션 0 · 시크릿 0 · env 0 · 이벤트 계약 0 · 배포 순서 제약 없음.**
사용자에게 보이는 변화 0 — admin-web 은 create/update/delete **응답 본문을 읽지 않는다**(`invalidateQueries` 만).

플랜: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-coupon-write-path-to-hooks.md`

---

## 무엇이 문제였나

`POST /admin/promotions` 가 워크플로를 돌린 **뒤** `promotionMetaService.upsert` 를 불렀다.
메타 쓰기가 **보상(compensation) 밖**이라, 두 쓰기 사이에서 실패하면 프로모션은 `active` 로 살아남고
`promotion_meta` 만 0행이 된다. 그리고 **메타가 없을 때의 기본값이 6곳 전부 `'public'`** 이었고,
카트 게이트와 주문 확정 백스톱은 `undefined` 라 그냥 통과했다.

→ **`assigned_only` 로 만들려던 쿠폰이 아무나 쓰는 쿠폰이 된다. 조용히.**

## 실측으로 먼저 닫은 것

#488 이 「PR 모양이 달라지므로 먼저 닫아라」고 지목한 질문:

**우리 파일이 `GET` 만 export 하면 코어의 `POST` 가 살아나는가? → 예. 메서드 단위 병합이다.**

| 확인 | 방법 | 결과 |
|---|---|---|
| 라이브러리 의미론 | 임시 디렉터리 2개로 실제 `RoutesLoader` 구동 | `GET → OURS` · `POST → CORE` |
| 등록 키 | `framework/dist/http/routes-loader.js` `registerRoute` | `#routes[matcher][method]` — 키가 **파일이 아니라 (경로, 메서드)** |
| 스캔 순서 | `medusa/dist/loaders/api.js:41` + `get-resolved-plugins.js` | `[코어/api, …플러그인, **프로젝트 src/api(마지막)**]` → 나중이 이긴다 |
| 끝단 | 우리 `route.ts` 에서 POST 제거 후 실부팅 | `POST /admin/promotions` **200, 프로모션 생성**, 응답에 `metadata` 없음(= 코어 핸들러) |

같은 실측에서 **계획을 바꾼 것 둘**:

- 🔴 `additionalDataValidator` 는 코어 POST 에 먹지만 **`additional_data` 객체 자체의 생략은 못 막는다**
  — 프레임워크가 `z.object(shape).nullish()` 로 감싼다(`middleware-file-loader.js:153`).
  → **닫힌 기본값이 곁다리가 아니라 그 구멍의 유일한 방어선이다.**
- 🔴 `z.object` 가 **strip** 이라 `additional_data` 안쪽 미지 키는 400 이 아니라 **조용히 버려진다.**
  → 스키마에 없는 키는 훅까지 못 간다. 「스키마 키 집합 ⊇ `META_KEYS`」를 유닛 테스트로 못 박았다
  (P10-B 의 `max_discount_amount` 가 여기 걸린다).

## 무엇이 들어갔나

| 커밋 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| `f84d125ac` | `scripts/local/run-medusa-integration.sh` — HTTP 통합 스펙 러너 |
| `52d9ff671` | 메타 동기화 판정을 순수 함수로 (`apply-promotion-meta.ts`) |
| `8f5f8adc0` | `promotionsCreated`/`promotionsUpdated`/`promotionsDeleted` 훅 3개 등록 |
| `dc01cb734` | `additionalDataValidator` 2건 + 어휘 드리프트 가드 사이트 2개 |
| `b6ccf60e0` | 읽기 5곳을 **닫힌 기본값**(`assigned_only`)으로 |
| `2483772b3` | `/admin/promotions*` 쓰기 핸들러 삭제, `GET` 만 남김 |
| `d99b8bd43` | 정본(#488 · 마스터플랜) 갱신 |

`7-8` 도 함께 닫힌다 — 은폐하던 `req.validatedBody ?? req.body` 폴백이 라우트와 함께 사라진다.
(그 폴백은 방어가 아니었다: 업그레이드로 코어 미들웨어 매칭이 어긋나면 크래시로 즉시 드러날 일을
**무검증 본문이 조용히 워크플로로 들어가게** 만든다.)

## 의도한 행동 변화 1건

**메타 행이 없는 프로모션은 이제 아무도 못 쓴다.** 라이브에 그런 프로모션은 0건이다
(쿠폰 적용 주문 0건 · active 프로모션 0개, ADR-0033 측정 2026-08-28) — **백필 없음.**

부수 효과는 의도한 것이다: 네이티브 Medusa 대시보드(`/app/promotions`, 아직 켜져 있다)로 만든 쿠폰은
메타가 없으므로 쓸 수 없게 된다. **감사되지 않은 쓰기 경로가 「위험」에서 「무해」로 바뀐다.**

## 검증

| 게이트 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| Medusa 유닛 (`npm run test:medusa`) | **28 suites / 243 tests** (기준선 25/225) |
| Medusa 타입 (`cd apps/medusa && npx tsc --noEmit`) | **3** — 선재분 그대로 |
| 쿠폰 통합, 실 DB (`scripts/local/run-medusa-integration.sh --testPathPattern 'coupon-'`) | **4 suites / 42 tests** (기준선 38 → 신규 4) |
| 루트 `npx jest` | **513 suites / 4497 tests, 실패 0** |
| 루트 `npm run type-check` | **0** |
| 실 스택 끝단 | 생성 200 + metadata 3키 / 어휘 밖 400 + 행 0 / DELETE 200 + 메타 0행 |

신규 통합 4건: 훅 실패 시 롤백 · 어휘 밖 400 + 행 0 · 상태 토글이 메타를 안 지움 ·
**메타 0행 쿠폰이 카트에서 차단됨**. 마지막 건은 닫힌 기본값을 옛 값(`'public'`)으로 되돌리면
실제로 빨개지는 것을 확인했다 — 동어반복이 아니다.

## ⚠️ 리뷰어가 알아야 할 것

- **CI 는 통합 스펙을 돌리지 않는다.** `medusa-unit-tests.yml` 은 DB 가 없어 `test:unit` 만 돌리고,
  루트 게이트는 `apps/medusa` 를 아예 제외한다. 위 42건은 **로컬에서만** 돌았다.
- **`npm run test:integration:http` 를 직접 부르지 말 것.** 러너는 `DATABASE_URL` 이 아니라
  `DB_HOST`/`DB_USERNAME`/`DB_PASSWORD`/`DB_PORT` 를 읽어서 전 스펙이
