## Что и почему

Рекомендованная работа по урезанию поставки (из ревью PR #364 green-means-checked). Запись ленты объёма от 28.08 прямо просила: тонкий запас поставки — **сигнал к отдельной работе по урезанию, а не к наращиванию потолка**.

`manifest/ai-ops-manifest.yaml` вёз в **каждую дочку ~213 КБ исторических аудит-записей**:
- `external_audit_2026_07_17_v2_79` (133 КБ) — внешний аудит эпохи v2.79 (оценка ~5/10);
- `execution_audit_2026_07_16`, `self_audit_2026_07_17`, `cross_platform_2026_07_17`, `live_qual_green_2026_07_17` — датированные снимки аудитов и dogfood-находки июля.

**Проверено, а не заявлено** (тот же метод, что при снятии `patch_note` из release-claims):
- `grep` по `ai_ops_kit/`, `tools/`, `installer/` — эти ключи не читает НИ ОДНА строка кода;
- схема `package-manifest.schema.json` их не требует (`additionalProperties: true`, в `required` только schema_version/kind/ai_ops/spec_protocol/update_policy);
- ни один тест/валидатор не ассертит на аудит-контент — все читают `update_policy.managed_set`, `package_version`, `skills.shipped`.

## Что сохранено

Машиночитаемый **индекс компонентов движка** (`tool_loop`, `tool_broker`, `run_plan`, `evidence_collector`, `project_detector`, `run_controller`, `execution_budget`, ...) и все читаемые ключи. История аудитов остаётся в git и в `docs/changelog/v2.md`.

## Результат

- Манифест **252 КБ → 39 КБ** (1048 → 468 строк).
- Запас объёма поставки: **~0.7 КБ (0.0%) → ~217 КБ (4.9%)** под тем же потолком 4 420 000. **Потолок НЕ трогали** — освобождённое место стало реальным запасом, а не поднятым потолком (прецедент release-claims: «потолок не опускаю до следующего независимого замера»).
- `check-fast` зелёный: **5012 passed, 16 skipped**. Валидаторы манифеста, ledger поставки, references, kit-only-paths — зелёные.

body:
Cierra la **0.2** (GLM, PR #67) tras verificarla contra la base VIVA.

## Verificado por el lead, con SELECT propio

| Afirmación | Resultado |
|---|---|
| 513 listings, mx 337 / us 176 | exacto |
| 265 productos distintos | exacto |
| Monedas MXN 337 / USD 176 | **exactamente el corte por plataforma** — la derivación es correcta |
| CHECK precio/moneda, ASIN duplicados, `external_id` vacíos | **0, 0, 0** |
| `ad_entity.listing_id` | **intacto en 0** — respetó el límite (eso es la 0.4) |
| **Recálculo independiente desde el bridge** | **513 / 337 / 176 / 265, idéntico** |
| No-op al re-correr | **tres veces** (38-40), en momentos distintos |

El bug propio que GLM cazó con la doble corrida —los SELECT previos abrían transacción implícita y `close()` revertía todo— dejó **cero daño verificado**: los `ingest_run` 35 y 36 **no existen** en la base.

## Corrección del lead: una sola fuente de moneda

La entrega definía `MONEDA_POR_PLATAFORMA` en `app/listings.py`, **idéntico** al `PLATAFORMAS_MONEDA` que ya vive en el motor y que importan `api.py` y `api_dashboard.py`. No había impedimento de arquitectura: la frontera prohíbe que el **motor** importe hacia afuera, no al revés.

Hoy los valores coincidían, así que no había dato malo. Pero un tercer marketplace actualizaría uno y no el otro — y este proyecto ya pagó ese error: un reporte que daba MXN para `amazon_us`, **18.66× siempre a favor de "todo es rentabilísimo"**.

Unificado, con **candado nuevo** que detecta por AST cualquier mapa plataforma→moneda en `app/` y exige que esté declarado. Trae su propio test de poder discriminante y **auto-limpieza de la allowlist**: un permiso muerto dejaría pasar la próxima duplicación en silencio.

Al ponerlo apareció una **tercera** definición, preexistente y **deliberada**: `PLATAFORMA_MONEDA` en `app/ads/write.py`, congelada y con su razón escrita (*"capa distinta, misma ley"*). Se declara como deuda conocida; **no se toca el cliente de escritura sellado por una constante**, y menos en vísperas del cutover.

## Residual y DoD

Residual de GLM, declarado: el camino "listing sin precio" no se ejercitó en producción (los 133 precios NULL cayeron todos en el conjunto sin mapeo); cubierto por test.

DoD que faltaban en la entrega y cierra el lead —igual que en la 0.1—: **marker 0.2 a `cc:完了`** y la línea de `CHAT-CONTEXT.md`.

author: sebitr
body:
`pnpm test:e2e` has been red on `main` since #259.

## The failure

    [desktop-chromium] › tests/e2e/pwa.spec.ts:141:5
      › shows an offline shell that explains the limitation

    Locator: getByText(/does not store expenses on your device/)
    Error: element(s) not found

The journey asserted that the offline shell says nothing typed there would be
saved. That was true, and asserting it was the point — right up until #259 gave
the shell an outbox to put an entry in. The shell now says the opposite, and
means it.

## The fix

The assertion follows the promise rather than the wording. What has to stay
true is that the page tells somebody *which* of the two things will happen to
what they type, because a reader who takes it at its word and closes the app is
owed an accurate answer either way. The test's name said "explains the
limitation", which is no longer what that screen is for, so it changed too.

## Why #259 did not catch it

`pnpm test:all` runs the unit, component and integration projects. Playwright
is a separate script (`pnpm test:e2e`), so #259 was green on every check that
was run and red on the one that was not. That is on me — I treated `test:all`
as the whole suite.

## One thing carried along

`openOnAmount` asserted its event target rather than narrowing it:

    const target = event.currentTarget as HTMLElement;

Radix raises `onOpenAutoFocus` from the focus scope rather than from the DOM,
so `currentTarget` is `EventTarget | null` and carries no `querySelector`. The
cast silenced that rather than answering it. `openOnContent` in
`src/components/ui/sheet.tsx` has guarded with `instanceof HTMLElement` all
along, and this now does the same. Failing the guard returns without preventing
the default, so focus lands where the scope would have put it — the behaviour
of a drawer that never asked for anything else.

**This hunk overlaps #261**, which found the same fault in the code #259 moved
out from under it. Whichever of the two lands second can drop its copy; the end
state is identical.

## What is not here

The nine unformatted files that make `pnpm format:check` red on `main` are
#261's, and they are the rest of what is failing. Left alone deliberately —
AGENTS.md asks that a second topic get its own branch, and that one already has
one.

## Verification, and its limit

The asserted phrase is `offline.note` in `messages/en.json` and appears once, so
there is no strict-mode ambiguity; I confirmed the rendered `/offline` page
carries it verbatim while building #259.

I could **not** run the suite locally: this machine's disk is at 100% (1.9 GiB
free of 228 GiB) and the Docker VM that holds the toolchain is now failing to
start containers. Both the Playwright run and `pnpm typecheck` are therefore
unverified here and are riding on this PR's own CI — which is the check being
fixed, so it is at least the right gate. Worth a second look at the diff for
that reason.

author: mrityunjaybhardwaj
body:
The bevel, end to end: from a descriptor kind that could mint elements, to an operator a director can point at a specific rim.

Five pieces that only make sense together, which is why they are one branch. Each one exists because the previous one exposed the next gap, and three of them are corrections rather than features.

## The arc

**A face order that can say "nowhere."** Every derived kind before the bevel MAPS — each output face came from exactly one source face. A bevel MINTS: it replaces each edge with a quad and each point with an n-gon, and those came from no source face at all. The order type widened to admit that hole.

**The bevel descriptor.** The first operator here that mints. Its layout is closed form — `F + E + V` faces, one output point per source face-corner — and it was predicted from that formula and then observed in a running Blender 5.1.1 at two shapes *before a line of the builder was written*. The arity multiset is what makes the check bite: a count-only comparison passes on a wrong rule.

**A `BevelModifier` node — a correctness fix, not polish.** The descriptor shipped with nothing in production able to construct one, which breaks the rule this repo already holds every kind to: a new kind cannot ship without its producing node. The cost was concrete rather than tidy — with no way to build a bevel in the running app, the *observe in the real app* step was impossible and every check on a minting kind was a unit test calling the builder directly. A zero amount is transparent rather than a throw, which is the reference's own answer (`MOD_bevel.cc:303-307`) and matters because `evaluate` runs on the render walk with no `try` above it.

**A minted face inherits from a representative.** The reference uses two rules and only one needs new machinery: face data is COPIED from one representative face (`bmesh_bevel.cc:1248-1254`), loop data is INTERPOLATED at a position (`:1279`). A copy is an index gather; a blend is not. The copy half is built, so a bevelled two-material box keeps both materials.

**A bevel that chamfers SOME edges — the miter rule.** At a point of valence `n` with `k` chamfered edges the point contributes `m` boundary vertices: 1 when `k = 0`, `k` when `k >= 2`, and it grows a polygon exactly when `m` reaches 3. Measured live over 15 selections spanning valence 3, 4, 5 and 8 — including two randomised toruses where four different `k` values sit side by side. `BevelModifier` declares `{ kind: 'source', domain: 'edge' }`, which makes it the first operator in the repo whose scope class is not `face`.

## Still open, and deliberately so

Two things this branch does not finish, each with its own issue.

The **terminal case** — a point with exactly one chamfered edge — is refused by name. It is the row that breaks every pattern: its count is `n - 1` rather than 1 or `k`, and it is the only case where a face's arity changes. Its positions need `offset_in_plane` and `slide_dist`, two rules this layout has never had to state, so guessing at them would put an unmeasured arm on the render path. A closed loop of edges works; a lone edge and an open chain are what it costs. Tracked as #830.

The **corner half** of what a minted element's attributes are worth is still open under #825 — the interpolation the reference does at a corner's position, which needs positions and weights the carriage road does not carry. The bevel deliberately emits no UVs at all, and that absence is load-bearing: it is what keeps the phase's discriminating observation able to discriminate.

## Three things the work caught in itself

**A missing CORNER order was killing the FACE domain.** Caught by observation, not by a test: the representative map was total and correct at two shapes and the geometry still had no attribute key.

**A gate was blind, and only falsification found it.** Flipping the edge tie-break changes which material every chamfer wears — and all 18 rows passed. It is now pinned against an independent oracle rather than a literal.

**A per-member declaration is only as good as its least careful reader.** The per-operator scope class was built precisely for the day an operator disagreed. That day arrived here — and the honouring gate beside it had hardcoded `'face'`. A box has 6 faces and 12 edges: both plausible integers, wrong mesh, nothing red.

## Test plan

- unit **4953 pass**, 1 local-only red (`external-model-audit` sees an untracked `blockbench/` dir that does not exist in CI — verified untracked)
- `scopedBevel.gate.test.ts` — 11 rows, **falsified four ways** (the terminal case answering instead of refusing; a `k = 0` point keeping one point per corner; the scope leaving the layout cache key; a vertex polygon at `m >= 2`). Each reds; the tree restores clean.
- `bevelNodeReach.gate.test.ts` — the node's passthrough arm and the builder's refusal partition the same predicate, compared as answers rather than spellings
- e2e **8/8** — `p818` (menu offers it · 24 → 96 · amount moves positions and not topology · zero is transparent · inspector routes amount · mute) and `p827` (24 → 40 → 24 on a scoped loop · a refused selection leaves the app alive and recovers)
- typecheck 0 · eslint 0 errors over tracked files · prettier clean over tracked files
- changed-file tsc sweep **3 before / 3 after**, identical file — the tier `npm run typecheck` cannot see
- `origin/main` merged in locally and the whole tier re-run on the merged tree, so the tick below is computed on the tree that will land

Closes #812
Closes #814
Closes #818
Closes #827

author: poolporg
body:
Three issues in the HTTP repository client.

### 1. Bearer token over cleartext

`init()` registers both `http` and `https`, and `sendRequest` sets `Authorization: Bearer` on whichever it gets. An `http://` repository URL therefore leaks the token to anyone on path, with no gate and no warning.

Now refused unless `insecure=true` acknowledges it. `https://` and a tokenless `http://` are unaffected — the gate is specifically about sending a credential in the clear.

### 2. No timeout, no context

```go
req, err := http.NewRequest(method, u.String(), payload)   // not NewRequestWithContext
...
httpClient := http.DefaultClient                            // Timeout: 0
```

Nothing propagated cancellation and there was no timeout at all, so a hung repository server stalled the caller forever. `ctx` is threaded through `sendRequest` and the client gets a 5 minute default, overridable with `timeout`.

### 3. Unbounded error bodies

Six call sites did:

```go
errmsg, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
...
return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s", errmsg)
```

A malicious server can drive memory use through that, and inject escape sequences into a terminal or a log. `errorBody` caps the read at 64 KiB and strips control characters, falling back to the status line when there's nothing usable.

### Also

The transport is cloned from `http.DefaultTransport`, so `tls_no_verify` keeps proxy support and connection pooling instead of dropping them, and pins TLS 1.2 as a floor.

Tests cover the token gate (all four combinations), the timeout default and parse errors, and `errorBody`'s cap and control-character stripping.

author: iman-nebulr
body:
React had **two of six** topics. An agent asked to integrate Bridge into a React app had nothing to consult and would invent an API — the exact failure `get_integration_guide` exists to prevent.

All four open with the decision that shapes everything after it, so an agent that reads only the first screen still chooses correctly:

- **integration** — hosted vs SDK auth. One config field (`loginRoute`) is the whole switch, and getting it wrong means rewriting the auth pages.
- **auth** — reach for `<LoginForm>`, do not hand-roll. It drives forgot-password, magic link, passkeys, MFA and workspace selection from server-side config the client cannot see.
- **team** — options ordered cheapest-correct-first, plus an explicit "do not proxy team CRUD through your own backend".
- **branding** — live data on `bridge.app.branding`, not a one-shot fetch.

React-specific traps documented, all of which fail *silently*: a missing router adapter, a missing stylesheet import, and a guard with no `isLoading` branch.

Docs-only; effective on merge.

Refs: TBP-573

author: theprimeagen
body: The control plane could type but not point. Hyprland focuses the window under the pointer, and a greeter or installer is a click, so a session could not sign in or use the desktop from the screenshot. ## QEMU mouse inventory Walked the current QMP UI schema (`qapi/ui.json`). What actually involves the mouse: | Item | What it does | Useful here? | | --- | --- | --- | | `input-send-event` + `abs` | Absolute pointer position, range `0..0x7fff` | Yes — click what you see on the screenshot | | `input-send-event` + `btn` | `left` / `middle` / `right` / `wheel-up` / `wheel-down` / `side` / `extra` / `wheel-left` / `wheel-right` / `touch` | Yes — left, right, middle, and the two wheel ticks. The rest is extra buttons and touch. | | `input-send-event` + `rel` | Relative motion | No — we never know where the pointer already is | | `input-send-event` + `mtt` | Multi-touch | No | | `input-send-event` + `key` | Keyboard via the same command | No — we already have `send-key` | | `query-mice` | Lists pointer devices (`name`, `index`, `current`, `absolute`) | No — diagnostic only | | HMP `mouse_move` / `mouse_button` / `mouse_set` | Legacy monitor | No — not QMP | | `usb-tablet` / `virtio-tablet-pci` | Guest device that accepts `abs` | Yes — without one, `abs` fails with "Input handler not found" | | `usb-mouse` / `virtio-mouse-pci` | Relative-only pointers | No | `usb-tablet` (via `qemu-xhci`) is the device that works from firmware through the greeter. `virtio-tablet-pci` needs a guest driver; the installer and OVMF setup would not see it. What is useful for signing in and using the desktop: - **Move** so Hyprland focuses the window under the pointer, then type - **Left click** a user, a password field, a login or installer button - **Double-click** to launch - **Right-click** a context menu - **Scroll** a list or settings page Relative motion, extra/side buttons, multi-touch, and `query-mice` stay unexposed. ## Surface One command, same shape as `send-keys`, through the QEMU client, the proxy, and the CLI. ``` oligarchy --agent-id send-mouse [button [clicks]] POST /send-mouse {"id", "x", "y", "button"?, "clicks"?, "agent"} ``` `x` and `y` are fractions of the screenshot (`0` is top/left, `1` is bottom/right). From a pixel `(px, py)` on a `W×H` image: `x = px / (W - 1)`, `y = py / (H - 1)`. Omit `button` to move only. `button` is `left`, `middle`, `right`, `wheel-up`, or `wheel-down`. `clicks` defaults to 1. Each QMP `input-send-event` is one action row. A click is two exchanges (button down, then button up) because `usb-tablet` syncs once per command — a press and release in the same list leave the button unchanged. A double-click is two of those pairs with a 50ms gap. ## Live proof (Omarchy 4.0.1) Booted the latest ISO, created user `demo`, installed, reached the Hyprland desktop, launched Chromium, opened Cookie Clicker, and clicked the cookie with `send-mouse`. The in-game counter went from 0 to 4 cookies; the last frame shows the hand cursor on the cookie and a `+1` pop. [Omarchy desktop after install and login](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a05443-fe80-7861-be58-13d5af3fdbe2/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fomarchy_desktop.png) [Cookie Clicker after send-mouse clicks, score 4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a05443-fe80-7861-be58-13d5af3fdbe2/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcookie_clicker_after.png) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: christianjosnik-ops
body:
Folge-PR zu #34 (gemergt). Ein Commit.

> **Hinweis:** Dieser PR enthielt urspruenglich einen Browser-Nachladeweg fuer GDELT. Dessen Annahme wurde durch einen Test widerlegt — GDELT ist auch aus dem Browser nicht erreichbar. Der Commit wurde ersetzt.

## Gemessen, nicht vermutet

Gemeldet war „GDELT nennt nie Meldungen" — in jeder Laenderzeile stand `0 Meldungen`. Die F9-Diagnose auf der echten Instanz zeigte den Grund:

```
GDELT (Weltlage, Nachrichtenvolumen)   kein Kontakt · 6001ms
GDELT Timeline (Trendverlauf)          kein Kontakt · 6000ms
```

Kein 429, keine kaputte Antwort. Der Host antwortet aus der Netlify-Region binnen sechs Sekunden ueberhaupt nicht — waehrend in **derselben** Diagnose antworteten:

| Quelle | Zeit |
| --- | --- |
| USGS | 246 ms ✓ |
| Yahoo | 281 ms ✓ |
| Frankfurter | 279 ms ✓ |

Serverseitig war nichts auszurichten: Netlify bricht synchrone Functions nach 10 s ab.

## Der Browserweg wurde versucht — und widerlegt

Naechster Ansatz war, GDELT aus dem **Browser** zu laden (derselbe Weg, der bei den USGS-Erdbeben aus #34 traegt). Test mit genau der Abfrage, die die App stellt: **auch dort keine Antwort.**

**Zwei unabhaengige Netze, dasselbe Ergebnis.** Vorher ausgeschlossen:

| Verdacht | Ergebnis |
| --- | --- |
| Abfragesyntax | gegen die GDELT-Doku geprueft — **korrekt** |
| HTTPS-Problem | DOC-API liefert laut Anbieter ueber HTTP **und** HTTPS |
| Bekannte Stoerung | keine gefunden |

Eine Quelle, die aus keinem erreichbaren Netz antwortet, ist fuer diese Anwendung tot. Sie stand nur noch als „0 Meldungen" in jeder Zeile — eine Anzeige, die wie ein Ergebnis aussah und keines war. **Genau das war der gemeldete Fehler.** Ein toter Codepfad, der Zahlen vortaeuscht, ist schaedlicher als eine fehlende Funktion, die sich benennt. Gleiche Entscheidung wie zuvor bei ReliefWeb.

## Was F6 jetzt zeigt

UCDP ist die einzige Konfliktquelle; die Stufe ist zweiwertig — **hoch** (UCDP fuehrt ein Ereignis) oder **keine** (geprueft, kein Ereignis). Die frueheren Zwischenstufen kamen ausschliesslich aus dem Nachrichtenvolumen; sie weiter anzuzeigen waere erfundene Genauigkeit.

**Neu und wichtig:** Ohne UCDP-Token gibt es gar kein Signal. Dann steht bei jedem Land `UNBEKANNT`, nicht `KEINE`, und der Reiter sagt oben ausdruecklich, dass keine Konfliktdaten vorliegen.

> Der Unterschied ist der Kern der Anzeige: „keine" hiesse *geprueft und ruhig*, „unbekannt" heisst *gar nicht geprueft*. Eine leere Weltlage als Entwarnung darzustellen waere schlimmer als gar keine Anzeige.

Die **USGS-Erdbeben** auf der Karte sind unberuehrt — mit 246 ms die schnellste Quelle der ganzen Diagnose, ohne Schluessel.

## Vereinfachung als Nebeneffekt

Mit GDELT entfielen **Wellen und Zeitbudget** der Function — die gab es nur fuer den Abruf je Land. UCDP ist ein einziger Aufruf, danach ist der Bericht fertig; der Zustand „nicht geprueft (Zeitbudget erreicht)" kann gar nicht mehr eintreten. Ebenso weg: die zwei GDELT-Diagnoseproben, die Trendchart-Komponente und die Felder `gdeltCount`/`headlines`/`gdeltTrend`/`error` aus jeder Laenderzeile.

## Test

- **Zehn** Testdateien gruen. `geopolitics.test.js` von 21 auf 11 Bloecke, `diag.test.js` von 15 auf 14.
- Die toten GDELT-Zweige wurden auch aus den **Test-Attrappen** entfernt — blieben sie stehen, wuerde ein versehentlich wieder eingebauter GDELT-Aufruf stillschweigend bedient statt als „unerwartete URL" aufzufallen.
- Ein Test prueft ausdruecklich, dass `gdeltCount` & Co. **nicht mehr geliefert** werden: ein zurueckgebliebenes `gdeltCount: 0` saehe sonst wieder wie „0 Meldungen" aus.
- In echtem Chromium beide Zustaende durchgespielt — ohne Token: Warnung, `UNBEKANNT` je Land, Detail-Hinweis „keine Pruefung"; mit Token: „UCDP: Konfliktereignis erfasst" bzw. „kein Konfliktereignis". Jede GDELT-Anfrage wurde mitgezaehlt: **0**.

author: livingstaccato
body:
Brings the `codex/fix-no-wait-click` work onto current `main` and reconciles it with the hang-resilience guards that landed in #168 while it was open.

Carries two commits from that branch — `fix(macros): support navigation-skipping clicks` and `fix(browser): preserve programmatic new-page navigation` — plus the merge and the fixes below.

## What broke, and why

The merge itself was clean. Five tests were not, all from the two branches not knowing about each other.

**Test doubles missing the new keyword.** Two doubles in the operation-gate integration suite mirror `BrowserSession.click`'s signature; a double that omits a parameter fails with `TypeError` rather than exercising the gate. One already carried a comment saying exactly that, written when `timeout_ms` did the same thing — `no_wait_after` has now done it a second time, so the comment records that. Two assertions pinning the forwarded call shape gained the keyword for the same reason.

**A duplicate LOC ceiling.** `test_core_page_mixin_stays_below_loc_ceiling` asserted 550 lines — a ratchet added by the commit that extracted expectations out of that file. It fired on a two-line feature addition while the file sat roughly two hundred lines under the 777 cap `scripts/check_max_loc.py` already enforces on every file. Two ceilings for one file drift, so it now derives from that single constant.

**The scanner allowlist was keyed by line number.** That is not a property of the call being exempted: an unrelated edit *above* a site shifts it out of the allowlist, and the scanner then reports a long-accepted exemption as a new offence. That happened twice today — once from a feature branch, once from this merge. It is now keyed by `(enclosing function, receiver expression)`, which moves with the code. Line numbers are still reported in the failure message, where they help, rather than relied on, where they don't.

Verified by inserting lines above the exempt sites and confirming the scanner stays green, then restoring the file byte-identical.

## The scanner earned its keep

It caught **two genuinely unbounded `Page`/`Frame` `evaluate()` calls** that this work introduces, written before that guard existed. Both are now wrapped in `bounded()`. A wedged target would have hung them forever — the exact incident #168 exists to prevent.

## Testing

`make lint` clean. All previously failing suites green.

**The full local suite cannot complete on this machine**, and that is not this branch. It wedges at 68%; excluding the first wedge point simply moves it to the next test, which is the signature of an inter-test leak (an unreaped subprocess). I confirmed by running the identical sweep against clean `origin/main` in an isolated worktree with `PYTHONPATH` pinned — it freezes at the same point with none of this code present, for 15+ minutes. The 11-test offset between the two runs is exactly what this branch adds. CI runs the full matrix on machines where it completes.

author: lucianlavric
body:
Lands Natalie's cheat-check sweep stack (#838 / #839 / #840) on current dev in one PR, with the review findings fixed. Her three commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved; the drafts #839 and #840 can be closed in favour of this.

## What this carries

1. **#838** — extract check logic out of the tRPC router into `cheat-check-runners` (its PR was closed by a history rewrite; the commit rides here so it finally gets merged reviewed).
2. **#839** — the sweep engine: `cheat_check_sweep` + `cheat_check_sweep_item`, a self-chaining `/api/cheat-check/sweep` worker under the 60s Hobby ceiling, batch claiming with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, a partial unique index so two sweeps can't run at once, secret-authenticated worker (timing-safe, fails closed).
3. **#840** — fire a sweep when the judging queue drains (post-commit, 30-min cooldown) plus the four organizer endpoints: `getSweepStatus`, `resumeSweep`, `startSweep`, `runAllTeamChecks`.

## Rebase + integration

- Migration regenerated as **`0015_cheat_check_sweep`** chained after `0014_team_join_codes` (the stack predated #852/#854/#875 and its `0012` collided with dev).
- `cheat-check.ts` router reconciled with #855's `getDisplayTeams`.
- Team fixtures across the new tests carry the `joinCode` required since #854.

## Review fixes on top (last commit)

- **Drain hook is awaited** — the biggest one: `void maybeTriggerSweepOnDrain()` dies when Vercel freezes the instance after the response, so in production sweeps would silently never fire while every test passed. Cost of the await is one COUNT per mark, ~2s once per actual drain, and the hook never throws.
- `createSweep` is transactional — no more strandable 0-item `running` sweep blocking all future sweeps.
- The worker chains only on strictly-pending items — an overlapped worker used to re-kick itself in a hot HTTP loop over another worker's claims.
- Per-invocation retry deferral — a failing team waits for the next chain link instead of burning its 3 attempts in seconds.
- `resumeSweep` refuses while the worker heartbeat is fresh (releasing a live worker's items double-processed teams); still works for stale heartbeats and rate-limit pauses, which is also how a rate-limited sweep resumes after reset.
- `getSweepStatus` no longer reports a rate-limit pause as `stalled`.
- `kickWorker` logs non-2xx kicks (a Deployment Protection 401 used to kill chains silently).
- `judging.test.ts` mocks `CHEAT_SWEEP_SECRET` unset like the sweep suites, so a real secret in `.env` can't leak into test HTTP; new tests for the `resumeSweep` guard.

## Verification

`npx vitest run` — 21/21 files. `tsc` clean. `drizzle-kit generate` — no drift. Prettier clean.

Known limitation (unchanged from the drafts, now documented in code): a rate-limited sweep does not self-resume — Hobby cron is daily, so recovery is the organizer's Resume button once the reset passes.

author: iman-nebulr
body:
Angular had **two of six** topics, so an agent integrating Bridge had nothing to read.

Angular turned out to have more surface than the coverage audit assumed: it ships a **declarative route guard** (`bridgeAuthGuard` + `RouteGuardConfig`) with the same `featureFlag` / `billing` / `redirectTo` rules as SvelteKit. The integration guide leads with it — gating a page with a rule rather than an `*ngIf` is the difference between redirecting before the component mounts and mounting, fetching, then hiding.

Angular-specific traps: `provideBridge()` missing or an empty `appId` fails silently (every flag reads as off), a login route not marked public gives an infinite redirect that presents as a hung page, and these are standalone components with no NgModule.

The team guide also notes that `TeamManagementPanelComponent` replaced a legacy iframe component, so an agent copying an older example does not reintroduce it.

Docs-only; effective on merge.

Refs: TBP-573

body:
## Summary

- Fetched and content-verified War and Peace in English (Gutenberg #2600, the Maude translation), the Russian original, and a real French translation (Bienstock, 1903, via Wikisource) — the corpus's own existing `gutenberg-non-en/` directory could not be used (20/20 files there are mislabeled, per the prior `CORPUS-INTEGRITY-FINDING.md`). Landed at `11-multi-language/war-and-peace/{en,ru,fr}/`.

author: joaocomini
body:
`box T` and `ref T` become `*T` and `&T`, and `box` takes over allocation from `new` as a prefix operator on a value.

```
struct Player {
    health: int,
    world: &World,
}

func spawn(w: &World): *Player {
    return box Player { health: 100, mana: 50, world: w };
}
```

Borrowing stays implicit — this changes how the two qualifiers are spelled and what `box` takes, nothing about who owns what.

## Why the value form

`new T` took a type and yielded a zeroed object you filled in afterwards. `box v` takes the value, so allocation and initialization are one expression, and the doubled-token shape `new box Box` becomes `box (box Box { n: 0 })`.

`box` allocates any value, not only a struct. `new T` could not allocate an `int` because it had no way to say *which* int; `box 7` does, so the restriction to structs and pointers is gone. A borrow still cannot be boxed — a heap slot holding one would outlive what it names.

```
let p: *int = box 7;
let b: *bool = box true;
```

## The consequence worth reviewing

A complete literal is required, so a self-referential borrow or owning field cannot be spelled at all — `struct Node { n: int, parent: &Node }` has no value to give `parent` at the point the literal is written, where `new Node` zeroed it and let a later assignment fill it in.

Two tests pinned exactly that shape and now state something weaker:

- `test/vm/ownership_test.c` — `test_a_ref_field_reads_and_writes` borrows a separate `Leaf` instead of another `Node`.
- `test/vm/generic_struct_test.c` — `test_a_declaration_reaches_itself_through_an_indirection` uses `*Leaf<T>` rather than `*Node<T>`, so it no longer reaches itself.

Both pass, but the self-reference is no longer exercised. That is a real gap in coverage rather than a cleanup, and it is the strongest argument against the value form.

## Codegen

`box v` evaluates the operand, emits `OP_NEW`, and stores through the pointer with `OP_STORE_PTR_N`.

Copying an owning value into the heap left the source registers still registered as owners, which double-freed anything owning — a double free in `string_test`, a segfault in `heap_test`. `codegen_disown_range` clears the operand's whole slot range rather than just its base.

Allocating a scalar then exposed a second one: `object_alloc` reserves `shape->size` (4 bytes for an `int`) while `OP_STORE_PTR_N` copies whole slots, overrunning the allocation by 4. Structs were safe because their size is slot-aligned. A narrow value now stores at its own width through the existing sized-field opcode. ASan catches it; the ordinary build does not.

Both guards were checked by disabling them and watching the failures return.

## Also

`&&T` lexes as one token, so the type parser splits it into a borrow of a borrow.

Diagnostics print the new spelling: `&int is not a struct, so it has no fields`.

50/50 pass, clean under ASan and UBSan.

author: fu351
body:
## Summary

Give every policy a version an auditor can match a decision to. A **policy version** is `pv1:` + the SHA-256 of a canonical snapshot of the effective policy — the saved policy document minus cosmetic text, the active role's globs, the ledger-verified enforcement state, and the engine version. Content identity, not a label: OPA's decision logs, SLSA, and OSCAL all converged on writing a hash of a canonical serialization inline; systems that stamped only a mutable name (IAM policy versions vs CloudTrail, Kubernetes admission audit annotations) had to bolt a side history on later.

- `src/doberman/storage/policy_catalogue.py` (new): the frozen `PolicySnapshotV1` model, the canonical JSON form (same shape `tool_pins` already uses), the `pv1:` id, and an **append-only** stdlib-sqlite3 store at `.doberman/policies.db` — `policy_versions` (each snapshot once) + `policy_observations` (a row whenever the version in force was seen to change). No `UPDATE`/`DELETE` statement exists in the module, and a test enforces that. Plain SHA-256, deliberately not the keyed HMAC: anyone holding the snapshot can recompute the id.
- `config.save_policy` records every saved policy as the version now in force, linked to the `policy_changes` row that authorised it: `ChangeOutcome` gains a `ts`, and every gated caller (enforcement, mode, prefs, egress-velocity, both default-role toggles, the revealed-preference nudge, `setup`'s first run) threads it through. Enforcement on the save path is resolved by the pure timer rule — `resolve_enforcement_sync` fails closed to `enforce` inside a running event loop, and the dashboard reaches `save_policy` inside one, so using it there would record a false version.
- `doberman policy-versions`: list (records an `observed` entry first, which is how a hand-edited `policies.yaml`/`role.yaml` enters the timeline), `--show <id>` (full id or ≥8 hex chars), `--json` (allowlist only, never snapshot content), and a read-only `--verify` that recomputes every stored digest and reports `ok` / `mismatch` / `drift`. `doberman doctor` gains a non-critical `Policy version` row.
- Docs: `docs/POLICY_VERSIONS.md` (what is hashed, the matching contract, what this does **not** prove), a published JSON Schema at `docs/schemas/policy-snapshot.v1.json` kept in sync by a drift test, CLI/README/TUNING rows.
- Never on the decision path: every write is best-effort, every read fails closed, and a subprocess test proves importing the host hooks and the proxy executor never imports the catalogue.

Design record: ADR 0088 (maintainer workspace). This is the store the upcoming "stamp `policy_version` on every decision row" issue matches against.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_policy_catalogue.py` (golden vector pinning the serialization, per-field sensitivity, redaction, store semantics, `version_at`, verify states), `tests/unit/test_cli_policy_versions.py` (listing, `--show` prefix/full-id/exit codes, read-only `--verify`), doctor/help/schema-doc/standalone additions, linkage tests at every chokepoint including `establish_ok` first-run. Full suite locally: 3410+ passed; the only failures are this box's two known environment-only ones (`test_version_is_exposed` dist metadata; the numpy2/pandas benchmark import), both green in CI.

body:
In a shared multi-project runtime without a host execution grant, `GET /api/agents` and `GET /api/agents/:id` called `ensureProjectDiscovery(ctx)` with no locality guard, so the `VeryfrontError` thrown by `src/server/handlers/request/api/project-discovery.ts:151` ("Remote executable discovery requires an isolated project runtime and cannot run in the shared host", INITIALIZATION_ERROR, 500) escaped the handler and surfaced in Sentry as an unhandled 500. Both `PublicAgentsListHandler` and `PublicAgentMetadataHandler` now check `requiresIsolatedProjectRuntime(ctx)` before discovery and return a structured RFC 9457 problem response (503, `application/problem+json`, type `https://veryfront.com/docs/code/guides/errors#project-execution-unavailable`) built through the response builder with CORS/security headers and `no-store` caching, exactly mirroring the sibling surfaces (ssr.handler, snippet.handler, app-router-handler). Shared runtimes the host granted execution (`allowHostProjectCodeExecution: true`) and explicit local projects still reach discovery and are served as before.

Fixes veryfront/veryfront-issue-inbox#854

## Red

```
deno task test:file src/server/handlers/request/public-agents-list.handler.test.ts src/server/handlers/request/public-agent-metadata.handler.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
shared runtime without a host execution grant ...
  fails closed with project-execution-unavailable instead of leaking the discovery error ... FAILED (1ms)
  serves a shared runtime the host granted execution ... ok

ERRORS
server/handlers/request/public-agents-list.handler ... fails closed with project-execution-unavailable instead of leaking the discovery error
error: VeryfrontError: Remote executable discovery requires an isolated project runtime and cannot run in the shared host
    at Object.create (src/errors/types.ts:111:14)
    at Object.ensureProjectDiscovery (src/server/handlers/request/api/project-discovery.ts:151:32)
    at src/server/handlers/request/public-agents-list.handler.ts:44:23
    at PublicAgentsListHandler.withProxyContext (src/security/http/base-handler.ts:211:24)
    at PublicAgentsListHandler.handle (src/server/handlers/request/public-agents-list.handler.ts:39:17)

server/handlers/request/public-agent-metadata.handler ... fails closed with project-execution-unavailable instead of leaking the discovery error
error: VeryfrontError: Remote executable discovery requires an isolated project runtime and cannot run in the shared host
    at Object.create (src/errors/types.ts:111:14)
    at Object.ensureProjectDiscovery (src/server/handlers/request/api/project-discovery.ts:151:32)
    at src/server/handlers/request/public-agent-metadata.handler.ts:53:23

FAILED | 0 passed (10 steps) | 2 failed (4 steps) (202ms)
```

## Green

After the fix, same command:

```
server/handlers/request/public-agents-list.handler ...
  returns every browser-safe agent, sorted by name ... ok
  skips ids that no longer resolve to an agent ... ok
  returns an empty list when the project exposes no agents ... ok
  ignores non-GET requests ... ok
  shared runtime without a host execution grant ...
    fails closed with project-execution-unavailable instead of leaking the discovery error ... ok
    serves a shared runtime the host granted execution ... ok
server/handlers/request/public-agent-metadata.handler ...
  returns browser-safe source-defined agent metadata ... ok
  returns 404 when the source-defined agent does not exist ... ok
  returns 400 when the agent id cannot be decoded ... ok
  ignores non-GET requests ... ok
  shared runtime without a host execution grant ...
    fails closed with project-execution-unavailable instead of leaking the discovery error ... ok
    serves a shared runtime the host granted execution ... ok

ok | 2 passed (14 steps) | 0 failed (232ms)
```

Affected suite: `deno task test:file src/server/handlers/request/` -> ok | 69 passed (612 steps) | 0 failed (10s). `deno check`, `deno fmt --check`, and `deno lint` are clean on both changed handlers.

## Revert check

Recorded HEAD 18bc7f453d84d1753d65088896df3fac46156cb9. `git revert --no-commit 18bc7f453` (only the two handler .ts files reverted; tests kept), then the red test command:

```
REVERTED -> FAILED | 0 passed (10 steps) | 2 failed (4 steps)
```

Both "fails closed with project-execution-unavailable instead of leaking the discovery error" steps fail with `VeryfrontError: Remote executable discovery requires an isolated project runtime and cannot run in the shared host` at `src/server/handlers/request/api/project-discovery.ts:151`, escaping via `withProxyContext` (`base-handler.ts:211`), which is the exact Sentry leak. `git reset --hard 18bc7f453` -> ok | 2 passed (14 steps) | 0 failed. Broader sweep at restored HEAD: `deno task test:file src/server/handlers/request/` -> ok | 69 passed (612 steps) | 0 failed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `GET /api/agents` and `GET /api/agents/:id` in a shared multi-project runtime without a host execution grant return a structured RFC 9457 problem response instead of letting the raw VeryfrontError escape the handler
- [x] The denial response is 503 with content-type `application/problem+json` and problem type `https://veryfront.com/docs/code/guides/errors#project-execution-unavailable`, matching the convention of sibling surfaces (ssr.handler, snippet.handler, app-router-handler, api-handler-wrapper)
- [x] A shared runtime whose host granted execution (`allowHostProjectCodeExecution: true`, or explicit local project) is still served: the guard is `requiresIsolatedProjectRuntime(ctx)`, not a blanket denial, and the granted-counterpart tests assert 200 plus that discovery ran
- [x] Existing handler behavior (200 list/metadata, 404 unknown agent, 400 bad id, non-GET passthrough) is preserved by the pre-existing tests in the same files

author: jasonsopko
body:
## What
Gives a BLAKE2b job a `blake2b_coinbase_index`, selected when its coinbases are generated: type 4, the largest payout-carrying budget, once the coinbaser has answered, and type 0 before that and for solo work. The commitment helper takes the index explicitly with bounds checks, `send_mining_notify` advertises it in the job ID, and the submit path and DATUM protocol already carry an index end to end, so shares and found blocks rebuild the same coinbase.

## Why
The BLAKE2b path pinned everything to type 0, the "empty" variant that pays only the pool address: `cbselect = 0` for every v2 job in notify, and `cb = &s->coinbase[0]` hardcoded in the commitment. The pool's `available_coinbase_outputs` were built into types 1 through 5 and never selected, so in pooled mode the pool address received 100% of every block found while the coinbaser page showed the split. All four OCEAN-tagged blocks on the BLAKE2b mainnet chain (961687, 961790, 961851, 961862) pay a single output at the pool address. Reported by MaVeTh on Discord; their fork carries an equivalent fix (`bip110_pow_v2_payout_coinbase`, fec073f). Every v2 client shares one coinbase per job either way, since the hasher extranonce lives in the header, so no per-client type selection is needed and none is added.

## Relation to #16
MaVeTh's #16 is the same idea, opened while this was being written. This one differs in three ways, detailed in a review there: the no-outputs fallback is type 0 rather than `subsidy_only` (which burns fees on solo blocks and, on reused job slots, can commit to a stale height), the job ID is authoritative so the commitment, submit and the DATUM protocol's per-index message always agree, and the previous job's payout plan is not carried across jobs. Whichever shape lands is fine; the bug is the thing.

## How I tested
`--test` passes with new cases: the commitment follows the requested index and matches one built from that type's raw transaction, the job-level freeze honors the selected index both ways, and out-of-range indexes are refused. Solo behavior is unchanged by construction (`empty_only` keeps index 0). I have not run this against a live DATUM Prime pool; the type-4 bytes reach the pool through the existing per-index 0x02 message, the same path SHA256d pooled clients use today.

## Risk and rollback
Solo mining is untouched. For pooled mining the risk is a pool whose BLAKE2b share validation assumed type 0: it would reject type-4 shares until it updates, which is visible immediately and recoverable by reverting the one commit. Given that the current behavior mis-pays every pooled block find, I think that trade is right.

## Still unsure about
Whether DATUM Prime deployments validate v2 shares against the coinbase bytes the gateway sends (as SHA256d does) or assume type 0; someone with a Prime instance should confirm shares still accept before this ships in a release. The pre-existing unlocked coinbase-buffer rewrite (#217 in the OCEAN repo) applies to this path as before; this change neither worsens nor fixes it.

author: wrexist
body:
Two shipped rendering bugs, the card-back system, and the capture rig that found them.

> Correction to the first version of this description: it also claimed the no-goalkeeper fix and the family-name import fix. Those are real, but they merged in #616/#617 and are already on `main` — they are not in this diff.

## The walkout OVR count-up has never been on screen

`WalkoutReveal` renders a giant number that ticks 0 → rating over the hero card at the flip. It is the app's best beat with the sound off, and it had never once reached a screen. Three faults, all confirmed against rendered frames rather than the DOM — the element was in the DOM, sized, at full opacity, and still painted nothing:

1. The overlay was declared **above** the hero card in the tree, so the card painted straight over it.
2. `mixBlendMode: 'screen'` on white type. Screen cannot darken, so over an icon card's white marble the number composited to exactly the card beneath it. Replaced with a scrim plus a hard dark shadow, which works on every card in the set rather than only the dark ones.
3. The opacity ran as a keyframe track with a `times` array that measured 0.38 opacity a third of the way through the beat — still fading in while already counting, and torn down before reaching full. Now a snap-in tween plus an `exit` fade.

Two smaller things fell out. The count read the rAF callback's timestamp while starting from `performance.now()` — the same clock in a browser, but not under the capture rig, which scales `performance.now` and cannot touch the rAF timestamp, so every captured walkout landed on the final rating with no count at all. And `ovrRollMs` was dead config: nothing read it, the roll ran for `ovrOverlayMs - 150`.

## The roll started at a rating the card could not have

A walkout only fires at 84+, so a count from 0 spent most of its visible life showing ratings the cinematic cannot be about, and a huge `27` on screen reads as a rating, not as a counter passing through. It now starts just under the walkout floor. Verified by capture: **79 → 84 → 87 → 90 → 92 → 94 → 95** across the flip.

## A card back for every card front

Card fronts do not share one outline — gold and silver are plain shields, icon carries an inner cut-out ring, each pack frame is notched differently. `CardBack` masks per-card with the same `getPlayerCardArt` URL the face renders, so back and front are geometrically identical by construction. 13 backs registered in `CARD_BACKS`; tests pin that every front has one, that each exists as `.webp`, and that an unknown front falls back to the universal back.

The 13 deleted `*_back.png` files are the sources for those webps — ~3.2 MB each against ~0.5 MB, and a test enforces the format.

## Marketing capture rig

- `SquadScene` takes `?fill=N`. The App Preview's squad beat needs the board *filling*, and the app already renders a part-filled lineup with real empty slots, so it is captured as four genuine app states rather than faked with masks.
- `CAP_SCALE` env var. The rig forced a device scale factor of 2 (780×1688) — already 1:1 against the 886-wide App Preview, so every punch-in was upscaling into render pixels. `CAP_SCALE=3` makes those crops downsamples.
- `?hero=<name>` pins who walks out, instead of re-rolling whole captures until the right name appears.
- **The `pack` plan was skipping every take's hero walkout.** Its blind tap loop kept tapping after the last reveal, and a tap on a running walkout means SKIP. Every 5-card capture ever filmed lost its hero to its own rig.

`marketing/scripts/app-store-trailer.md` carries the research, the shot list as shot, and the reasoning behind each revision of the preview.

## Testing

`npm run preflight` green on every commit (lint, typecheck, docs drift, i18n ceiling, fast tests, build, eager-bundle budget).

Not tested: none of this ran on device. The walkout changes are pure rendering — no state, no persistence, no save-schema change, and nothing touching a sim parameter. The rig changes are marketing-only and ship no app code.

## Qué hace

Desbloquea el login OAuth2 de **C4 (US-402)** creando el cliente OAuth de Google y cableando sus credenciales en Cloud Run. Es la dependencia **D-A** del plan de S5 (parte deploy/C5).

## Cambios

| Credencial | Naturaleza | Dónde vive |
|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | público (viaja en la URL de consentimiento) | `--set-env-vars` |
| `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` | público (URL del callback) | `--set-env-vars` |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | **secreto** | Secret Manager (`google-client-secret`), `--set-secrets` |

- **`deploy-cloud-run.sh`**: env vars OAuth públicas + `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` desde Secret Manager + hook **comentado** `ANALISTA_EMAILS` (allowlist del rol `analista`, US-403; dueño PO pendiente, no se versiona ningún correo).
- **`Cloud_Run_Deploy.md` §4.5**: tabla público/secreto, alta del cliente (External+Testing, redirect canónico), validación e2e del login (v1.2).
- **DevLog** `2026-08-30-luis-tellez-oauth-creds-deploy.md` + fila en `_index.md`.
- **`Traceability_Matrix.md`**: DevLog enlazado en REQ-005 y en REQ-004/US-402.

## Decisiones

- **Pantalla de consentimiento External + modo "Prueba" (Testing):** la org (`luis-g-roses-org`) es personal, así que "Internal" sólo dejaría entrar al dominio del dueño y excluiría al equipo + evaluadores. Testing admite 100 test users, sin verificación de Google (scopes `openid email profile` no sensibles).
- **Redirect = URL canónica** (`https://faro-api-eanzfglvyq-uc.a.run.app/api/v1/auth/callback`), no un alias → evita `redirect_uri_mismatch`.

## Validación en prod (norma: validar lo desplegado ANTES del PR)

- Redeploy aplicado → revisión **`faro-api-00007-4dd`**. Verificado con `gcloud run services describe`: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`REDIRECT_URI` como env vars; `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` como `secretKeyRef` (Secret Manager, no texto plano).
- **Login e2e:** el `/callback` responde **401 (no 500)** → confirma que las credenciales están bien cableadas; sólo falta implementar `RealGoogleVerifier.verify()` (**C4**).
- `/health` 200, `/escuelas` 200 (25 escuelas) — sin regresión de Fase 2.
- `vault_lint.py` verde; diff sin secretos (`client_secret` **nunca** pasó por el agente ni el repo).

## Fuera de alcance (gated por C4)

- Implementar `RealGoogleVerifier.verify()`.

author: tyevans
body:
Derives Cachette's rule set from two mature sibling projects by measuring their record corpora rather than by copying their rules.

## What I measured

106 records with full commit history across `eventsource-py` (61) and `redstring` (45). Numbers in `docs/research/adr-scope-findings.md`.

- **Length predicts churn.** Pearson r = 0.704 and 0.715, derived independently in the two corpora. Records ≥4000 words were edited 3.7× as often as records <1200 words.
- **Records that hold a value churn more.** Version pins: 1.5× and 1.7× the corpus mean. Measured figures: 1.67× the mean. One record selects a testing tool by version; its own text now says that release line is superseded, and nothing cites it.
- **Two records were superseded within 1 and 2 days.** Both recorded a module arrangement. redstring 0018 says in its own status block that every decision in it still holds, but that none is held there any more. The decisions survived; the records died when the modules moved.
- **Five records were deleted in one commit, without supersession.** eventsource-py 0002–0006, all status `Accepted`, alive 70 days, all topic-titled, none stating a constraint, none cited.
- **Uncited records are short.** The 8 uncited records in eventsource-py average 779 words against a corpus mean of 1582. redstring has only 1, and it is the second-shortest file.
- **Both projects drifted from topic titles to claim titles** with no shared rule: 3%→21% and 57%→82%. In redstring a topic title churned 4.50× against 2.13× for a claim title, at 4178 words against 1887.

## What I concluded

The owner's framing holds, with one correction. The evidence for leaving a decision unstated is strong: the five deleted records are the clean case. The evidence does **not** support deleting a record because nothing cites it — redstring's one uncited record is correct and small. Low citation is a signal to review, not a verdict, and the rule says so.

The evidence also does not support a word limit. redstring 0013 runs 10810 words, churned 6 times, and is healthy, because its subject is one large thing. The rule asks for one claim per record instead.

**This bears directly on Cachette.** All six drafts are longer than both reference medians (1777–4570 words vs ~1300), four sit in the highest-churn band, and five of six carry a topic title — the form that churned twice as much. That is flagged in the registry, not acted on, since the drafts are in review elsewhere.

## Scope categories derived

Section 1 of the rule is the hard part: three conditions that must all hold before a decision earns a record — a contributor could reasonably choose otherwise; choosing otherwise costs more than changing it later; the reasoning is not visible in the artefact. With a counter-test, because a determinism decision always earns a record.

Section 4 is what must not go in one, each category tied to an observed failure: a value a measurement can change; a version or named release; a count, file table or survivor list; a module arrangement; a value an unanswered question governs; a capability nothing invokes.

## Rules adopted and skipped

| Rule | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `adr-scope.md` | **New** | The main deliverable. Neither reference project has one; both needed one. |
| `commits.md` | **Adapt** | The commit message is the only document that never decays, so it is where counts and figures go instead of a record. Load-bearing for the scope rule. Reference format differs between the two projects; took redstring's imperative style. |
| `testing.md` | **Adapt, cut short** | The gates are already in the definition of done; restating them would be a second declaration site. What is new is test design under determinism — a determinism test must have a proven failure mode, and nothing may assert on time. |
| `user-trust.md` | **Adopt** | Identical in both projects, 211 bytes, and nothing here changes it. Rewritten to STE with one addition: report contrary evidence in a sentence, then proceed. |
| `recurring-defects.md` | **Adapt, with provenance** | Cachette has no code and no defect history. Importing six shapes as if they were local evidence is what redstring's own provenance note warns against. Kept the shapes with local evidence or catastrophic consequence, each marked local or imported, and added one the references cannot have: nondeterminism the tests cannot see. |
| `architecture.md` | **Skip** | The reference rule encodes Python dependency rings. This project's structural boundaries — the crate boundary, the arithmetic module, the interpreter lock — are already in ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ADR-0006 and CLAUDE.md. A rule file would be a third copy of a fact with nothing to fail when the copies disagree. Worth writing once crates exist, deriving from the records rather than restating them. |

## What the checks cover

`scripts/check-adrs.sh` → `scripts/check_adrs.py`. One file, standard library only, wired to `.github/workflows/adr-check.yml`.

Fails on: a missing or out-of-order required section; `## References` not last; a title whose number disagrees with the file name; a version pin or a latency, throughput, percentage or budget figure in the body; a citation of a record number that no record and no registry row has; a citation of `ADR-NNNN Dn` where the target does not define `Dn`; a footnote path that does not resolve; a file with no registry row, a row still marked `Proposed` when the file exists, or a row with a status but no file.

Reports without failing: a record that no other record and no source file cites.

**Result against the six drafts: 0 failures, 0 notes.** Verified against a deliberately broken record: every class of failure fires.

The volatile check carries a baseline of the 15 figures already in the drafts (`scripts/adr-volatile-baseline.txt`), since those records are in review on another branch and are off-limits here. The baseline is falsifiable — an entry matching nothing fails the check — so it can only shrink. It also exempts code blocks, tables, inline code and the References section, and is deliberately narrow: a cache line size is a platform property, not a budget, and a check that flags it would train everyone to ignore the check.

Also creates `docs/reference/budgets.md`. The registry already named it and two drafts already cite it, so the reference dangled and the check found it. It copies no value out of a record — that would be the second declaration site the defect rule warns about — and instead lists which records still hold figures that belong there.

## On the definition of done

No contradiction found; not edited. One suggestion for its review: §"By kind of work" says a decision record "must not hold material that changes". That is now backed by measurement and extended by `adr-scope.md`, so a pointer to the scope rule there would close the loop. Worth doing in that PR rather than this one.

The AI could already point at the graph — five `ui_directive` verbs, live and wired. It could not **hold** a gaze or **say anything where it pointed**.

**A held attention channel**, separate from the applied-edit pulse by design: those answer different questions, and lengthening the pulse to serve both would make every applied edit hold too — two intents under one name.

- Derives its dim rather than writing `dimmedNodeIds` (which already has two writers and a documented precedence rule).
- Carries `turnId` + `modelVersion`, answering PR #747's objection that the canvas is one global slot — the card says when the model has moved instead of presenting a stale note as current.
- A highlight carrying a note routes to attention; a bare highlight keeps the existing pulse, so **no current emitter changes behaviour**.
- The card mounts inside the viewport transform, so it tracks its anchor through pans and zooms.
- Its actions open the conversation carrying the element, prefilled with a **question**.

Authors nothing: every string is the producer's own. The only decision this code makes is which of four reasoning moves labels the card.

Two readers decided from `kernel.package` and one from `kernel.source`. `cjk_kernel_problems` was the one reading the source, so a non-amd64 install whose `kernel.package` names a cjktty atom took the architecture refusal past the rule — and `plan/kernel.py` merges the override, so emerge stopped with the disk already partitioned.

The trim from atom to bare name existed three times over: `validate._package_name` and two more lines in `compat.py`, all with `-\\d[\\w.]*$`, which does not strip the `*` in `=sys-kernel/gentoo-sources-6.12*`. Portage takes that form, so the `-sources` refusal never fired and the install finished with a source tree and an empty `/boot`. One `compat.kernel_package_name(config)` now, reading the override first and stripping the asterisk.

Both controls were run red.

body:
## Summary

- Running this repo's own flagship specimen (War and Peace, the text P5.2/P5.3/P50 already verify 11,132/11,132 passages against) through the full reading process in English, Russian, and French (`live_priors`, LP7) surfaced a real defect this repo's own `hypergraph.js`/`holon.js` relation tier has been carrying unmeasured: `discoverRelationVocab`'s surface lookup uses JS's `\b`, which is ASCII-only with no Unicode mode, so a name written in a non-Latin script could never be located at all.
- Fixed in eoreader7 (`READING-SPEC.md` S34) — the exact `native/adapters/text/relations.js` file `app.js:167` already imports `discoverRelationVocab`/`extractRelations` from. Not a new capability; a correctness fix to one this repo already depends on.
- Disclosed, not overclaimed: closes reachability, not vocabulary precision (P29/live_priors' own LP6 gate is English-only and unloaded for any language in this measurement).

Full account: live_priors `POLICIES.md` LP7 (the corpus and measurement), eoreader7 `READING-SPEC.md` S34 (the mechanism fix). This PR adds only the pointer entry, P72, to this repo's own `POLICIES.md` — no code in this repo changed.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test generality-gate.test.mjs` — 4/4, P72 carries the required `**Generality:**` tag
- [x] `node --test *.test.mjs` — 1060/932/126/2, failure names diffed against a `git stash`-recovered baseline: byte-identical, zero regressions (this is a documentation-only change — no `.js` file in this repo was touched)

## Amended 2026-08-30 — all 516 real UN UDHR translations, read for blind spots

User direction: apply the same process to every UDHR translation this corpus holds, "more than a universal reading, we're looking for our blindspots." Pointer only, same reasoning as the entry above: this repo's relation reader and referent machinery depend on `surfaces.js`'s capitalisation layer through the native import path P69's ratchet crossed `app.js` onto. eoreader7 S36 closes a subtler script-blindness case (a script that IS Unicode-cased but never actually uses the case contrast the extraction mechanism depends on — Georgian, Cherokee, and several 20th-century Latin-alphabet orthographies that never adopted capitalisation-marks-a-name); live_priors' own LP8 is the corpus-side census. No code in this repo changed.

## Amended 2026-08-31 — the three blind spots the UDHR census found, closed

User direction, verbatim: *"fix the issues."* Pointer only, same reasoning as both entries above.

eoreader7 `native/READING-SPEC.md` S37/S38 are the law for the two mechanism fixes; live_priors' POLICIES.md LP9 is the corpus-side wiring and the full 516-file re-sweep:

1. `capitalisationIsSignificant`'s normal-approximation significance test — found under-powered on a Czech specimen, but the real defect (found by an exhaustive sweep, not that one specimen) was a systematic small-sample bias, 24 false positives out of 1,711 checked pairs, all in the same direction — replaced with an exact one-sided binomial tail.
2. A highly-inflected language's own name declension (Russian's "Кутузов"/"Кутузова"/"Кутузову", "Анна"/"Анне"/"Анны") fragmenting one referent into several strangers, closed by a new pairwise case-fold organ, verified at 38 correct merges and zero false ones against real fetched Russian War and Peace.
3. live_priors' own POS-vocabulary gate, described in that repo's `loadOrgans` as measured and working while its actual import path pointed at an empty submodule — never loaded, for English or any other language, until this pass.

None of the three required a code change in this repo; P12's grounding ladder and the relation tier it stands on inherit all three the moment either sibling repo's fix lands, the same way P69's ratchet was designed to work.

author: momad-y
body:
Pulls `ls` / `cd` / `pwd` / `cat` forward from Phase 6, adds `dir`, and fixes a
latent terminal bug they would have made routine.

Owner chose the path style (POSIX over the real drive) and asked for the banner
joke. Plan, both red-team records and the corrections applied are in
`docs/cmd-filesystem-plan.md`.

## Why now, not Phase 6

Every prerequisite had already shipped: the folder tree is in
`hard_drive.json`, `resolve_portfolio_ref()` already renders an entry, and
`DEFERRED_COMMANDS` meant Tab actively completed you to a command that then
answered "not available yet".

## What it does

- Walks the **live `hardDrive` store** — the same one Explorer renders — so a
  folder created on the desktop shows up in the next `ls`. There is an E2E for
  exactly that, and it is the one assertion the whole design rests on.
- POSIX paths over the real drive (`/c/Experience`, git-bash style) with `~` as
  the C: drive, so `cd experience` works from the first prompt. §3.2 specifies
  bash emulation while the filesystem underneath is a Windows drive.
- Names match case-**in**sensitively (NTFS); commands stay case-**sensitive**
  (bash). Two namespaces, two correct answers.
- `ls` hides what Explorer hides; `ls -a` shows it. Order is `children` order,
  never alphabetical — Explorer renders the same array and the seed order is
  reverse-chronological, so sorting would open the CV with "Corporatica".
- Tab completes names containing spaces and both dashes the seed ships, and
  terminates a directory with `/` rather than a space.
- `dir` ribs the visitor, then runs `ls` anyway.
- The banner's original third line is restored, plus the joke about a Command
  Prompt that only speaks Linux.

## The terminal fix (own commit, stands alone)

`redraw()` was `\r` + erase-to-end-of-**line** — column 0 of the *current* row,
clearing only that row. Any input longer than the window reprinted the prompt
per keystroke: **typing 140 characters put 25 prompts on screen.** Reachable on
production today via `echo`; routine once `cat` exists, where the longest seeded
filename is 71 characters at a 27-column prompt.

Row maths moved to a pure `src/lib/term/render.ts`, shared with the standalone
REPL, which had the same defect in the same shape. State is a column **offset**,
not a row — the window is resizable and xterm reflows.

## Red-team findings applied

Gate 2 killed the plan's load-bearing claim that completion already worked
(`word_at` splits on the last space, so it could never complete a name on this
drive) and caught that the seed ships **two** dashes, 7 em and 8 en.

Gate 6 found four defects, each reproduced before fixing:

1. The **bell re-armed** the bug commit 1 fixed — a zero-motion write that reset
   the cursor row.
2. Every other write assumed the cursor was at the line's **end**; after Home,
   output landed on top of what you typed.
3. A **resize mid-edit** made the next redraw climb into the previous output.
4. The stale-cwd fallback lived only in `resolve()`, so with a deleted working
   directory `cd` recovered while `ls` printed nothing and `pwd` claimed `~`.

It also found **four tests that could not fail**, including a `cat` E2E
asserting a substring of a filename already on screen, and a test named
"survives a python session" that never started python. Each replacement was
mutation-verified.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` — 0 errors (128 warnings, not grown)
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm run format:check` — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run --coverage` — **689 passed**; `lib/cmd` 98.9%, `lib/term` 100%
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `npx playwright test` — **150 passed, 0 failed** (incl. `@online` Pyodide)
- [x] Mutation-verified: `render.ts` (6), `path.ts` (8), `fs_commands.ts` (9),
      `format.ts`, the rewritten registry/completion tests (3), and both new
      cursor E2Es
- [ ] Deploy preview: open CMD, `ls`, `cd experience`, `cat` an entry via Tab,
      create a desktop folder and confirm `ls Desktop` sees it

## Docs

`SPECIFICATION.md` §3.2 rewritten and the Phase 6 checklist item ticked;
`phase-3-guide.md`, `phase-3-spec.md` and `phase-3-plan.md` carry
superseded-notes rather than rewrites — they are the record of what was decided
at the time; `CLAUDE.md`'s phase-guide pointer had stopped at 2.

author: abonforti
body:
Closes #198. The Map was the last placeholder view.

Executed on a Node 22 host, because this one cannot build under the `engine-strict` gate that #204 added: 990 vitest tests, 91 Playwright tests across four projects, `npm run build`, `tsc --noEmit` and `svelte-check` all clean. The built bundle contacts exactly one external origin, the tile template; the three marker icons are `data:` URIs.

## What execution found that reading did not

Two defects, and neither was visible in review.

**The view overflowed the slot in landscape**, on both engines: `Expected: <= 403 / Received: 417.1875`. The height was `min(60vh, 480px)`, a fraction of the viewport rather than of the slot it lives in. Fixed with the flex-from-the-slot technique the Log view already uses.

**Leaflet's default attribution flag fails WCAG AA.** `rgb(255, 213, 0)` on `rgb(248, 248, 248)` is **1.34:1 against a 3:1 floor**, in both palettes and all four projects. Fixed with `setPrefix()`, which keeps Leaflet's own credit and drops only the decoration. `prefix: false` would have dropped the credit too, established from `Control.Attribution.js` at the `v1.9.4` tag rather than from the documentation.

A third would have been found in CI rather than locally: `geometry.spec.ts` would have fetched real OpenStreetMap tiles on all four projects once the placeholder skip stopped firing. Stubbed with `page.route`.

## Decisions worth naming

- **Three empty states, not two.** No captures at all, captures but none with a position, and a position that is not finite are different sentences, and the third exists because #109 established the client trusts every frame it parses.
- The marker is **the unit's position**, never the phone's.
- The popup is built as an element, never as a string, so nothing in a capture's name can reach `innerHTML`.
- Marker images are bundled rather than fetched. `L.Icon.Default.mergeOptions` alone does not repoint them: `_getIconUrl` prefixes an auto-detected `imagePath`, and it works today only because Vite's hashed name defeats `_stripUrl`'s regex, so `_getIconUrl` is deleted first.
- `leaflet` is pinned exactly while `@types/leaflet` keeps the caret its eleven neighbours use, and SPEC records why the asymmetry is deliberate.

`import L from 'leaflet'` would fail TS1259: there is no `esModuleInterop` in `tsconfig.json` and no default export in `@types/leaflet`. Both verified rather than assumed.

author: flyon
body:
## The bug

`Prefix.toPrefixed()` guarded only against `/` in the local part. When a registered namespace is a proper **string** prefix of an IRI's own namespace, it emitted names like:

```sparql
?a0 rdf:type create-now:access#PolicyRegistry .
```

for `https://data.create.now/access#PolicyRegistry` under `PREFIX create-now: <https://data.create.now/>`.

`#` is not in the SPARQL 1.1 `PN_LOCAL` production. The tokenizer ends the prefixed name at `create-now:access` and reads `#PolicyRegistry .` as a **comment to end of line** — eating the triple terminator. The store then rejects the query with a parse error pointing at the *following* line:

```
Parse error: Encountered " "}" "}" at line 8, column 3
Parse error: Encountered " <VAR1> "?a0 "" at line 6, column 3
```

That off-by-one is why this was misattributed to the where-clause builder for months. Two queries in Create Now's policy repository have been rejected since they were written; `@_linked/fuseki` 2.x turned the rejection into an empty result set, so an **authorization** store silently read as "no grants". 3.0.0 made it throw, which is what finally surfaced it.

## The fix

- `Prefix.toPrefixed()` validates the local part against a conservative `PN_LOCAL` allowlist and returns `undefined` otherwise, so `formatUri` falls back to `<full-iri>`. An allowlist rather than adding `#` to the `/` blocklist: a blocklist is wrong again the moment another illegal character appears, and over-rejecting only costs a longer IRI, never correctness.
- `collectPrefixes` now asks `toPrefixed` instead of re-implementing the `/` rule, so the `PREFIX` block and the terms can never disagree about what is prefixable.

Only affects IRIs that could not legally be compacted anyway — `rdf:type`, `schema:name` and friends are unchanged.

## Tests

`src/tests/sparql-prefixed-names.test.ts` covers the rule, the two real queries as goldens, and — importantly — **executes both against a live SPARQL endpoint**. No golden string can tell you a query parses, and that is exactly what went unnoticed here.

Every assertion fails without the fix, including both live checks (Fuseki 400).

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New test | 13 passed (all fail on the parent commit) |
| Full suite | 1667 passed, 68 suites |
| `tsc -p tsconfig-tests.json` | clean |

## Summary
<!-- Provide a brief summary of the changes you have made and most importantly what they aim to achieve -->
Fixes #4534.

A camera notification's long look on the Watch streams `camera_proxy_stream` through `VideoStreamer()`, but its session delegate had no mTLS handling on watchOS — `MJPEGCertificateSessionDelegate` sat behind `#if !os(watchOS)`. An mTLS server refuses that stream, so the long look shows "the server requires a client certificate" instead of the camera.

- The two near-identical MJPEG delegates collapse into one that handles both the response boundary and the client certificate challenge, on every platform. Nothing about it was iOS-only — token refresh already uses `ClientCertificateSessionDelegate` on watchOS.
- It is attached unconditionally instead of being gated on `clientCertificate != nil`, matching `makeCertificateAwareURLSession`. The delegate resolves the certificate at challenge time, and on the Watch the streamer is often built before the certificate-bearing server config has been applied.
- The Watch now asks the phone to re-send the certificate at launch when a server references one its Keychain doesn't have. Previously only a database mirror apply noticed that, so a cold launch failed every mTLS request with `certificateNotFound` until the user hit refresh.
