body:
## Objetivo
Integrar en Jadel Tech RD un registro institucional y auditable de agentes, madurez, controles, blockers de producción y puntos HITL, y añadir el primer runtime comercial fail-closed para convertir el configurador en una futura superficie transaccional real.

## Cambios de readiness
- `config/agent-production-manifest.json`: manifiesto central fail-closed con control plane, OPA/Rego, OpenBao, OpenTelemetry, durable workflow semantics, supply-chain y promotion gates.
- `agent-readiness.html` + `agent-readiness.js`: superficie pública estática de readiness.
- `scripts/validate-agent-manifest.mjs`: validación determinista de contrato y claims.
- `.github/workflows/agent-production-manifest.yml`: CI de readiness.

## P1 Commercial Runtime
- `commercial-runtime/src/worker.mjs`: `POST /api/v1/project-requests` con Turnstile server-side, rate limiting, 16 KiB request limit, exact-origin review, schema estricta, idempotency key, D1 batch y correlation/evidence IDs.
- `commercial-runtime/migrations/0001_init.sql`: `project_requests`, `evidence_events` y transactional dispatch outbox.
- `commercial-runtime/src/project-workflow.mjs`: Cloudflare Workflow durable que consulta Nexus mediante service binding y sólo puede promover hasta `POLICY_ALLOWED`; ausencia/fallo de Nexus cae a revisión humana.
- `security/api-security-manifest.json`: contrato para la nueva superficie dinámica.
- `commercial-runtime/test/*`: pruebas adversariales de injection, SSRF, replay/idempotency y access control.
- `.github/workflows/commercial-runtime.yml`: syntax, tests, migración D1, security manifest y bloqueo de claims de producción.
- `docs/P1-COMMERCIAL-RUNTIME-2026.md`: arquitectura, lifecycle, SLO draft y blockers.

## Arquitectura elegida
Frontend/configurador → Turnstile → Worker API → Rate Limiter → D1 transaction → Evidence Ledger + Outbox → Cloudflare Workflow → Nexus readiness/policy → OPA/Rego → Service Registry/Agent Adapter → quote/HITL → payment/reconciliation → provisioning → ACTIVE sólo con promotion gates.

Se usa transactional outbox para que una caída entre persistencia y orquestación no pierda pedidos ni fuerce side effects duplicados. Queues se reserva para fan-out/telemetry porque su entrega es at-least-once y requiere de-duplicación.

## Política de promoción
Este PR **no despliega** el Worker ni habilita pagos, publicación externa, trading live, gastos, credenciales o servicios de terceros. El endpoint público sólo crea `VALIDATED`; Nexus/readiness nunca puede autorizar por sí solo un efecto crítico. Credenciales/scopes, producción, contratos/compromisos pagados, publicación y capital siguen HITL.

## Evidencia investigada
La implementación sigue documentación actual de Cloudflare para Turnstile Siteverify, Workers Rate Limiting, D1 transactional batches, Workflows durable execution/HITL, Queues at-least-once e Workers observability/OTel; además conserva los patrones institucionales existentes de OPA/Rego, OpenBao y evidencia auditable.

## Gate
Merge sólo después de CI verde y revisión de claims/madurez. Los agentes con blockers permanecen Pilot/Research/Degraded. El despliegue real del P1 requiere provisioning de Cloudflare/D1/Turnstile/rate-limit/Workflow/Nexus binding y aprobación humana explícita.

author: shubhs-dev
body:
## What

Adds `-l, --list [FILE]` to `optimiselib`:

```bash
optimiselib /srv/library -l                 # print every video, alphabetically
optimiselib /srv/library -l library.txt     # write that list to library.txt instead
```

## Why

There was no way to get a plain "what's actually in the library" listing. `-r/--report` is
close but answers a different question — it reads the state log for sub-1080p files and the
review queue, not the library's real contents.

## How

- `list_library()` reuses the existing `all_videos()` walker, so the listing covers the
  **whole** library — root plus every trip folder, `_review/` excluded, dotfiles / `.tmp` /
  `.processing` / non-video files filtered out by `_is_video()`. That's deliberately a wider
  scope than the pipeline itself (root-only), because the question is "what's in here", not
  "what's pending".
- Filenames only, one per line, sorted case-insensitively (`key=str.lower`), followed by a
  count.
- With a `FILE` value the list is written there instead of printed; the path is taken relative
  to the cwd, an existing file prompts via `_common.confirm` (default N), and a write failure
  goes through `die()`.
- Dispatches alongside `--report` in `main()`, ahead of the `ffprobe` / `HandBrakeCLI`
  `require_tool` checks — listing needs neither binary.

## Notes for review

- **`markup=False` on the print path is load-bearing.** `console.print` would otherwise parse a
  `[1080p]` tag in a filename as rich markup. `highlight=False` and `soft_wrap=True` keep long
  names intact and unstyled.
- `dest="list_files"` because `args.list` would shadow the builtin name.
- Module docstring, README example block, README flag table and a new "Listing" paragraph all
  updated together — the docstring doubles as `--help` output.

## Verification

Manually exercised against a fixture library (no test framework in this repo): recursion into
trip folders, `_review/` exclusion, junk-file filtering, case-insensitive ordering, the empty
library, file output, and the overwrite prompt. All 18 commands still `--help` cleanly.

author: hitmaizer
body:
Resolve a #26 (SEO-16) da auditoria SEO de 2026-08-30.

## Problema

`app/sitemap.ts` carimbava `new Date()` nos 20 URLs, portanto cada deploy declarava que o site inteiro tinha acabado de mudar. O Google aprende a desvalorizar — e acaba por ignorar — um `lastmod` que não acompanha alterações reais.

## Mudança

Cada projeto passa a ter um `updatedAt`, semeado a partir do histórico do git: o último commit que tocou **no bloco daquele projeto**, não a data do ficheiro inteiro. As páginas traduzidas levam a mais recente entre a base e a tradução, porque a copy portuguesa se sobrepõe à inglesa. A homepage fica tão fresca como a case study mais recente que lista.

## Verificação

Sitemap de um build de produção: **8 valores distintos** em vez de 20 iguais.

```
15:12:54  /
14:29:14  /projects/endesa-portugal
15:12:54  /projects/padaria-alianca
14:47:48  /projects/munchie
15:04:42  /projects/feel-better
...
10:24:16  /en/projects/endesa-portugal
14:29:14  /en/projects/lr-opticas
```

As páginas EN aparecem mais antigas porque a revisão de copy portuguesa de hoje não lhes tocou — é precisamente o sinal que o `lastmod` deve dar.

`pnpm lint --max-warnings 0`, `pnpm check-types` e o build de produção verdes.

## Duas decisões que vale a pena registar

- **Não usei a data do último commit do ficheiro**, a outra hipótese da issue: os nove projetos vivem todos no mesmo `projects.ts`, portanto daria a mesma data a todos e não resolvia nada. Calcular git em build time também é frágil na Vercel, que faz clone raso.
- **O campo é manual**, com um comentário a pedir que seja bumpado quando a copy muda e não quando o ficheiro é tocado. Se ninguém o bumpar, envelhece — o que continua a ser preferível a declarar «mudou agora» em cada deploy.

## Ordem

Sem conflito com os PRs abertos: o #35 não toca no `sitemap.ts`, e os campos novos em `projects.ts` ficam em linhas diferentes das do #34.

Closes #26

author: arckomvandrike
culturereset
body:
Recreates the SpotOn point-of-sale merchant platform on two surfaces, built from the same brand tokens and the same seeded data layer.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Web dashboard** | repo root | Next.js 15 · 17 sections · responsive 390→1440px |
| **Android app** | `android/` | Kotlin · Jetpack Compose · Material 3 · 33 screens |

Both show the same restaurant, on the same day, with the same numbers, so they can be read side by side.

> The repository had no commits before this. `main` was created afterwards as a baseline (placeholder `.gitignore` + README) purely so this branch had something to merge into — hence the merge commit at the tip. You may want to make `main` the default branch in repo settings.

## Web dashboard

Sign-in is four steps (email → password → 2FA → location) with per-step validation, auto-advancing code inputs and paste support.

Seventeen sections, grouped the way the merchant dashboard groups them:

| Group | Sections |
|---|---|
| Overview | Dashboard, Sales, Reporting |
| Operations | Orders, Menus, Team & labor, Reservations |
| Guests | Customers, Loyalty, Campaigns, Reviews |
| Channels | Online ordering, Gift cards |
| Money | Statements |
| Setup | Devices, Dashboard users, Settings |

The shell adapts rather than reflows: desktop gets a collapsible grouped sidebar plus a top bar carrying ⌘K search, date range, location switcher, notifications and profile. Below 1024px that becomes a full-IA drawer, a thumb-reachable bottom tab bar, a More sheet, and a scrolling date-range chip row.

## Android app

Native, not a web port. `NavigationBar`, `TopAppBar`, `ModalBottomSheet`, `FilterChip` and `OutlinedTextField` are the real Material 3 components, with the SpotOn palette mapped onto the M3 `ColorScheme` plus a token set for the ink ramp, status pairs and chart series that M3 has no slot for. Poppins is bundled rather than falling back to Roboto.

- **Bottom-sheet controls** — location, date range and More are all reachable with one thumb.
- **Detail is a destination, not a dialog** — the system back gesture works.
- **Touch replaces hover explicitly** — tapping a line chart selects the nearest day and a readout names every series' value there; bars and heat-grid cells do the same.
- **Edge to edge** — the scaffold's top inset goes to the `NavHost`, the bottom inset to each list's `contentPadding`, so content scrolls under the nav bar rather than being clipped.

## Notes for review

**Brand tokens are sourced, not guessed.** Brand blue `#0759ef`, the ink scale, hairlines and Poppins were read off the live spoton.com stylesheet. Section names come from SpotOn's own knowledge base rather than being invented.

**One filter, one scope.** The date range scopes every card on every page on both surfaces — no per-card filters. Each range carries its immediately preceding window, so deltas are real comparisons; metrics where lower is better (labor %) invert the good/bad colouring.

**Charts are hand-built** — SVG on web, Compose `Canvas` on Android, no charting dependency on either. Same rules on both: one y-axis ever (labor cost and sales share a dollar axis, with the labor *rate* on its own chart rather than a second scale), solid hairline gridlines, rounded data ends, a legend for two or more series. The categorical palette is brand-anchored and validated for colour-vision deficiency (worst adjacent ΔE 9.1) and normal-vision separation (19.6); since three slots fall under 3:1 on white, every chart also ships direct labels and a data-table twin, so no value is reachable through colour or hover alone.

**Data is seeded.** `lib/data.ts` and its Kotlin port share a `mulberry32` seed and a fixed reference date, so server and client render identical markup and both surfaces agree.

## Verification

**Web** — `tsc --noEmit` clean under strict mode; all 19 routes build; rendered in Chromium at 390 / 768 / 1440px with no console errors and no horizontal overflow on any page or the login flow.

**Android** — debug and release APKs both build; **38 unit tests pass**, of which 35 are Roborazzi screenshot tests rendering every screen at 411×891dp to PNG on the JVM, and 3 are navigation tests that compose the real `NavHost`, walk sign-in through all four steps to the dashboard, and visit every bottom-nav tab.

Six bugs were caught by rendering rather than by the build passing, and are fixed here:

- Charts overflowed their cards on mobile web — an SVG `viewBox` gives the element an intrinsic width that fed back into the container being measured, and grid items default to `min-width: auto` so they could not shrink back.
- Card headers collided with their controls on narrow screens.
- The axis tick generator could emit a top tick **below** the data max, clipping the tallest mark. This existed on both surfaces and is fixed on both.
- A zero-based axis on the rating chart flattened a 4.0–4.5 range into a straight line.
- "Filled" stars rendered as outlines.
- The Android logo mark drew its ring gap in hardcoded white, collapsing into a solid blob on the dark sign-in panel.

## Not included

An interface recreation with a mock data layer — no backend, and no affiliation with SpotOn Transact, LLC.

body:
# Turn an entrapment sequence into a database entry

> **Stacks on #1254 → #1253 → #1250.** This branch carries their commits; its own is `44f9447e`.
> Merge those three and this diff reduces to the files below.

Completes the round trip. With this, an entrapment database can be written, reloaded, searched, and
every discovery paired back to the target peptide it was built from -- **with nothing carried
alongside the file**.

```
target protein -> entrapment protein -> WriteXmlDatabase -> LoadProteinXML
               -> Digest -> EntrapmentPairing.TryResolve -> the target peptide
```

## Three pieces

**`EntrapmentAccession`** -- what an entrapment protein is called, and how to read the target and
fold back out. It follows two conventions already in the codebase rather than inventing a third:

- the **marker goes first**, because `ProteinDbLoader` decides a protein is entrapment by looking
  for the identifier *anywhere* in its accession and prepends it when absent. An accession shaped
  this way reloads as entrapment with no extra argument and is never double-prefixed.
- the **fold goes last**, matching `VariantApplication.GetAccession`, which appends derived detail.

Parsing takes the fold from the **last** `_f<digits>` rather than splitting on underscores --
UniProt entry names always contain them, and a naive split loses the target. Tested with
`SP_HUMAN_P12345`.

**`EntrapmentProteinGenerator`** -- builds the protein. Two steps, both through existing
constructors and neither through reflection: `CloneWithNewSequenceAndMods` for the sequence and
modifications, then `Protein`'s copy constructor for the accession and the entrapment flag.

Modifications move along the position map to the residue they were on, so their motif still fits
without anything being re-checked. A modification whose residue was **excised is dropped, not
relocated** -- putting it elsewhere would invent a site the target never had.

**`EntrapmentPairing`** -- resolves a discovery back to its target peptide.

## Why no index file is needed

A rearrangement preserves the residue multiset and leaves every cleavage-site residue in place, so
those two things together are a key: the partner of an entrapment peptide is the target peptide of
the same protein with the same free-residue composition and the same pinned pattern. That is
**guaranteed by the construction** rather than recorded somewhere, so there is no side file to
write, ship, or keep in step with the database. A search reports a protein accession and a peptide
sequence, and that is enough.

It indexes **missed cleavages as well as base peptides**. A missed-cleavage peptide is a run of
adjacent base pieces and composition adds, so it pairs for the same reason. (This was found by a
failing test, not by design -- the first version indexed base pieces only, and any search reporting
a missed-cleavage peptide would have failed to pair.)

Keys can collide: `P57071` really does contain `LIHTGVK` and `LIHTVGK` -- same residues, same
pinned `K`, different order. Those are reported in `AmbiguousPeptides` and **refuse to resolve**,
because guessing between them would be wrong half the time and silently so. Measured across the
human reviewed proteome, this affects **274 of 1,315,124** base peptides (0.021%).

## One change to existing code, called out deliberately

`ProteinDbLoader` gains `public const string DefaultEntrapmentIdentifier = "Random"`, and the two
existing default parameters that spelled that literal out now reference it. **The value is
identical**, so this is a duplicated literal replaced by a name rather than a behaviour change --
but it does touch existing signatures, so it should be seen rather than found.

## Tests

Thirteen, in `Test/DatabaseTests/TestEntrapmentProtein.cs`, in three groups:

- **accession** -- marker first, target and fold round-trip, non-entrapment accessions refused,
  and a target accession containing underscores;
- **generation** -- isomeric with the target, modifications landing on the residue their motif
  requires, modifications on excised residues dropped, a distinct accession and sequence per fold;
- **pairing and round trip** -- resolution from composition alone, ambiguous keys refusing to
  guess, reload from XML recognised as entrapment by accession alone, and pairing surviving a full
  write/read/digest cycle.

870 passed / 0 failed across the database, decoy, entrapment and protein-DB suites.

## Notes for review

- `MzLibException` throughout, matching the neighbours.
- `#nullable enable`; zero warnings.
- Protein-specific. `IBioPolymer` exposes `CloneWithNewSequenceAndMods` but no way to set an
  accession, so RNA parity needs a separate look rather than a speculative generic signature here.

author: posidev-coding
body:
`rankings()` read `Ranking::max('created_at')` and warned past four days. It
was amber at six days for polls a completed `sync:rankings-current` had
confirmed the day before -- the command healthy, the assertion measuring the
wrong thing.

Swapping to `updated_at` does not fix it, which is the part worth being
careful about. `SyncRankings` reconciles with `updateOrCreate`, so Eloquent's
`save()` writes nothing at all when the model is not dirty -- the project's own
rule that keeps writes off a scale-to-zero database is exactly what stops any
row timestamp recording that a run happened. Between Tuesday and Sunday the
poll does not change; in the preseason one poll stands unchanged for weeks.
Neither column was ever going to answer this question.

So a completed rankings run that reconciled rows counts as evidence alongside
the rows themselves, and the check takes the later of the two. `records > 0`
is load-bearing there rather than defensive: the site host answers a
disallowed User-Agent with a 403, `EspnClient` returns null, and the sync
completes having written nothing -- a bare run row would dress that silence up
as freshness, which is the failure this class exists to catch.

The null path is kept and made stricter. A run refines the age of data we
hold; it cannot invent data we do not, so with no ranking rows the ledger is
not consulted at all and the check stays FAIL however recently the command ran.

Second defect, the cadence. The command runs Sunday and Tuesday at 19:00, so
five days is the widest gap two healthy runs can leave, against a four-day
warn -- amber every weekend of the season, on the weekend, which is when
someone is most likely to be reading the board. Six days gives that gap a day
of headroom and nine is two consecutive missed runs. The other option was a
mid-week run, rejected: polls drop Sunday and Tuesday, so a Thursday pass
spends six requests reconciling a poll that cannot have changed, which is the
waste the current-week tier was introduced to stop.

Five cases, each verified by breaking the fix back: restoring
`max('created_at')` turns three red, dropping the `records > 0` guard lets the
403 shape read as fresh, letting the ledger answer for an empty table turns
the no-rows case green, and restoring the 4/8 thresholds turns the
five-day-weekend case amber again.

The poll fixture builds its week on the pinned season rather than letting
RankingFactory reach Season::factory() through WeekFactory: that draw is a
twelve-year range against a (year, type) unique, and it collided with the
pinned 2026 season about one run in twelve -- green under --filter, red in the
suite, the exact shape the factory rule describes.

author: trognes-claude
body:
`-S m4a10` and `-S m4f10` **do not terminate** when built with g++ on arm64. The test suite hangs rather than failing — the failure mode the histogram path's own notes predict: *"a CI failure here can present as a timeout rather than a `FAIL` line."*

Found by the arm64 `build & test` job (#256). This fix is separate so it can be reviewed and merged on its own.

## The invariant that breaks

The low-order climb stages (`-S i/m/k`) score from a co-occurrence histogram instead of decoding, and the design rests on the two paths returning the **same double**. `hillclimb` takes `best_score` from `score_iter()` (the decoder) and compares it against move scores from `hist_probe()` (the histogram), looping while the score improves:

```c
do {
    best_score = score_iter(m);             // decoder
    ...
    score = hist_probe(m, pos, val, cnt);   // histogram
    if (score > move_score) { ... }
} while (best_score > last_best);
```

One ULP of disagreement is therefore not a rounding difference — a no-op move looks improving **forever**.

## Why a compiler can break it

The integers were never the problem. Both paths then assemble the mono score as `isum/scale + textlength*bias`, and a compiler is free to contract that multiply-add into an **FMA at one site and not the other**. On x86-64 without `-march` there is no FMA in the baseline ISA and it cannot happen. On **arm64 FMA is baseline and g++ contracts by default**.

## Evidence

Reproduced without arm64 hardware, via `aarch64-linux-gnu-g++` + `qemu-aarch64`:

| build | `-c --score m4a10 --random 2 -R 4 --polish` |
|---|---|
| x86-64 g++ | 0.11 s, exit 0 |
| aarch64 g++, default | **hangs — killed at 120 s** |
| aarch64 g++, `-ffp-contract=off` | 1.2 s, exit 0 |

`ENIGMA_HIST` discriminates it exactly:

| | result |
|---|---|
| `0` (decoder path) | exit 0 |
| `1` (histogram path) | **hangs** |
| `2` (histogram + integer self-check) | hangs, **self-check silent** |

The counts were right all along — only the float assembly diverged. That is also why the existing self-check could not catch it: it verifies integers.

## Scope

IC-only stages are **safe by construction** — one division, nothing to contract. The exposure is exactly the mono and mono+IC models:

| schedule | aarch64 g++ default |
|---|---|
| `m4a10`, `m4f10` | **hang** |
| `k4f10`, `i4f10`, `i3q`, `iq`, `mq`, `kq` | ok on this fixture |

**`k4f10` — the recommended pre-pass — is in the at-risk class.** It did not trip on this input, but it is mono+IC and assembles the score through the same expression.

## The fix costs nothing where it is not needed

Settled by comparison rather than by a bench: the **x86-64 binary is byte-identical with and without the flag**, and contains **zero FMA instructions**. There is no throughput question to measure.

## Why nothing caught it

`Bench` has used the arm64 runners from the start, but it measures **time, not answers** — and not one of its five tiers uses a low-order climb stage: `search`, `icscan` and `crib` run without `-c`, `hillclimb` is `-q`, `fused` is `-f`. **The histogram path had never executed on arm64 at all** until a `build & test` job was added there.

## The general rule, added to CLAUDE.md

Any invariant of the form *"these two code paths produce the same double"* is **not** established by reading the two expressions — it also needs the compiler forbidden from contracting one of them.

## Changes

- `Makefile` — `-ffp-contract=off` in `CXXFLAGS`, with the reasoning inline so it is not later removed as noise.
- `CLAUDE.md` — the note beside the byte-identity claim it protects, plus why the coverage gap existed.

author: levonmendall
body:
## Production evidence
Exact production release `f0a7d4b22f18b5a64c16a46a8aa93bcfa3a935b1` completed the all-market analytical and operational path through `paper_implementation_boundary`, then the exact-release verifier failed closed on one predicate only: `all_market_certification_aggregate_sha256`.

## Confirmed defect
The certification-v2 lane projection already verifies that the immutable input payload hashes exactly to `certification_id`, but then publishes `all_market_certification_aggregate_sha256` as `None`. This makes the public proof incomplete despite the integrity-bound digest already being established.

## Repair
Project the already-verified content-addressed `certification_id` as the v2 aggregate SHA-256. The unavailable/fail-closed path still publishes no digest.

## Regression coverage
- successful v2 lane proof must publish an aggregate digest equal to the verified immutable certification input id;
- unavailable v2 lane proof must not invent an aggregate digest.

No strategy, threshold, market scope, history horizon, freshness rule, memory ceiling, CIO authority, construction rule, execution authority, or paper-only restriction changes.

author: a1994sc
body:
## Description

End-to-end coverage for every cargoship command that does not need a cluster: the misc group (`version`, `sha256sum`, `vault-encrypt`) and the package group (`create`, `publish`, `pull`, `sign`). Each test drives the built binary as a subprocess, the same way a user would.

This is the first half of the e2e work. The install group needs Docker, a nine-container bootloose cluster and a ~1.5 GB distro package, so it lives in a follow-up PR and is deliberately absent here. The suites are split by Go package rather than by test-name filters, so this one cannot accidentally pull in the cluster machinery:

```
src/test/e2e/noncluster/   misc + package groups, no Docker, no network
src/test/e2e/cluster/      install group (follow-up PR)
```

The whole suite in this PR runs in about six seconds and starts no containers, which is what makes it usable as a pull request gate.

### Coverage

| Command | Cases |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | plain output, `v` alias, `-o json` and `--output yaml` parsed and asserted (build version/commit/platform/go plus a non-empty dependency map), unsupported format errors |
| `sha256sum` | local file, `sum` alias, `http(s)` source via `httptest`, `--extract-path` and its `-e` shorthand, missing archive member, missing file, no args |
| `vault-encrypt` | argument and stdin input, `CARGOSHIP_VAULT_PASSWORD`, `ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD`, no password available, empty stdin, unreadable password file, missing required flag, too many args |
| `create` | package naming and metadata, `-o`, `--reproducible` producing byte-identical archives across runs, `--signing-key` producing `distro.bundle.sig` and `build.signed: true`, three `--registry-override` parse failures, nonexistent directory, too many args, and the real `example/rke2-cilium` build gated behind `-short` |
| `publish` | round trip against an in-process registry, destination missing the `oci://` prefix, missing source, argument count |
| `pull` | round trip byte-identical to the published package, `--shasum` matching and mismatching the manifest digest, unknown tag, `http(s)` source with matching, mismatching and absent shasum, argument count |
| `sign` | sign to `-o`, default in-place output, re-sign refused without `--overwrite`, `--verify=always` passing with the matching key and failing with an unrelated one, wrong key password, neither `--signing-key` nor `--keyless`, the two being mutually exclusive, missing source, argument count, and signing straight to an `oci://` destination followed by a verifying pull |

Verification is exercised in both directions: a package signed with one key verifies, and the same package fails against a second, unrelated key.

### Fixtures

Three choices keep the suite fast and hermetic:

- **`src/test/e2e/noncluster/testdata/minimal`** is a valid distro definition with no images and no files. `assemble.AssembleDistro` only reaches out to a registry when `config.imageConfig.images` or `config.files` are populated, so this builds in milliseconds into a 386-byte package. Every package-group test uses it; only `TestCargoshipCreateExample` builds a real example, and it is skipped under `-short`.
- **Signing keys are generated per test** with `cosign.GenerateKeyPair`, so no key material is committed and two calls naturally yield unrelated keys for the negative cases.
- **`test.SetupInMemoryRegistry`** starts an OCI registry in-process on a random localhost port, so publish and pull need no registry container and no network. `docs/agent/choice-in-memory-oci-registry.md` records why `google/go-containerregistry` was chosen over `distribution/distribution` for this. The registry logs one line per request, which buries the output of the test being run, so it writes to a file under the user cache directory instead (`~/.cache/cargoship/e2e-logs/registry-<timestamp>.log`, named the way the CLI names its own log files). The file is removed when the test passes and kept, with its path reported, when it fails; `CARGOSHIP_E2E_KEEP_REGISTRY_LOG=1` keeps it either way.

### Tooling

- `.github/workflows/e2e.yaml` gains an `e2e-noncluster` job that reuses the binary built by `build-e2e`, stages it where the suite expects it, and runs `go test -short ./src/test/e2e/noncluster/...`.
- `mage test:endToEndNonCluster` mirrors that job locally; `mage test:endToEnd` runs everything including the example packages. The mage test targets are split one per file with the shared helper in `magefiles/test-common.go`.
- `daggerBuildLocal` now picks `--progress=plain` when stdout is not a terminal, since the tty renderer errors out in CI.
- `docs/dev/e2e-tests.md` documents how to run the suite directly with `go test`, without the mage wrappers: building the binary the tests exec, running a single test or subtest, the environment variables, where the artifacts and logs land, and how to reproduce a failing case by hand. Linked from `docs/SUMMARY.md`.
- `src/pkg/utils/files.go` exports `TmpPathPrefix` (previously unexported) so the test harness can create temp directories with the same prefix the binary uses.

### Dependencies

`go mod tidy` promotes two modules from indirect to direct: `github.com/sigstore/cosign/v3` (key generation) and `github.com/google/go-containerregistry` (in-memory registry). Both were already in the module graph, so this adds nine vendored files and no new transitive dependencies. `go.sum` is unchanged.

### Findings, not fixed here

Writing these tests turned up four things worth a separate look. The tests pin current behavior rather than changing it:

- `publish` registers `--verify` and `-k` through `addVerifyFlags`, but its `distro.Load` call never sets `VerificationStrategy` or builds verify options, so both flags are silently ignored. Verification only actually happens on `pull` and `sign`.
- `create --skip-sbom` is a no-op: `distro.Create` hardcodes `SkipSBOM: true` and ignores the option.
- `--verify` is declared with a `NoOptDefVal`, so `--verify always` parses `always` as a positional argument and fails with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 2`. Only the attached form `--verify=always` works, which is worth checking against the docs and examples.
- `vault-encrypt` marks `--vault-password-file` as required, so the `CARGOSHIP_VAULT_PASSWORD` and `ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD` fallbacks are only reachable by passing the flag with an empty value.

Also worth noting: `install engine-config-sync` has no e2e coverage in either half, so it should not be assumed covered once the cluster PR lands.

### Unrelated one-line fix

`defaultLogFilePath` in `src/cmd/root.go` described its log file as "named to the second", but `config.TimeFormat` ends in fractional seconds, so the name is to the hundredth. Comment only, no behavior change.

### Verification

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./src/...` and `golangci-lint run ./src/...` are clean, and `go test -short ./src/test/e2e/noncluster/...` passes with all eleven suites green in about six seconds with Docker stopped.

## Related Issue

Relates to #18

## Checklist before merging

- [x] Test, docs, adr added or updated as needed

one of four ways to run a notebook and links to it, rather than carrying
a second description that drifts from the one the Marketplace shows.

section here.

Three fixes in the source, because splitting is what made them visible:

Connections had no section. Its two headings sat under Projects, which
is not where anyone would look for them.

Retention is about run history and the artifacts beside it, not about
projects — it was a ### under Projects by accident of layout.

author: johnhboyer-sys
body:
Follow-up to #33, and a **separate defect** from the label/form pairing that PR fixed. Found by the Grok review of homer-reader's equivalent PR; homer split it the same way (#23 → #24).

## The defect

`buildFormsBlock`'s `formAt` opens the forms table at the first `lsj-greek` span that has an `lsj-bibl` behind it in the same colon-segment. A headword's **quantity mark** is an `lsj-greek` span, and the entry's own citations follow it — so it qualified, and the table opened on the lemma:

| entry | label | body |
|---|---|---|
| ἀγλαός | `ἀγλαός [` | `ᾱγλᾰ-], ή, όν, also ός, όν Thgn. 985` |
| ἀπατάω | `ἀπατάω` | `[ᾰπ], late Ion. ἀπατ-έω Luc. Syr.D. 27` |

ἀπατάω's table should open at `impf. ἠπάτων`; ἀγλαός has no inflected form at all and should get no block.

The second harm is worse than misplacement. Label text runs through `plainLabel`, which strips `:;—` off both ends — so every entry whose head got pulled into a label **lost its sense separator**. The defect deleted source punctuation rather than merely moving it, which is why the fix *restores* characters (see the audit).

## The rule

A quantity mark is known by its brackets, in the two shapes LSJ writes them: inside the span (`[ᾰπ`), or wrapped around it (`[` + `ᾱγλᾰ-` + `]`). `formAt` now walks past those spans instead of stopping at the first one.

Two constraints that are load-bearing, both verified against Plato's data:

- **Square brackets only.** A parenthesis in the identical position opens an *etymology*. Accepting `(` would eat the opening bracket of `Ἀδράστεια, ἡ, (ἀ- priv., διδράσκω)` and of ἀδελφός. Both are confirmed present in Plato's shards and both are left untouched by this change.
- **No length test.** The senses-block skip nearby uses `length <= 4`; it does not generalise. ὕβρις marks quantity in forty characters — `[ῠ by nature, ῡ by position in Ep. etc.]` — and ἦν is a genuine form in two.

Ported from homer-reader `claude/lsj-quantity-mark` (`396e159f0`). Plato's `html.ts` was byte-identical to homer's at `main`, the patch applied clean, and `formAt`/`quantityMark` diff empty against the reference.

## Verification

**Tests** — `shared/` 361 passed (up from 357, the 4 new cases), exit 0; `app/` 2 passed, exit 0.

**Audit over this repo's own 12,097 entries**, baseline (post-#33 `main`) vs fixed:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| entries changed | 61 |
| unbalanced tags | **0** |
| senses lost | **0** |
| characters **lost** | **0** |
| characters gained | `:`×33, `—`×14, `;`×9 |
| per-entry shape | `:`×19, `:—`×14, `;`×9 — **42 entries** |
| **characters invented** | **0** |

Two things about the audit shape, both of which caught real over-reach upstream:

- It compares **non-whitespace** characters. A flat tag-strip lies here: when the cut moves later, a trailing space is legitimately absorbed at the label/body boundary, which reads as entries losing a character and is not.
- Every gained character is a separator being **restored**, not invented — confirmed corpus-wide by checking that each entry's output characters are a sub-multiset of its *source* characters. 0 exceptions.

The `:—` restorations are the same separator as the earlier homonym-separator work on this repo, which is consistent: this defect was one of the things deleting it.

## Known limits, deliberately not chased

Of **1,970** entries with a forms block, exactly **one** quantity mark still opens a table: **κάτειμι**, where `[κάτε]ιτι` is an epigraphic restoration *inside a real form*. It is correct as it stands, and extending the rule to `lsj-cit` spans would break it. Homer's one real miss (Ἴτων) is not in Plato's shards, so Plato has **no** real misses.

Separately, **921** entries still open their first label with the headword (`ἀγωνίζομαι, fut.`). That is the lead-cut threshold, not `formAt`, and is left alone. **τίθημι is in this family** — its mark is tagged `lsj-pron`, which `formAt` never inspects — so it looks like the same bug and isn't. This is the τίθημι oddity I flagged in #33; it now has an explanation and a separate cause.

λέγω, τίθημι and κάτειμι are all confirmed byte-unchanged by this fix, so #33's work is preserved intact.

Renderer-only — no pipeline stage, no data rebuild. **Not deployed.**

author: rubanikov
body:
Closes #19 (TICK-011).

## What

- `src/frontdoor/split_seed.json` — the committed seed, in its own file, committed at `bab15548d9439ea3ff6aa0579cb4a35ceb5f199d` on 2026-08-30, before the first capture.
- `src/frontdoor/split.py` — `assign_split(entrance_id)`: `sha256(entrance_id + seed)`, first 8 bytes as a big-endian unsigned integer mod 100; below 30 `sealed`, below 50 `calib`, otherwise `dev`. Pure function of ID and seed: no clock, no random source, no ordering dependence, and no reassign/rebalance/override path exists. Also runnable as a tool: `python -m frontdoor.split E-001 E-002` (or IDs on stdin) prints `entrance_id,split` lines.
- `CHANGES.log` — dated entry recording the seed commit SHA, the algorithm, and the proportions, as the ticket requires. Logged in a second commit because the SHA only exists after the first.
- `tests/test_split.py` — determinism, order independence over a shuffled list, distribution over 1000 synthetic IDs, changed seed changes assignments, pinned known answers for the committed seed (so any later change to seed or algorithm fails loudly), and the CLI.
- The same packaging files as #97 (`pyproject.toml`, `src/frontdoor/__init__.py`, `.gitignore` Python entries), byte-identical, so this PR merges cleanly whether or not #97 lands first.

## Decisions worth review

- **Proportions: 30% sealed / 20% calib / 50% dev.** The PRD fixes only ~30% sealed (D-007); the ticket says calib and dev make up the rest without a ratio. 20% calib is sized so that split conformal prediction (D-011, unconfirmed, O-4) has a held-out set distinct from sealed without carving one out after capture. If D-011 is dropped, calib folds into dev at analysis time. **These constants must be settled before the first photo** — changing them afterwards would reassign entrances, which is exactly what this ticket forbids. If you want a different calib share, say so before capture starts and I will amend the seed commit entry.
- **Bucket = first 8 bytes mod 100** rather than a fraction of the full 256-bit digest, so the capture app (TICK-025, Swift) can reproduce it with a `UInt64` and no big-integer arithmetic. The modulo bias is on the order of 1e-18 and irrelevant.
- **Seed lives inside the package** (`src/frontdoor/split_seed.json`) rather than under `data/`, so the tool loads it via `importlib.resources` and works from any install, not only a repo checkout. The manifest tool (TICK-013) and the app both read the same file.
- Please **merge, not squash**: the SHA recorded in CHANGES.log is the branch commit, and a merge commit keeps it reachable from `main` (as with PRs #1–#3).

## Verification

`python -m pytest tests/test_split.py` — 7 passed. Over 1000 synthetic IDs the committed seed yields 30.3% sealed / 18.4% calib / 51.3% dev. Known answers with the committed seed: `E-001 → dev`, `E-002 → sealed`, `E-014 → sealed`, `E-042 → calib`.

Out of scope, per the ticket: refusing to load sealed rows (TICK-070), the D-011 decision (TICK-050), and per-capture splits (splits attach to the entrance).

author: hopetambala
body:
## Goals

Gives Manage's OrganizationAdmin screen the one fact it cannot work out for itself: what the viewer may administer.

## Related context

- Spec: `docs/self-service-organizations.md` §2 — staff see every organization, an org admin sees only their own
- Uses `isStaff` and `isOrgAdmin` from [#625](https://github.com/hopetambala/puente-node-cloudcode/pull/625)

## Updates made

**`cloud/src/definer/organization.definer.js`** — `myOrganizationAccess`, returning `{ isStaff, orgAdminOf }`.

**`_tests_/integration/organization.test.js`** — 2 tests.

## Notes for reviewers

**Why this can't be derived client-side.** Org admin roles are created with **no public read**, so a browser querying `_Role` gets nothing back and every admin would render as non-admin. Same reason `isStaff` is a cloud function rather than a client query.

**Staff aren't enumerated across every organization.** The client is told `isStaff` and treats that as "all". Returning an explicit list would go stale the moment an organization is added.

**It is not the security boundary, and says so.** Every privileged endpoint checks for itself; this only decides what to *draw*. It **fails closed** — an unauthenticated caller gets an empty list rather than an error, because a guard that throws blanks the page while one that assumes access renders a surface whose every action then fails.

**The loop is sequential and deliberate**, matching the seed plan: dozens of organizations, and a burst of parallel role reads against Back4App buys nothing but throttling risk.

## Testing

- [x] Both behaviours seen failing first (`Invalid function`)
- [x] Reports the organizations a real signed-in org admin administers, via a session token
- [x] Returns `{ isStaff: false, orgAdminOf: [] }` for an unauthenticated caller
- [x] `npm run lint` clean; full suite was 153 passing locally before push — CI is the gate below

## Cross-repo impact

One new read-only cloud function; nothing existing changes shape. **Merging auto-deploys to production Back4App.**

## AI usage

Written by Claude (Opus 4.8) under red-green-tdd.

body:
Commits the parallel review session's notifications rework (signed in-file: Kev + claude-opus-5, 2026-08-30) — it was stranded uncommitted when that session's git process crashed mid-commit.

## What it fixes
- **Stacking banners:** `UUID().uuidString` made every post a NEW notification — six pulses a day stacked six banners, and a re-fired "ready" showed up twice (observed live). Stable per-kind identifiers mean a re-post **replaces** its predecessor: Notification Centre holds the *current* pulse, not a transcript of them.
- **Scattered pings:** `threadIdentifier` per kind groups each kind under one stack.
- **The chiming heartbeat:** demoted to `sound = nil` + `.passive` + relevance 0.2 — an ambient 2-hourly chime is a notification you switch off, not one you read. Everything else answers something you started, so it keeps its chime and `.active` level.
- **Wasted titles:** macOS already prints "M1K3" in the banner header, so "M1K3 is ready" said the app name twice and the news never. Titles now lead with the news ("Lil is ready", "Heartbeat") — say a promise once, doctrine principle 5.

App-target only (no package-test surface); the banner's live look, replace-in-place behaviour, and passive level are **verify-by-launch** — ⌘R with both toggles on. App target compiled locally.

author: brendanpotter00
body:
> "can you build it left to right rather than right to left? It makes more sense for the newest week to be to the right and August 17 to be at the far left, because that aligns with the grid."

The order was already oldest-left. What was wrong was the **anchor**: #42 laid out sixteen slots however few were filled, and the empty ones came first — so two weeks of history put both bars hard against the right edge of a card whose heatmap starts at the left. At the 880px window minimum they were at opposite ends of the same box.

## Before / after, at 880px with the owner's two weeks

| | |
|---|---|
| **before** | heatmap: two columns at the far left · strip: two bars at the far right, ~700px away |
| **after** | heatmap: two columns at the far left · strip: two bars under them |

## Why the pitch is still a constant

The obvious version of this fix is to drop the empty slots and divide the width by what is left. At two weeks that is a **369px pitch** — two slabs a third of a card apart, re-spacing themselves every time a week rolls over. That is why the first version anchored right.

So only the slot **count** moves. The pitch stays `HEATMAP_GRID_W / MAX_WEEKS` = **46.19px**, and the plot grows rightward as history accumulates — which is what the heatmap above it already does, since `heatmap()` returns only the days a row exists for.

| weeks of history | slots drawn | pitch | first bar at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2 | 46.19px | x = 23.1 |
| 16 | 16 | 46.19px | x = 23.1 |
| 20 | 16 (newest) | 46.19px | x = 23.1 |

Measured off the real screenshots at 2x: the first bar occupies device px **192–235 in both the two-week and the sixteen-week build**, and neighbouring bars are 93 device px apart.

## And the 33px the strip was out by all along

`<ActivityCalendar>` renders its "Mon / Wed / Fri" labels to the *left* of its SVG and pushes everything it draws right by `ceil(widest label) + 8` — **33px on this Mac**, and not a number anybody can hard-code, because the library measures it from the real font at runtime. A sibling starting at 0 was therefore 33px left of the grid's first column. #42 noted it; it was invisible while the bars sat at the far right, and it is the first thing you see once they start at the left.

`src/renderer/lib/heatmap-gutter.ts` re-derives the same arithmetic — same strings, same font size, `getBBox` then `ceil` then `+ LABEL_MARGIN` — in an element **of our own**, rather than `querySelector`-ing into a third party's subtree to read the margin it computed. A transcription rots, so the test mounts the real calendar and asserts our `margin-left` **equals the one the calendar actually applied**: if the library changes its gutter, that fails loudly instead of drifting back to being 33px out.

Measured after: the strip's baseline rule starts at device px 168 and the grid's first column at 170 — within a pixel, at 2x.

## Unchanged, deliberately

- `null` (untracked) is still **absent from the DOM**; `0` (tracked, no work) is still a drawn 2px bar.
- The heading still counts what is **drawn** — two weeks reads "last 2 weeks", never "last 16 weeks".
- The greys are still the heatmap's ramp, stops 1/2/3, never stop 0.

author: pedro-cmyks
body:
A clean VPS could not finish the install. Setup reported **"The service returned an invalid response"** on every attempt and never left step 1, while the service sat there `Running` and logged one useless line a second.

Three defects. The third is why the first two shipped.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Impersonated before reading** | `ControlPipeServer` called `RunAsClient` the instant the pipe connected. Windows does not publish the caller's token until the client has written at least once. The call threw, the supervisor tore the connection down, Setup saw a severed pipe. Now the request frame is read first. |
| **A failed impersonation killed the call** | The exception escaped `IsAdministrator`. It is caught now and the caller is treated as unprivileged: `status` still answers, and anything privileged returns `administrator_required` instead of a dead socket. |
| **Setup forbade impersonation** | `ControlPipeClient` used the overload that leaves `TokenImpersonationLevel` at `None`, so `pair` would have been refused no matter who ran Setup. It asks for `Impersonation` explicitly now. |
| **The supervisor erased the evidence** | `catch { }` with no variable. Type, message and stack discarded, which is why this could only be guessed at. `LoopFailed` now carries the exception; the reporter logs its type and message, never the stack trace. |

## Tests

`ControlPipeTransportTests` tests the transport rather than the handler, which is exactly where the bug lived while every handler test passed. `EventLogReporterTests` pins how much of a failure may reach the log.

186 pass. **The two transport tests have not executed anywhere yet** — they were written on macOS and need a Windows runner, so CI is the first thing that will run them.

## Not in this PR

The NinjaTrader AddOn is still absent from the published package: the `ninjatrader-addon` job needs a self-hosted runner with NinjaTrader 8 and is gated off. A VPS can now install, pair and connect, but capture stays dark until the AddOn ships separately.

author: blackilli
body:
Beat has been scheduling tasks correctly and Docker has been reporting the container unhealthy the whole time.

## Why

The check looked for the literal string `celery beat`:

```yaml
test: [CMD-SHELL, ps aux | grep 'celery beat' | grep -v grep]
```

but the process is `celery -A otterball_v2 beat`:

```
appuser   1  uv run celery -A otterball_v2 beat --loglevel=info
appuser  21  /app/.venv/bin/python /app/.venv/bin/celery -A otterball_v2 beat --loglevel=info
```

celery only renames its process to "celery beat" when `setproctitle` is installed, and it isn't. So the grep matched nothing and exited 1 on every interval. This was invisible until recently because before `procps` was added the check exited 127 and looked broken for an entirely different reason.

## The bracket trick is load-bearing

The check runs as `sh -c "<test>"`, so the shell's own command line contains the pattern. A `pgrep -f 'celery -A otterball_v2 beat'` version therefore matches **itself** — verified by running exactly that inside the `web` container, which has no beat process at all:

```
pgrep -f 'celery -A otterball_v2 beat'          → exit 0   ← false positive
ps aux | grep -q '[c]elery -A otterball_v2 beat' → exit 1   ← correct
```

`[c]elery` cannot match its own shell, because the shell's command line contains `[c]elery`, not `celery`.

## Verified

With the fix, `beat` reaches `healthy` on its first probe (`health log: [exit 0]`), and the same pattern still exits 1 in a container where beat is not running.

author: companion
body:
## Problem

Lune's implementation of `Color3:ToHex()` differs from Roblox in two ways:

* Colour channels are truncated instead of rounded to the nearest integer
* Hexadecimal characters are uppercase instead of lowercase

For example:

```luau
Color3.new(0.9999, 0, 0):ToHex()  -- Lune: FE0000, Roblox: ff0000
Color3.new(0.5, 0.5, 0.5):ToHex() -- Lune: 7F7F7F, Roblox: 808080
Color3.new(1, 1, 1):ToHex()       -- Lune: FFFFFF, Roblox: ffffff
```

## Change

Round each colour channel to the nearest integer after clamping and emit lowercase hexadecimal output.

Clamping behaviour is unchanged, and `Color3.fromHex` continues to accept the resulting values for round-tripping.

Fixes #407.

## Testing

Added a dedicated `Color3ToHex.luau` regression test covering:

* Zero and maximum channel values
* Values requiring rounding
* Independent colour channels
* Lowercase hexadecimal characters
* Out-of-range clamping
* `fromHex(ToHex())` round-tripping
* Mixed-case `fromHex` input

Existing `Color3.luau` expectations were updated for lowercase output without removing any existing coverage.

The casing and rounding tests were verified to fail independently when their respective changes were temporarily reverted.

Formatting, Clippy and the workspace build pass. On Windows, the complete test suite increased from 169 to 170 passing tests, with the same unrelated `process_exec_shell` failure before and after.

author: iderex
body:
Closes #61.

The page for #61 landed on `899d83d` with two of its three conditions met. The
first waited on the self read it draws from, which was cut out as #274 and is on
`master`. This is the piece that was left over once that read existed: the page
and the endpoint agreeing, held by something rather than by nobody.

## The means

A C# case in `Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests`, beside `YourYearPageTests.cs` and
`UsageOverTimePageTests.cs`, which are the same shape for the other two pages.
The comparison has to read a JavaScript module and drive a C# endpoint in one
place, and only the C# suite can do the second half; a node case could read the
module and would have nothing to compare it against. No language, runtime or
dependency arrives.

## What was missing, measured at `faf6a65`

The module declares three addresses and reads a fixed set of names off the
figures answer:

    git show origin/master:Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats/Pages/yourStatisticsPage.js | sed -n '54,58p'
    export const SELF_PATHS = {
        statistics: 'Stats/Users/{userId}/Statistics/{window}',
        consent: 'Stats/Users/{userId}/Consent',
        plays: 'Stats/Users/{userId}/Plays',
    };

Nothing compared either against the C# side. The other two pages had that
comparison and this one did not:

    git grep -l 'Pages/.*Page.js' origin/master -- 'Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests/*.cs'
    origin/master:Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests/UsageOverTimePageTests.cs
    origin/master:Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests/YourYearPageTests.cs

The failure that leaves is silent from both sides. The node suite drives the
module over fixtures written by hand, so it agrees with itself whatever the
server sends; the endpoint suite reads the record, so it agrees with itself
whatever the page reads. A name renamed on either side keeps every suite in this
tree green and reaches a browser as a page that refuses every answer and draws
the window as one that could not be read.

## What the case holds

- The figures address, joined from the controller's `[Route]` and the action's
  `[HttpGet("{window}")]` the way the framework joins them, because the window
  is a segment rather than a query and a page holding only the controller's half
  would ask for the collection.
- The consent address and the deletion address, against their controllers' own
  route attributes.
- The page being one the server is told about, by name and by embedded resource
  path.
- Every field the drawing reads, looked for on a real answer. The names are
  taken out of the body of `forDrawing` rather than typed into the case, bounded
  to that one function because the module holds a second reader for the consent
  answer and folding the two together would ask this endpoint for fields it never
  carries. The answer is fetched through the framework the server runs on, over a
  store on disk holding a stretch of May that the endpoint's fixed clock of the
  first of June leaves inside the last thirty days, so the casing, the naming
  policy and the serializer are the ones a browser meets. The series and the top
  list are read one element deep, which is why the window has plays in it rather
  than being empty.

## Three guards broken to watch them bite, each restored afterwards

A name renamed on the record, `[JsonPropertyName("playsTotal")]` on
`OwnFigures.Plays`:

    dotnet test Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests/Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~YourStatisticsPageTests"
    Fehler Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests.YourStatisticsPageTests.EveryFieldTheDrawingReadsIsOnTheAnswerTheEndpointSends
    The drawing reads `plays` off a figures answer and the endpoint sent none.
    Fehler: 1, erfolgreich: 4, gesamt: 5

A name renamed inside the series, `[property: JsonPropertyName("name")]` on
`UsagePoint.Label`, which is the nested arm rather than the top-level one:

    Fehler Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests.YourStatisticsPageTests.EveryFieldTheDrawingReadsIsOnTheAnswerTheEndpointSends
    The drawing reads `label` off a point of the series and the endpoint sent none.
    Fehler: 1, erfolgreich: 4, gesamt: 5

The declared address moved, `Statistics` to `Figures` in `SELF_PATHS`:

    Fehler Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests.YourStatisticsPageTests.ThePageAsksTheAddressTheFiguresAreServedAt
    Assert.Equal() Failure: Strings differ
    Fehler: 1, erfolgreich: 4, gesamt: 5

## The suites, whole

    dotnet test Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests/Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests.csproj
    Bestanden! : Fehler: 0, erfolgreich: 1024, gesamt: 1024 (net10.0)
    Bestanden! : Fehler: 0, erfolgreich: 1023, gesamt: 1023 (net9.0)

    node --test "Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests/Pages/*.test.js"
    ℹ pass 201
    ℹ fail 0

    bash tools/invariants/lint.sh
    21 rule(s) checked over the tree, no match.

The counts differ between the two frameworks by one for a reason that predates
this change and is not touched by it; five of each are this file.

## Why this closes #61 and what it does not claim

> Opened by a user, the page shows that user's data and no aggregate that would
> let them derive somebody else's.

The second half was proven when the page landed, by the closed set of addresses
the module may reach. The first half waited on the read existing, and the reading
on the issue of 2026-08-29 says so in as many words. It exists, at
`Stats/Users/{userId}/Statistics/{window}`, and this case is what says the page
and that endpoint are talking about the same thing: the address resolves and
every field the drawing reads is on the answer.

**Nothing here opens a browser, and that is a refusal rather than an omission.**
`docs/what-no-test-may-need` in `docs/headless-tests.md` refuses a browser driven
by a test by name, and names the replacement: the page's data shaping in a plain
module tested directly, the endpoints tested in process, and a short manual
reading in the release checklist recorded as a reading and never described as a
test. So "opened by a user" in the literal sense is a reading this board does not
take in a suite, and what is proven is everything up to the browser. That limit
is this board's policy rather than this change's shortfall, and the condition is
met to the edge of it.

The other two conditions are where the reading of 2026-08-29 left them and are
not re-argued here.

## The scope line

`Scope:` on #61 names `Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats/Pages/`, `Plugin.cs`, the project
file and `Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests/Pages/`. This file is
`Jellyfin.Plugin.Stats.Tests/YourStatisticsPageTests.cs`, one directory up,
because that is where the two cases it is modelled on live and a case that has to
reference `Plugin` and drive the endpoint belongs with them rather than beside
the JavaScript. The declaration is widened on the issue in the same pass, which
is what it did once before rather than leaving a line no landing could match.

## Second reader

There is no second reader on this board tonight. The three broken guards above
stand in place of one: each was run, each named the property it was meant to
name, and each was restored before the commit.

author: alistairjcbrown
body:
## Summary

Fix flaky smoke test assertions for page titles by normalizing whitespace before comparison. The `document.title` getter automatically collapses internal whitespace runs and trims edges, but expected titles scraped from the DOM with `textContent` preserve the original whitespace. This caused false failures when film titles contained multiple consecutive spaces.

## Changes

- Added `normalizeWhitespace()` utility function that collapses internal whitespace runs to single spaces and trims edges, matching the behavior of `document.title`
- Updated `expectIndexableMetadata()` to normalize both the actual and expected title before the substring assertion
- Added detailed comment explaining the whitespace normalization issue and its precedent in Playwright's own `toContainText` method

## Implementation Details

The normalization uses a simple regex (`/\s+/g`) to replace any sequence of whitespace characters with a single space, then trims the result. This aligns with how browsers handle the `document.title` property and ensures consistent comparisons regardless of how whitespace is formatted in the source data.

The fix is scoped to the title substring check only; the "Clusterflick" brand name assertion remains unchanged as it's less likely to have internal whitespace variations.

author: chenmingwei23
body:
## What is the problem?

Dev Fleet's Pull + Build runs a full `npm ci` into a scratch directory on **every** sync, including ones that change no frontend file at all.

That install is the dependency preflight, and it earns its cost when the lockfile is new: `npm ci` deletes `website/node_modules` before it installs, so a registry that refuses one package used to leave the checkout with new source, a new lockfile and no frontend dependencies. The probe answers "can the incoming lockfile be installed?" between `fetch` and `merge`, where a refusal still costs nothing. It performs a real script-free install rather than `npm ci --dry-run` for a measured reason documented in the module: a dry run does not attempt retrieval, so against a lockfile pinning a tarball that 404s it exits 0 and reports "added 1 package" -- it would pass exactly the case the probe exists to catch.

The gap is that nothing asks whether the question is open. In `_sync_start_locked` the probe is gated on one condition:

```python
frontend_half = not frontend.edition_configured()
...
if frontend_half:
    preflight_steps = [( ... npm_preflight ... )]
```

So on any ordinary checkout it runs unconditionally. A backend-only sync -- the common case, since most syncs move Python and never touch `website/` -- pays a full scratch install plus its registry traffic to re-derive an answer that is already sitting on disk.

## Why this issue matters to the user

Pull + Build is an interactive button. The operator presses it and waits, and this step is on the critical path before the merge even starts, so its cost is wall-clock time they watch. It also spends registry bandwidth and scratch disk (the probe needs roughly a `node_modules` worth of space, which is why it has its own `EXIT_NO_SPACE` class) on every press.

**The win here is partial, and it is worth saying so up front rather than in a footnote.** This removes the SMALLEST of three redundant frontend costs a backend-only sync pays; the real `npm ci --prefix website` and the vite build still run unconditionally and together outweigh the probe, so the operator will still notice a wait. Those two are tracked as #7132 and the reasons they are a separate change are in section 5.

None of that buys anything when the sync changes no resolution input. The lockfile being installed is the same lockfile whose install is already unpacked in the checkout.

## How our fix solves it

Symptom: an install on every sync. Cause: the probe never asked whether its question was already answered. Fix: ask, and skip only when the answer is provably on disk.

`_install_already_proven` returns a skip reason, or `None` to run the install, and it refuses to skip unless **both** hold:

- **The whole frontend subtree is unchanged** between the incoming ref and the working tree -- `git diff --name-only <ref> -- website` empty, not merely the resolution files identical. This started as a comparison of `package-lock.json` / `package.json` / `.npmrc` alone, and GPT 5.6 found the gap that made it insufficient: with those three identical but frontend SOURCE changed, a skipped probe lets the merge land, and a failing `npm ci` afterwards leaves the checkout with new source and the previously-built bundle -- the stale-bundle half of the very defect the probe exists to prevent. Requiring the entire subtree to be identical makes that unreachable, since with no frontend change there is no new bundle owed. It is also what the item asked for in the first place: skip when the diff touches no frontend files.
- **There is a populated `website/node_modules`** to point at. That tree beside those exact files IS an install of that exact resolution -- it is the evidence. Populated rather than merely present, because an interrupted `npm ci` leaves an empty directory behind and an empty tree proves nothing. With no tree there is no evidence at all, so a fresh checkout's first sync still probes, which is exactly when the answer is least known.

**What makes this safe rather than merely cheap is where a failure lands.** The probe exists because a refusal after the merge left new source beside an emptied tree. Under the unchanged-inputs condition that outcome is unreachable: the runner's `node_modules` transaction (same subsystem, already on main) moves the tree aside and restores it on any non-zero step, and the lockfile it matches did not change -- so a post-merge npm failure restores a tree that is still correct for the merged source. A skipped probe can only leave a state a later `npm ci` fixes, never one no revision produced. That reasoning is why the skip is conditioned on resolution inputs specifically, and why it would NOT be safe as a blanket skip.

Placement: the check lives inside the probe, after the extraction and before the install. It cannot live at step-assembly time in `server.py`, because the incoming ref is created by the sync's own `fetch` step (`+refs/heads/<base>:refs/kirocrew/sync-base-<pid>`) and does not exist yet when the step list is built. After the extraction is the first moment both sides are readable, and before the install is the point of skipping it.

The decision asks `git` and reads one directory -- no `npm`, no network, and nothing that touches the checkout's own `node_modules`. That is what lets the choice to skip a safety probe be tested without running the thing it guards: `npm` is the guarded step, `git` is not.

A skip is reported on the run's `preflight:` detail line instead of the generic pass line, so `main()` now prints the detail when there is one. A skipped safety step should be visible in the log, not inferable from a missing pause.

## What tests we did

Targeted only, with an explicit worker cap (`-p no:randomly -n 4`) -- 55 passed in `test/test_dev_fleet_npm_preflight.py` and 296 in the `test_dev_fleet_app.py` sync/preflight group. CI runs the full suite.

**No real `npm ci` was run to test this.** The decision is exercised against real temp trees with `subprocess.run` stubbed, so `git` answers from a fixture while any `npm ci` invocation fails the test outright. Sixteen new cases in the existing suite:

- The skip fires when the frontend subtree is untouched, and its reason says so -- an operator reading the log must be able to tell why the safety step did not run.
- It does NOT fire for any changed frontend path (parametrized over the lockfile, `package.json`, `.npmrc`, a `.tsx` source file and `index.html`). The source row carries the reason the narrower condition was insufficient in its own assertion message, so the rationale sits on the case it explains rather than in a second test that asserted the same thing -- First Principles asked for that consolidation.
- It does NOT fire with no dependency tree, a present-but-empty tree, or `node_modules` as a file rather than a directory.
- It does NOT fire when the comparison cannot be answered (parametrized over a non-zero `git`, a missing `git`, and a timeout) -- the unknown case costs an install, never a guarantee.
- The diff is pathspec-limited to the frontend half, so a backend-only sync is not disqualified by its own backend diff.
- `probe()` starts no npm process at all when the skip fires -- the point is the cost removed, not the verdict -- and still pays for the install when the frontend did change.
- The CLI reports the skip reason rather than the generic pass line, and still reports the generic line when the install really ran.

Mutation-verified both load-bearing conditions: dropping the populated-tree requirement reddens all three evidence cases, and narrowing the pathspec back to the three resolution files reddens the scope assertion. That second mutation is also documented in the test itself, because it showed the pathspec-width guarantee rests on the scope assertion ALONE -- the stub returns its fixture regardless of pathspec, so the source-only case would have kept passing under the narrowed form. The pair is what covers the gap, and a reader should not have to rediscover whic

author: martien-wdy
body:
## Problem

The Wendy Business Intelligence (BI) episodes browser will play episode video in a browser via signed Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) straight from the bucket. Browsers cannot play what episodes carry today: camera capture is a raw H.264 Annex-B elementary stream (`cameras/<source>/segment-NNNNNN.h264`) with no container and therefore no timing. An earlier decision kept the conversion laptop-side (`episode-playable`) for the demo; the browser-playback requirement reverses that decision deliberately.

## Cause

Nothing in the seal path produced a playable container, so the only playable form of an episode lived outside the episode, unlisted, unchecksummed, and never uploaded. The exact muxer needed already exists on the read side: `go/internal/episodeexport` remuxes the raw stream into a fragmentless MP4 whose per-sample durations come from `index.jsonl` `canonical_episode_nanos` (verified on hardware: 173/173 frames, 174 ns span error, plays in VLC and AVFoundation).

## Solution

Sealing an episode now runs that same remux per camera source, writing `cameras/<source>/playable.mp4` beside the raw capture before `sealFiles` walks the directory. Because it lands before the file list is sealed, the clip gets a size and SHA-256 manifest entry and the rest of the pipeline needs no change at all: `DataTransferWorker` uploads it because it is listed, cloud commit-time verification covers it for the same reason, `wendy data download` and `inspect` verify it like any other listed file, and the bucket object plays in a browser after a plain download.

- **Derived marking**: the entry carries `"role": "derived"` (`File.Role`, `FileRoleDerived`). A derived file is never capture payload; model-input and payload-retention accounting resolve payload bytes through `index.jsonl` into the raw segments, which stay byte-for-byte untouched, so the correlation join is unaffected. The manifest also gains `playable_notes`.
- **Failure honesty**: sealing never fails or waits on the mux. A source whose stream cannot become an honestly timed, seekable clip (B slices, slice headers the muxer cannot parse, no random-access frame, or an outright mux failure) seals without its `playable.mp4`, and `playable_notes` names the reason. A clip that omitted frames whose bytes were missing gets a note too. The gates are the hardened form of the warnings `episode-playable` prints (`BFrames`, `UndecodedSliceHeaders`, `SyncSamples`, `SkippedReason`).
- **Latency shape preserved**: sealing was already a synchronous pass over every episode byte (the checksum walk). The remux is a copy, not a transcode, so the seal gains one more read of the camera bytes, no external dependency, and no new failure mode.
- **Cost bound**: the clip is roughly the size of the raw stream it derives from (verbatim coded pictures plus container overhead). That counts against the episode's size through both the manifest total and the disk-usage walk `enforceQuota` performs.
- **Recovery**: interrupted `.partial` episodes derive the same clips when recovery seals them, after the truncated Javascript Object Notation Lines (JSONL) tails are cut.
- **CLI touch**: `episode-playable` detects an episode whose sources all carry a seal-time `playable.mp4`, says so, and converts nothing. It remains the path for episodes sealed by older agents.
- **Docs**: `docs/clients/wendy-cli/commands/data.md` and the data platform demo runbook now describe the sealed clip and demote the laptop-side conversion to older episodes.

## Verification

- `CC=/usr/bin/clang go build ./go/...` clean; `gofmt -l go/` empty; `go vet` clean on all touched packages.
- `go test ./go/internal/agent/data/... ./go/internal/episodeexport/... ./go/internal/agent/services/... ./go/internal/cli/commands/...` all pass.
- New unit tests: seal produces the MP4 with a matching manifest SHA-256, format `mp4`, role `derived`, source association, and full `Inspect(verify)` passing; B-slice, unparseable-header and no-sync-sample streams seal cleanly with no MP4 on disk, no manifest entry, and a note naming why; raw files stay unmarked and listed; the episode size (and therefore quota) includes the clip; recovery seals the clip too; `ConvertSourceInPlace` leaves the raw capture byte-identical and no `.tmp` behind.

### Hardware verification plan (no device installs done here)

1. Deploy the agent to a camera-bearing device and trigger a campaign episode (or `wendy data start`/`stop`).
2. `wendy data inspect <id>` on the device: expect `cameras/<source>/playable.mp4` listed with `"role": "derived"` and empty `playable_notes`.
3. Let the transfer worker upload, then confirm the cloud commit verified the episode (upload state `uploaded`).
4. Download the bucket object for `cameras/<source>/playable.mp4` with a plain HTTP GET (signed URL) and open it directly in a browser tab; confirm it plays and seeks, and that duration matches the episode span.
5. `wendy data download <id>` on a laptop: verification must pass, and `episode-playable` must report the episode already carries playable files.

author: bpapillon
body:
Adds OTLP trace export to the replicator, off by default.

Tracing turns on only when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set. With it unset — every self-hosted deployment that has not opted in — no exporter is started and no spans are recorded.

This service is run by people outside Schematic, so it is deliberately vendor-neutral: a plain OTLP producer configured entirely through the standard `OTEL_*` variables, with no Datadog attributes and no switch of our own. It will talk to any collector that speaks the protocol. README gains an "OpenTelemetry tracing" section covering how to turn it on, the variables that matter, what gets traced, and how to verify it locally.

Spans are per batch rather than per message: the batch is the unit that succeeds or fails, and a span per message would be enormous and uninformative. Roots are `replicate company` / `user` / `flags`, with the Redis pipeline writes as children. A batch dropped by the open circuit breaker is a failed span carrying `replicator.circuit_breaker.open`.

Sampling is not exposed as a variable of ours — the replicator samples everything and leaves the decision to the collector, where an operator can change it without redeploying.
